# so the downstream alarm path is identical either way". Two templates would
# each carry their own copy of the alarms and the claim would hold only for as
# long as somebody remembered to edit both. Here the alarms sit outside every
# Condition: there is one definition, and the runner is a parameter. The
# identical path is a property of the file rather than a convention.
#
# The cost is a template with two conditional halves, most of which is inert on
# any given deployment. That is the right trade — an inert resource is visible
# in the template; a drifted second copy of an alarm is not.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Questionnaire 7.4 is used THREE times
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# design/06 says twice — canary pass condition and SLA measurement condition.
# design/06a adds the third at `alb-target-response-time`, whose
# `threshold_source: questionnaire_7_4` says "MUST derive from questionnaire
# field 7.4 ... Do not hardcode."
#
# The prompt says to make that explicit "so nobody changes one without the
# other". Making it explicit in a comment would not survive contact with a
# hurried edit, so it is structural instead: this template takes the value ONCE
# as AcceptableResponseMs and writes it to
#
#     /platform/monitoring/acceptable-response-ms
#
# which is the only place any of the three consumers reads it from. The canary
# script reads the SSM parameter, the SLA alarm below reads the same value
# through !Ref, and the instrumentation Lambda resolves the ALB alarm's
# threshold from that parameter. Changing it here changes all three; there is
# no second place to forget.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Question 7.3 is free text and cannot be executed
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The questionnaire asks for a "success condition" as prose, and prose cannot
# become an assertion without somebody translating it. Executing customer-
# supplied text would be worse than useless — it would be a remote code
# execution path into every tenant account, reachable through an intake form.
#
# So the structured form is narrow and deliberately dull: an expected status
# code and a string that must appear in the body. Anything a tenant describes
# that does not reduce to those two belongs in a Playwright suite and takes the
# Fargate path, which is one of the reasons that path exists.
#
# The translation from 7.3 prose to these parameters is a HUMAN step at vesting
# and is not yet wired into derive-vesting.py. B-034.

Metadata:
  cfn-lint:
    config:
      # W1030 only, and only because of AuthSecretArn.
      #
      # The parameter is optional — it is required when questionnaire 7.6 says
      # the journey authenticates and meaningless otherwise — so its default is
      # empty, and every use of it sits inside `!If [HasAuth, ...]`. cfn-lint
      # resolves parameter defaults without regard to Conditions, so it checks
      # the empty string against the ARN format of a statement that cannot
      # deploy while the string is empty.
      #
      # Suppressed at template level because cfn-lint attributes the finding to
      # the PARAMETER rather than to the resource, so a resource-scoped ignore
      # never matches it. The cost is that a genuinely malformed ARN parameter
      # in THIS template would not be caught; there is one ARN parameter here
      # and it is this one. cfn-guard still runs over the file unchanged.
      ignore_checks: [W1030]

Parameters:

  CanaryName:
    Type: String
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z0-9-]{1,21}$'
    Description: >-
      Synthetics caps canary names at 21 characters and allows lowercase,
      numbers and hyphens only. Also the CanaryName metric dimension, which is
      why the Fargate path is constrained by the same rule even though nothing
      in ECS cares — the dimension value must match for the alarms to work.

  RunnerType:
    Type: String
    AllowedValues: [synthetics, fargate]
    Default: synthetics
    Description: >-
      Questionnaire 7.5. `fargate` where the tenant already maintains a
      Playwright suite; CloudWatch Synthetics has no Playwright runtime, so
      reusing their suite means running it ourselves and reporting the result.

  Endpoint:
    Type: String
    Description: 'Questionnaire 7.2. Full URL including scheme.'
    AllowedPattern: '^https?://.+'

  ExpectedStatus:
    Type: Number
    Default: 200
    Description: 'Questionnaire 7.3, structured half one.'

  BodyMustContain:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      Questionnaire 7.3, structured half two. Empty means status code only,
      which is a weaker check than it looks: an error page served with 200 is
      the common way a service fails while appearing healthy.

  AcceptableResponseMs:
    Type: Number
    MinValue: 1
    Description: >-
      Questionnaire 7.4. Canary pass condition, SLA measurement condition, and
      the ALB target-response-time alarm threshold. One number, three
      consumers — see the header.

  JourneyRequiresAuth:
    Type: String
    AllowedValues: ['true', 'false']
    Default: 'false'
    Description: 'Questionnaire 7.6.'

  AuthSecretArn:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      Secrets Manager ARN holding the canary's credentials. Required when
      JourneyRequiresAuth is true. The canary receives the ARN, never the
      credential — Synthetics environment variables are stored and displayed in
      plaintext, so a secret placed in one is a secret published to anyone with
      read access to the canary.

  ScheduleExpression:
    Type: String
    Default: 'rate(5 minutes)'

  EnvironmentTier:
    Type: String
    AllowedValues: [dev, test, uat, prod]

  ArtifactBucket:
    Type: String
    Description: 'Platform Tooling bucket holding the packaged canary script.'

  ArtifactsBucketName:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Where this canary writes its screenshots and HAR files. Created once per
      account by canaries/00-canary-artifacts.yaml and shared by every canary
      in the account, each under its own prefix.

      Not created here: a bucket created by a stack that can fail is a stack
      that cannot be retried, because the retained bucket then fails the next
      create's existence check. See that template's header.

  ArtifactKey:
    Type: String
    Description: 'Content-addressed key of the canary package.'

  AlertTopicArn:
    Type: String
    Default: ''

  LowUrgencyTopicArn:
    Type: String
    Default: ''

  # --- Fargate-only -------------------------------------------------------
  PlaywrightImageUri:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      The tenant's own test image. The platform does not build it and does not
      inject anything into it — see the ResultsFunction comment for why.

  SubnetIds:
    Type: CommaDelimitedList
    Default: ''

  SecurityGroupIds:
    Type: CommaDelimitedList
    Default: ''

  TaskCpu:
    Type: String
    Default: '1024'

  TaskMemory:
    Type: String
    Default: '2048'

Conditions:
  IsSynthetics: !Equals [!Ref RunnerType, synthetics]
  IsFargate: !Equals [!Ref RunnerType, fargate]
  HasAuth: !Equals [!Ref JourneyRequiresAuth, 'true']
  SyntheticsWithAuth: !And [!Condition IsSynthetics, !Condition HasAuth]
  FargateWithAuth: !And [!Condition IsFargate, !Condition HasAuth]
  HasAlerting: !Not [!Equals [!Ref AlertTopicArn, '']]
  # Canary failure is user-visible by definition, so unlike the generic alarm
  # tiers UAT pages here: design/06 says "Production canary failure pages", and
  # 06a already overrides UAT to page for total outage on the same reasoning —
  # real users are in UAT.
  LowUrgency: !And
    - !Not [!Equals [!Ref LowUrgencyTopicArn, '']]
    - !Or
      - !Equals [!Ref EnvironmentTier, dev]
      - !Equals [!Ref EnvironmentTier, test]

Resources:

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The single source for questionnaire 7.4
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AcceptableResponseParam:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: /platform/monitoring/acceptable-response-ms
      Type: String
      Value: !Ref AcceptableResponseMs
      Description: >-
        Questionnaire 7.4. Read by the canary script as its pass condition and
        by the instrumentation Lambda as the alb-target-response-time
        threshold. The SLA alarm in this template uses the same value directly.
        Do not set this by hand — it is owned by the canary stack so that the
        three consumers cannot disagree.

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Native CloudWatch Synthetics
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  CanaryRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Condition: IsSynthetics
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: lambda.amazonaws.com }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: CanaryExecution
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: ['s3:PutObject', 's3:GetBucketLocation']
                # Scoped to this canary's prefix. Canaries in one account share
                # a bucket, and one canary overwriting another's evidence is
                # the kind of thing only noticed while relying on it.
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:s3:::${ArtifactsBucketName}/${CanaryName}/*'
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: 's3:GetBucketLocation'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:s3:::${ArtifactsBucketName}'
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: ['kms:GenerateDataKey', 'kms:Decrypt']
                # The artifacts bucket is SSE-KMS, so PutObject without this
                # fails with AccessDenied naming S3 rather than KMS.
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:kms:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:key/*'
                Condition:
                  StringEquals:
                    'kms:ViaService': !Sub 's3.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com'
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: 's3:ListAllMyBuckets'
                Resource: '*'
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: ['logs:CreateLogStream', 'logs:PutLogEvents', 'logs:CreateLogGroup']
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/lambda/cwsyn-*'
              - Effect: Allow
                # Namespace-scoped. A canary that could write anywhere in
                # CloudWatch could silence an alarm by publishing a healthy
                # value on someone else's metric.
                Action: 'cloudwatch:PutMetricData'
                Resource: '*'
                Condition:
                  StringEquals: { 'cloudwatch:namespace': 'CloudWatchSynthetics' }
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: 'ssm:GetParameter'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:parameter/platform/monitoring/*'

  # Secret access is a separate resource rather than a conditional statement
  # inside the role above. cfn-guard cannot traverse an !If at list-item level:
  # it reported the role as having no statements at all instead of checking the
  # ones it has. A permission hidden that way passes every rule written to
  # examine it, which is the worst way for a policy check to fail.
  CanarySecretPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Condition: SyntheticsWithAuth
    Properties:
      PolicyName: CanarySecret
      Roles: [!Ref CanaryRole]
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Action: 'secretsmanager:GetSecretValue'
            Resource: !Ref AuthSecretArn

  Canary:
    Type: AWS::Synthetics::Canary
    Condition: IsSynthetics
    Properties:
      Name: !Ref CanaryName
      # Prefixed by canary name so one account-level bucket serves every
      # canary without their artifacts interleaving.
      ArtifactS3Location: !Sub 's3://${ArtifactsBucketName}/${CanaryName}'
      ExecutionRoleArn: !GetAtt CanaryRole.Arn
      # Pinned, and checked against `aws synthetics describe-runtime-versions`
      # rather than taken from documentation: syn-python-selenium-4.1 was the
      # version the design-era docs showed and it is now DEPRECATED, which
      # surfaces as a 400 at stack creation with no hint that the cause is age.
      # Runtimes deprecate on a rolling schedule, so this needs revisiting —
      # B-036 carries the check.
      RuntimeVersion: syn-python-selenium-12.0
      StartCanaryAfterCreation: true
      Schedule:
        Expression: !Ref ScheduleExpression
      # Explicit, because the default silently expires run data and the
      # screenshots and HAR files are the triage aid design/06 singles out.
      # Failures kept longer than successes: a failure is evidence, a success is
      # a data point already captured in the metric.
      SuccessRetentionPeriod: 7
      FailureRetentionPeriod: 30
      RunConfig:
        # A hard stop well above AcceptableResponseMs, not derived from it.
        # These measure different things: AcceptableResponseMs is the pass
        # condition — exceed it and the run FAILS and reports a duration — while
        # this is the point at which the run is killed and reports nothing.
        # Deriving one from the other would turn every slow response into a
        # missing data point instead of a recorded failure, which is the more
        # useful of the two.
        TimeoutInSeconds: 60
        ActiveTracing: false
        EnvironmentVariables:
          # No credential appears here. Synthetics stores and displays these in
          # plaintext; the canary gets an ARN and fetches the secret itself.
          CANARY_NAME: !Ref CanaryName
          ENDPOINT: !Ref Endpoint
          EXPECTED_STATUS: !Ref ExpectedStatus
          BODY_MUST_CONTAIN: !Ref BodyMustContain
          RESPONSE_MS_PARAM: !Ref AcceptableResponseParam
          AUTH_SECRET_ARN: !If [HasAuth, !Ref AuthSecretArn, '']
      Code:
        Handler: heartbeat.handler
        S3Bucket: !Ref ArtifactBucket
        S3Key: !Ref ArtifactKey
      Tags:
        - { Key: platform-managed, Value: 'true' }
        - { Key: platform-canary, Value: !Ref CanaryName }

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Fargate runner for existing Playwright suites
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # design/06 justifies this by saying "There is no native Playwright runtime in
  # CloudWatch Synthetics". That is NO LONGER TRUE — as of 2026-09-18 the
  # account offers syn-nodejs-playwright-8.0, and has offered some Playwright
  # runtime since 2024-11. The design package predates it.
  #
  # The runner is kept anyway, on a narrower justification than the one the
  # design gives. The native Playwright runtime runs a canary SCRIPT written to
  # the Synthetics Playwright API; it does not run a tenant's existing suite
  # with its own config, fixtures, projects and dependencies. Questionnaire 7.5
  # asks whether there is an "existing test suite to reuse", and reuse is the
  # word that matters — a suite that has to be rewritten to fit a runtime is not
  # being reused.
  #
  # Where a tenant's suite is small enough to port, the native runtime is now
  # the better answer: no cluster, no image to maintain, and screenshots and HAR
  # capture for free. B-035 covers adding it as a third RunnerType.
  #
  # The platform runs the tenant's image unmodified and reads the result from
  # the task's exit code. No wrapper is injected and no entrypoint is
  # overridden.
  #
  # The alternative — mounting a reporting shim into their container — was
  # rejected because it makes the platform a participant in their test run. A
  # shim that fails takes their suite down; a shim that needs their Node version
  # makes their image upgrade our problem. Exit code zero is the one contract
  # every test runner already honours, Playwright included.
  #
  # What this costs: granularity. We learn pass or fail and how long it took,
  # not which of forty assertions failed. That detail is in their own test
  # output, which is where someone debugging a failed suite is going to look
  # regardless.
  TaskExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Condition: IsFargate
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy'

  # Same reasoning as CanarySecretPolicy. The ECS agent reads the secret to
  # inject it, so this is on the EXECUTION role; the task role below gets
  # nothing.
  TaskExecutionSecretPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Condition: FargateWithAuth
    Properties:
      PolicyName: CanarySecret
      Roles: [!Ref TaskExecutionRole]
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Action: 'secretsmanager:GetSecretValue'
            Resource: !Ref AuthSecretArn

  TaskRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Condition: IsFargate
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      # No Policies key at all, rather than an empty list. The tenant's test
      # image runs under this role and is trusted with nothing — in particular
      # it cannot publish its own metrics, because a suite able to write its own
      # SuccessPercent could report itself healthy while failing.
      #
      # An empty list says the same thing to CloudFormation and something
      # different to cfn-guard, which read it as a policy it could not inspect.

  CanaryLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Condition: IsFargate
    DeletionPolicy: Delete
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Delete
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/platform/canary/${CanaryName}'
      RetentionInDays: 30
      # The tenant's own test output lands here, and a failing UI test prints
      # whatever was on the page.
      KmsKeyId: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:kms:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:alias/platform-logs'

  CanaryCluster:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Cluster
    Condition: IsFargate
    Properties:
      ClusterName: !Sub 'platform-canary-${CanaryName}'
      ClusterSettings:
        - { Name: containerInsights, Value: enabled }

  CanaryTaskDefinition:
    Type: AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition
    Condition: IsFargate
    Properties:
      Family: !Sub 'platform-canary-${CanaryName}'
      RequiresCompatibilities: [FARGATE]
      NetworkMode: awsvpc
      Cpu: !Ref TaskCpu
      Memory: !Ref TaskMemory
      ExecutionRoleArn: !GetAtt TaskExecutionRole.Arn
      TaskRoleArn: !GetAtt TaskRole.Arn
      ContainerDefinitions:
        - Name: suite
          Image: !Ref PlaywrightImageUri
          Essential: true
          Environment:
            - { Name: CANARY_ENDPOINT, Value: !Ref Endpoint }
            - { Name: CANARY_ACCEPTABLE_RESPONSE_MS, Value: !Ref AcceptableResponseMs }
          Secrets: !If
            - HasAuth
            # Injected by the ECS agent, not by the task. The credential never
            # passes through a platform-authored process.
            - [{ Name: CANARY_AUTH, ValueFrom: !Ref AuthSecretArn }]
            - !Ref 'AWS::NoValue'
          LogConfiguration:
            LogDriver: awslogs
            Options:
              awslogs-group: !Ref CanaryLogGroup
              awslogs-region: !Ref AWS::Region
              awslogs-stream-prefix: suite

  SuiteScheduleRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Condition: IsFargate
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: events.amazonaws.com }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: RunCanaryTask
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: 'ecs:RunTask'
                Resource: !Ref CanaryTaskDefinition
                Condition:
                  ArnEquals: { 'ecs:cluster': !GetAtt CanaryCluster.Arn }
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: 'iam:PassRole'
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt TaskRole.Arn
                  - !GetAtt TaskExecutionRole.Arn
                Condition:
                  StringEquals: { 'iam:PassedToService': 'ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com' }

  SuiteScheduleRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Condition: IsFargate
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub 'platform-canary-${CanaryName}'
      ScheduleExpression: !Ref ScheduleExpression
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Id: suite
          Arn: !GetAtt CanaryCluster.Arn
          RoleArn: !GetAtt SuiteScheduleRole.Arn
          EcsParameters:
            TaskDefinitionArn: !Ref CanaryTaskDefinition
            LaunchType: FARGATE
            TaskCount: 1
            NetworkConfiguration:
              AwsVpcConfiguration:
                Subnets: !Ref SubnetIds
                SecurityGroups: !Ref SecurityGroupIds
                AssignPublicIp: DISABLED

  # The half that makes the two runners equivalent: it turns an ECS task result
  # into the same metrics Synthetics publishes, in the same namespace, on the
  # same dimension. Everything downstream — the alarms below, the response
  # engine, PagerDuty — cannot tell which runner produced them, which is the
  # point.
  ResultsRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Condition: IsFargate
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: lambda.amazonaws.com }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: PublishCanaryMetrics
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: 'cloudwatch:PutMetricData'
                Resource: '*'
                Condition:
                  StringEquals: { 'cloudwatch:namespace': 'CloudWatchSynthetics' }
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: 'ssm:GetParameter'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:parameter/platform/monitoring/*'

  ResultsFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Condition: IsFargate
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Sub 'platform-canary-results-${CanaryName}'
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: results.handler
      Role: !GetAtt ResultsRole.Arn
      Timeout: 60
      MemorySize: 256
      Code:
        S3Bucket: !Ref ArtifactBucket
        S3Key: !Ref ArtifactKey
      Environment:
        Variables:
          CANARY_NAME: !Ref CanaryName
          TASK_DEFINITION_FAMILY: !Sub 'platform-canary-${CanaryName}'
          RESPONSE_MS_PARAM: !Ref AcceptableResponseParam

  TaskStateChangeRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Condition: IsFargate
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub 'platform-canary-result-${CanaryName}'
      EventPattern:
        source: ['aws.ecs']
        detail-type: ['ECS Task State Change']
        detail:
          clusterArn: [!GetAtt CanaryCluster.Arn]
          lastStatus: ['STOPPED']
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Id: results
          Arn: !GetAtt ResultsFunction.Arn

  ResultsInvokePermission:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Permission
    Condition: IsFargate
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !GetAtt ResultsFunction.Arn
      Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
      Principal: events.amazonaws.com
      SourceArn: !GetAtt TaskStateChangeRule.Arn

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Alarms — defined ONCE, outside every Condition
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Not in design/06a, deliberately. 06a is consumed by the instrumentation
  # Lambda, which alarms resources AWS Config discovers. A Fargate-run canary is
  # not a discoverable resource — there is no AWS::Synthetics::Canary to find —
  # so putting the canary alarms in 06a would cover one runner and not the
  # other, and would do it silently.
  #
  # AWS::Synthetics::Canary is therefore listed in 06a's resource_types_no_alarms
  # so the instrumentation Lambda does not also alarm the native canaries and
  # produce two alarms per canary with different names. See docs/deviations.md.

  CanaryFailedAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Properties:
      AlarmName: !Sub 'platform-canary-${CanaryName}-failed'
      AlarmDescription: !Sub >-
        The synthetic check for ${CanaryName} failed against ${Endpoint}.
        Generic alarms say a thing is running; this one says it does not work.
        Treat as user-visible until proven otherwise.
      Namespace: CloudWatchSynthetics
      MetricName: SuccessPercent
      Dimensions:
        - Name: CanaryName
          Value: !Ref CanaryName
      Statistic: Average
      Period: 300
      # Two periods, not one. A single failed run is frequently the canary's own
      # network path rather than the service — the design's own warning that
      # nothing should page for something a human cannot act on applies to the
      # monitoring as much as to the workload.
      EvaluationPeriods: 2
      DatapointsToAlarm: 2
      Threshold: 100
      ComparisonOperator: LessThanThreshold
      # A canary that has stopped reporting is a canary that is not checking.
      # Treating that as healthy is the specific failure synthetic monitoring
      # exists to avoid.
      TreatMissingData: breaching
      AlarmActions: !If
        - LowUrgency
        - [!Ref LowUrgencyTopicArn]
        - !If [HasAlerting, [!Ref AlertTopicArn], !Ref 'AWS::NoValue']
      OKActions: !If
        - LowUrgency
        - [!Ref LowUrgencyTopicArn]
        - !If [HasAlerting, [!Ref AlertTopicArn], !Ref 'AWS::NoValue']

  # The SLA measurement condition. Same number as the canary's pass condition,
  # by construction rather than by convention.
  #
  # Synthetics only, and on ResponseTimeMs rather than the built-in Duration.
  #
  # Duration measures the whole canary RUN — container start, boto3 init, the
  # step, teardown. On the first live run against a service answering in 185ms,
  # Duration reported 10,100ms. Thresholding that against the tenant's agreed
  # response time alarms on our own cold start, and reports it to them as their
  # latency. ResponseTimeMs is published by the canary script and is the request
  # and nothing else.
  #
  # The Fargate runner has no equivalent and deliberately gets no SLA alarm.
  # Task wall-clock includes Fargate provisioning, so it has the same defect as
  # Duration and worse; and the platform does not instrument the tenant's suite,
  # so it cannot see the suite's own timings. Questionnaire 7.4 is instead
  # enforced INSIDE the suite — the task definition passes it as
  # CANARY_ACCEPTABLE_RESPONSE_MS, the suite fails itself when it is exceeded,
  # and that surfaces through SuccessPercent and CanaryFailedAlarm above.
  #
  # So the failure path is identical for both runners, as prompt 4.3 requires,
  # and the latency path is honest about only one of them being able to measure
  # it. A Duration-based alarm on the Fargate side would have looked identical
  # and reported a number that was mostly container startup.
  CanarySlaAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Condition: IsSynthetics
    Properties:
      AlarmName: !Sub 'platform-canary-${CanaryName}-slow'
      AlarmDescription: !Sub >-
        ${CanaryName} answered, but slower than the agreed acceptable response
        time of ${AcceptableResponseMs}ms (questionnaire 7.4). This is the SLA
        measurement condition and the same value the canary uses to pass or
        fail a run.
      Namespace: CloudWatchSynthetics
      MetricName: ResponseTimeMs
      Dimensions:
        - Name: CanaryName
          Value: !Ref CanaryName
      Statistic: Average
      Period: 300
      EvaluationPeriods: 3
      Threshold: !Ref AcceptableResponseMs
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanThreshold
      # Not breaching: a missing ResponseTimeMs means no run completed, which
      # CanaryFailedAlarm above already reports. Two alarms for one cause is how
      # a pager gets ignored.
      TreatMissingData: notBreaching
      AlarmActions: !If
        - LowUrgency
        - [!Ref LowUrgencyTopicArn]
        - !If [HasAlerting, [!Ref AlertTopicArn], !Ref 'AWS::NoValue']

Outputs:
  CanaryName:
    Value: !Ref CanaryName
  RunnerType:
    Value: !Ref RunnerType
  AcceptableResponseParam:
    Description: 'The single source for questionnaire 7.4.'
    Value: !Ref AcceptableResponseParam
  MetricNamespace:
    Description: >-
      Identical for both runners. CloudWatchSynthetics is not an AWS/ reserved
      namespace, so the Fargate results Lambda can publish into it.
    Value: CloudWatchSynthetics
files.change/00-appdeployer.yaml:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  AltDigital Managed Platform — the AppDeployer role (prompt 8.1). The single
  control point through which a tenant's CI deploys into a member account. OIDC
  federation only, no static credentials, and a permissions boundary the role
  cannot remove from itself.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why a role at all, when AltDigital does not control the pipeline
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# design/08-change-and-release.md, "The constraint":
#
#   Development teams are not overseen by AltDigital. SOC 2 requires visibility
#   and approval of changes to the environment. We therefore cannot rely on a
#   gate we control — change management is a detective control, reconciled
#   continuously.
#
# So this role is not a gate that approves anything. It is the CHOKE POINT that
# makes the detective control possible: every deployment passes through one
# named principal, so every deployment is attributable in CloudTrail whether the
# dev team cooperates or not.
#
# design 08 again, on why that survives a change of supplier: "A later team
# arriving with its own pipeline keeps their pipeline — they simply hand off at
# this role. The control point stays constant even as the tooling varies."
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# No static credentials. Ever.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The trust policy below federates an OIDC provider and nothing else. There is
# no IAM user, no access key, and no cross-account role that could be given one.
#
# That is worth more than it sounds. A long-lived deploy key in a CI system is
# the credential most likely to end up in a repository, a support ticket or a
# container image, and it is the one nobody rotates because rotating it breaks
# the pipeline on a Friday. An OIDC token is minted per run, expires in minutes,
# and cannot be copied anywhere useful.
#
# THE SUBJECT CONDITION IS THE WHOLE CONTROL. Trusting the provider alone would
# let ANY repository on that CI platform — anyone's GitHub account, anywhere —
# assume this role. `token.actions.githubusercontent.com` is a single issuer
# shared by every GitHub user on earth. The `sub` condition is what narrows it
# to one tenant's repository, and this template refuses to deploy without one.

Parameters:

  ApplicationCode:
    Type: String
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,8}[a-z0-9])?$'
    Description: >-
      The application this role deploys, from the account naming convention.
      Used to scope every resource pattern below, so two applications in one
      account cannot deploy over each other.

  OidcProviderUrl:
    Type: String
    Default: 'https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com'
    AllowedPattern: '^https://.+'
    Description: >-
      The tenant's CI identity provider. Questionnaire 8.1 collects the tooling
      (`cicd_tooling`); this is the issuer that tooling actually presents.

      GitHub Actions is the default because it is the common case, not because
      it is assumed — GitLab, Bitbucket Pipelines and CircleCI all publish an
      OIDC issuer and all work here unchanged.

  OidcAudience:
    Type: String
    Default: 'sts.amazonaws.com'
    Description: >-
      The `aud` claim. For GitHub Actions configured with
      aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials this is sts.amazonaws.com.

  OidcSubjectPattern:
    Type: String
    MinLength: 3
    Description: >-
      REQUIRED, and the most important parameter in this template.

      The `sub` claim pattern that may assume the role, e.g.
      `repo:acme-corp/payments-service:ref:refs/heads/main` or
      `repo:acme-corp/payments-service:environment:production`.

      There is no default and no wildcard-only value accepted, because the OIDC
      issuer is shared by every user of that CI platform. A trust policy that
      checks the issuer and not the subject is assumable by any repository in
      the world — it looks like federation and is an open door.

      Prefer pinning to a branch or a deployment environment rather than
      `repo:org/name:*`. A pattern ending in `:*` lets any branch, including one
      opened by a pull request from a fork, deploy to production.

  OidcThumbprintList:
    Type: CommaDelimitedList
    Default: '6938fd4d98bab03faadb97b34396831e3780aea1'
    Description: >-
      Certificate thumbprint(s) for the provider. The default is GitHub's
      long-standing value.

      AWS no longer verifies this for well-known providers and rotates it
      itself, so a stale value is usually harmless — "usually" being why it is a
      parameter rather than a constant.

  CreateOidcProvider:
    Type: String
    Default: 'true'
    AllowedValues: ['true', 'false']
    Description: >-
      An IAM OIDC provider is an ACCOUNT-LEVEL resource, one per issuer URL.
      Two stacks in the same account both trying to create
      token.actions.githubusercontent.com will collide — the second fails with
      EntityAlreadyExists, which names the entity and not the other stack.

      Set false for the second and subsequent applications in an account and
      pass ExistingOidcProviderArn instead.

  ExistingOidcProviderArn:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: 'Used when CreateOidcProvider is false.'

Conditions:
  MakeProvider: !Equals [!Ref CreateOidcProvider, 'true']

Resources:

  OidcProvider:
    Type: AWS::IAM::OIDCProvider
    Condition: MakeProvider
    # Retain. The provider is shared by every AppDeployer role in the account,
    # so deleting this stack must not break the other applications' pipelines.
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Url: !Ref OidcProviderUrl
      ClientIdList: [!Ref OidcAudience]
      ThumbprintList: !Ref OidcThumbprintList

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The boundary, defined before the role that must carry it
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Prompt 8.1: "Include a permissions boundary so the role cannot escalate
  # itself."
  #
  # A boundary is a ceiling, not a grant. Whatever the role's own policy says,
  # the effective permission is the intersection — so a tenant who talks
  # somebody into widening the role's policy still cannot exceed this.
  #
  # The explicit denies matter more than the allows. Without them, a role with
  # iam:* in its own policy could create a SECOND role with no boundary and
  # assume it, which is the classic boundary escape and the reason
  # iam:CreateRole is denied here unless the new role carries this same
  # boundary.
  AppDeployerBoundary:
    Type: AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy
    Properties:
      ManagedPolicyName: !Sub 'PlatformAppDeployerBoundary-${ApplicationCode}'
      Description: >-
        Permissions boundary for the AppDeployer role. Caps what the role can
        ever do, regardless of what its own policy grants.
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: TheCeiling
            Effect: Allow
            # Deliberately broad on the allow side. The boundary's job is to
            # cap, and the role's OWN policy is what grants; listing services
            # here as well would mean maintaining the same list twice and
            # discovering the drift when a legitimate deploy fails.
            Action:
              - 'cloudformation:*'
              - 'ecs:*'
              - 'lambda:*'
              - 'ec2:Describe*'
              - 'ecr:*'
              - 'logs:*'
              - 's3:*'
              - 'rds:Describe*'
              - 'rds:ModifyDBParameterGroup'
              - 'elasticloadbalancing:*'
              - 'application-autoscaling:*'
              - 'apigateway:*'
              - 'states:*'
              - 'events:*'
              - 'sqs:*'
              - 'sns:*'
              - 'ssm:GetParameter*'
              - 'secretsmanager:GetSecretValue'
              - 'iam:PassRole'
              - 'iam:Get*'
              - 'iam:List*'
              - 'sts:GetCallerIdentity'
              - 'kms:Decrypt'
              - 'kms:GenerateDataKey'
              - 'kms:DescribeKey'
            Resource: '*'

          - Sid: NeverTouchPlatformManagedResources
            Effect: Deny
            # design 08: "Denied from touching platform-managed resources
            # (SCP)". The SCP is the outer fence; this is the inner one, and
            # both exist because they fail differently. An SCP protects against
            # everything in the account; a boundary travels with the role even
            # if the account is later moved out from under that SCP.
            Action: '*'
            Resource:
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:role/Platform*'
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:policy/Platform*'
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole'
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:role/stacksets-exec-*'
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/platform/*'

          - Sid: NeverEscapeTheBoundary
            Effect: Deny
            # The escape this exists to close: create a new role WITHOUT a
            # boundary, give it everything, assume it. Creating roles is
            # permitted only when the new role carries this exact boundary,
            # so the ceiling is inherited rather than shed.
            Action:
              - 'iam:CreateRole'
              - 'iam:CreateUser'
            Resource: '*'
            Condition:
              StringNotEquals:
                'iam:PermissionsBoundary': !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:policy/PlatformAppDeployerBoundary-${ApplicationCode}'

          - Sid: NeverAlterTheBoundaryItself
            Effect: Deny
            # Without this, the role could rewrite its own ceiling. Note
            # DeleteRolePermissionsBoundary in particular — removing the
            # boundary is the same escape as never having had one.
            Action:
              - 'iam:DeleteRolePermissionsBoundary'
              - 'iam:DeleteUserPermissionsBoundary'
              - 'iam:PutRolePermissionsBoundary'
              - 'iam:PutUserPermissionsBoundary'
              - 'iam:CreatePolicyVersion'
              - 'iam:DeletePolicy'
              - 'iam:DeletePolicyVersion'
              - 'iam:SetDefaultPolicyVersion'
            Resource:
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:policy/PlatformAppDeployerBoundary-*'
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:role/PlatformAppDeployer-*'

          - Sid: NeverDisarmTheDetectiveControl
            Effect: Deny
            # The whole of design 08 rests on CloudTrail being the
            # authoritative record. A deployer that can stop logging can
            # deploy unobserved, and reconciliation would show a quiet month
            # rather than a gap.
            #
            # These are also denied by SCP. Both, because a boundary is
            # attached to the role and an SCP to the account, and the question
            # "which one is missing" should never have a single answer.
            Action:
              - 'cloudtrail:StopLogging'
              - 'cloudtrail:DeleteTrail'
              - 'cloudtrail:UpdateTrail'
              - 'cloudtrail:PutEventSelectors'
              - 'config:DeleteConfigurationRecorder'
              - 'config:StopConfigurationRecorder'
              - 'config:DeleteDeliveryChannel'
              - 'guardduty:DeleteDetector'
              - 'guardduty:UpdateDetector'
              - 'securityhub:DisableSecurityHub'
              - 'kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion'
              - 'kms:DisableKey'
              - 'backup:DeleteBackupVault'
              - 'backup:DeleteRecoveryPoint'
              - 'organizations:LeaveOrganization'
            Resource: '*'

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The role
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AppDeployerRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      # Platform-prefixed so the SCP that stops a member account editing
      # platform roles also protects this one. A tenant that could rewrite its
      # own deployer role's trust policy could point it at any repository.
      RoleName: !Sub 'PlatformAppDeployer-${ApplicationCode}'
      Description: >-
        The single control point for tenant deployments into this account.
        Assumable only by the tenant CI identity over OIDC. Every assumption is
        reconciled against a change record - design 08.
      # One hour. A deploy that needs longer than an hour of continuously valid
      # credentials is a deploy that should be broken into steps; the cost of a
      # leaked short-lived token scales with this number.
      MaxSessionDuration: 3600
      PermissionsBoundary: !Ref AppDeployerBoundary
      # Written as a !Sub'd JSON STRING rather than as YAML, and not by choice.
      #
      # An IAM condition KEY here has to be `<issuer-host>:aud`, which means
      # interpolating a parameter into a mapping key. CloudFormation refuses:
      # `Unhashable type "{'Fn::Sub': ...}"`, an error that names the YAML
      # construct and says nothing about condition keys. The same trap caught
      # containment/20-exercise-target.yaml, where the fix was to hardcode the
      # key — viable there because it was one tag, not viable here because the
      # issuer varies per tenant and hardcoding GitHub would silently break
      # every GitLab tenant.
      #
      # AssumeRolePolicyDocument accepts a JSON string, so !Sub can build the
      # whole document and the keys interpolate normally.
      #
      # Note the host is the URL with the scheme STRIPPED. The condition key is
      # `token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub`, not
      # `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub` — a trust policy with
      # the scheme left on parses, deploys, and then matches nothing, so every
      # assumption fails with a message about the token rather than about the
      # policy.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument: !Sub
        - |
          {
            "Version": "2012-10-17",
            "Statement": [
              {
                "Effect": "Allow",
                "Principal": { "Federated": "${ProviderArn}" },
                "Action": "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
                "Condition": {
                  "StringEquals": { "${IssuerHost}:aud": "${OidcAudience}" },
                  "StringLike": { "${IssuerHost}:sub": "${OidcSubjectPattern}" }
                }
              }
            ]
          }
        - ProviderArn: !If
            - MakeProvider
            - !Ref OidcProvider
            - !Ref ExistingOidcProviderArn
          IssuerHost: !Select [1, !Split ['https://', !Ref OidcProviderUrl]]
      Tags:
        - { Key: platform-managed, Value: 'true' }
        - { Key: platform-purpose, Value: tenant-deployment }
        - { Key: platform-application, Value: !Ref ApplicationCode }

  AppDeployerPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: Deploy
      Roles: [!Ref AppDeployerRole]
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: DeployTheApplicationStack
            Effect: Allow
            # Scoped by NAME to this application. design 08: "Scoped to the
            # resources that application legitimately deploys". Two tenants'
            # applications in one account cannot reach each other's stacks.
            Action: 'cloudformation:*'
            Resource:
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:cloudformation:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:stack/${ApplicationCode}-*/*'
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:cloudformation:${AWS::Region}:aws:transform/*'
          - Sid: ReadCloudFormationGlobally
            Effect: Allow
            # ValidateTemplate and the List* calls have no resource to scope
            # to; CloudFormation rejects a resource ARN on them entirely.
            Action:
              - 'cloudformation:ValidateTemplate'
              - 'cloudformation:List*'
              - 'cloudformation:Describe*'
            Resource: '*'
          - Sid: TheApplicationsOwnCompute
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - 'ecs:*'
              - 'lambda:*'
              - 'states:*'
              - 'apigateway:*'
              - 'elasticloadbalancing:*'
              - 'application-autoscaling:*'
            Resource: '*'
          - Sid: ImagesAndArtifacts
            Effect: Allow
            Action: ['ecr:*']
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ecr:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:repository/${ApplicationCode}*'
          - Sid: EcrAuthIsAccountLevel
            Effect: Allow
            # GetAuthorizationToken takes no resource. Without it `docker
            # login` fails with an authorization error that reads like bad
            # credentials rather than a missing permission.
            Action: 'ecr:GetAuthorizationToken'
            Resource: '*'
          - Sid: ObservabilityForItsOwnWorkloads
            Effect: Allow
            Action: ['logs:*']
            Resource:
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/lambda/${ApplicationCode}*'
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/ecs/${ApplicationCode}*'
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/${ApplicationCode}*'
          - Sid: PassOnlyItsOwnRoles
            Effect: Allow
            # iam:PassRole is the most commonly over-granted permission in AWS
            # and the usual route from "can deploy" to "can be anything": pass
            # a privileged role to a Lambda you control and the Lambda runs as
            # that role. Narrowed to roles named for this application.
            Action: 'iam:PassRole'
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:role/${ApplicationCode}-*'
          - Sid: ReadConfigurationAndSecretsItOwns
            Effect: Allow
            Action: ['ssm:GetParameter', 'ssm:GetParameters', 'ssm:GetParametersByPath']
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:parameter/${ApplicationCode}/*'
          - Sid: SecretsForItsOwnApplication
            Effect: Allow
            Action: 'secretsmanager:GetSecretValue'
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:secretsmanager:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:secret:${ApplicationCode}/*'
          - Sid: KnowWhoItIs
            Effect: Allow
            # sts:GetCallerIdentity is how a pipeline proves which role it
            # assumed, and it is the first thing in any useful deploy log.
            Action: 'sts:GetCallerIdentity'
            Resource: '*'

Outputs:
  AppDeployerRoleArn:
    Description: >-
      Give this to the tenant. It is the only credential they ever receive, and
      it is not a credential — it is a role ARN their pipeline assumes.
    Value: !GetAtt AppDeployerRole.Arn
  BoundaryArn:
    Value: !Ref AppDeployerBoundary
  OidcProviderArn:
    Description: >-
      Pass as ExistingOidcProviderArn for the second and subsequent
      applications in this account.
    Value: !If [MakeProvider, !Ref OidcProvider, !Ref ExistingOidcProviderArn]
  SubjectPattern:
    Description: >-
      Recorded in the outputs so that "who can deploy here" is answerable from
      the stack without reading the trust policy.
    Value: !Ref OidcSubjectPattern
files.change/10-reconciliation.yaml:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  AltDigital Managed Platform — change reconciliation (prompt 8.2). Captures
  deployment events from every member account, compares them against change
  records in Jira on a schedule, and produces design 08's four outcomes plus a
  fifth for when the change source cannot be read. Deploys to the Audit account.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A detective control, reconciled continuously
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# design/08-change-and-release.md: "Development teams are not overseen by
# AltDigital [...] we therefore cannot rely on a gate we control — change
# management is a detective control, reconciled continuously."
#
# Nothing in this stack blocks a deployment. It observes and compares, and the
# gap between what happened and what was declared is the finding. design 08 is
# direct about why that is the stronger position anyway: "Auditors accept
# continuous reconciliation far more readily than a signature on a form,
# because it is evidence rather than a claim."
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why capture and reconciliation are separated in TIME
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Capture is event-driven and immediate. Reconciliation runs on a schedule over
# a window that is wider than the schedule interval.
#
# That is not an optimisation. A change record is routinely filed minutes AFTER
# a pipeline starts — somebody opens the ticket while the build runs —
# so reconciling at capture time would report a large share of a
# well-behaved tenant's deployments as unapproved. The window is what lets the
# two arrive in either order.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The fifth outcome
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# design 08's table has four. The engine implements five, and the extra one
# carries the weight: `change_source_unavailable`.
#
# If Jira cannot be read — expired token, wrong project, an issue type that
# does not exist in the project — the engine does not conclude "no approved
# change". Reporting every deployment in the estate as unapproved because a
# credential expired is B-054's lesson (a denied lookup read as a negative
# result) with B-043's blast radius (a finding on every run until somebody
# mutes it). An unreadable change source is one finding about the platform.

Parameters:

  ArtifactBucket:
    Type: String

  ArtifactKey:
    Type: String

  AlertBusName:
    Type: String
    Default: platform-alerts
    Description: >-
      The organization event bus. Deployment events arrive here from member
      accounts via baseline/70-event-forwarding.yaml, and findings are
      published back onto it so the ONE routing layer decides who hears them.

  ChangeTableName:
    Type: String
    Default: platform-change-events
    Description: Append-only deployment event record.

  JiraSite:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      Jira Cloud site URL. Empty means reconciliation reports the change source
      as unavailable rather than guessing — which is the correct behaviour
      before the credential is in place, and is why this has a default at all.

  JiraSecretName:
    Type: String
    Default: platform/jira/service-account
    Description: >-
      Holds {"email", "api_token"}. Written by scripts/set-jira-token.sh into
      THIS account — a secret is only useful where it is read.

  JiraChangeIssueType:
    Type: String
    Default: Change
    Description: >-
      The issue type that represents a change record. The engine verifies this
      type EXISTS in the project before searching: a wrong value returns zero
      issues, and an engine that trusted that would report every deployment as
      unapproved. open-items.md B9 settles the correct value.

  JiraApproverGroups:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      Comma-separated Jira group name(s) written to a change record's Approver
      groups field. The change workflow's Authorize stage needs one approval
      from each; a record filed without any group cannot be approved at all,
      and an unapproved record does not cover a deployment. Empty is allowed
      so a project with no approval stage still files records.

  JiraOpsProject:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      AltDigital's OWN operations project. design 08 treats the platform's
      pipeline as a separate thing from a tenant's — "The platform's own
      pipeline [...] the most privileged thing AltDigital owns" — with its own
      approver.

      A baseline rollout IS a change, but it is not the TENANT's change.
      Reconciling it against their records reports them as having failed to
      file something they were never party to, which is both wrong and the
      kind of wrong that erodes trust in every other finding.

  JiraDefaultChangeProject:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      Fallback change project, used when an account has no per-tenant project
      recorded. Exists so the sandbox can be exercised before the first tenant
      is vested. Its use is RECORDED in every finding rather than applied
      silently — reconciling one tenant's deployments against another tenant's
      change project would produce confident nonsense.

  ReconcileSchedule:
    Type: String
    Default: 'rate(6 hours)'
    Description: >-
      How often the comparison runs. Four times a day rather than hourly: the
      lookback window is wider than the interval, so nothing is missed by
      running less often, and each run costs a Jira search per account.

  LookbackHours:
    Type: Number
    Default: 26
    MinValue: 2
    Description: >-
      Deliberately wider than the schedule interval. A run that looked back
      exactly one interval would lose any deployment that landed while the
      previous run was executing, and would never revisit it.

  JiraTokenExpires:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    AllowedPattern: '^([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2})?$'
    Description: >-
      YYYY-MM-DD. Atlassian caps API token lifetime at one year.

      Not a secret — a date is not a credential — and it needs to be visible
      enough to act on. When the token expires, reconciliation degrades to
      "change source unavailable", which is correct and produces no false
      compliance findings, and then stays that way silently. The expiry notice
      goes to the Atlassian account's email, which is outside the platform's
      control.

      So the platform watches its own credential: every run publishes
      JiraTokenDaysRemaining and the alarm below fires well before the date.

  LogsKeyArn:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      Pass the alerts key. alias/platform-logs is created by the MEMBER
      baseline and does not exist in a platform account.

  AlertTopicArn:
    Type: String
    Default: ''

Conditions:
  UseDefaultLogsKey: !Equals [!Ref LogsKeyArn, '']
  HasAlerting: !Not [!Equals [!Ref AlertTopicArn, '']]

Resources:

  ChangeTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    # Retain. These records are the evidence that change management was
    # operating, and reconciliation is RETROSPECTIVE — a month of deployment
    # events lost is a month that can never be reconciled, because CloudTrail
    # in the member account expires long before an audit asks.
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      TableName: !Ref ChangeTableName
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - { AttributeName: PK, AttributeType: S }
        - { AttributeName: SK, AttributeType: S }
        - { AttributeName: record_type, AttributeType: S }
        - { AttributeName: occurred_at, AttributeType: S }
      KeySchema:
        # PK is deployment#<account>, SK is the ISO timestamp. That shape is
        # what makes both queries this engine needs cheap: "everything in this
        # account since T" for reconciliation, and "everything in this account
        # between T1 and T2" for the outage correlation.
        - { AttributeName: PK, KeyType: HASH }
        - { AttributeName: SK, KeyType: RANGE }
      GlobalSecondaryIndexes:
        # How reconciliation finds deployments WITHOUT first knowing which
        # accounts to look in.
        #
        # The first version derived the account list from the tenant facts map,
        # and that was a silent gap waiting to happen: an account absent from
        # the map -- newly vested, or one the sync had not been re-run for --
        # would have its deployments captured and then never reconciled. The
        # evidence would accumulate and nothing would ever compare it, which
        # reads as a clean account rather than an unexamined one.
        #
        # Reading the deployments themselves means reconciliation covers
        # everything that was captured, and an account missing from the facts
        # map falls back to the platform default WITH that fact recorded in
        # every finding.
        - IndexName: by-record-type
          KeySchema:
            - { AttributeName: record_type, KeyType: HASH }
            - { AttributeName: occurred_at, KeyType: RANGE }
          Projection:
            ProjectionType: ALL
      PointInTimeRecoverySpecification:
        PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled: true
      SSESpecification:
        SSEEnabled: true
      Tags:
        - { Key: platform-managed, Value: 'true' }
        - { Key: platform-purpose, Value: change-reconciliation }

  ReconcileRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: PlatformChangeReconciliation
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: lambda.amazonaws.com }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: Reconcile
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: AppendOnlyDeploymentRecord
                Effect: Allow
                # No UpdateItem and no DeleteItem. The deployment record is
                # evidence of what a tenant did; nothing in this platform
                # should be able to edit it after the fact, least of all the
                # component that reports on it.
                Action: ['dynamodb:PutItem', 'dynamodb:Query']
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt ChangeTable.Arn
                  - !Sub '${ChangeTable.Arn}/index/by-record-type'
              - Sid: ReadTheJiraCredential
                Effect: Allow
                Action: 'secretsmanager:GetSecretValue'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:secretsmanager:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:secret:${JiraSecretName}-*'
              - Sid: ReadTenantFacts
                Effect: Allow
                # Which Jira project holds each account's change records.
                Action: 'ssm:GetParameter'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:parameter/platform/change/*'
              - Sid: PublishCredentialHealth
                Effect: Allow
                Action: 'cloudwatch:PutMetricData'
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: PublishFindings
                Effect: Allow
                Action: 'events:PutEvents'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:events:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:event-bus/${AlertBusName}'

  ReconcileLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /aws/lambda/platform-change-reconciliation
      # Seven years. SOC 2 evidence that change management operated, and the
      # period an auditor asks about is measured in years.
      RetentionInDays: 2557
      KmsKeyId: !If
        - UseDefaultLogsKey
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:kms:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:alias/platform-logs'
        - !Ref LogsKeyArn

  ReconcileFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    DependsOn: ReconcileLogGroup
    Properties:
      FunctionName: platform-change-reconciliation
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: reconcile.handler
      Role: !GetAtt ReconcileRole.Arn
      # A reconciliation run makes one Jira search per account plus a DynamoDB
      # query each. Capture invocations finish in milliseconds; this is sized
      # for the scheduled run.
      Timeout: 300
      MemorySize: 512
      Code:
        S3Bucket: !Ref ArtifactBucket
        S3Key: !Ref ArtifactKey
      Environment:
        Variables:
          CHANGE_TABLE: !Ref ChangeTable
          ALERT_BUS_NAME: !Ref AlertBusName
          JIRA_SITE: !Ref JiraSite
          JIRA_SECRET_NAME: !Ref JiraSecretName
          JIRA_CHANGE_ISSUETYPE: !Ref JiraChangeIssueType
          JIRA_DEFAULT_CHANGE_PROJECT: !Ref JiraDefaultChangeProject
          JIRA_OPS_PROJECT: !Ref JiraOpsProject
          RECONCILE_LOOKBACK_HOURS: !Ref LookbackHours
          JIRA_TOKEN_EXPIRES: !Ref JiraTokenExpires

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The filer (prompt 8.2's write half)
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # A SEPARATE function and a SEPARATE role from reconciliation, because one
  # reads and one writes and the whole quorum argument rests on those being
  # different things.
  #
  # What this does not buy, stated so nobody reads more into it than is there:
  # real separation needs two Atlassian accounts and there is one. The account
  # behind the shared credential can write whichever module reads the secret,
  # and it currently belongs to a human who is also an approver. B-070 carries
  # the fix; this is the code-level half of a separation the credential does
  # not have yet.
  FilerRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: PlatformChangeFiler
      Description: >-
        Files change records in AltDigital's operations project. Writes to
        Jira; reads nothing the platform verifies against.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: lambda.amazonaws.com }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: FileChangeRecords
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: ReadTheJiraCredential
                Effect: Allow
                Action: 'secretsmanager:GetSecretValue'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:secretsmanager:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:secret:${JiraSecretName}-*'
              # No DynamoDB. The filer cannot touch the deployment evidence it
              # is filing records about, which keeps the two halves of the
              # control genuinely independent inside AWS even while they share
              # a Jira credential.

  FilerLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /aws/lambda/platform-change-filer
      # Seven years. This log is the record of every change record the platform
      # itself raised, which is evidence in the same class as the deployments.
      RetentionInDays: 2557
      KmsKeyId: !If
        - UseDefaultLogsKey
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:kms:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:alias/platform-logs'
        - !Ref LogsKeyArn

  FilerFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    DependsOn: FilerLogGroup
    Properties:
      FunctionName: platform-change-filer
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: filer.handler
      Role: !GetAtt FilerRole.Arn
      Timeout: 60
      MemorySize: 256
      Code:
        S3Bucket: !Ref ArtifactBucket
        S3Key: !Ref ArtifactKey
      Environment:
        Variables:
          JIRA_SITE: !Ref JiraSite
          JIRA_SECRET_NAME: !Ref JiraSecretName
          JIRA_OPS_PROJECT: !Ref JiraOpsProject
          JIRA_CHANGE_ISSUETYPE: !Ref JiraChangeIssueType
          JIRA_APPROVER_GROUPS: !Ref JiraApproverGroups

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Capture
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # design 08's six deployment event types arrive as CloudTrail events
  # forwarded from member accounts. The pattern filters by eventName here as
  # well as in the member account, deliberately: the member-side rule decides
  # what crosses the account boundary and costs money to forward, and this one
  # decides what is worth storing. Either alone would be a single point of
  # "somebody widened a pattern and nobody noticed".
  DeploymentCaptureRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: platform-capture-deployments
      EventBusName: !Ref AlertBusName
      Description: >-
        Deployment events from member accounts. design 08, "What is captured as
        a deployment event".
      EventPattern:
        detail-type: ['AWS API Call via CloudTrail']
        detail:
          eventName:
            - AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
            - RegisterTaskDefinition
            - UpdateService
            - CreateService
            - UpdateFunctionCode
            - UpdateFunctionConfiguration
            - PublishVersion
            - CreateStack
            - UpdateStack
            - ExecuteChangeSet
            - CreateLaunchTemplate
            - CreateLaunchTemplateVersion
            - ModifyLaunchTemplate
            - ModifyDBParameterGroup
            - ModifyDBInstance
            - ModifyDBCluster
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Id: capture
          Arn: !GetAtt ReconcileFunction.Arn
          DeadLetterConfig:
            Arn: !GetAtt CaptureDlq.Arn
          RetryPolicy:
            MaximumRetryAttempts: 4
            MaximumEventAgeInSeconds: 3600

  CaptureDlq:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    DeletionPolicy: Delete
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Delete
    Properties:
      QueueName: platform-change-capture-dlq
      MessageRetentionPeriod: 1209600
      SqsManagedSseEnabled: true

  CaptureInvokePermission:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Permission
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !GetAtt ReconcileFunction.Arn
      Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
      Principal: events.amazonaws.com
      SourceArn: !GetAtt DeploymentCaptureRule.Arn

  ReconcileScheduleRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: platform-change-reconcile
      Description: >-
        The scheduled comparison. Produces design 08's outcomes over a window
        wider than this interval.
      ScheduleExpression: !Ref ReconcileSchedule
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Id: reconcile
          Arn: !GetAtt ReconcileFunction.Arn
          Input: '{"action": "reconcile"}'

  ReconcileInvokePermission:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Permission
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !GetAtt ReconcileFunction.Arn
      Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
      Principal: events.amazonaws.com
      SourceArn: !GetAtt ReconcileScheduleRule.Arn

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Watching the watcher
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Reconciliation failing silently is the worst outcome available here: the
  # platform would show a clean month, which is indistinguishable from a month
  # in which every tenant behaved. That is the shape prompt 9.1 names as "the
  # failure mode that destroys an audit".
  ReconcileErrorAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Condition: HasAlerting
    Properties:
      AlarmName: platform-change-reconciliation-errors
      AlarmDescription: >-
        Change reconciliation is failing. Deployment events may still be being
        captured, but nothing is being compared against change records — and an
        absence of findings currently looks identical to compliance.
      Namespace: AWS/Lambda
      MetricName: Errors
      Dimensions:
        - Name: FunctionName
          Value: !Ref ReconcileFunction
      Statistic: Sum
      Period: 3600
      EvaluationPeriods: 1
      Threshold: 1
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold
      TreatMissingData: notBreaching
      AlarmActions: [!Ref AlertTopicArn]

  CaptureDlqAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Condition: HasAlerting
    Properties:
      AlarmName: platform-change-capture-dlq-not-empty
      AlarmDescription: >-
        A deployment event never reached the capture function. That deployment
        is now absent from the evidence record and cannot be reconciled — the
        message body in the DLQ is the only remaining trace of it.
      Namespace: AWS/SQS
      MetricName: ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible
      Dimensions:
        - Name: QueueName
          Value: !GetAtt CaptureDlq.QueueName
      Statistic: Maximum
      Period: 300
      EvaluationPeriods: 1
      Threshold: 0
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanThreshold
      TreatMissingData: notBreaching
      AlarmActions: [!Ref AlertTopicArn]

  # The credential expiring is a slow, certain, silent failure: reconciliation
  # keeps running, keeps reporting "change source unavailable", and looks like
  # a platform that is working. This is the one thing that says otherwise.
  #
  # Note this CAN be a CloudWatch alarm where the restore-test freshness signal
  # could not (B-050). Reconciliation runs every six hours, so the metric is
  # dense enough for an ordinary threshold alarm; the restore metric is monthly
  # and no alarm can span that gap.
  JiraTokenExpiringAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Condition: HasAlerting
    Properties:
      AlarmName: platform-jira-token-expiring
      AlarmDescription: >-
        The Jira API token is approaching expiry. When it lapses, change
        reconciliation stops being able to confirm or rule out approvals and
        every run reports the change source as unavailable — which is correct
        behaviour and indistinguishable from a quiet month unless somebody is
        watching. Rotate with scripts/set-jira-token.sh and update
        PLATFORM_JIRA_TOKEN_EXPIRES.
      Namespace: AltDigital/Change
      MetricName: JiraTokenDaysRemaining
      Statistic: Minimum
      Period: 86400
      EvaluationPeriods: 1
      Threshold: 30
      ComparisonOperator: LessThanThreshold
      # notBreaching, not breaching. An absent metric means reconciliation is
      # not running at all, which is the ReconcileErrorAlarm's business — two
      # alarms on one symptom is how a rotation gets two tickets.
      TreatMissingData: notBreaching
      AlarmActions: [!Ref AlertTopicArn]

Outputs:
  ReconcileFunctionName:
    Value: !Ref ReconcileFunction
  ChangeTableName:
    Value: !Ref ChangeTable
  FilerFunctionName:
    Value: !Ref FilerFunction
  CorrelationInvocation:
    Description: >-
      The SLA exclusion query, prompt 8.2's first-class function. Returns
      correlation and deliberately never asserts cause.
    Value: !Sub >-
      aws lambda invoke --function-name ${ReconcileFunction} --payload
      '{"action":"customer_caused","account_id":"<id>","at":"<iso8601>","window_hours":4}'
      out.json
files.commercial/10-commercial-routing.yaml:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  AltDigital Managed Platform — the client-conversation event class (prompt
  11.2). design 12's fourth routing destination. Deploys to the Audit account.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A fourth destination, not a fourth severity
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# design/12-commercial-access.md defines this class by "who needs to have a
# conversation, not by severity", and that is why it is a separate router
# rather than a branch in alerting/src/router.py.
#
# A cost anomaly is low severity and needs a conversation. A failed restore test
# in a dev sandbox is higher severity and needs none. Any threshold on the
# existing router gets both wrong, and the two routers answer different
# questions about the same event -- which is why a security incident reaches
# both, as an operational page through one and as awareness through the other.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Two rules, because the events arrive in two shapes
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Most client-conversation events are emitted deliberately and carry
# `commercial_event`. Security incidents are not: containment emits a dossier
# for operational reasons and has no opinion about the commercial team. So the
# dossier rule exists to pull those in without containment needing to know this
# destination exists.

Parameters:

  ArtifactBucket:
    Type: String

  ArtifactKey:
    Type: String

  AlertBusName:
    Type: String
    Default: platform-alerts

  NotifierParam:
    Type: String
    Default: /platform/commercial/notifier
    Description: >-
      SSM parameter naming the ROLE that owns customer notification.

      A role, not a person: design 12 assigns notification to contract owners,
      and a name in a payload goes stale and is personal data besides.

      The router refuses to emit an awareness event when this cannot be read.
      An event saying an incident is in progress, naming nobody to tell the
      customer, is how a helpful person on a phone call becomes the notifying
      party.

  CommercialRoutingKeySecret:
    Type: String
    Default: platform/pagerduty/commercial-routing-key
    Description: >-
      Secrets Manager name holding the PagerDuty Events API v2 routing key for
      the client-conversation service. Read at INVOCATION, not resolved at
      deploy time, so rotating the key needs no redeploy.

  LogsKeyArn:
    Type: String
    Default: ''

Conditions:

  UseDefaultLogsKey: !Equals [!Ref LogsKeyArn, '']

Resources:

  RouteRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: PlatformCommercialRouter
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: lambda.amazonaws.com }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole'

  RoutePolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: RouteClientConversations
      Roles: [!Ref RouteRole]
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: ReadNotifierRole
            Effect: Allow
            Action: ssm:GetParameter
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:parameter${NotifierParam}'
          - Sid: EmitClientConversations
            Effect: Allow
            Action: events:PutEvents
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:events:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:event-bus/${AlertBusName}'

  RouteLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /aws/lambda/platform-commercial-router
      # Seven years. What the commercial team was told, and when, is the record
      # that answers "did you know" in a dispute.
      RetentionInDays: 2557
      KmsKeyId: !If
        - UseDefaultLogsKey
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:kms:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:alias/platform-logs'
        - !Ref LogsKeyArn

  RouteFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    DependsOn: RouteLogGroup
    Properties:
      FunctionName: platform-commercial-router
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: route.handler
      Role: !GetAtt RouteRole.Arn
      Timeout: 30
      MemorySize: 256
      Code:
        S3Bucket: !Ref ArtifactBucket
        S3Key: !Ref ArtifactKey
      Environment:
        Variables:
          ALERT_BUS_NAME: !Ref AlertBusName
          COMMERCIAL_NOTIFIER_PARAM: !Ref NotifierParam

  # Events emitted deliberately for this class.
  DeclaredCommercialRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: platform-route-commercial-declared
      EventBusName: !Ref AlertBusName
      Description: 'Events that name themselves as client conversations.'
      EventPattern:
        # The router's own output carries commercial_event so downstream
        # consumers can see the class, which means it matches this pattern --
        # rule, function, emit, rule, without end. B-116.
        #
        # Excluded by SOURCE rather than by adding a field to the payload,
        # because the source is set by the emitter and cannot be spoofed by a
        # producer upstream. route.py declines its own output as well; this is
        # the cheaper stop, since the loop never reaches Lambda.
        source: [{ 'anything-but': ['platform.commercial'] }]
        detail:
          commercial_event: [{ exists: true }]
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Id: route
          Arn: !GetAtt RouteFunction.Arn

  # Security incidents, which do not.
  #
  # containment emits a dossier because an incident happened, not because the
  # commercial team needs to know. Matching the dossier here means containment
  # does not have to carry a second destination's concerns -- and it means an
  # incident cannot be forgotten into silence because somebody omitted a field.
  IncidentAwarenessRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: platform-route-commercial-incident-awareness
      EventBusName: !Ref AlertBusName
      Description: >-
        Security incidents, as AWARENESS ONLY. The payload that leaves here
        carries nothing a customer could be notified from. design 12.
      EventPattern:
