        detail-type: ['Platform Incident Dossier']
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Id: route
          Arn: !GetAtt RouteFunction.Arn

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The notifier: the link that carries the event to PagerDuty
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # B-115. Before this existed, route.py emitted `client-conversation` onto
  # the bus and nothing listened -- a router that decided correctly and a
  # destination that received nothing, with the failure invisible because the
  # deciding half worked.

  NotifyRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: PlatformCommercialNotifier
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: lambda.amazonaws.com }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole'

  NotifyPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: NotifyClientConversations
      Roles: [!Ref NotifyRole]
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          # The commercial routing key ONLY. Deliberately not the platform
          # routing key: anything holding that can page the on-call rotation,
          # and this function has no business being able to.
          - Sid: ReadCommercialRoutingKey
            Effect: Allow
            Action: secretsmanager:GetSecretValue
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:secretsmanager:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:secret:${CommercialRoutingKeySecret}-*'

  NotifyLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /aws/lambda/platform-commercial-notifier
      # Seven years, matching the router. This log is the record of what
      # actually crossed the boundary to a third party.
      RetentionInDays: 2557
      KmsKeyId: !If
        - UseDefaultLogsKey
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:kms:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:alias/platform-logs'
        - !Ref LogsKeyArn

  NotifyFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    DependsOn: NotifyLogGroup
    Properties:
      FunctionName: platform-commercial-notifier
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: notify.handler
      Role: !GetAtt NotifyRole.Arn
      Timeout: 30
      MemorySize: 256
      Code:
        S3Bucket: !Ref ArtifactBucket
        S3Key: !Ref ArtifactKey
      Environment:
        Variables:
          COMMERCIAL_ROUTING_KEY_SECRET: !Ref CommercialRoutingKeySecret

  ClientConversationRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: platform-notify-client-conversations
      EventBusName: !Ref AlertBusName
      Description: >-
        Routed client-conversation events, on their way to the PagerDuty
        business service. This is the ONLY rule that should match the
        router's own output.
      EventPattern:
        source: ['platform.commercial']
        detail-type: ['client-conversation']
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Id: notify
          Arn: !GetAtt NotifyFunction.Arn

  NotifyPermission:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Permission
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !GetAtt NotifyFunction.Arn
      Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
      Principal: events.amazonaws.com
      SourceArn: !GetAtt ClientConversationRule.Arn

  DeclaredPermission:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Permission
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !GetAtt RouteFunction.Arn
      Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
      Principal: events.amazonaws.com
      SourceArn: !GetAtt DeclaredCommercialRule.Arn

  IncidentPermission:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Permission
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !GetAtt RouteFunction.Arn
      Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
      Principal: events.amazonaws.com
      SourceArn: !GetAtt IncidentAwarenessRule.Arn

Outputs:

  RouteFunctionName:
    Description: The client-conversation router.
    Value: !Ref RouteFunction

  NotifyFunctionName:
    Description: >-
      The client-conversation notifier, which carries a routed event to the
      PagerDuty business service. Without it the router decides correctly and
      nothing arrives (B-115).
    Value: !Ref NotifyFunction

  NotifierParam:
    Description: >-
      Set this before relying on incident awareness. The router refuses to
      emit an awareness event without it.
    Value: !Ref NotifierParam
files.config/tiers.yaml:
# Environment tiers, as two axes rather than four columns.
#
# Source: design/14-environment-tiers.md, "Revised environment matrix".
# Consumed by: scripts/lib/tiers.py, scripts/publish-tiers.sh
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why this file exists at all
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# prompt 13.1: "Do not implement UAT by copying the test parameterisation and
# adjusting. Build the tier table in design 14 as explicit configuration so the
# two axes stay visibly separate."
#
# The instruction is unusually specific, and the reason is in design 14:
#
#   | Axis            | dev / test     | uat                   | prod       |
#   | Data handling   | Non-production | Production-equivalent | Production |
#   | Resilience      | Non-production | Non-production        | Production |
#
# dev, test and prod keep those two axes ALIGNED, which is why three tiers can
# be implemented as a single ordered scale and why doing so works right up
# until UAT exists. UAT is the tier where they diverge: its data is real and
# its infrastructure is not.
#
# Copying test and adjusting produces a UAT that is out of compliance scope
# with a reduced retention floor, because those are the settings you do not
# think to change. The failure is quiet, it is discovered during an audit, and
# by then the environment has been holding regulated data for months.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# So nothing about a tier is written per tier
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Each tier declares only its POSITION on the two axes. Every attribute that
# follows an axis is resolved from that position. UAT's compliance scope is
# not set here — it falls out of `data_handling: production_equivalent`, which
# is the same value production uses.
#
# That makes the failure mode structurally unavailable. There is no field to
# forget, because there is no per-tier field.
#
# A handful of attributes genuinely follow neither axis. They are in
# `tier_specific` below, which is deliberately small and deliberately awkward:
# anything added there is a claim that it depends on the tier's NAME rather
# than on what the tier is, and that claim should have to be defended.

version: 1

axes:

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Data handling — what the environment HOLDS
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Drives compliance, retention, evidence and the severity at which a finding
  # about the data is treated. design 14: "The distinction that matters is not
  # its purpose but what data it holds."
  data_handling:
    attributes:
      - compliance_scope
      - retention_floor
      - regulated_data_expected
      - regulated_data_is_finding
      - finding_severity
      - restore_testing
      - canary_required
      - backup_policy

    values:
      non_production:
        compliance_scope: out
        retention_floor: reduced
        regulated_data_expected: false
        # The scope-change finding that fires when regulated data turns up
        # somewhere it was not expected.
        regulated_data_is_finding: true
        finding_severity: non_production
        restore_testing: false
        canary_required: false
        backup_policy: reduced

      production_equivalent:
        compliance_scope: in
        retention_floor: full
        regulated_data_expected: true
        # prompt 13.1: "regulated data in UAT must NOT trigger the
        # scope-change finding that applies to dev and test. UAT is in scope
        # from the outset." Real users bring real data -- design 14 calls this
        # "not misconduct, it is how UAT works" -- and a control that fires on
        # the expected case trains people to close it without reading.
        regulated_data_is_finding: false
        finding_severity: production
        # design 14: "An environment holding regulated data with an untested
        # restore path is an audit finding regardless of its SLA status."
        restore_testing: true
        canary_required: true
        # design 14 gives UAT "Full policy, reduced frequency". The POLICY
        # follows the data -- an environment holding regulated data is backed
        # up the same way production is -- while the FREQUENCY follows the
        # resilience axis below. The two halves of one row landing on
        # different axes is the clearest illustration in the file of why
        # there are two.
        backup_policy: full

      production:
        compliance_scope: in
        retention_floor: full
        regulated_data_expected: true
        regulated_data_is_finding: false
        finding_severity: production
        restore_testing: true
        canary_required: true
        backup_policy: full

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Resilience — what the environment PROMISES
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Drives availability, SLA, backup frequency, paging and whether the thing
  # may be switched off at night. None of this is affected by how sensitive
  # the data is.
  resilience:
    attributes:
      - availability_zones
      - sla_commitment
      - backup_frequency
      - pagerduty_routing
      - schedulable
      - multi_az_required

    values:
      non_production:
        availability_zones: single
        sla_commitment: false
        backup_frequency: reduced
        # No paging. NOT no alerting -- see D-018 and alarm_routing below.
        pagerduty_routing: false
        schedulable: true
        multi_az_required: false

      production:
        availability_zones: multi
        sla_commitment: true
        backup_frequency: full
        pagerduty_routing: true
        # design 14 marks production "No" for HOOPs, and prompt 13.2 says to
        # "enforce that, do not rely on configuration". This value is what the
        # scheduler checks; the enforcement is that it refuses regardless.
        schedulable: false
        multi_az_required: true

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The tiers, as positions
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Note what is NOT here: no tier sets compliance_scope, retention_floor or any
# other axis attribute. UAT differs from test in exactly one character of this
# file, which is the whole point.

tiers:

  dev:
    purpose: Where developers build. Things break.
    data_handling: non_production
    resilience: non_production
    provisioned_by_default: true

  test:
    purpose: QA verifies function against specification.
    data_handling: non_production
    resilience: non_production
    provisioned_by_default: true

  uat:
    purpose: Do the users accept this, or are adjustments needed?
    # The divergence. Real users bring real data; the infrastructure behind it
    # is still non-production.
    data_handling: production_equivalent
    resilience: non_production
    # design 14: "UAT is optional and opt-in. It is not provisioned by
    # default, because it raises the customer's AWS cost and not every
    # customer runs a formal acceptance stage." Opt-in rather than opt-out so
    # that a customer who never uses UAT does not have to notice it in order
    # to stop paying for it.
    provisioned_by_default: false

  prod:
    purpose: Production.
    data_handling: production
    resilience: production
    provisioned_by_default: true

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Attributes that follow NEITHER axis
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Kept separate and kept short. Everything here is an assertion that the value
# depends on which tier this is rather than on what the tier IS, and each one
# carries its reason so the assertion can be argued with.
#
# If this section grows, the axis model is wrong and should be fixed rather
# than worked around.

tier_specific:

  monitoring_depth:
    reason: >-
      A gradient rather than a consequence of either axis. design 14's matrix
      lists four distinct values, and UAT's "moderate" is neither the
      non-production nor the production setting.
    dev: light
    test: light
    uat: moderate
    prod: pervasive

  alarm_routing:
    reason: >-
      Follows resilience for the PAGING half and data handling for the rest,
      so it belongs to both axes and therefore to neither. UAT reaches Jira
      and the commercial channel without paging anybody, which is exactly the
      combination that has no single axis to inherit from.
    dev: digest
    test: digest_and_jira
    uat: jira_and_commercial
    prod: pagerduty

  developer_console_access:
    reason: >-
      Follows design 11's access model, which is about blast radius rather
      than about data or resilience. Test is more open than UAT despite both
      being non-production for resilience.
    dev: full_within_guardrails
    test: read_and_limited_ops
    uat: read_only
    prod: read_only

  path_to_change:
    reason: >-
      Direct access in dev only. Everything else goes through AppDeployer,
      which is a deployment-mechanism decision rather than a tier property.
    dev: direct
    test: app_deployer
    uat: app_deployer
    prod: app_deployer

  change_reconciliation:
    reason: >-
      Follows path_to_change rather than either axis. design 14 has test at
      Yes despite test being non-production on BOTH axes -- reconciliation
      exists wherever deployment goes through AppDeployer, which is everywhere
      except dev's direct access. Deriving this from the data axis would have
      silently turned test's reconciliation off.
    dev: false
    test: true
    uat: true
    prod: true

  hoop_aggressiveness:
    reason: >-
      All three non-production tiers are schedulable -- that comes from the
      resilience axis -- but how hard they are scheduled does not. design 14
      distinguishes "aggressive" from "conservative": UAT may have real users
      in it at unpredictable hours, and switching it off underneath an
      acceptance session is a different kind of wrong from switching off an
      idle dev box.
    dev: aggressive
    test: aggressive
    uat: conservative
    prod: none
files.containment/00-responder-role.yaml:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  AltDigital Managed Platform — the role security containment assumes INTO a
  member account (prompt 7.1). Part of the member baseline. Deliberately holds
  no destructive permission of any kind.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why this role exists in the member account at all
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# design/07-response-automation.md: "Containment automation executes from the
# platform account via a role that member accounts cannot modify, deny or
# delete. If an attacker holds admin in the member account, the response
# capability must still function."
#
# That is two halves. This template is the member half: a role the platform
# assumes to act inside the account. The Audit half — the state machine and the
# principal that assumes this — is containment/10-containment.yaml.
#
# What stops a compromised member account simply deleting this role is NOT
# anything in this file. It is `DenyPlatformRoleModification` in
# policies/scp/03-protect-platform-identity.json, which denies IAM write actions
# against `arn:aws:iam::*:role/Platform*` for every principal in every member
# account. THE NAME IS LOAD-BEARING: rename this role to something outside the
# `Platform*` prefix and it silently becomes deletable by the very account it
# exists to contain.
#
# open-items.md V3 — "Containment role cannot be blocked by a compromised member
# account" — is the scheduled test of that assumption, built by prompt 7.4.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The permission list is the whole control
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLAUDE.md: "Never write code that terminates, deletes, deregisters, rolls back
# or purges a resource as part of automated remediation. Security automation
# isolates and preserves."
#
# design 07 says the same thing harder: "Terminate. Delete. Deregister. Roll
# back. Purge." are what automation may NEVER do, because terminating a
# compromised instance destroys the evidence needed to understand what happened.
#
# So the rule is enforced here, in IAM, rather than left to the code to honour.
# There is no ec2:TerminateInstances, no ec2:DeleteSnapshot, no
# ec2:DeleteVolume, no iam:DeleteRole, no iam:DeleteUser, no
# rds:DeleteDBInstance, and no s3:DeleteObject in this role. A bug in the
# containment Lambda cannot destroy evidence, because the credentials it holds
# cannot express the request.
#
# Every grant below is additive (create a snapshot, attach a policy) or
# reversible (change which security group an instance uses). Read the list with
# that test in mind before adding to it.

Parameters:

  ContainmentRoleArn:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      The Audit-account role that may assume this one — the state machine's
      execution role from containment/10-containment.yaml. Exactly one
      principal, named in full.

      NOT a wildcard and not an account root. `:root` would let ANY principal in
      the Audit account assume a role that can isolate production instances and
      revoke credentials across the estate, which is a far larger blast radius
      than it looks: it would make every future Lambda in that account a
      containment-capable principal by default.
    AllowedPattern: '^arn:aws[a-z-]*:iam::[0-9]{12}:role/.+$'

  ForensicsAccountId:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      Where preserved evidence is shared to. Snapshots are created in THIS
      account and then shared with Forensics — AWS has no "create a snapshot
      directly into another account" operation, so preservation is always two
      steps, and the second one is what puts the evidence beyond the reach of
      an attacker holding admin here.
    AllowedPattern: '^([0-9]{12})?$'

  ExternalId:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    NoEcho: true
    Description: >-
      Optional sts:ExternalId. Belt and braces on top of the exact-principal
      trust above; the confused-deputy problem this defends against does not
      really apply within a single organization, so it is off by default rather
      than being ceremony everybody copies.

Conditions:
  HasForensics: !Not [!Equals [!Ref ForensicsAccountId, '']]
  HasExternalId: !Not [!Equals [!Ref ExternalId, '']]

Resources:

  SecurityResponderRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    # Retain on delete. If this stack is removed from an account — by a
    # StackSet operation, a mistake, or an attacker with enough access to
    # deregister the instance — the containment capability should not leave
    # with it. A stale role that can only preserve and isolate is a far better
    # failure than an account that has quietly become uncontainable.
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      # `Platform` prefix, not decorative. See the header: the SCP that stops a
      # compromised account deleting this role matches on this exact prefix.
      RoleName: PlatformSecurityResponder
      Description: >-
        Security incident containment. Assumed by the platform from the Audit
        account. Preserves evidence and isolates; holds no permission to
        terminate, delete or purge anything.
      MaxSessionDuration: 3600
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Ref ContainmentRoleArn
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition: !If
              - HasExternalId
              - StringEquals:
                  'sts:ExternalId': !Ref ExternalId
              - !Ref AWS::NoValue
      Policies:

        # -------------------------------------------------------------------
        # Stage 1 — Preserve. Nothing destructive happens before this completes.
        # -------------------------------------------------------------------
        - PolicyName: Preserve
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: ReadWhatIsThere
                Effect: Allow
                # Describes only. The readout (prompt 7.2) is built from these,
                # and so is the decision about what to isolate — containment
                # that cannot see the instance cannot safely act on it.
                Action:
                  - 'ec2:DescribeInstances'
                  - 'ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute'
                  - 'ec2:DescribeVolumes'
                  - 'ec2:DescribeSnapshots'
                  - 'ec2:DescribeSecurityGroups'
                  - 'ec2:DescribeNetworkInterfaces'
                  - 'ec2:DescribeVpcs'
                  - 'ec2:DescribeSubnets'
                  - 'ec2:DescribeTags'
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: SnapshotVolumes
                Effect: Allow
                # CreateSnapshots (plural) captures every volume attached to an
                # instance in ONE crash-consistent set. Taking them one at a
                # time gives a set of snapshots from different moments, which
                # for a multi-volume database is evidence that never existed in
                # that combination on the running machine.
                Action:
                  - 'ec2:CreateSnapshot'
                  - 'ec2:CreateSnapshots'
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: TagEvidence
                Effect: Allow
                # The incident id goes onto every artifact at creation. Without
                # it, a year later nobody can say which snapshot belonged to
                # which incident, and evidence nobody can attribute is not
                # evidence.
                Action: 'ec2:CreateTags'
                Resource: '*'
                Condition:
                  StringEquals:
                    'ec2:CreateAction': ['CreateSnapshot', 'CreateSnapshots']
              - Sid: ShareEvidenceWithForensics
                Effect: Allow
                # ModifySnapshotAttribute is how a snapshot reaches the
                # Forensics account. It ADDS a permission; it cannot remove the
                # snapshot. Note this is the only path evidence takes out of a
                # possibly-compromised account, which is why the Forensics
                # account exists at all.
                Action: 'ec2:ModifySnapshotAttribute'
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: ReadWhereEvidenceGoes
                Effect: Allow
                # Without this the Forensics lookup is DENIED, the denial gets
                # swallowed into "no Forensics account configured", and
                # evidence silently stays in the account being contained. That
                # is B-042 exactly -- a missing describe permission swallowed
                # into "cannot tell" -- and it was reproduced here on the first
                # live containment despite the parameter existing with the
                # right value. B-054.
                Action: 'ssm:GetParameter'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:parameter/platform/security/*'
              - Sid: ReadCloudTrailForTheReadout
                Effect: Allow
                # "What the principal did in the preceding 24 hours" — design
                # 07's readout. Read-only, and it reads the account's own trail.
                Action:
                  - 'cloudtrail:LookupEvents'
                  - 'cloudtrail:DescribeTrails'
                  - 'cloudtrail:GetTrailStatus'
                Resource: '*'

        # -------------------------------------------------------------------
        # Stage 2 — Isolate. The instance STAYS RUNNING.
        # -------------------------------------------------------------------
        - PolicyName: Isolate
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: SwapSecurityGroups
                Effect: Allow
                # ModifyInstanceAttribute changes which security groups an ENI
                # uses. It does not stop, reboot or terminate anything — the
                # instance keeps running and only its reachability changes,
                # which is design 07's explicit requirement and the reason the
                # evidence survives.
                #
                # ModifyNetworkInterfaceAttribute is the same operation for an
                # instance with several interfaces; isolating one interface and
                # leaving another reachable is a half-isolated instance, which
                # design doc 02 calls out as worse than either extreme.
                Action:
                  - 'ec2:ModifyInstanceAttribute'
                  - 'ec2:ModifyNetworkInterfaceAttribute'
                Resource: '*'
              # No ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroup* and no ec2:RevokeSecurityGroup*.
              # The isolation group is PRE-STAGED by
              # baseline/40-network.yaml and applied as-is. Letting containment
              # edit security group rules during an incident would let a bug
              # open a path rather than close one, and the group it would be
              # editing is the one thing that must be known-good.

        # -------------------------------------------------------------------
        # Stage 3 and 4 — Revoke, and contain blast radius.
        # -------------------------------------------------------------------
        - PolicyName: RevokeWithoutDeleting
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: ReadPrincipals
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'iam:GetRole'
                  - 'iam:GetUser'
                  - 'iam:ListAttachedRolePolicies'
                  - 'iam:ListAttachedUserPolicies'
                  - 'iam:ListRolePolicies'
                  - 'iam:ListUserPolicies'
                  - 'iam:GetRolePolicy'
                  - 'iam:GetUserPolicy'
                  - 'iam:ListAccessKeys'
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: AttachDenyPolicies
                Effect: Allow
                # PutRolePolicy / PutUserPolicy ADD an inline policy. They are
                # how both stage 3 (deny-all) and stage 4 (session revocation by
                # token issue time) are applied, and neither removes anything:
                # the principal keeps its identity, its trust policy and its
                # audit trail, and simply stops being able to do anything.
                #
                # design 07: "Attach a deny-all policy to the compromised
                # principal — do not delete it. Deletion loses the audit trail
                # and breaks attribution."
                #
                # DeleteRolePolicy and DeleteUserPolicy are deliberately ABSENT.
                # Containment can apply a deny and cannot lift it; standing the
                # incident down is a human action taken with human credentials.
                # An automation that can un-contain is an automation an attacker
                # can use to un-contain.
                Action:
                  - 'iam:PutRolePolicy'
                  - 'iam:PutUserPolicy'
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:role/*'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:user/*'
              - Sid: NeverContainThePlatformItself
                Effect: Deny
                # The one that stops containment eating its own hands.
                #
                # Without this, a finding naming a `Platform*` principal — a
                # compromised-looking instrumentation Lambda, or this very role
                # — would have containment attach a deny-all to the platform's
                # own machinery. In the worst ordering it revokes the role it is
                # currently using, mid-sequence, leaving the account isolated,
                # the evidence half-copied and no way back in.
                #
                # Containing a platform principal is a real scenario and it must
                # be a human decision with human credentials, not something the
                # automation does to itself at 3am.
                Action:
                  - 'iam:PutRolePolicy'
                  - 'iam:PutUserPolicy'
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:role/Platform*'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:role/stacksets-exec-*'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:role/AWSReservedSSO*'

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Where evidence is allowed to go
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Published so the containment automation does not have to be told, per
  # account, where Forensics is. It reads it from the account it is acting on,
  # which means an account onboarded before Forensics existed starts working the
  # moment this parameter is filled in rather than needing the automation
  # redeployed.
  ForensicsAccountParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Condition: HasForensics
    Properties:
      Name: /platform/security/forensics-account
      Type: String
      Value: !Ref ForensicsAccountId
      Description: >-
        Account that preserved evidence is shared with during containment.

Outputs:
  ResponderRoleArn:
    Description: >-
      Assumed by the containment state machine in Audit.
    Value: !GetAtt SecurityResponderRole.Arn
  ForensicsConfigured:
    Description: >-
      "none" means preservation creates snapshots locally and cannot move them
      out of the account — which is reported as a finding on every incident
      rather than passing silently.
    Value: !If [HasForensics, !Ref ForensicsAccountId, 'none']
files.containment/10-containment.yaml:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  AltDigital Managed Platform — declaration and containment (prompt 7.1).
  Deploys to the Audit account. Declares security incidents without debate on
  design 07's defined conditions, then runs preserve, isolate, revoke and blast
  radius against the member account through a role that account cannot deny.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why this runs in Audit and not in the member account
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# design/07-response-automation.md: "Containment automation executes from the
# platform account via a role that member accounts cannot modify, deny or
# delete. If an attacker holds admin in the member account, the response
# capability must still function."
#
# Response automation for OPERATIONAL incidents (baseline/60-response.yaml)
# runs inside each member account, and that is correct for it: an operational
# runbook acts on a healthy account and the blast radius of a bug is one
# tenant. Security containment cannot work that way. The account it acts on is
# by definition the one that may be under someone else's control, and an
# attacker with local admin would simply disable the thing coming for them.
#
# design 02 names "Shared Services (platform automation)" as the account for
# platform automation, and it does not exist. Audit is used instead: it is
# already the delegated administrator for Security Hub, GuardDuty and Config,
# it already hosts the routing layer and the organization event bus, and
# containment is a security function reading security findings. Standing up a
# seventh account to hold one state machine is ceremony. Recorded as a
# deviation.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# discovery_time is immutable by SHAPE, not by discipline
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# design 07: "discovery_time is legally significant. It is set by the system at
# detection and is never editable."
#
# Code cannot credibly promise that about itself. So the incident table is
# APPEND ONLY and the guarantee is made three times over:
#
#   * the header item carrying discovery_time is written with
#     ConditionExpression attribute_not_exists(PK), so a second write fails
#   * everything that happens afterwards is a separate event item under its own
#     sort key, so nothing ever needs to update the header
#   * the IAM policies below grant NO dynamodb:UpdateItem and NO
#     dynamodb:DeleteItem on the table, to any principal in this stack
#
# Rewriting a discovery_time is therefore not a matter of nobody choosing to.
# There is no API call available to these functions that would do it.

Parameters:

  ArtifactBucket:
    Type: String
    Description: Artifact bucket in Platform Tooling holding the containment package.

  ArtifactKey:
    Type: String
    Description: Content-addressed package key.

  AlertBusName:
    Type: String
    Default: platform-alerts
    Description: >-
      The organization event bus from alerting/20-router.yaml. Declaration
      rules are attached to it, and the containment summary is published back
      onto it so the ONE routing layer decides who is woken.

  IncidentTableName:
    Type: String
    Default: platform-security-incidents
    Description: Append-only incident record.

  ResponderRoleName:
    Type: String
    Default: PlatformSecurityResponder
    Description: >-
      The member-side role from containment/00-responder-role.yaml. The name is
      load-bearing in both templates: the SCP that stops a compromised account
      deleting it matches on the `Platform*` prefix.

  ResponderExternalId:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    NoEcho: true

  ExerciseAccountId:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      The isolated account prompt 7.4's scheduled exercise fires against. EMPTY
      UNTIL 7.4 BUILDS IT, and exercise mode refuses to run rather than falling
      back to the account named in the finding — a drill that reaches a real
      account is worse than a drill that does not run.

  EscalationFractions:
    Type: String
    Default: '0.5,0.75,0.9,1.0'
    Description: >-
      Fractions of a notification window at which the clock speaks up. design
      07 says "escalating at defined fractions of the window" and does not
      define them; these are the build's choice.

      Deliberately sparse. Every escalation that is not actionable trains
      somebody to stop reading them, so: half the window is the last
      comfortable moment to start drafting, 90% is the stop-what-you-are-doing
      point, and 1.0 records the breach itself, because a missed contractual
      deadline is a fact somebody will later need the exact time of.

  ClockSweepExpression:
    Type: String
    Default: 'rate(5 minutes)'
    Description: >-
      How often deadlines are recomputed. Five minutes is the granularity of
      the countdown; the arithmetic is redone from discovery_time each time, so
      a missed sweep catches up rather than losing a deadline.

  LogsKeyArn:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      REQUIRED IN PRACTICE, despite the empty default. The fallback is
      alias/platform-logs, which is created by baseline/20-log-data-protection
      .yaml — the MEMBER baseline, which does not reach platform accounts. This
      stack deploys to Audit, where that alias does not exist, and leaving this
      empty fails every log group with "The specified KMS key does not exist or
      is not allowed to be used", an AccessDenied that names the log group and
      not the missing alias.

      Pass the alerts key from alerting/10-alert-topic.yaml. Its policy already
      admits the regional CloudWatch Logs service principal for any log group
      in the account, which is why the router's own log group works.

      The empty default is kept rather than made required so that the same
      template can be deployed to a member account, where the alias does exist.

  AlertTopicArn:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      Where this stack's OWN failures go, by the direct SNS path rather than
      through the router. A containment engine that is broken cannot report
      that it is broken through the layer it publishes to.

Conditions:
  UseDefaultLogsKey: !Equals [!Ref LogsKeyArn, '']
  HasAlerting: !Not [!Equals [!Ref AlertTopicArn, '']]

Resources:

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The incident record
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  IncidentTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    # Retain on both. This table holds discovery_time, which is legally
    # significant and cannot be reconstructed from anything else — CloudTrail
    # expires, GuardDuty findings archive, and the whole point of the field is
    # that it is the record of when the platform knew. A stack delete that took
    # it would destroy the evidence a regulator asks for first.
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      TableName: !Ref IncidentTableName
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - { AttributeName: PK, AttributeType: S }
        - { AttributeName: SK, AttributeType: S }
        - { AttributeName: record_type, AttributeType: S }
        - { AttributeName: discovery_time, AttributeType: S }
      KeySchema:
        - { AttributeName: PK, KeyType: HASH }
        - { AttributeName: SK, KeyType: RANGE }
      GlobalSecondaryIndexes:
        # How the notification clock finds incidents whose deadline may still
        # be live, without scanning the table.
        #
        # SPARSE BY DESIGN: only the header item carries BOTH record_type and
        # discovery_time, so containment events and clock announcements are not
        # indexed at all. The index holds exactly one entry per incident, which
        # is what makes a range query on discovery_time the right shape.
        #
        # record_type is a single value for every header, so this is a
        # one-partition index. Acceptable here and not in general: security
        # incidents are rare by construction, and if they ever are not, the
        # platform has a larger problem than a hot partition.
        - IndexName: by-record-type
          KeySchema:
            - { AttributeName: record_type, KeyType: HASH }
            - { AttributeName: discovery_time, KeyType: RANGE }
          Projection:
            ProjectionType: ALL
      PointInTimeRecoverySpecification:
        PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled: true
      SSESpecification:
        SSEEnabled: true
      Tags:
        - { Key: platform-managed, Value: 'true' }
        - { Key: platform-purpose, Value: security-incident-record }

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Declaration
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  DeclarationRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: PlatformIncidentDeclaration
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: lambda.amazonaws.com }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: Declare
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: AppendOnlyIncidentRecord
                Effect: Allow
                # PutItem and nothing else that writes. No UpdateItem and no
                # DeleteItem anywhere in this stack — that absence IS the
                # immutability guarantee for discovery_time, and adding either
                # one here would quietly remove it.
                Action: ['dynamodb:PutItem', 'dynamodb:GetItem', 'dynamodb:Query']
                Resource: !GetAtt IncidentTable.Arn
              - Sid: StartContainment
                Effect: Allow
                Action: 'states:StartExecution'
                Resource: !Ref ContainmentStateMachine
              - Sid: ReadAccountTiers
                Effect: Allow
                # The same map the router reads. The tier is the input to
                # design 07's confidence table, so it decides whether a
                # production service gets isolated; reading it from a second
                # source is how the two answers start disagreeing (B-041).
                Action: 'ssm:GetParameter'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:parameter/platform/routing/*'

  DeclarationLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /aws/lambda/platform-incident-declaration
      # Seven years. This log is the contemporaneous record of what the
      # platform saw and when it decided it was an incident, which is the same
      # class of evidence as the change records in baseline/60-response.yaml.
      RetentionInDays: 2557
      KmsKeyId: !If
        - UseDefaultLogsKey
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:kms:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:alias/platform-logs'
        - !Ref LogsKeyArn

  DeclarationFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    DependsOn: DeclarationLogGroup
    Properties:
      FunctionName: platform-incident-declaration
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: declare.handler
      Role: !GetAtt DeclarationRole.Arn
      Timeout: 60
      MemorySize: 256
      Code:
        S3Bucket: !Ref ArtifactBucket
        S3Key: !Ref ArtifactKey
      Environment:
        Variables:
          INCIDENT_TABLE: !Ref IncidentTable
          CONTAINMENT_STATE_MACHINE_ARN: !Ref ContainmentStateMachine

  # design 07's declaration conditions. One rule per family rather than one
  # catch-all, so a source that stops producing is visibly a rule with no
  # invocations rather than a share of one rule's traffic nobody can pick apart
  # — the same reasoning as baseline/70-event-forwarding.yaml.
  #
  # Note these sit ALONGSIDE the router's own rules on the same bus. The router
  # decides who is paged; this decides whether an incident exists and whether
  # anything is contained. Both must see the finding.
  GuardDutyDeclarationRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: platform-declare-guardduty
      EventBusName: !Ref AlertBusName
      Description: 'GuardDuty finding at high severity (design 07).'
      EventPattern:
        detail-type: ['GuardDuty Finding']
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Id: declare
          Arn: !GetAtt DeclarationFunction.Arn
          DeadLetterConfig:
            Arn: !GetAtt DeclarationDlq.Arn
          RetryPolicy:
            MaximumRetryAttempts: 4
            MaximumEventAgeInSeconds: 3600

  SecurityHubDeclarationRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: platform-declare-securityhub
      EventBusName: !Ref AlertBusName
      Description: >-
        Credential exposure, unexpected egress, unauthorised data store access
        and ransomware indicators all reach us as Security Hub findings.
      EventPattern:
        detail-type: ['Security Hub Findings - Imported']
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Id: declare
          Arn: !GetAtt DeclarationFunction.Arn
          DeadLetterConfig:
            Arn: !GetAtt DeclarationDlq.Arn
          RetryPolicy:
            MaximumRetryAttempts: 4
            MaximumEventAgeInSeconds: 3600

  # "Any ScheduleKeyDeletion, CloudTrail disable, or vault lock modification
  # attempt." Successful or DENIED — a denied attempt is either confusion or
  # something worse, and both are worth a record.
  ProtectedActionDeclarationRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: platform-declare-protected-actions
      EventBusName: !Ref AlertBusName
      Description: 'Key deletion, trail tampering, vault lock modification.'
      EventPattern:
        detail-type: ['AWS API Call via CloudTrail']
        detail:
          eventName:
            - ScheduleKeyDeletion
            - DisableKey
            - StopLogging
            - DeleteTrail
            - UpdateTrail
            - PutBackupVaultLockConfiguration
            - DeleteBackupVaultLockConfiguration
            - DeleteBackupVault
            - DeleteRecoveryPoint
            # design 03's quorum list has four actions; these complete it.
            # The original list came from design 07's prose summary, which
            # names key deletion, CloudTrail disable and vault lock
            # modification but not account removal or the Config recorder.
            # Two of the four were going undeclared. B-083.
            - RemoveAccountFromOrganization
            - StopConfigurationRecorder
            - DeleteConfigurationRecorder
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Id: declare
          Arn: !GetAtt DeclarationFunction.Arn
          DeadLetterConfig:
            Arn: !GetAtt DeclarationDlq.Arn
          RetryPolicy:
            MaximumRetryAttempts: 4
            MaximumEventAgeInSeconds: 3600

  # "Plus manual declaration by any engineer." An engineer who believes
  # something is wrong must not have to wait for a detector to agree.
  ManualDeclarationRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: platform-declare-manual
      EventBusName: !Ref AlertBusName
      Description: >-
        Manual declaration. Put an event with detail-type "Platform Manual
        Declaration" onto the bus; see docs/runbooks.md.
      EventPattern:
        detail-type: ['Platform Manual Declaration']
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Id: declare
          Arn: !GetAtt DeclarationFunction.Arn
          DeadLetterConfig:
            Arn: !GetAtt DeclarationDlq.Arn

  DeclarationDlq:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    DeletionPolicy: Delete
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Delete
    Properties:
      QueueName: platform-declaration-dlq
      MessageRetentionPeriod: 1209600
      SqsManagedSseEnabled: true

  DeclarationInvokePermission:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Permission
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !GetAtt DeclarationFunction.Arn
      Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
      Principal: events.amazonaws.com
      SourceAccount: !Ref AWS::AccountId

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Containment
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ContainmentRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: PlatformContainment
      Description: >-
        Assumes PlatformSecurityResponder in member accounts. Holds no
        destructive permission of its own and gains none by assuming - see
        containment/00-responder-role.yaml.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: lambda.amazonaws.com }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: Contain
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: AssumeTheResponderRoleAnywhereInTheOrg
                Effect: Allow
                # Wildcard ACCOUNT, exact ROLE NAME. The account cannot be
                # enumerated here — member accounts are created continuously by
                # the vesting pipeline and a fixed list would mean every new
                # tenant is uncontainable until somebody remembers to redeploy
                # this stack.
                #
                # What narrows it is the far side: each PlatformSecurityResponder
                # trusts THIS role by full ARN and nothing else, so this grant
                # can only reach roles that have already chosen to accept it.
                Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::*:role/${ResponderRoleName}'
              - Sid: AppendOnlyIncidentRecord
                Effect: Allow
                Action: ['dynamodb:PutItem', 'dynamodb:GetItem', 'dynamodb:Query']
                Resource: !GetAtt IncidentTable.Arn
              - Sid: PublishTheSummaryToTheOneRoutingLayer
                Effect: Allow
                Action: 'events:PutEvents'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:events:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:event-bus/${AlertBusName}'

  ContainmentLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /aws/lambda/platform-containment
      RetentionInDays: 2557
      KmsKeyId: !If
        - UseDefaultLogsKey
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:kms:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:alias/platform-logs'
        - !Ref LogsKeyArn

  ContainmentFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    DependsOn: ContainmentLogGroup
    Properties:
      FunctionName: platform-containment
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: contain.handler
      Role: !GetAtt ContainmentRole.Arn
      # Snapshot creation returns as soon as the snapshots are REQUESTED, so no
      # stage here waits on data movement. Five minutes is generous for the
      # slowest stage, which is preserve describing a large instance.
      Timeout: 300
      MemorySize: 512
      Code:
        S3Bucket: !Ref ArtifactBucket
        S3Key: !Ref ArtifactKey
      # No ReservedConcurrentExecutions. The Audit account's total concurrency
      # is 10 and reserving any amount is refused outright — B-040, which also
      # carries the quota increase. Worth noting the consequence HERE
      # specifically: a broad compromise declaring many incidents at once is
      # exactly when this must not throttle.
      Environment:
        Variables:
          INCIDENT_TABLE: !Ref IncidentTable
          RESPONDER_ROLE_NAME: !Ref ResponderRoleName
          RESPONDER_EXTERNAL_ID: !Ref ResponderExternalId
          EXERCISE_ACCOUNT_ID: !Ref ExerciseAccountId
          ALERT_BUS_NAME: !Ref AlertBusName


  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The readout (prompt 7.2)
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Runs after containment has published its summary. The two carry the same
  # account, resource and title, so the router derives the same dedup key and
  # PagerDuty treats this as an UPDATE to the incident already raised: the page
  # goes out with what was done, and the evidence catches up.
  ReadoutRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: PlatformIncidentReadout
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: lambda.amazonaws.com }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: Readout
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: AssumeTheResponderRole
                Effect: Allow
                # The same role containment uses, for the same reason: reading
                # a member account CloudTrail and IAM needs a principal in that
                # account, and the responder role is the one the member cannot
                # deny.
                Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::*:role/${ResponderRoleName}'
              - Sid: TheCrossAccountSweep
                Effect: Allow
                # The permission that makes prompt 7.2's cross-account
                # indicator check possible without a single cross-account call.
                # Audit is the Security Hub delegated administrator, so
                # findings from every account in the organization are already
                # local to it.
                Action:
                  - 'securityhub:GetFindings'
                  - 'securityhub:DescribeHub'
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: AppendOnlyIncidentRecord
                Effect: Allow
                Action: ['dynamodb:PutItem', 'dynamodb:GetItem', 'dynamodb:Query']
                Resource: !GetAtt IncidentTable.Arn
              - Sid: PublishTheReadout
                Effect: Allow
                Action: 'events:PutEvents'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:events:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:event-bus/${AlertBusName}'

  ReadoutLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /aws/lambda/platform-incident-readout
      RetentionInDays: 2557
      KmsKeyId: !If
        - UseDefaultLogsKey
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:kms:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:alias/platform-logs'
        - !Ref LogsKeyArn

  ReadoutFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    DependsOn: ReadoutLogGroup
    Properties:
      FunctionName: platform-incident-readout
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: readout.handler
      Role: !GetAtt ReadoutRole.Arn
      # Longer than any containment stage. A 24-hour CloudTrail lookup and an
      # organization-wide Security Hub sweep are both slow, and prompt 7.2 is
      # explicit that the cross-account check must not be skipped for speed.
      Timeout: 600
      MemorySize: 512
      Code:
        S3Bucket: !Ref ArtifactBucket
        S3Key: !Ref ArtifactKey
      Environment:
        Variables:
          INCIDENT_TABLE: !Ref IncidentTable
          RESPONDER_ROLE_NAME: !Ref ResponderRoleName
          RESPONDER_EXTERNAL_ID: !Ref ResponderExternalId
          ALERT_BUS_NAME: !Ref AlertBusName

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The notification clock (prompt 7.3)
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ClockRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: PlatformNotificationClock
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: lambda.amazonaws.com }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: Clock
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: ReadIncidentsAndAnnounceOnce
                Effect: Allow
                # PutItem, Query, and no UpdateItem or DeleteItem -- the same
                # append-only guarantee the rest of this stack keeps. An
                # escalation that has been announced cannot be unannounced.
                Action: ['dynamodb:PutItem', 'dynamodb:Query']
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt IncidentTable.Arn
                  - !Sub '${IncidentTable.Arn}/index/by-record-type'
              - Sid: ReadNotificationWindows
                Effect: Allow
                Action: 'ssm:GetParameter'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:parameter/platform/incident/*'
              - Sid: AnnounceDeadlines
                Effect: Allow
                Action: 'events:PutEvents'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:events:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:event-bus/${AlertBusName}'

  ClockLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /aws/lambda/platform-notification-clock
      RetentionInDays: 2557
      KmsKeyId: !If
        - UseDefaultLogsKey
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:kms:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:alias/platform-logs'
        - !Ref LogsKeyArn

  ClockFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    DependsOn: ClockLogGroup
    Properties:
      FunctionName: platform-notification-clock
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: clock.handler
      Role: !GetAtt ClockRole.Arn
      Timeout: 120
      MemorySize: 256
      Code:
        S3Bucket: !Ref ArtifactBucket
        S3Key: !Ref ArtifactKey
      Environment:
        Variables:
          INCIDENT_TABLE: !Ref IncidentTable
          ALERT_BUS_NAME: !Ref AlertBusName
          ESCALATION_FRACTIONS: !Ref EscalationFractions

  # A sweep, not a timer per deadline.
  #
  # One-shot schedules per escalation would be the obvious build and fail in
  # the one way that matters: a schedule that was never created, or was created
  # and removed, fires nothing and reports nothing. Recomputing every deadline
  # from discovery_time on a fixed cadence is idempotent and self-healing -- a
  # missed sweep catches up on the next one rather than losing a deadline
  # permanently.
  ClockSchedule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: platform-notification-clock-sweep
      Description: >-
        Recomputes every live notification deadline from discovery_time and
        announces the ones that have newly crossed an escalation fraction.
      ScheduleExpression: !Ref ClockSweepExpression
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Id: clock
          Arn: !GetAtt ClockFunction.Arn

  ClockInvokePermission:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Permission
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !GetAtt ClockFunction.Arn
      Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
      Principal: events.amazonaws.com
      SourceArn: !GetAtt ClockSchedule.Arn

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The sequence
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ContainmentStateMachineRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: PlatformContainmentStateMachine
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: states.amazonaws.com }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'aws:SourceAccount': !Ref AWS::AccountId
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: InvokeStages
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              # BOTH stages. The state machine invokes ContainArn and
              # ReadoutArn; granting only the first meant every containment
              # contained correctly and then failed at the readout with a 403,
              # failing the execution and firing
              # platform-containment-execution-failed -- which publishes
              # straight to SNS and pages.
              #
              # Silent from Phase 7 until B-087 started forwarding
              # protected-action attempts, because nothing was triggering
              # containment before that. The DefinitionSubstitutions listed
              # both ARNs and the IAM policy listed one, and nothing compares
              # the two. B-096.
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: 'lambda:InvokeFunction'
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt ContainmentFunction.Arn
                  - !GetAtt ReadoutFunction.Arn
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'logs:CreateLogDelivery'
                  - 'logs:GetLogDelivery'
                  - 'logs:UpdateLogDelivery'
                  - 'logs:DeleteLogDelivery'
                  - 'logs:ListLogDeliveries'
                  - 'logs:PutResourcePolicy'
                  - 'logs:DescribeResourcePolicies'
                  - 'logs:DescribeLogGroups'
                Resource: '*'

  ContainmentStateMachineLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /aws/vendedlogs/states/platform-containment
      RetentionInDays: 2557
      KmsKeyId: !If
        - UseDefaultLogsKey
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:kms:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:alias/platform-logs'
        - !Ref LogsKeyArn

  ContainmentStateMachine:
    Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
    Properties:
      StateMachineName: platform-containment
      RoleArn: !GetAtt ContainmentStateMachineRole.Arn
      LoggingConfiguration:
        Level: ALL
        # The execution data is the incident: instance ids, principal ARNs,
        # finding text. It is already written to the append-only table with a
        # seven-year retention and a KMS key; duplicating it into the state
        # machine log doubles the places it has to be protected for no gain.
        IncludeExecutionData: false
        Destinations:
          - CloudWatchLogsLogGroup:
              LogGroupArn: !GetAtt ContainmentStateMachineLogGroup.Arn
      DefinitionSubstitutions:
        ContainArn: !GetAtt ContainmentFunction.Arn
        ReadoutArn: !GetAtt ReadoutFunction.Arn
      # The sequence design 07 calls non-negotiable, written out so an auditor
      # and whoever is on call at 3am read the same thing.
      #
      # PRESERVE RUNS BEFORE THE CONTAIN DECISION IS ACTED ON. That ordering is
      # the whole point: "Stage 1 — Gather (always runs, always safe)", and
      # "nothing destructive happens before preservation completes". A
      # medium-confidence finding in production is preserved and then left
      # alone, so that when a human decides twenty minutes later to contain it,
      # the evidence from twenty minutes ago still exists.
      DefinitionString: |
        {
          "Comment": "Prompt 7.1. Preserve, then isolate, then revoke, then blast radius. Mode parameter per P4: incident and exercise differ only in target.",
          "StartAt": "Initialise",
          "States": {

            "Initialise": {
              "Type": "Pass",
              "Comment": "Seeds every field Finalise reads. Step Functions FAILS a state whose Parameters reference a JSONPath that is not present, and most of these exist only on some paths: the gather-and-page route never isolates or revokes, and $.error exists only when a Catch fired. Without this, the happy path and the gather path both died at the last step, after containment had already acted -- the one place a failure destroys the record of what was done. Found by deploying.",
              "Parameters": {
                "mode.$": "$.mode",
                "incident.$": "$.incident",
                "triage": null,
                "preserve": null,
                "isolate": null,
                "revoke": null,
                "blast_radius": null,
                "error": null
              },
              "Next": "Triage"
            },

            "Triage": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Comment": "design 07's confidence-by-environment table. Decides CONTAIN or GATHER_AND_PAGE before anything touches the account, and records why.",
              "Resource": "${ContainArn}",
              "Parameters": {
                "step": "triage",
                "started_at.$": "$$.Execution.StartTime",
                "mode.$": "$.mode",
                "incident.$": "$.incident"
              },
              "ResultPath": "$.triage",
              "Retry": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["Lambda.ServiceException", "Lambda.AWSLambdaException", "Lambda.SdkClientException", "Lambda.TooManyRequestsException"], "IntervalSeconds": 3, "MaxAttempts": 3, "BackoffRate": 2 }
              ],
              "Catch": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["States.ALL"], "ResultPath": "$.error", "Next": "Finalise" }
              ],
              "Next": "Preserve"
            },

            "Preserve": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Comment": "Stage 1. ALWAYS runs, for every declared incident, including the ones that will not be contained. Evidence is perishable and the decision to contain may be a human's, taken later.",
              "Resource": "${ContainArn}",
              "Parameters": {
                "step": "preserve",
                "started_at.$": "$$.Execution.StartTime",
                "mode.$": "$.mode",
                "incident.$": "$.incident",
                "triage.$": "$.triage"
              },
              "ResultPath": "$.preserve",
              "Retry": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["Lambda.ServiceException", "Lambda.AWSLambdaException", "Lambda.SdkClientException", "Lambda.TooManyRequestsException"], "IntervalSeconds": 3, "MaxAttempts": 3, "BackoffRate": 2 }
              ],
              "Catch": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["States.ALL"], "ResultPath": "$.error", "Next": "Finalise" }
              ],
              "Next": "ShouldContain"
            },

            "ShouldContain": {
              "Type": "Choice",
              "Comment": "Not a mode branch. This is design 07's confidence table: production plus a medium-confidence finding gathers and pages, because isolating a healthy production service on a false positive is its own incident.",
              "Choices": [
                { "Variable": "$.triage.decision", "StringEquals": "contain", "Next": "Isolate" }
              ],
              "Default": "Finalise"
            },

            "Isolate": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Comment": "Stage 2. Applies the pre-staged isolation group to every interface. The instance STAYS RUNNING; only reachability changes.",
              "Resource": "${ContainArn}",
              "Parameters": {
                "step": "isolate",
                "started_at.$": "$$.Execution.StartTime",
                "mode.$": "$.mode",
                "incident.$": "$.incident",
                "triage.$": "$.triage"
              },
              "ResultPath": "$.isolate",
              "Retry": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["Lambda.ServiceException", "Lambda.AWSLambdaException", "Lambda.SdkClientException", "Lambda.TooManyRequestsException"], "IntervalSeconds": 3, "MaxAttempts": 3, "BackoffRate": 2 }
              ],
              "Catch": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["States.ALL"], "ResultPath": "$.error", "Next": "Finalise" }
              ],
              "Next": "Revoke"
            },

            "Revoke": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Comment": "Stage 3. Deny-all inline policy on the principal. It is NOT deleted: deletion loses the audit trail and breaks attribution.",
              "Resource": "${ContainArn}",
              "Parameters": {
                "step": "revoke",
                "started_at.$": "$$.Execution.StartTime",
                "mode.$": "$.mode",
                "incident.$": "$.incident",
                "triage.$": "$.triage"
              },
              "ResultPath": "$.revoke",
              "Retry": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["Lambda.ServiceException", "Lambda.AWSLambdaException", "Lambda.SdkClientException", "Lambda.TooManyRequestsException"], "IntervalSeconds": 3, "MaxAttempts": 3, "BackoffRate": 2 }
              ],
              "Catch": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["States.ALL"], "ResultPath": "$.error", "Next": "Finalise" }
              ],
              "Next": "BlastRadius"
            },

            "BlastRadius": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Comment": "Stage 4. Session revocation by token issue time -- required, not optional. Disabling a principal does not invalidate sessions already issued, and this is the step most often missed.",
              "Resource": "${ContainArn}",
              "Parameters": {
                "step": "blast_radius",
                "started_at.$": "$$.Execution.StartTime",
                "mode.$": "$.mode",
                "incident.$": "$.incident",
                "triage.$": "$.triage"
              },
              "ResultPath": "$.blast_radius",
              "Retry": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["Lambda.ServiceException", "Lambda.AWSLambdaException", "Lambda.SdkClientException", "Lambda.TooManyRequestsException"], "IntervalSeconds": 3, "MaxAttempts": 3, "BackoffRate": 2 }
              ],
              "Catch": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["States.ALL"], "ResultPath": "$.error", "Next": "Finalise" }
              ],
              "Next": "Finalise"
            },

            "Finalise": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Comment": "What was done, what was deliberately NOT done, and how long it took from discovery_time. Every path arrives here, including every Catch -- P5: automation that cannot complete an action produces an exception record, never silence.",
              "Resource": "${ContainArn}",
              "Parameters": {
                "step": "finalise",
                "started_at.$": "$$.Execution.StartTime",
                "mode.$": "$.mode",
                "incident.$": "$.incident",
                "triage.$": "$.triage",
                "preserve.$": "$.preserve",
                "isolate.$": "$.isolate",
                "revoke.$": "$.revoke",
                "blast_radius.$": "$.blast_radius",
                "error.$": "$.error"
              },
              "ResultPath": "$.summary",
              "Retry": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["States.ALL"], "IntervalSeconds": 3, "MaxAttempts": 3, "BackoffRate": 2 }
              ],
              "Catch": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["States.ALL"], "ResultPath": "$.finaliseError", "Next": "RecordingFailed" }
              ],
              "Next": "Readout"
            },

            "Readout": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Comment": "Prompt 7.2. Runs AFTER the summary has been published, because the summary is what pages somebody and this is slow -- a 24-hour CloudTrail lookup and an organization-wide indicator sweep. Carries the same account, resource and title, so the router derives the same dedup key and PagerDuty updates the open incident rather than raising a second one.",
              "Resource": "${ReadoutArn}",
              "Parameters": {
                "incident.$": "$.incident"
              },
              "ResultPath": "$.readout",
              "Retry": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["Lambda.ServiceException", "Lambda.AWSLambdaException", "Lambda.SdkClientException", "Lambda.TooManyRequestsException"], "IntervalSeconds": 5, "MaxAttempts": 3, "BackoffRate": 2 }
              ],
              "Catch": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["States.ALL"], "ResultPath": "$.readoutError", "Next": "ReadoutFailed" }
              ],
              "Next": "Done"
            },

            "ReadoutFailed": {
              "Type": "Fail",
              "Comment": "CONTAINMENT SUCCEEDED; the readout did not. Marked failed deliberately so it reaches a human: an incident that paged with what was done, and then produced no dossier, leaves whoever picks it up without the principal's activity, its reach, or the cross-account answer -- and the cross-account answer is the one that says whether this is one workload or the whole platform.",
              "Error": "ReadoutFailed",
              "Cause": "Containment completed and was recorded. The readout could not be generated; the incident record holds the containment stages, and the cross-account indicator question is UNANSWERED."
            },

            "RecordingFailed": {
              "Type": "Fail",
              "Comment": "Containment may have acted and failed to write down that it did. That is the one outcome nothing downstream can see, so the execution is marked failed to make it visible in the console next to the incident.",
              "Error": "ContainmentRecordingFailed",
              "Cause": "The containment engine could not write its own summary. Check the incident table and the isolation state of the named resource by hand."
            },

            "Done": { "Type": "Succeed" }
          }
        }

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Watching the watcher
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # These publish to SNS directly rather than through the router. A containment
  # engine that is broken cannot credibly report that it is broken through the
  # layer it publishes into -- the same fallback reasoning that kept the
  # CloudWatch subscription in alerting/10-alert-topic.yaml.
  ContainmentFailureAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Condition: HasAlerting
    Properties:
      AlarmName: platform-containment-execution-failed
      AlarmDescription: >-
        A containment execution failed. A security incident was declared and
        the automation did not complete the sequence — check the incident table
        for what stage it reached and what state the named resource is in.
      Namespace: AWS/States
      MetricName: ExecutionsFailed
      Dimensions:
        - Name: StateMachineArn
          Value: !Ref ContainmentStateMachine
      Statistic: Sum
      Period: 300
      EvaluationPeriods: 1
      Threshold: 1
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold
      TreatMissingData: notBreaching
      AlarmActions: [!Ref AlertTopicArn]

  DeclarationDlqAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Condition: HasAlerting
    Properties:
      AlarmName: platform-declaration-dlq-not-empty
      AlarmDescription: >-
        A finding that should have been considered for declaration never
        reached the declaration function. Silence here looks exactly like a
        quiet week.
      Namespace: AWS/SQS
      MetricName: ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible
      Dimensions:
        - Name: QueueName
          Value: !GetAtt DeclarationDlq.QueueName
      Statistic: Maximum
      Period: 300
      EvaluationPeriods: 1
      Threshold: 0
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanThreshold
      TreatMissingData: notBreaching
      AlarmActions: [!Ref AlertTopicArn]

Outputs:
  ContainmentRoleArn:
    Description: >-
      Pass to containment/00-responder-role.yaml as ContainmentRoleArn. The
      member-side role trusts this ARN and nothing else.
    Value: !GetAtt ContainmentRole.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ContainmentRoleArn'
  StateMachineArn:
    Value: !Ref ContainmentStateMachine
  IncidentTableName:
    Value: !Ref IncidentTable
  ReadoutFunctionName:
    Value: !Ref ReadoutFunction
  ClockFunctionName:
    Value: !Ref ClockFunction
  ExerciseConfigured:
    Description: >-
      "none" until prompt 7.4. Exercise mode refuses to run while unset.
    Value: !Ref ExerciseAccountId
files.containment/20-exercise-target.yaml:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  AltDigital Managed Platform — the exercise account's side of the scheduled
  containment drill (prompt 7.4). Deploys to altdig-sandbox-exercise ONLY.
  Creates the harness that plants a drill target, and the deliberately
  over-permissioned principal that proves a member account cannot block
  containment.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why this is not part of the member baseline
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Everything in here can create and destroy things. It is deployed to exactly
# one account — the purpose-built exercise account — with
# scripts/deploy-to-account.sh, not as a StackSet to the Sandbox OU.
#
# That distinction is the whole safety argument. If this were a baseline
# stack it would place instance-creation and instance-termination rights into
# the canary account and, later, into every member account in the OU. The
# exercise needs an account where creating and destroying things is the point;
# nowhere else should have a principal that can.
#
# design 07: "a scheduled exercise fires the REAL automation against a
# purpose-built target in an isolated account."
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Yes, this template terminates instances
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLAUDE.md's hard rule is about REMEDIATION: automation must never destroy a
# resource in response to a finding, because the resource is evidence and the
# finding may be wrong. Nothing here responds to a finding. The harness creates
# a throwaway instance so that containment has something to contain, and then
# removes the instance it just made.
#
# The same provenance discipline recovery/src/teardown.py uses applies, and for
# the same reason: every delete permission below is conditioned on a tag that
# only this harness applies, so the role cannot express a request against
# anything it did not create. A drill that could terminate an arbitrary
# instance would be a worse thing than no drill.

Parameters:

  ExerciseRoleArn:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      The Audit-account role that drives the exercise — the state machine's
      Lambda role from containment/40-exercise.yaml. Exactly one principal,
      named in full, for the same reason the responder role names exactly one.
    AllowedPattern: '^arn:aws[a-z-]*:iam::[0-9]{12}:role/.+$'

Resources:

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The harness: plants a target, then removes it
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ExerciseHarnessRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: PlatformExerciseHarness
      Description: >-
        Creates and removes containment drill targets in the exercise account.
        Every destructive permission is conditioned on a tag this harness
        applies at creation.
      MaxSessionDuration: 3600
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { AWS: !Ref ExerciseRoleArn }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: PlantAndRemoveDrillTargets
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: LookAround
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'ec2:DescribeInstances'
                  - 'ec2:DescribeImages'
                  - 'ec2:DescribeSubnets'
                  - 'ec2:DescribeSecurityGroups'
                  - 'ec2:DescribeVpcs'
                  - 'ec2:DescribeSnapshots'
                  - 'ec2:DescribeTags'
                  - 'ssm:GetParameter'
                  - 'ssm:GetParameters'
                Resource: '*'
