              - Sid: PlantTheTarget
                Effect: Allow
                # RunInstances must be unconditioned on the tag, because the
                # tag does not exist until the instance does. What narrows it
                # is the instance TYPE condition below and the fact that this
                # role exists in one throwaway account.
                Action: 'ec2:RunInstances'
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: OnlySmallInstances
                Effect: Deny
                # A bug that launches a fleet of large instances in a drill
                # account is a bill nobody notices until the month closes. The
                # drill needs a machine that boots; it does not need a big one.
                Action: 'ec2:RunInstances'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ec2:*:*:instance/*'
                Condition:
                  StringNotEquals:
                    'ec2:InstanceType': ['t3.micro', 't3.nano', 't2.micro']
              - Sid: TagWhatItCreates
                Effect: Allow
                Action: 'ec2:CreateTags'
                Resource: '*'
                Condition:
                  StringEquals:
                    'ec2:CreateAction': 'RunInstances'
              - Sid: RemoveOnlyWhatItCreated
                Effect: Allow
                # THE control. Terminating an instance is permitted only where
                # the instance carries the exercise tag, which only this
                # harness applies and only at creation. An instance that
                # belongs to somebody else is outside the reach of these
                # credentials entirely — not merely outside the code path.
                Action: 'ec2:TerminateInstances'
                Resource: '*'
                Condition:
                  StringLike:
                    # LITERAL, not a parameter reference. An IAM condition KEY
                    # cannot be a !Sub — CloudFormation reports "Unhashable
                    # type", which names the YAML construct and not the rule.
                    #
                    # The tag key was a parameter and is now hardcoded in both
                    # halves, which is better anyway: a tag key configured in
                    # one place and applied in another is two values that must
                    # agree, and the failure when they do not is that teardown
                    # silently cannot touch what it created.
                    'aws:ResourceTag/platform-exercise-id': '*'

              - Sid: PlantAndRemoveTheDrillPrincipal
                Effect: Allow
                # Name-gated rather than tag-gated: IAM role creation and
                # deletion do not support a resource-tag condition the way EC2
                # does, so the boundary is the path and the name prefix. The
                # prefix is deliberately nothing like `Platform*`, so this can
                # never reach a platform role even by accident.
                Action:
                  - 'iam:CreateRole'
                  - 'iam:DeleteRole'
                  - 'iam:GetRole'
                  - 'iam:TagRole'
                  - 'iam:PutRolePolicy'
                  - 'iam:DeleteRolePolicy'
                  - 'iam:ListRolePolicies'
                  - 'iam:ListAttachedRolePolicies'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:role/ExerciseDrillPrincipal*'

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The blast-radius test subject (open-items.md V3)
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # design 07: "If an attacker holds admin in the member account, the response
  # capability must still function. This assumption is load-bearing and must be
  # tested — verify periodically that a member account with full local admin
  # cannot block the containment role."
  #
  # This role is the "member account with full local admin", narrowed to the
  # exact question being asked.
  #
  # It does NOT carry AdministratorAccess, and that is a deliberate improvement
  # on a literal reading. With AdministratorAccess, a denial proves the SCP
  # works but so would a dozen other things; with a policy that grants EXACTLY
  # the IAM actions the SCP is supposed to block, a denial can only have come
  # from the SCP. The test isolates its variable.
  #
  # It also keeps the blast radius of a standing permissive role down to: can
  # modify Platform* roles in one empty drill account, if and only if the SCP
  # that is supposed to stop it has failed — which is precisely the condition
  # the exercise exists to detect and report.
  BlastRadiusSubjectRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: PlatformExerciseLocalAdmin
      Description: >-
        Stands in for a compromised member account holding local admin. Used
        once a month to attempt to disable the containment role and confirm the
        SCP refuses. Grants IAM rights that an SCP is expected to override.
      MaxSessionDuration: 3600
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { AWS: !Ref ExerciseRoleArn }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: AttemptToBlockContainment
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: EverythingTheScpShouldRefuse
                Effect: Allow
                # IAM says yes. The SCP is expected to say no. If the attempt
                # succeeds, the platform has a critical finding: a member
                # account can disarm its own containment, and every tenant is
                # affected, not just this one.
                Action:
                  - 'iam:TagRole'
                  - 'iam:UntagRole'
                  - 'iam:PutRolePolicy'
                  - 'iam:DeleteRolePolicy'
                  - 'iam:UpdateAssumeRolePolicy'
                  - 'iam:DeleteRole'
                  - 'iam:AttachRolePolicy'
                  - 'iam:DetachRolePolicy'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:role/Platform*'
              - Sid: ReadBackWhatHappened
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'iam:GetRole'
                  - 'iam:ListRoleTags'
                  - 'iam:ListRolePolicies'
                Resource: '*'

Outputs:
  HarnessRoleArn:
    Description: 'Assumed by the exercise state machine to plant and remove targets.'
    Value: !GetAtt ExerciseHarnessRole.Arn
  BlastRadiusSubjectRoleArn:
    Description: >-
      Assumed by the exercise to attempt, and fail, to disable containment.
    Value: !GetAtt BlastRadiusSubjectRole.Arn
files.containment/30-forensics-reader.yaml:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  AltDigital Managed Platform — a read-only role in the Forensics account that
  lets the containment exercise confirm preserved evidence actually arrived
  (prompt 7.4). Deploys to altdig-security-forensics ONLY.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why the check has to run from this side
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Prompt 7.4: "Verify snapshots landed in Forensics."
#
# The exercise could check that from the account being contained, by reading
# the snapshot's createVolumePermission and confirming the Forensics account id
# is on it. That proves the share was REQUESTED. It does not prove it worked.
#
# The difference is not academic. A share can be requested against an account
# id that is wrong, or that no longer exists, or that is in a different
# partition; a snapshot can be shared and then made unusable by a KMS key
# policy that does not admit the far account, which is the common failure and
# produces exactly no error on the sharing side. In every one of those cases
# the source account reports success and the evidence is not there.
#
# So the exercise assumes this role and asks the Forensics account what it can
# actually see. That is the question the auditor is really asking.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read-only, deliberately and permanently
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# This role can describe snapshots and nothing else. The Forensics account
# holds preserved evidence from real incidents; a role reachable from another
# account should never be able to alter or remove any of it, and the exercise
# has no reason to want to. If a future need appears to write here, it should
# be a different role with its own argument, not an extension of this one.

Parameters:

  ExerciseRoleArn:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      The Audit-account role that drives the exercise. Exactly one principal,
      named in full — not an account root, which would make every present and
      future principal in Audit a reader of the forensics account.
    AllowedPattern: '^arn:aws[a-z-]*:iam::[0-9]{12}:role/.+$'

Resources:

  ForensicsReaderRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: PlatformForensicsReader
      Description: >-
        Read-only. Lets the scheduled containment exercise confirm that
        preserved evidence is visible from the Forensics account.
      MaxSessionDuration: 3600
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { AWS: !Ref ExerciseRoleArn }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: SeeWhatArrived
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: DescribeSharedSnapshots
                Effect: Allow
                # Describe only. No CopySnapshot, no CreateVolume, no
                # DeleteSnapshot — the exercise needs to know the evidence is
                # visible, not to do anything with it.
                Action:
                  - 'ec2:DescribeSnapshots'
                  - 'ec2:DescribeSnapshotAttribute'
                Resource: '*'

Outputs:
  ForensicsReaderRoleArn:
    Description: >-
      Assumed by the exercise to confirm evidence is visible from this side.
    Value: !GetAtt ForensicsReaderRole.Arn
files.containment/40-exercise.yaml:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  AltDigital Managed Platform — the scheduled containment exercise (prompt
  7.4). Deploys to the Audit account alongside containment. Fires the REAL
  declaration and containment automation at a purpose-built target in the
  isolated exercise account, verifies what actually happened from both ends,
  and produces tabletop evidence with real timings.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What makes this evidence rather than a narrative
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# design 07: "This also produces tabletop evidence with real timings rather
# than a narrated walkthrough — a considerably stronger audit artifact."
#
# The exercise plants a finding on the same event bus a GuardDuty finding
# arrives on and then does not participate again until verification.
# Declaration runs declare.py. Containment runs contain.py. The readout runs
# readout.py. If the drill passes, the code that passed is the code that runs
# during an incident, which is the whole of P4's claim and the reason design 07
# says containment has the worst testing problem in the design.
#
# The verification is deliberately adversarial about its own result:
#
#   * isolation is checked by reading the instance's security groups AND by
#     confirming the isolation group has no ingress rules. A correctly attached
#     group with a permissive rule is isolation that looks right and is not.
#   * the instance is asserted to be STILL RUNNING, because containment that
#     stopped it would have destroyed the volatile evidence preservation exists
#     to capture.
#   * preserved evidence is confirmed FROM THE FORENSICS ACCOUNT, not from the
#     account that shared it. A share can be requested against a wrong account
#     id, or be unusable because of a KMS key policy, and the sharing side
#     reports success in both cases.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The blast-radius verification (open-items.md V3)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Prompt 7.4: "confirm a member account with full local admin cannot block the
# containment role. Run it on the same schedule."
#
# Run as part of the same state machine rather than as a second scheduled
# thing, because the two answer one question together: containment works, AND
# it cannot be switched off by the account it is pointed at. Either alone is a
# weaker claim than an auditor will accept.

Parameters:

  ArtifactBucket:
    Type: String

  ArtifactKey:
    Type: String

  IncidentTableName:
    Type: String
    Default: platform-security-incidents

  AlertBusName:
    Type: String
    Default: platform-alerts

  ExerciseAccountId:
    Type: String
    AllowedPattern: '^[0-9]{12}$'
    Description: >-
      The isolated account the drill runs in. REQUIRED — there is no default
      and no fallback. contain.py refuses to run in exercise mode against any
      other account, and this stack refuses to deploy without one.

  ForensicsAccountId:
    Type: String
    AllowedPattern: '^[0-9]{12}$'
    Description: >-
      Checked from the far side to confirm preserved evidence actually arrived.

  ExerciseSubnetId:
    Type: String
    AllowedPattern: '^subnet-[0-9a-f]+$'
    Description: >-
      Where the drill instance is launched, in the exercise account. Explicit
      rather than discovered: a drill that picks its own subnet will eventually
      pick a different one and quietly change what is being tested.

  ScheduleExpression:
    Type: String
    Default: 'cron(0 14 ? * 3#2 *)'
    Description: >-
      Monthly. Second Wednesday at 14:00 UTC, which is deliberately the day
      AFTER the restore test in recovery/20-restore-schedule.yaml. Running both
      exercises on the same morning would make a bad day look like two
      unrelated failures, and they contend for the same attention.

  ScheduleEnabled:
    Type: String
    Default: 'ENABLED'
    AllowedValues: ['ENABLED', 'DISABLED']
    Description: >-
      The exercise launches and terminates a real instance. This stops it per
      account without deleting the stack.

  AwaitSeconds:
    Type: Number
    Default: 240
    MinValue: 60
    Description: >-
      How long the exercise waits for containment to record a summary. A
      timeout is a FINDING about containment being slow, not an error: the
      exercise records the timings it has and tears down anyway, because
      raising here would leave a live instance behind.

  LogsKeyArn:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      Pass the alerts key. alias/platform-logs does not exist in a platform
      account — it comes from the member baseline. See B-060's sibling in
      containment/10-containment.yaml.

  AlertTopicArn:
    Type: String
    Default: ''

Conditions:
  UseDefaultLogsKey: !Equals [!Ref LogsKeyArn, '']
  HasAlerting: !Not [!Equals [!Ref AlertTopicArn, '']]

Resources:

  ExerciseRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: PlatformContainmentExercise
      Description: >-
        Drives the scheduled containment drill. Holds no destructive permission
        in this account; everything destructive happens in the exercise account
        through a role conditioned on a tag the drill applies at creation.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: lambda.amazonaws.com }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: RunTheExercise
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: PlantAndRemoveDrillTargets
                Effect: Allow
                # Three named roles in two named accounts. Not a wildcard
                # account, because unlike the responder role these are not
                # deployed everywhere — there is exactly one exercise account
                # and exactly one forensics account, and naming them means a
                # misconfiguration cannot point the drill somewhere real.
                Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${ExerciseAccountId}:role/PlatformExerciseHarness'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${ExerciseAccountId}:role/PlatformExerciseLocalAdmin'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${ForensicsAccountId}:role/PlatformForensicsReader'
              - Sid: PlantTheFinding
                Effect: Allow
                Action: 'events:PutEvents'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:events:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:event-bus/${AlertBusName}'
              - Sid: WatchTheIncidentRecordAndWriteEvidence
                Effect: Allow
                # Query to observe what containment recorded, PutItem to write
                # the exercise evidence. No UpdateItem and no DeleteItem — the
                # exercise cannot alter the incident it is observing, which is
                # what keeps its own evidence worth having.
                Action: ['dynamodb:Query', 'dynamodb:PutItem']
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:dynamodb:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:table/${IncidentTableName}'

  ExerciseLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /aws/lambda/platform-containment-exercise
      # Seven years. This is the tabletop evidence an auditor asks for, and the
      # question "when did you last prove containment works" is asked years
      # after the exercise that answers it.
      RetentionInDays: 2557
      KmsKeyId: !If
        - UseDefaultLogsKey
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:kms:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:alias/platform-logs'
        - !Ref LogsKeyArn

  ExerciseFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    DependsOn: ExerciseLogGroup
    Properties:
      FunctionName: platform-containment-exercise
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: exercise.handler
      Role: !GetAtt ExerciseRole.Arn
      # The await step polls for up to AwaitSeconds, and the prepare step waits
      # for an instance to reach running. Both are bounded well inside this.
      Timeout: 600
      MemorySize: 512
      Code:
        S3Bucket: !Ref ArtifactBucket
        S3Key: !Ref ArtifactKey
      Environment:
        Variables:
          INCIDENT_TABLE: !Ref IncidentTableName
          ALERT_BUS_NAME: !Ref AlertBusName
          EXERCISE_ACCOUNT_ID: !Ref ExerciseAccountId
          FORENSICS_ACCOUNT_ID: !Ref ForensicsAccountId
          EXERCISE_SUBNET_ID: !Ref ExerciseSubnetId
          AWAIT_SECONDS: !Ref AwaitSeconds

  ExerciseStateMachineRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: PlatformContainmentExerciseStateMachine
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: states.amazonaws.com }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'aws:SourceAccount': !Ref AWS::AccountId
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: InvokeSteps
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: 'lambda:InvokeFunction'
                Resource: !GetAtt ExerciseFunction.Arn
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'logs:CreateLogDelivery'
                  - 'logs:GetLogDelivery'
                  - 'logs:UpdateLogDelivery'
                  - 'logs:DeleteLogDelivery'
                  - 'logs:ListLogDeliveries'
                  - 'logs:PutResourcePolicy'
                  - 'logs:DescribeResourcePolicies'
                  - 'logs:DescribeLogGroups'
                Resource: '*'

  ExerciseStateMachineLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /aws/vendedlogs/states/platform-containment-exercise
      RetentionInDays: 2557
      KmsKeyId: !If
        - UseDefaultLogsKey
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:kms:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:alias/platform-logs'
        - !Ref LogsKeyArn

  ExerciseStateMachine:
    Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
    Properties:
      StateMachineName: platform-containment-exercise
      RoleArn: !GetAtt ExerciseStateMachineRole.Arn
      LoggingConfiguration:
        Level: ALL
        IncludeExecutionData: false
        Destinations:
          - CloudWatchLogsLogGroup:
              LogGroupArn: !GetAtt ExerciseStateMachineLogGroup.Arn
      DefinitionSubstitutions:
        ExerciseArn: !GetAtt ExerciseFunction.Arn
      DefinitionString: |
        {
          "Comment": "Prompt 7.4. Plant a target, plant a finding, let the REAL automation run, verify from both ends, prove the account cannot block containment, tear down, record.",
          "StartAt": "Initialise",
          "States": {

            "Initialise": {
              "Type": "Pass",
              "Comment": "Seeds every field the later states read. Step Functions FAILS a state whose Parameters name a JSONPath that is absent, and every one of these is absent on some path -- B-057, found the same way in the containment state machine.",
              "Parameters": {
                "prepared": null,
                "planted": null,
                "awaited": null,
                "verified": null,
                "blast": null,
                "teardown": null,
                "error": null
              },
              "Next": "Prepare"
            },

            "Prepare": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Comment": "Launch the drill instance and create the drill principal, both tagged with this exercise id at creation. Nothing is reused between runs: a long-lived drill target drifts, and an exercise that passes against a target nobody has rebuilt proves less than it looks like.",
              "Resource": "${ExerciseArn}",
              "Parameters": { "step": "prepare" },
              "ResultPath": "$.prepared",
              "Retry": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["Lambda.ServiceException", "Lambda.AWSLambdaException", "Lambda.SdkClientException", "Lambda.TooManyRequestsException"], "IntervalSeconds": 5, "MaxAttempts": 2, "BackoffRate": 2 }
              ],
              "Catch": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["States.ALL"], "ResultPath": "$.error", "Next": "Teardown" }
              ],
              "Next": "Plant"
            },

            "Plant": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Comment": "Put a finding on the platform bus. From here until Verify the exercise does not participate: declaration, containment and the readout all run their real code.",
              "Resource": "${ExerciseArn}",
              "Parameters": { "step": "plant", "prepared.$": "$.prepared" },
              "ResultPath": "$.planted",
              "Catch": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["States.ALL"], "ResultPath": "$.error", "Next": "Teardown" }
              ],
              "Next": "Await"
            },

            "Await": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Comment": "Poll the append-only incident record until containment writes its summary. The RECORD, not the execution status -- an execution that succeeded without recording anything is exactly the failure this drill exists to catch.",
              "Resource": "${ExerciseArn}",
              "Parameters": { "step": "await", "prepared.$": "$.prepared", "planted.$": "$.planted" },
              "ResultPath": "$.awaited",
              "Catch": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["States.ALL"], "ResultPath": "$.error", "Next": "Teardown" }
              ],
              "Next": "Verify"
            },

            "Verify": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Comment": "Assert what happened, adversarially: the isolation group is attached AND denies all ingress, the instance is still running, and the evidence is readable FROM the Forensics account rather than merely shared towards it.",
              "Resource": "${ExerciseArn}",
              "Parameters": { "step": "verify", "prepared.$": "$.prepared", "awaited.$": "$.awaited" },
              "ResultPath": "$.verified",
              "Catch": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["States.ALL"], "ResultPath": "$.error", "Next": "Teardown" }
              ],
              "Next": "BlastRadius"
            },

            "BlastRadius": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Comment": "open-items.md V3. Assume a role that IAM has granted the exact rights to disable the containment role, and attempt it. A denial can then only have come from the SCP, which is what isolates the variable.",
              "Resource": "${ExerciseArn}",
              "Parameters": { "step": "blast", "prepared.$": "$.prepared" },
              "ResultPath": "$.blast",
              "Catch": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["States.ALL"], "ResultPath": "$.error", "Next": "Teardown" }
              ],
              "Next": "Teardown"
            },

            "Teardown": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Comment": "EVERY path arrives here, including every Catch, because every path may have left a running instance behind. Removes only what this exercise can prove it created; anything else is reported as an orphan and left alone.",
              "Resource": "${ExerciseArn}",
              "Parameters": { "step": "teardown", "prepared.$": "$.prepared" },
              "ResultPath": "$.teardown",
              "Retry": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["States.ALL"], "IntervalSeconds": 5, "MaxAttempts": 3, "BackoffRate": 2 }
              ],
              "Catch": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["States.ALL"], "ResultPath": "$.teardownError", "Next": "Record" }
              ],
              "Next": "Record"
            },

            "Record": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Comment": "Tabletop evidence with real timings, written to the append-only record and routed through the one routing layer. A PASSED exercise declares digest -- it is evidence, not news. A FAILED one declares nothing, so the tier decides and it pages where paging exists.",
              "Resource": "${ExerciseArn}",
              "Parameters": {
                "step": "record",
                "prepared.$": "$.prepared",
                "awaited.$": "$.awaited",
                "verified.$": "$.verified",
                "blast.$": "$.blast",
                "teardown.$": "$.teardown",
                "error.$": "$.error"
              },
              "ResultPath": "$.evidence",
              "Retry": [
                { "ErrorEquals": ["States.ALL"], "IntervalSeconds": 5, "MaxAttempts": 3, "BackoffRate": 2 }
              ],
              "Next": "Outcome"
            },

            "Outcome": {
              "Type": "Choice",
              "Comment": "The execution status mirrors the drill's verdict, so the console shows at a glance whether containment was last proven to work.",
              "Choices": [
                { "Variable": "$.evidence.passed", "BooleanEquals": true, "Next": "Passed" }
              ],
              "Default": "Failed"
            },

            "Passed": { "Type": "Succeed" },

            "Failed": {
              "Type": "Fail",
              "Comment": "Containment could not be demonstrated. The evidence record names the specific checks that failed; this state exists so that the failure is visible in the console next to every previous month's success.",
              "Error": "ContainmentExerciseFailed",
              "Cause": "The scheduled containment exercise did not pass. See the exercise evidence record for the failed checks and the blast-radius verdict."
            }
          }
        }

  ExerciseSchedule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: platform-containment-exercise-monthly
      Description: >-
        Prompt 7.4 — monthly containment drill against the purpose-built target
        in the isolated exercise account.
      ScheduleExpression: !Ref ScheduleExpression
      State: !Ref ScheduleEnabled
      Targets:
        - Id: exercise
          Arn: !Ref ExerciseStateMachine
          RoleArn: !GetAtt ExerciseScheduleRole.Arn

  ExerciseScheduleRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: PlatformContainmentExerciseSchedule
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: events.amazonaws.com }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'aws:SourceAccount': !Ref AWS::AccountId
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: StartTheExercise
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: 'states:StartExecution'
                Resource: !Ref ExerciseStateMachine

  # The exercise proves containment works. THIS proves the exercise is still
  # running -- which is a different question, and the one that goes unnoticed.
  #
  # Unlike the restore test (B-050), this CAN be a CloudWatch alarm: the drill
  # is monthly, but a state machine emits ExecutionsStarted on the day it runs
  # and the alarm only has to notice a FAILED one, which is a same-day signal
  # rather than an absence spanning weeks.
  ExerciseFailedAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Condition: HasAlerting
    Properties:
      AlarmName: platform-containment-exercise-failed
      AlarmDescription: >-
        The scheduled containment exercise failed. Containment could not be
        demonstrated against a purpose-built target, which means the platform
        cannot currently show that it would work during a real incident. Check
        the exercise evidence record for the failed checks.
      Namespace: AWS/States
      MetricName: ExecutionsFailed
      Dimensions:
        - Name: StateMachineArn
          Value: !Ref ExerciseStateMachine
      Statistic: Sum
      Period: 3600
      EvaluationPeriods: 1
      Threshold: 1
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold
      TreatMissingData: notBreaching
      AlarmActions: [!Ref AlertTopicArn]

Outputs:
  StateMachineArn:
    Value: !Ref ExerciseStateMachine
  ExerciseRoleArn:
    Description: >-
      Pass to containment/20-exercise-target.yaml and
      containment/30-forensics-reader.yaml as ExerciseRoleArn. Both trust this
      ARN and nothing else.
    Value: !GetAtt ExerciseRole.Arn
files.design/06a-alarm-specification.yaml:
# =============================================================================
# AltDigital Platform — Standard Alarm Specification
# Companion to design/06-observability.md "Auto-instrumentation"
# Consumed by: instrumentation Lambda (Claude Code prompt 4.1)
#
# version: 1
# status:   DRAFT — thresholds marked [TUNE] require per-application review
#           before production use. Thresholds marked [DEFAULT] are conventional
#           and may be adopted as-is.
#
# This file is the data half of the data-driven instrumentation layer. Adding a
# resource type or changing a threshold must not require a code change.
# =============================================================================

version: 1

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Environment tiers. Source: design/14-environment-tiers.md
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
tiers:
  dev:
    monitoring_depth: light
    default_routing: digest
    canaries: false
    alarm_actions_enabled: true
  test:
    monitoring_depth: light
    default_routing: digest_and_jira
    canaries: optional
    alarm_actions_enabled: true
  uat:
    monitoring_depth: moderate
    default_routing: jira_and_commercial
    canaries: true
    alarm_actions_enabled: true
  prod:
    monitoring_depth: pervasive
    default_routing: pagerduty
    canaries: true
    alarm_actions_enabled: true

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Routing destinations. Source: design/06-observability.md, design/12
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
routing_destinations:
  pagerduty:        { pages: true,  ticket: true,  digest: true }
  jira_and_commercial: { pages: false, ticket: true,  digest: true, commercial_event: true }
  digest_and_jira:  { pages: false, ticket: true,  digest: true }
  digest:           { pages: false, ticket: false, digest: true }
  review_queue:     { pages: false, ticket: false, digest: false }

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Global defaults. Any alarm may override.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
defaults:
  period_seconds: 300
  evaluation_periods: 2
  datapoints_to_alarm: 2
  treat_missing_data: notBreaching
  tags:
    platform-managed: "true"
  # Suppression: alarms are suppressed while the environment is outside its HOOP
  # or inside a declared maintenance window. See design/14-environment-tiers.md.
  respect_hoop_suppression: true
  respect_maintenance_window: true

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Resource types IN SCOPE.
#
# An EventBridge resource-creation event for a type NOT in this list produces an
# EXCEPTION RECORD, never a silent no-op. See design/06 and prompt 4.1.
#
# "agent_required: true" means the CloudWatch agent must be installed for some
# alarms in the set. Absence of the agent is itself a gap — see the
# telemetry_gap block and design/11-developer-access.md.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
resource_types_in_scope:
  - AWS::EC2::Instance
  - AWS::RDS::DBInstance
  - AWS::RDS::DBCluster
  - AWS::ECS::Service
  - AWS::Lambda::Function
  - AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::LoadBalancer
  - AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::TargetGroup
  - AWS::S3::Bucket
  - AWS::DynamoDB::Table
  - AWS::SQS::Queue
  - AWS::ElastiCache::ReplicationGroup
  - AWS::ApiGateway::RestApi
  - AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Api
  - AWS::EFS::FileSystem
  - AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup

# Types explicitly known and deliberately NOT instrumented. These do not raise an
# exception; they are recorded as "known, no alarms applicable".
resource_types_no_alarms:
  # --- platform's own infrastructure -----------------------------------------
  # Added 2026-09-17 while building prompt 4.1, after these caused a feedback
  # loop in the canary account.
  #
  # The instrumentation Lambda creates a CloudWatch alarm; AWS Config discovers
  # that alarm as a resource; EventBridge fires; the Lambda does not recognise
  # AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm and raises an exception. Every alarm it created
  # produced an exception ABOUT ITSELF — eight within the hour — which pinned
  # platform-instrumentation-exception permanently in ALARM and destroyed the
  # one signal that says a real resource came up unmonitored.
  #
  # These belong here rather than in a list inside the handler, because
  # resource_types_no_alarms is exactly the mechanism this file defines for
  # "known, and deliberately not instrumented". A second list in code would be
  # the same two-copies problem that deleting instrumentation/alarm-sets.yaml
  # removed.
  #
  # Note none of these is ever a tenant WORKLOAD resource. A tenant Lambda
  # function is in scope and stays in scope; an alarm is not a thing you alarm
  # on.
  - AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
  - AWS::Events::Rule
  - AWS::Logs::LogGroup
  - AWS::Logs::MetricFilter
  - AWS::SSM::Association

  # Canaries are alarmed by canaries/10-canary.yaml, not from here.
  #
  # Added 2026-09-18 while building prompt 4.3. The reason is not that a canary
  # is unimportant — it is the most important thing in this file, being the only
  # check that says the service WORKS rather than that it is running.
  #
  # The reason is that half of them are invisible to this mechanism. A tenant
  # with an existing Playwright suite is monitored by a Fargate task publishing
  # the same metrics, and there is no AWS::Synthetics::Canary resource for AWS
  # Config to discover. Alarming canaries from here would cover the native
  # runner and silently miss the Fargate one, and prompt 4.3 requires the
  # downstream alarm path to be identical either way. So both are alarmed by the
  # canary template, which is the one place that knows about both.
  #
  # Listed here rather than omitted so the instrumentation Lambda treats a
  # canary as "known, deliberately not instrumented" instead of raising an
  # exception for a type it does not recognise — and so that it does not create
  # a second alarm, with a different name, on the native canaries only.
  - AWS::Synthetics::Canary

  # AWS Config's own pseudo-resources. Not resources at all — they are Config's
  # records OF resources, emitted once per rule evaluation, so they arrive at
  # the rate Config evaluates rather than the rate infrastructure changes.
  - AWS::Config::ResourceCompliance
  - AWS::Config::ConformancePackCompliance
  - AWS::SSM::ManagedInstanceInventory

  # --- genuinely not worth a metric alarm ------------------------------------
  - AWS::IAM::Role
  - AWS::IAM::Policy
  - AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
  - AWS::EC2::Subnet
  - AWS::EC2::RouteTable
  - AWS::KMS::Key            # covered by CloudTrail event alarms, not metrics
  - AWS::SecretsManager::Secret
  - AWS::CloudFormation::Stack

# =============================================================================
# ALARM SETS
#
# threshold_by_tier: omit a tier to suppress that alarm in that tier.
# severity_by_tier:  overrides the tier default_routing where stated.
# =============================================================================

alarm_sets:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AWS::EC2::Instance:
    agent_required: true
    alarms:

      - id: ec2-cpu-high
        metric: CPUUtilization
        namespace: AWS/EC2
        statistic: Average
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 3
        datapoints_to_alarm: 3
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        unit: Percent
        treat_missing_data: notBreaching
        threshold_by_tier: { dev: 95, test: 95, uat: 85, prod: 80 }   # [DEFAULT]
        note: >
          Sustained 15 min. Deliberately loose in dev/test — a build machine at
          95% is working, not failing.

      - id: ec2-status-check-failed
        metric: StatusCheckFailed
        namespace: AWS/EC2
        statistic: Maximum
        period_seconds: 60
        evaluation_periods: 2
        datapoints_to_alarm: 2
        comparison: GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold
        treat_missing_data: breaching
        threshold_by_tier: { dev: 1, test: 1, uat: 1, prod: 1 }       # [DEFAULT]
        note: >
          Hypervisor-level, no agent required. treat_missing_data is breaching
          because absence here means the instance is unreachable.

      - id: ec2-disk-high
        metric: disk_used_percent
        namespace: CWAgent
        statistic: Average
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 2
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        unit: Percent
        treat_missing_data: notBreaching
        dimensions_additional: [path, device, fstype]
        threshold_by_tier: { dev: 90, test: 90, uat: 85, prod: 85 }   # [DEFAULT]
        remediation_runbook: ec2-disk-exhaustion

      - id: ec2-memory-high
        metric: mem_used_percent
        namespace: CWAgent
        statistic: Average
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 3
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        unit: Percent
        treat_missing_data: notBreaching
        threshold_by_tier: { uat: 90, prod: 90 }                      # [TUNE]
        note: >
          Omitted in dev/test. Memory thresholds are workload-specific; 90 is a
          starting point, not a considered value.

      - id: ec2-agent-telemetry-gap
        metric: mem_used_percent
        namespace: CWAgent
        statistic: SampleCount
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 3
        datapoints_to_alarm: 3
        comparison: LessThanThreshold
        treat_missing_data: breaching          # <-- the whole point of this alarm
        threshold_by_tier: { dev: 1, test: 1, uat: 1, prod: 1 }
        severity_by_tier:
          dev: digest
          test: digest_and_jira
          uat: jira_and_commercial
          prod: pagerduty
        correlation_required:
          - ec2-status-check-failed == OK      # instance provably alive
          - vpc_flow_logs_active == true       # passing traffic
          - hoop_state != scheduled_down       # not a scheduled turndown
        note: >
          SENTINEL ALARM. mem_used_percent exists only if the CloudWatch agent is
          running. Instance alive + traffic flowing + telemetry silent is the
          agent-killed signature. See design/11-developer-access.md.
          Escalate only if the gap survives the next SSM association run.
        grace_period_seconds: 900

      - id: ec2-instance-age
        metric: derived
        source: config_resource_age
        period_seconds: 86400
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        threshold_by_tier: { uat: 45, prod: 30 }                      # [TUNE]
        unit: Days
        severity_by_tier: { uat: digest_and_jira, prod: digest_and_jira }
        note: >
          Patching posture proxy under the golden-AMI model — instance age is the
          metric, not patch state. See design/09. Never pages.

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AWS::RDS::DBInstance:
    agent_required: false
    alarms:

      - id: rds-cpu-high
        metric: CPUUtilization
        namespace: AWS/RDS
        statistic: Average
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 3
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        unit: Percent
        treat_missing_data: notBreaching
        threshold_by_tier: { dev: 95, test: 95, uat: 85, prod: 80 }   # [DEFAULT]

      - id: rds-connections-high
        metric: DatabaseConnections
        namespace: AWS/RDS
        statistic: Maximum
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 2
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        treat_missing_data: notBreaching
        threshold_mode: percent_of_max_connections                    # [DEFAULT]
        threshold_by_tier: { uat: 80, prod: 80 }
        note: >
          Threshold is a PERCENTAGE of the instance class max_connections, which
          the instrumentation Lambda must resolve at alarm-creation time from the
          parameter group. A fixed number is wrong across instance classes.
        remediation_runbook: rds-high-connections

      - id: rds-free-storage-low
        metric: FreeStorageSpace
        namespace: AWS/RDS
        statistic: Minimum
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 2
        comparison: LessThanThreshold
        unit: Bytes
        treat_missing_data: breaching
        threshold_mode: percent_of_allocated
        threshold_by_tier: { dev: 10, test: 10, uat: 15, prod: 20 }   # [DEFAULT]
        note: Resolve against AllocatedStorage at creation time.

      - id: rds-freeable-memory-low
        metric: FreeableMemory
        namespace: AWS/RDS
        statistic: Minimum
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 3
        comparison: LessThanThreshold
        unit: Bytes
        treat_missing_data: notBreaching
        threshold_mode: percent_of_instance_memory
        threshold_by_tier: { uat: 10, prod: 10 }                      # [TUNE]

      - id: rds-read-replica-lag
        metric: ReplicaLag
        namespace: AWS/RDS
        statistic: Maximum
        period_seconds: 60
        evaluation_periods: 5
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        unit: Seconds
        treat_missing_data: notBreaching
        applies_when: { read_replica: true }
        threshold_by_tier: { uat: 300, prod: 60 }                     # [TUNE]
        note: >
          Prod threshold must be tighter than the tenant's RPO. Default 2h RPO
          makes 60s conservative and appropriate.

      - id: rds-failover-event
        metric: event
        source: rds_event_category
        event_categories: [failover, failure, maintenance, deletion]
        treat_missing_data: notBreaching
        severity_by_tier:
          dev: digest
          test: digest_and_jira
          uat: jira_and_commercial
          prod: pagerduty
        note: EventBridge rule, not a metric alarm.

      - id: rds-auto-restart-detected
        metric: event
        source: rds_event_category
        event_categories: [notification]
        event_message_match: "DB instance started"
        applies_when: { hoop_configured: true, hoop_state: scheduled_down }
        severity_by_tier: { dev: digest, test: digest, uat: digest_and_jira }
        note: >
          THE SEVEN-DAY PROBLEM. AWS auto-starts stopped RDS instances after 7
          days. The scheduler must re-stop and RECORD each occurrence, and the
          cost report must surface it. See design/14-environment-tiers.md.

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AWS::RDS::DBCluster:
    inherits: AWS::RDS::DBInstance
    additional_alarms:
      - id: aurora-volume-bytes-high
        metric: VolumeBytesUsed
        namespace: AWS/RDS
        statistic: Maximum
        period_seconds: 3600
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        threshold_by_tier: { prod: null }                             # [TUNE]
        note: No sensible default — depends entirely on the workload.

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AWS::ECS::Service:
    agent_required: false
    alarms:

      - id: ecs-running-vs-desired
        metric: derived
        source: "RunningTaskCount / DesiredTaskCount"
        namespace: ECS/ContainerInsights
        statistic: Average
        period_seconds: 60
        evaluation_periods: 3
        comparison: LessThanThreshold
        treat_missing_data: breaching
        threshold_by_tier: { dev: 1.0, test: 1.0, uat: 1.0, prod: 1.0 }
        note: >
          Any shortfall is a shortfall. treat_missing_data breaching because a
          service reporting nothing is not a service running fine.
        remediation_runbook: ecs-task-flapping

      - id: ecs-task-restart-rate
        metric: derived
        source: task_stopped_events_per_window
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 2
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        treat_missing_data: notBreaching
        threshold_by_tier: { dev: 10, test: 10, uat: 5, prod: 3 }     # [DEFAULT]
        capture_on_alarm: [stoppedReason, exitCode, taskDefinitionArn]
        note: >
          stoppedReason and exitCode are the ONLY evidence for OOM kills and
          scheduler evictions — the app cannot log its own death. Capture is
          mandatory, and these are visible to developers per design/11.
        remediation_runbook: ecs-task-flapping

      - id: ecs-cpu-high
        metric: CPUUtilization
        namespace: AWS/ECS
        statistic: Average
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 3
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        unit: Percent
        threshold_by_tier: { uat: 85, prod: 80 }                      # [DEFAULT]

      - id: ecs-memory-high
        metric: MemoryUtilization
        namespace: AWS/ECS
        statistic: Average
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 3
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        unit: Percent
        threshold_by_tier: { dev: 95, test: 95, uat: 90, prod: 85 }   # [DEFAULT]
        note: Leading indicator of the OOM kill that ecs-task-restart-rate catches after the fact.

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AWS::Lambda::Function:
    agent_required: false
    alarms:

      - id: lambda-error-rate
        metric: derived
        source: "Errors / Invocations"
        namespace: AWS/Lambda
        statistic: Sum
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 2
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        unit: Percent
        treat_missing_data: notBreaching
        threshold_by_tier: { dev: 25, test: 25, uat: 5, prod: 1 }     # [DEFAULT]
        minimum_invocations: 10
        note: >
          Rate, not count — a count threshold is meaningless across functions
          invoked once a day and ten thousand times a minute. minimum_invocations
          prevents 1-of-1 failures alarming at 100%.
        remediation_runbook: lambda-error-rate

      - id: lambda-throttles
        metric: Throttles
        namespace: AWS/Lambda
        statistic: Sum
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 1
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        threshold_by_tier: { uat: 5, prod: 0 }                        # [DEFAULT]

      - id: lambda-duration-approaching-timeout
        metric: Duration
        namespace: AWS/Lambda
        statistic: p99
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 3
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        unit: Milliseconds
        threshold_mode: percent_of_configured_timeout                 # [DEFAULT]
        threshold_by_tier: { uat: 80, prod: 75 }
        note: Resolve against the function's configured timeout at creation time.

      - id: lambda-dlq-depth
        metric: ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible
        namespace: AWS/SQS
        statistic: Maximum
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 1
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        treat_missing_data: notBreaching
        applies_when: { dlq_configured: true }
        threshold_by_tier: { dev: 10, test: 10, uat: 1, prod: 0 }     # [DEFAULT]

      - id: lambda-concurrent-executions
        metric: ConcurrentExecutions
        namespace: AWS/Lambda
        statistic: Maximum
        period_seconds: 60
        evaluation_periods: 3
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        threshold_mode: percent_of_account_limit
        threshold_by_tier: { prod: 80 }                               # [DEFAULT]

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::LoadBalancer:
    agent_required: false
    alarms:

      - id: alb-5xx-rate
        metric: derived
        source: "HTTPCode_ELB_5XX_Count / RequestCount"
        namespace: AWS/ApplicationELB
        statistic: Sum
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 2
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        unit: Percent
        treat_missing_data: notBreaching
        threshold_by_tier: { dev: 25, test: 25, uat: 5, prod: 1 }     # [DEFAULT]
        minimum_requests: 20
        remediation_runbook: alb-5xx-elevated

      - id: alb-target-5xx-rate
        metric: derived
        source: "HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count / RequestCount"
        namespace: AWS/ApplicationELB
        statistic: Sum
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 2
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        unit: Percent
        threshold_by_tier: { uat: 5, prod: 2 }                        # [DEFAULT]
        note: Distinguishes application failure from load balancer failure.

      - id: alb-target-response-time
        metric: TargetResponseTime
        namespace: AWS/ApplicationELB
        statistic: p99
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 3
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        unit: Seconds
        threshold_by_tier: { uat: null, prod: null }                  # [TUNE]
        threshold_source: questionnaire_7_4
        note: >
          MUST derive from questionnaire field 7.4 (acceptable response time).
          That value is used THREE times: canary timeout, SLA pass condition, and
          this alarm. Do not hardcode. See design/06 "Canaries".

      - id: alb-rejected-connections
        metric: RejectedConnectionCount
        namespace: AWS/ApplicationELB
        statistic: Sum
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 1
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        threshold_by_tier: { uat: 10, prod: 0 }                       # [DEFAULT]

  AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::TargetGroup:
    alarms:
      - id: tg-unhealthy-hosts
        metric: UnHealthyHostCount
        namespace: AWS/ApplicationELB
        statistic: Maximum
        period_seconds: 60
        evaluation_periods: 3
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        treat_missing_data: breaching
        threshold_by_tier: { dev: 0, test: 0, uat: 0, prod: 0 }       # [DEFAULT]

      - id: tg-no-healthy-hosts
        metric: HealthyHostCount
        namespace: AWS/ApplicationELB
        statistic: Minimum
        period_seconds: 60
        evaluation_periods: 2
        comparison: LessThanThreshold
        treat_missing_data: breaching
        threshold_by_tier: { dev: 1, test: 1, uat: 1, prod: 1 }
        severity_by_tier: { uat: pagerduty, prod: pagerduty }
        note: >
          Total outage. Pages even in UAT, overriding the tier default — real
          users are in UAT and a dead environment is a customer-facing failure.

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AWS::S3::Bucket:
    agent_required: false
    alarms:
      - id: s3-5xx-rate
        metric: 5xxErrors
        namespace: AWS/S3
        statistic: Average
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 2
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        unit: Percent
        applies_when: { request_metrics_enabled: true }
        threshold_by_tier: { uat: 1, prod: 1 }                        # [DEFAULT]

      - id: s3-replication-failure
        metric: OperationsFailedReplication
        namespace: AWS/S3
        statistic: Sum
        period_seconds: 900
        evaluation_periods: 1
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        applies_when: { replication_configured: true }
        threshold_by_tier: { uat: 0, prod: 0 }
        note: Load-bearing for cross-region evidence and backup replication.

      - id: s3-public-access-change
        metric: event
        source: cloudtrail
        event_names:
          - PutBucketAcl
          - PutBucketPolicy
          - DeletePublicAccessBlock
          - PutBucketPublicAccessBlock
        severity_by_tier:
          dev: digest_and_jira
          test: digest_and_jira
          uat: pagerduty
          prod: pagerduty
        note: >
          Not a metric alarm. Config auto-remediation reverts; this alarm exists
          so the attempt is visible even when remediation succeeds.

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AWS::DynamoDB::Table:
    alarms:
      - id: ddb-throttled-requests
        metric: ThrottledRequests
        namespace: AWS/DynamoDB
        statistic: Sum
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 2
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        threshold_by_tier: { dev: 100, test: 100, uat: 10, prod: 0 }  # [DEFAULT]

      - id: ddb-system-errors
        metric: SystemErrors
        namespace: AWS/DynamoDB
        statistic: Sum
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 1
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        threshold_by_tier: { uat: 5, prod: 0 }

      - id: ddb-consumed-vs-provisioned
        metric: derived
        source: "ConsumedReadCapacityUnits / ProvisionedReadCapacityUnits"
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 3
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        unit: Percent
        applies_when: { billing_mode: PROVISIONED }
        threshold_by_tier: { uat: 85, prod: 80 }                      # [DEFAULT]

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AWS::SQS::Queue:
    alarms:
      - id: sqs-message-age
        metric: ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage
        namespace: AWS/SQS
        statistic: Maximum
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 2
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        unit: Seconds
        threshold_by_tier: { uat: 3600, prod: 900 }                   # [TUNE]

      - id: sqs-dlq-depth
        metric: ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible
        namespace: AWS/SQS
        statistic: Maximum
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 1
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        applies_when: { is_dlq: true }
        threshold_by_tier: { dev: 10, test: 10, uat: 1, prod: 0 }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AWS::ElastiCache::ReplicationGroup:
    alarms:
      - id: cache-cpu-high
        metric: EngineCPUUtilization
        namespace: AWS/ElastiCache
        statistic: Average
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 3
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        unit: Percent
        threshold_by_tier: { uat: 85, prod: 80 }                      # [DEFAULT]

      - id: cache-evictions
        metric: Evictions
        namespace: AWS/ElastiCache
        statistic: Sum
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 3
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        threshold_by_tier: { uat: 1000, prod: 100 }                   # [TUNE]

      - id: cache-memory-pressure
        metric: DatabaseMemoryUsagePercentage
        namespace: AWS/ElastiCache
        statistic: Average
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 3
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        unit: Percent
        threshold_by_tier: { uat: 90, prod: 85 }                      # [DEFAULT]

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AWS::ApiGateway::RestApi:
    alarms:
      - id: apigw-5xx-rate
        metric: 5XXError
        namespace: AWS/ApiGateway
        statistic: Average
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 2
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        unit: Percent
        threshold_by_tier: { dev: 25, test: 25, uat: 5, prod: 1 }     # [DEFAULT]

      - id: apigw-latency
        metric: Latency
        namespace: AWS/ApiGateway
        statistic: p99
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 3
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        unit: Milliseconds
        threshold_source: questionnaire_7_4                           # [TUNE]
        threshold_by_tier: { uat: null, prod: null }

  AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Api:
    inherits: AWS::ApiGateway::RestApi

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AWS::EFS::FileSystem:
    alarms:
      - id: efs-burst-credit-low
        metric: BurstCreditBalance
        namespace: AWS/EFS
        statistic: Minimum
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 3
        comparison: LessThanThreshold
        applies_when: { throughput_mode: bursting }
        threshold_by_tier: { uat: 1.0e+12, prod: 2.0e+12 }            # [DEFAULT]

      - id: efs-percent-io-limit
        metric: PercentIOLimit
        namespace: AWS/EFS
        statistic: Average
        period_seconds: 300
        evaluation_periods: 3
        comparison: GreaterThanThreshold
        unit: Percent
        threshold_by_tier: { uat: 90, prod: 85 }                      # [DEFAULT]

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup:
    alarms:
      - id: asg-in-service-below-desired
        metric: GroupInServiceInstances
        namespace: AWS/AutoScaling
        statistic: Minimum
        period_seconds: 60
        evaluation_periods: 5
        comparison: LessThanThreshold
        treat_missing_data: breaching
        threshold_mode: reference_metric
        threshold_reference: GroupDesiredCapacity
        threshold_by_tier: { dev: 1.0, test: 1.0, uat: 1.0, prod: 1.0 }
        note: >
          Must not fire during a HOOP turndown, when desired is deliberately 0.
          respect_hoop_suppression handles this — verify it.

      - id: asg-failed-scaling
        metric: event
        source: autoscaling_event
        event_types: [EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE_ERROR]
        severity_by_tier: { uat: jira_and_commercial, prod: pagerduty }

# =============================================================================
# CROSS-CUTTING: telemetry gap detection
# Source: design/11-developer-access.md
# =============================================================================
telemetry_gap:
  sentinel_metric: { namespace: CWAgent, metric: mem_used_percent }
  log_stream_staleness:
    check_interval_seconds: 900
    stale_after_seconds_by_tier: { dev: 86400, test: 86400, uat: 7200, prod: 3600 }
    note: >
      CloudWatch Logs does not alarm on absence natively. This is a scheduled
      check against lastIngestionTime per EXPECTED stream. Absence is only
      detectable against a declared expectation — the expectation registry is
      populated by this instrumentation layer.
  discriminator:
    agent_killed:
      status_checks: passing
      flow_logs: traffic_present
      ssm_ping: any
      cw_telemetry: silent
      hoop_state: not_scheduled_down
  grace_period_seconds: 900
  escalate_if_survives: next_ssm_association_run
  ssh_inbound_detection:
    enabled: true
    note: >
      There is no SSH path in this architecture. Inbound on 22 in flow logs is a
      finding in its own right, independent of telemetry.
    severity_by_tier: { dev: digest_and_jira, test: digest_and_jira, uat: pagerduty, prod: pagerduty }

# =============================================================================
# CROSS-CUTTING: safety rails (framework-level, not per-alarm)
# Source: design/07-response-automation.md
# =============================================================================
safety_rails:
  circuit_breaker: { same_remediation_count: 3, window_seconds: 3600, action: stop_and_page }
  rate_limit: { max_automated_actions_per_account_per_hour: 20 }
  stage_3_requires_redundancy_check: true
  stage_3_one_resource_at_a_time: true
  kill_switch: { per_account: true, global: true, requires_deployment: false }
  every_action_emits_change_record: true

# =============================================================================
# EXCEPTION HANDLING — prompt 4.1
# =============================================================================
exceptions:
  unrecognised_resource_type:
    action: create_exception_record
    never: silent_no_op
    surfaces_in: [instrumentation_digest, platform_health_report]
  agent_not_installed:
    action: create_exception_record
    also: trigger_ssm_association
  threshold_unset:
    action: create_exception_record
    note: >
      A [TUNE] threshold of null means the alarm cannot be created. That is an
      exception, not a skip — it must appear in the digest as pending.
  metric_not_available:
    action: create_exception_record
    note: e.g. S3 request metrics not enabled on the bucket.
files.evidence/10-evidence.yaml:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  AltDigital Managed Platform — the evidence pipeline to Truveon (prompt 9.1).
  Collects the four categories design 04 names, numbers them per tenant stream,
  buffers them, delivers them, and proves nothing was silently dropped. Deploys
  to the Audit account.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The completeness controls are the stack
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# design/04-security-controls-and-evidence.md:
#
#     Because we push, we must prove nothing was silently dropped.
#     [...] A silently failed pipeline that looks like a clean month is the
#     failure mode that destroys an audit. This is the control that prevents it.
#
# Each of design 04's four controls is a named resource here:
#
#   sequence numbering   SequenceTable, allocated on INGEST (see record.py)
#   heartbeat            HeartbeatSchedule
#   buffering            EvidenceQueue, with a DLQ and 14-day retention
#   reconciliation       CountReconciliationSchedule
#
# And a fifth that design 04 does not name but the other four require:
#
#   replay               ReplaySchedule
#
# Without replay, the gap detector finds a hole, reports it correctly, and
# nobody can fill it. A detection with no remedy is half a control.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The ledger is the record. The queue is transport.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A message leaves the queue when the sender takes it, delivered or not. So the
# queue cannot be what remembers that evidence is owed — the LedgerTable is,
# and the replay schedule is what reads it back.
#
# This matters more than it sounds. It is what makes "a Truveon outage delays
# delivery rather than losing it" true for outages longer than the queue's
# retention, and it is why the pipeline can be deployed today with no Truveon
# at all: records accumulate as pending, and drain when an endpoint exists.
# B-088.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# This pipeline is itself in SOC 2 scope
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# design 15 puts "evidence pipeline" inside AltDigital's own reference report,
# which partners rely on through the carve-out. design 04 does not mention it.
#
# So the completeness results are written as evidence in their own right rather
# than only alerted — a Type II auditor asks whether a control operated
# THROUGHOUT the period, and an alert that fired once proves nothing about the
# months either side of it. D-016.

Parameters:

  ArtifactBucket:
    Type: String

  ArtifactKey:
    Type: String

  AlertBusName:
    Type: String
    Default: platform-alerts
    Description: >-
      The organization event bus. Every evidence category already arrives here
      from member accounts; this stack recognises and numbers it rather than
      producing anything new.

  TruveonEndpoint:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      Base URL of the Truveon ingestion API, e.g. https://truveon.example.

      EMPTY IS A SUPPORTED STATE and is the current one. The sender does not
      mark records delivered when it has nowhere to deliver them — they stay
      pending, the pipeline reports that it is not delivering, and the backlog
      drains when an endpoint appears. A stub that acknowledged locally would
      reproduce design 04's "clean month" inside the thing built to prevent it.
      B-088.

  TruveonSecretName:
    Type: String
    Default: platform/truveon/ingest
    Description: >-
      Bearer token for the ingestion API. One credential for all tenants: the
      record's `tenant` field carries the isolation and Truveon enforces it.
      Per-tenant credentials would mean N secrets to rotate, with the failure
      mode that one expires quietly and that tenant's evidence stops while
      every other tenant looks fine.

  TenantMapParam:
    Type: String
    Default: /platform/evidence/tenants
    Description: >-
      Tenants, their partners and their account ids. Partner and tenant travel
      ON each record rather than being derived at query time, because an
      account can be re-parented and evidence about March must not change in
      September. D-016.

  InflightGraceMinutes:
    Type: Number
    Default: 60
    Description: >-
      How long a record may sit undelivered before its absence counts as a gap
      rather than as in-flight. Shared by the gap detector and the replay, which
      must agree: replaying earlier than this is wasted work, and reporting a
      gap earlier raises a finding against something already being fixed.

      Generous rather than tight. A gap reported an hour late is still
      reported; a control nobody trusts is not. B-043, B-081.

  HeartbeatSchedule:
    Type: String
    Default: 'rate(1 hour)'

  GapScanSchedule:
    Type: String
    Default: 'rate(1 hour)'

  ReplaySchedule:
    Type: String
    Default: 'rate(1 hour)'

  ReconcileSchedule:
    Type: String
    Default: 'rate(12 hours)'

  LogsKeyArn:
    Type: String
    Default: ''

Conditions:

  UseDefaultLogsKey: !Equals [!Ref LogsKeyArn, '']
  HasEndpoint: !Not [!Equals [!Ref TruveonEndpoint, '']]

Resources:

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # State
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

  SequenceTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    # Retain. Losing the counters would restart every stream at 1, which makes
    # every previously delivered record look like a duplicate and every future
    # gap uncomputable. The sequence is the only thing that makes absence
    # provable.
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      TableName: platform-evidence-sequence
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - { AttributeName: stream_id, AttributeType: S }
      KeySchema:
        - { AttributeName: stream_id, KeyType: HASH }
      PointInTimeRecoverySpecification:
        PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled: true
      SSESpecification:
        SSEEnabled: true

  LedgerTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    # Retain, emphatically. This is the platform's own copy of what it owes
    # Truveon and what it has delivered. It is the answer to "how do you know
    # nothing was dropped", which is the question design 04 exists to answer.
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      TableName: platform-evidence-ledger
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - { AttributeName: PK, AttributeType: S }
        - { AttributeName: SK, AttributeType: S }
      KeySchema:
        # PK is the stream, SK is the zero-padded sequence. Padded so lexical
        # order IS numeric order: without it sequence 9 sorts after 10 and a
        # range query returns nonsense.
        - { AttributeName: PK, KeyType: HASH }
        - { AttributeName: SK, KeyType: RANGE }
      PointInTimeRecoverySpecification:
        PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled: true
      SSESpecification:
        SSEEnabled: true

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Buffer. design 04's third completeness control.
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

  EvidenceDlq:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    # Delete, explicitly, and it is safe for the same reason the main queue is.
    # A message here has a pending ledger row behind it; losing the message
    # loses a diagnostic copy, not the evidence.
    DeletionPolicy: Delete
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Delete
    Properties:
      QueueName: platform-evidence-dlq
      # 14 days, the maximum. A message here is evidence that could not be
      # delivered after every retry, and the ledger row behind it stays pending
      # and keeps being reported as a gap — so the DLQ is a diagnostic aid
      # rather than the last line of defence.
      MessageRetentionPeriod: 1209600
      SqsManagedSseEnabled: true

  EvidenceQueue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    # Delete rather than Retain, deliberately.
    #
    # Retain looks like the cautious choice and would be the wrong one. The
    # queue is transport; the LEDGER is the record of what is owed. Every
    # message in here has a pending ledger row behind it, so destroying the
    # queue destroys a copy and not the evidence -- the replay schedule
    # re-queues anything still pending on its next run.
    #
    # Retaining it would leave an orphaned queue after a stack replacement,
    # holding messages nothing consumes, while the replay quietly refills a new
    # one. Two queues, one consumer, and a pile of duplicates that only look
    # harmless because ingest happens to be idempotent.
    DeletionPolicy: Delete
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Delete
    Properties:
      QueueName: platform-evidence
      MessageRetentionPeriod: 1209600
      # Longer than the sender's FUNCTION timeout (300s), not than its HTTP
      # timeout. If visibility expired first, SQS would hand the same batch to
      # a second invocation while the first was still working on it -- two
      # senders posting the same records concurrently.
      #
      # Harmless for correctness, because ingest is idempotent on
      # (stream_id, sequence), and wasteful and confusing in the logs. cfn-lint
      # catches this; it was set to 180 against the 20s HTTP timeout, which is
      # the wrong one of the two to reason from.
      VisibilityTimeout: 360
      SqsManagedSseEnabled: true
      RedrivePolicy:
        deadLetterTargetArn: !GetAtt EvidenceDlq.Arn
        # Generous. Truveon being down is the expected reason for failure and
        # is not the message's fault; the replay schedule re-queues anything
        # that lands in the DLQ anyway, because the ledger still says it is
        # owed.
        maxReceiveCount: 10

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Collection
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

  CollectRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: PlatformEvidenceCollect
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: lambda.amazonaws.com }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole'

  CollectPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: NumberAndBufferEvidence
      Roles: [!Ref CollectRole]
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllocateSequenceNumbers
            Effect: Allow
            Action: dynamodb:UpdateItem
            Resource: !GetAtt SequenceTable.Arn
          # PutItem only. The collector records that evidence is owed; it must
          # not be able to mark anything delivered, which is the sender's job
          # and the thing that stops the gap detector looking.
          - Sid: AppendToLedger
            Effect: Allow
            Action: dynamodb:PutItem
            Resource: !GetAtt LedgerTable.Arn
          - Sid: Buffer
            Effect: Allow
            Action: sqs:SendMessage
            Resource: !GetAtt EvidenceQueue.Arn
          - Sid: ReadTenantMap
            Effect: Allow
            Action: ssm:GetParameter
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:parameter${TenantMapParam}'
          - Sid: ReportCollectionProblems
            Effect: Allow
            Action: events:PutEvents
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:events:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:event-bus/${AlertBusName}'

  CollectLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /aws/lambda/platform-evidence-collect
      RetentionInDays: 2557
      KmsKeyId: !If
        - UseDefaultLogsKey
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:kms:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:alias/platform-logs'
        - !Ref LogsKeyArn

  CollectFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    DependsOn: CollectLogGroup
    Properties:
      FunctionName: platform-evidence-collect
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: collect.handler
      Role: !GetAtt CollectRole.Arn
      Timeout: 30
      MemorySize: 256
      Code:
        S3Bucket: !Ref ArtifactBucket
        S3Key: !Ref ArtifactKey
      Environment:
        Variables:
          EVIDENCE_SEQUENCE_TABLE: !Ref SequenceTable
          EVIDENCE_LEDGER_TABLE: !Ref LedgerTable
          EVIDENCE_QUEUE_URL: !Ref EvidenceQueue
          EVIDENCE_TENANT_MAP_PARAM: !Ref TenantMapParam
          ALERT_BUS_NAME: !Ref AlertBusName

  # design 04's four categories, as they arrive on the bus. Deliberately
  # enumerated rather than matched by a wildcard: a pattern broad enough to
  # catch everything would also number things that are not evidence, and the
  # sequence would then include records no auditor recognises.
  EvidenceCollectionRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: platform-collect-evidence
      EventBusName: !Ref AlertBusName
      Description: 'The four categories design 04 names, plus quorum outcomes.'
      EventPattern:
        source:
          - aws.config
          - aws.securityhub
          - aws.guardduty
          - platform.change
          - platform.quorum
          - platform.response
          - platform.security
          - platform.recovery
          - platform.exercise
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Id: collect
          Arn: !GetAtt CollectFunction.Arn

  CollectPermission:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Permission
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !GetAtt CollectFunction.Arn
      Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
      Principal: events.amazonaws.com
      SourceArn: !GetAtt EvidenceCollectionRule.Arn

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Delivery
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

  SenderRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: PlatformEvidenceSender
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: lambda.amazonaws.com }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole'

  SenderPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: DeliverEvidence
      Roles: [!Ref SenderRole]
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          # UpdateItem to mark delivered, Scan and SendMessage for replay.
          #
          # No DeleteItem. A delivered row and a pending row are both evidence
          # of what the pipeline did; a component that could remove either
          # could erase the trace of a record it failed to deliver.
          - Sid: MarkDeliveredAndReplay
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - dynamodb:UpdateItem
              - dynamodb:Scan
            Resource: !GetAtt LedgerTable.Arn
          - Sid: DrainAndRequeue
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - sqs:ReceiveMessage
              - sqs:DeleteMessage
              - sqs:GetQueueAttributes
              - sqs:SendMessage
            Resource: !GetAtt EvidenceQueue.Arn
          - Sid: ReadTruveonCredential
            Effect: Allow
            Action: secretsmanager:GetSecretValue
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:secretsmanager:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:secret:${TruveonSecretName}-*'
          - Sid: ReportDeliveryProblems
            Effect: Allow
            Action: events:PutEvents
