            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:events:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:event-bus/${AlertBusName}'

  SenderLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /aws/lambda/platform-evidence-sender
      RetentionInDays: 2557
      KmsKeyId: !If
        - UseDefaultLogsKey
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:kms:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:alias/platform-logs'
        - !Ref LogsKeyArn

  SenderFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    DependsOn: SenderLogGroup
    Properties:
      FunctionName: platform-evidence-sender
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: sender.handler
      Role: !GetAtt SenderRole.Arn
      Timeout: 300
      MemorySize: 256
      Code:
        S3Bucket: !Ref ArtifactBucket
        S3Key: !Ref ArtifactKey
      Environment:
        Variables:
          EVIDENCE_LEDGER_TABLE: !Ref LedgerTable
          EVIDENCE_QUEUE_URL: !Ref EvidenceQueue
          EVIDENCE_INFLIGHT_GRACE_MINUTES: !Ref InflightGraceMinutes
          TRUVEON_ENDPOINT: !Ref TruveonEndpoint
          TRUVEON_SECRET_NAME: !Ref TruveonSecretName
          ALERT_BUS_NAME: !Ref AlertBusName

  SenderQueueSource:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::EventSourceMapping
    Properties:
      EventSourceArn: !GetAtt EvidenceQueue.Arn
      FunctionName: !GetAtt SenderFunction.Arn
      BatchSize: 10
      # Only the failed records redrive. Failing a whole batch would delay
      # every healthy record behind one poisoned one — harmless for
      # correctness, because ingest is idempotent, but slow for no reason.
      FunctionResponseTypes: [ReportBatchItemFailures]

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Completeness
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

  CompletenessRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: PlatformEvidenceCompleteness
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: lambda.amazonaws.com }
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole'

  CompletenessPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: ProveNothingWasDropped
      Roles: [!Ref CompletenessRole]
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllocateSequenceNumbers
            Effect: Allow
            Action: dynamodb:UpdateItem
            Resource: !GetAtt SequenceTable.Arn
          # Query and PutItem: reads the ledger to find gaps, and writes its
          # own findings back as evidence. No UpdateItem on the ledger — the
          # component that decides whether records are missing must not be able
          # to mark one delivered.
          - Sid: ReadLedgerAndRecordFindings
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - dynamodb:Query
              - dynamodb:PutItem
            Resource: !GetAtt LedgerTable.Arn
          - Sid: ReadTenantMap
            Effect: Allow
            Action: ssm:GetParameter
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:parameter${TenantMapParam}'
          - Sid: ReadTruveonCredential
            Effect: Allow
            Action: secretsmanager:GetSecretValue
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:secretsmanager:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:secret:${TruveonSecretName}-*'
          - Sid: ReportFindings
            Effect: Allow
            Action: events:PutEvents
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:events:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:event-bus/${AlertBusName}'

  CompletenessLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /aws/lambda/platform-evidence-completeness
      RetentionInDays: 2557
      KmsKeyId: !If
        - UseDefaultLogsKey
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:kms:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:alias/platform-logs'
        - !Ref LogsKeyArn

  CompletenessFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    DependsOn: CompletenessLogGroup
    Properties:
      FunctionName: platform-evidence-completeness
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: completeness.handler
      Role: !GetAtt CompletenessRole.Arn
      Timeout: 600
      MemorySize: 512
      Code:
        S3Bucket: !Ref ArtifactBucket
        S3Key: !Ref ArtifactKey
      Environment:
        Variables:
          EVIDENCE_SEQUENCE_TABLE: !Ref SequenceTable
          EVIDENCE_LEDGER_TABLE: !Ref LedgerTable
          EVIDENCE_TENANT_MAP_PARAM: !Ref TenantMapParam
          EVIDENCE_INFLIGHT_GRACE_MINUTES: !Ref InflightGraceMinutes
          TRUVEON_ENDPOINT: !Ref TruveonEndpoint
          TRUVEON_SECRET_NAME: !Ref TruveonSecretName
          ALERT_BUS_NAME: !Ref AlertBusName

  # design 04's second control. One record per tenant per run, so that silence
  # is readable: a live heartbeat with no other evidence is a quiet tenant, and
  # an absent heartbeat is a stopped pipeline. Without it the two are identical.
  HeartbeatRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: platform-evidence-heartbeat
      ScheduleExpression: !Ref HeartbeatSchedule
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Id: heartbeat
          Arn: !GetAtt CompletenessFunction.Arn
          Input: '{"action": "heartbeat"}'

  GapScanRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: platform-evidence-gap-scan
      ScheduleExpression: !Ref GapScanSchedule
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Id: gaps
          Arn: !GetAtt CompletenessFunction.Arn
          Input: '{"action": "detect_gaps"}'

  ReconcileRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: platform-evidence-count-reconciliation
      ScheduleExpression: !Ref ReconcileSchedule
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Id: reconcile
          Arn: !GetAtt CompletenessFunction.Arn
          Input: '{"action": "reconcile_counts"}'

  CompletenessPermission:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Permission
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !GetAtt CompletenessFunction.Arn
      Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
      Principal: events.amazonaws.com
      SourceAccount: !Ref AWS::AccountId

  # The remedy for what the gap scan detects. See the header: a detection with
  # no remedy is half a control.
  ReplayRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: platform-evidence-replay
      ScheduleExpression: !Ref ReplaySchedule
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Id: replay
          Arn: !GetAtt SenderFunction.Arn
          Input: '{"action": "replay_pending"}'

  ReplayPermission:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Permission
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !GetAtt SenderFunction.Arn
      Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
      Principal: events.amazonaws.com
      SourceArn: !GetAtt ReplayRule.Arn

Outputs:

  EvidenceQueueUrl:
    Description: The buffer. design 04's third completeness control.
    Value: !Ref EvidenceQueue

  LedgerTableName:
    Description: What the platform owes Truveon and what it has delivered.
    Value: !Ref LedgerTable

  SequenceTableName:
    Description: Per-stream counters. Losing these makes absence unprovable.
    Value: !Ref SequenceTable

  Delivering:
    Description: >-
      Whether an endpoint is configured. 'false' means evidence is being
      collected and numbered but not delivered — records accumulate as pending
      and drain when an endpoint appears. B-088.
    Value: !If
      - HasEndpoint
      - 'true'
      - 'false - collecting and numbering, not delivering (B-088)'
files.identity/00-commercial-readonly.yaml:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  AltDigital Managed Platform — CommercialReadOnly permission set.
  Billing and cost data only, for the commercial function (design doc 12).
  Assigned to an Identity Center GROUP, never to a user. Grants no access to
  any member account and no read of any operational telemetry.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Scope, and why this is not "read-only everywhere plus billing"
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Design doc 12 is explicit: this grant is billing only. Cost data reveals that
# an account exists and roughly what shape it is; it reveals nothing about its
# contents. That is the correct exposure for a commercial function and it is
# what the deny statements below enforce.
#
# The assignment targets ONE account. Identity Center assignments are
# per-account, so "no member account access of any kind" is achieved by never
# assigning this permission set anywhere else — not by policy. Whoever reviews
# this template should read the Assignment resource as the real boundary and
# the deny statements as defence in depth.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why the deny statements carry the weight here
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The target is the Organization MANAGEMENT account. SCPs do not apply to the
# management account — that is an AWS property, not a configuration choice. So
# there is no outer guardrail behind this permission set. Its own inline policy
# is the entire boundary, which is why the denies are constructed to hold even
# if the attached AWS managed policy grows new actions later.
#
# Two layers, deliberately:
#
#   1. DenyOutsideBillingDomain — a NotAction deny. Anything whose service
#      prefix is not in the billing domain is denied outright, regardless of
#      what any Allow grants. This is what makes "no CloudWatch, no logs, no
#      Config, no Security Hub, no GuardDuty" true by construction rather than
#      by enumeration. An enumerated deny list is incomplete the day AWS ships
#      a new service.
#
#   2. DenyWritesWithinBillingDomain — layer 1 permits the billing services to
#      be reached at all, so writes inside those services still need denying.
#      Enumerated by verb prefix per service, because there is no valid IAM
#      syntax for "any action that is not a Get/List/Describe".
#
# AWSBillingReadOnlyAccess is attached as the base grant. It is maintained by
# AWS and picks up new read actions as billing services evolve, which is worth
# more than a frozen hand-written list. Layer 1 is what makes trusting it safe:
# if AWS ever adds a non-billing action to it, the deny still holds.

Parameters:

  InstanceArn:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      IAM Identity Center instance ARN. Resolved at deploy time by
      scripts/deploy-commercial-access.sh from sso-admin:ListInstances and
      published to /platform/identity/instance-arn.
    AllowedPattern: '^arn:aws[a-zA-Z-]*:sso:::instance/(sso)?ins-[0-9a-f]{16}$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be an Identity Center instance ARN.

  GroupId:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Identity store group id for the CommercialReadOnly group. The group is
      NOT created here on purpose — see the note on the Assignment resource.
    AllowedPattern: '^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be an identity store group id (UUID form).

  TargetAccountId:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Account the permission set is assigned to. Currently the Organization
      management account, which is deviation D-009 — the aggregation layer that
      should hold this does not exist yet.
    AllowedPattern: '^[0-9]{12}$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be a 12-digit AWS account id.

  SsmPrefix:
    Type: String
    Default: /platform
    Description: SSM Parameter Store namespace for published platform facts.
    AllowedPattern: '^/[a-zA-Z0-9._/-]+$'

Resources:

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # CommercialReadOnly
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  CommercialReadOnlyPermissionSet:
    Type: AWS::SSO::PermissionSet
    Properties:
      Name: CommercialReadOnly
      Description: >-
        Billing and cost data only. No member account access, no operational
        telemetry, no write actions anywhere. Design doc 12.
      InstanceArn: !Ref InstanceArn

      # Four hours, not the one hour PlatformBootstrapAdmin uses. This role is
      # read-only over a single data domain and cannot change anything, so the
      # re-authentication tax buys much less here than it does on an admin
      # role — a month-end close should not need six sign-ins.
      #
      # Literal rather than a parameter on purpose. cfn-guard evaluates the
      # template statically and cannot resolve a !Ref, so a parameterised
      # duration would pass SSO_PERMISSION_SET_SESSION_DURATION_BOUNDED by
      # being unreadable rather than by being correct. A parameter with
      # AllowedValues would enforce it at deploy time, but only the literal
      # also enforces it at review time, which is where it matters.
      SessionDuration: PT4H

      # Drops the portal straight into Cost Management rather than the generic
      # console home. The Cost Explorer and Billing consoles are served from
      # us-east-1 regardless of the platform home region.
      RelayStateType: 'https://us-east-1.console.aws.amazon.com/costmanagement/home#/home'

      ManagedPolicies:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AWSBillingReadOnlyAccess

      InlinePolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:

          # -----------------------------------------------------------------
          # What AWSBillingReadOnlyAccess does not cover
          # -----------------------------------------------------------------
          # Checked against version v28 of that policy on 2026-09-16. It is
          # strong on the Billing console — invoices, credits, tax, payments,
          # purchase orders — and thin on Cost Explorer's analytical surface.
          # Everything below is absent from it.
          - Sid: CostExplorerAnalysisAndForecasts
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              # Forecasting. The reason this statement exists at all: the
              # managed policy grants GetCostAndUsage but not either forecast
              # call, so Cost Explorer renders history and fails on the
              # forward-looking view, which is the half the commercial
              # function actually needs.
              - ce:GetCostForecast
              - ce:GetUsageForecast
              # Remaining Cost Explorer reads
              - ce:GetApproximateUsageRecords
              - ce:GetCostAndUsageWithResources
              - ce:GetCostCategories
              - ce:GetPreferences
              # Anomaly detection — feeds the cost-anomaly event in doc 12
              - ce:GetAnomalies
              - ce:GetAnomalyMonitors
              - ce:GetAnomalySubscriptions
              # Commitment reporting (Savings Plans, Reserved Instances)
              - ce:GetReservationCoverage
              - ce:GetReservationPurchaseRecommendation
              - ce:GetReservationUtilization
              - ce:GetRightsizingRecommendation
              - ce:GetSavingsPlanPurchaseRecommendationDetails
              - ce:GetSavingsPlansCoverage
              - ce:GetSavingsPlansPurchaseRecommendation
              - ce:GetSavingsPlansUtilization
              - ce:GetSavingsPlansUtilizationDetails
              - ce:ListSavingsPlansPurchaseRecommendationGeneration
              - savingsplans:DescribeSavingsPlanRates
              - savingsplans:DescribeSavingsPlans
              - savingsplans:DescribeSavingsPlansOfferingRates
              - savingsplans:DescribeSavingsPlansOfferings
              - savingsplans:ListTagsForResource
              # Cost Optimization Hub
              - cost-optimization-hub:GetPreferences
              - cost-optimization-hub:GetRecommendation
              - cost-optimization-hub:ListEnrollmentStatuses
              - cost-optimization-hub:ListRecommendationSummaries
              - cost-optimization-hub:ListRecommendations
              # Data Exports — the modern CUR API. The export itself does not
              # exist yet (phase 11.1); this is here so that when it lands the
              # permission set does not need reopening.
              - bcm-data-exports:GetExecution
              - bcm-data-exports:GetExport
              - bcm-data-exports:GetTable
              - bcm-data-exports:ListExecutions
              - bcm-data-exports:ListExports
              - bcm-data-exports:ListTables
              - bcm-data-exports:ListTagsForResource
              # Public price list, for modelling uplift against list price
              - pricing:DescribeServices
              - pricing:GetAttributeValues
              - pricing:GetPriceListFileUrl
              - pricing:GetProducts
              - pricing:ListPriceLists
            Resource: '*'

          # -----------------------------------------------------------------
          # Organization structure, read only
          # -----------------------------------------------------------------
          # Without this, every Cost Explorer row is a bare 12-digit account id
          # and the by-partner / by-client roll-ups are unreadable. This is a
          # real widening: it exposes the account and OU tree, which is the
          # client roster. That is accepted — a commercial function that cannot
          # see which clients it is billing for is not a commercial function.
          # It exposes names and structure only, never contents.
          - Sid: OrganizationStructureRead
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - organizations:DescribeAccount
              - organizations:DescribeOrganization
              - organizations:DescribeOrganizationalUnit
              - organizations:ListAccounts
              - organizations:ListAccountsForParent
              - organizations:ListOrganizationalUnitsForParent
              - organizations:ListParents
              - organizations:ListRoots
              - organizations:ListTagsForResource
            Resource: '*'

          # Console chrome. Without GetCallerIdentity and ListAccountAliases
          # the console header renders an error banner on every page, which
          # trains people to ignore error banners.
          - Sid: ConsoleIdentityChrome
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - iam:ListAccountAliases
              - sts:GetCallerIdentity
            Resource: '*'

          # -----------------------------------------------------------------
          # Layer 1 — nothing outside the billing domain
          # -----------------------------------------------------------------
          # NotAction, so the list below is the complete set of service
          # prefixes this role can reach. Everything else is denied: EC2, S3,
          # RDS, CloudWatch, CloudTrail, Config, Security Hub, GuardDuty, KMS,
          # Secrets Manager, SSM, Lambda, Step Functions, Identity Center,
          # IAM beyond the one chrome call, and every service AWS has not
          # launched yet.
          #
          # Wildcards are used per service on purpose. Layer 2 removes the
          # writes; keeping layer 1 at service granularity means a new READ
          # action in a billing service works on the day it ships instead of
          # producing a support request that resolves to "add one action".
          - Sid: DenyOutsideBillingDomain
            Effect: Deny
            NotAction:
              - account:GetAccountInformation
              - aws-portal:*
              - bcm-data-exports:*
              - billing:*
              - budgets:*
              - ce:*
              - consolidatedbilling:*
              - cost-optimization-hub:*
              - cur:*
              - freetier:*
              - iam:ListAccountAliases
              - invoicing:*
              - mapcredits:*
              - organizations:Describe*
              - organizations:List*
              - payments:*
              - pricing:*
              - purchase-orders:*
              - savingsplans:*
              - sts:GetCallerIdentity
              - sustainability:*
              - tax:*
            Resource: '*'

          # -----------------------------------------------------------------
          # Layer 2 — no writes inside the billing domain either
          # -----------------------------------------------------------------
          # Enumerated by verb prefix per service. IAM has no syntax for "every
          # action that is not a read", so this is the honest construction:
          # explicit, greppable, and reviewable against the AWS action tables.
          #
          # Includes tagging. Tag and untag look harmless and are not — Cost
          # Categories and cost allocation tags are the mechanism the whole
          # billing model rests on, so a tag change is a billing change.
          - Sid: DenyWritesWithinBillingDomain
            Effect: Deny
            Action:
              - account:Accept*
              - account:Delete*
              - account:Disable*
              - account:Enable*
              - account:Put*
              - account:Start*
              - aws-portal:Modify*
              - bcm-data-exports:Create*
              - bcm-data-exports:Delete*
              - bcm-data-exports:Tag*
              - bcm-data-exports:Untag*
              - bcm-data-exports:Update*
              - billing:Create*
              - billing:Delete*
              - billing:Put*
              - billing:Redeem*
              - billing:Tag*
              - billing:Untag*
              - billing:Update*
              - budgets:Create*
              - budgets:Delete*
              - budgets:Execute*
              - budgets:Modify*
              - budgets:Update*
              - ce:Create*
              - ce:Delete*
              - ce:Provide*
              - ce:Start*
              - ce:Tag*
              - ce:Untag*
              - ce:Update*
              - cost-optimization-hub:Update*
              - cur:Delete*
              - cur:Modify*
              - cur:Put*
              - cur:Tag*
              - cur:Untag*
              - freetier:Put*
              - freetier:Upgrade*
              - invoicing:Create*
              - invoicing:Delete*
              - invoicing:Put*
              - invoicing:Tag*
              - invoicing:Untag*
              - invoicing:Update*
              # Accept* is not a verb prefix used elsewhere in this list. It is
              # here because payments:AcceptFinancingApplicationTerms is a
              # write that none of the usual prefixes catch — the kind of thing
              # enumerating by verb misses, which is why cfn-lint's action-name
              # check is load-bearing here rather than cosmetic.
              - payments:Accept*
              - payments:Create*
              - payments:Delete*
              - payments:Make*
              - payments:Tag*
              - payments:Untag*
              - payments:Update*
              - purchase-orders:Add*
              - purchase-orders:Delete*
              - purchase-orders:Modify*
              - purchase-orders:Tag*
              - purchase-orders:Untag*
              - purchase-orders:Update*
              - savingsplans:Create*
              - savingsplans:Delete*
              - savingsplans:Return*
              - savingsplans:Tag*
              - savingsplans:Untag*
              - tax:Batch*
              - tax:Delete*
              - tax:Put*
              - tax:Update*
            Resource: '*'

      Tags:
        - { Key: platform-managed, Value: 'true' }
        - { Key: Purpose,          Value: commercial-billing-readonly }
        - { Key: DesignDoc,        Value: '12' }

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Assignment — to a GROUP, never to a user
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Design doc 03: "Permission sets are defined centrally and assigned to Entra
  # groups; access is granted by group membership, never per-account
  # configuration." Group membership is the only lever; joiners and leavers are
  # one change in one place.
  #
  # The group is NOT an AWS::IdentityStore::Group resource in this template,
  # and that is deliberate. The identity source is still the built-in Identity
  # Center directory. Switching it to Entra deletes every directory user and
  # group, which would leave a CloudFormation resource pointing at something
  # that no longer exists and a stack that fails on its next update. Taking the
  # group id as a parameter means this template is unchanged across that
  # cutover: before it, the deploy script creates the group; after it, SCIM
  # does, and only the parameter value differs.
  #
  # Membership is likewise not in CloudFormation. It is personal data, and the
  # repository holds none — see config/identity.env.
  CommercialReadOnlyAssignment:
    Type: AWS::SSO::Assignment
    Properties:
      InstanceArn: !Ref InstanceArn
      PermissionSetArn: !GetAtt CommercialReadOnlyPermissionSet.PermissionSetArn
      PrincipalType: GROUP
      PrincipalId: !Ref GroupId
      TargetType: AWS_ACCOUNT
      TargetId: !Ref TargetAccountId

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Published facts
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  PermissionSetArnParam:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${SsmPrefix}/identity/permission-set/commercial-readonly'
      Type: String
      Value: !GetAtt CommercialReadOnlyPermissionSet.PermissionSetArn
      Description: CommercialReadOnly permission set ARN
      Tags: { platform-managed: 'true' }

  AssignedAccountParam:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${SsmPrefix}/identity/permission-set/commercial-readonly/account'
      Type: String
      Value: !Ref TargetAccountId
      Description: >-
        Account CommercialReadOnly is assigned to. Deviation D-009 while this
        is the management account.
      Tags: { platform-managed: 'true' }

Outputs:

  PermissionSetArn:
    Description: CommercialReadOnly permission set ARN
    Value: !GetAtt CommercialReadOnlyPermissionSet.PermissionSetArn

  GroupId:
    Description: Identity store group the permission set is assigned to
    Value: !Ref GroupId

  TargetAccountId:
    Description: Account the permission set is assigned to
    Value: !Ref TargetAccountId
files.identity/10-developer-access.yaml:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  AltDigital Managed Platform — developer permission sets (prompt 10.1).
  design 11's Layer 3, three grants across the environment gradient. Deployed to
  the Identity Center delegated administrator.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Three sets in one template, because the GRADIENT is the thing being reviewed
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# design/11-developer-access.md's table is the specification:
#
#              dev            test           uat        prod
#   console    full           read + ops     read       read + observe
#   create     yes            pipeline       pipeline   pipeline
#   IAM roles  yes, bounded   no             no         no
#
# Split across three files, a reviewer checks each against the table. Together,
# they check each against EACH OTHER, which is where the mistakes are — a grant
# that appears in prod and not in dev is almost always wrong, and is invisible
# when the two are in different files.
#
# UAT uses the prod set. design 11: "UAT is treated as production for access
# purposes, because it holds real data."
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The production grant is deliberately WIDER than logs
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# design 11 argues against its own first instinct at length, and the argument
# is worth keeping next to the policy:
#
#     It fails where it matters most. The failure modes where an application
#     CANNOT log: OOM kill (process is gone), task evicted by the scheduler,
#     health check failing before startup completed, container exiting on a
#     non-zero code. The ECS stopped reason and exit code are the entire story,
#     and no amount of better logging produces them.
#
#     The compliance argument runs the opposite way. Logs are the MOST
#     sensitive artifact — they are where PHI and cardholder data actually
#     leak. Granting logs while withholding metrics and stopped reasons grants
#     the risky thing and withholds the safe things.
#
# So: everything about infrastructure STATE, nothing about data.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# One requirement AWS will not express, stated rather than fudged
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# design 11 grants "env var KEYS" and denies "env var VALUES". ECS returns both
# from the same call — `ecs:DescribeTaskDefinition` has no way to project away
# the values, and there is no separate action for the keys.
#
# So the prod set DENIES DescribeTaskDefinition and gets the deployed revision
# from `ecs:DescribeServices` instead, which returns the task definition ARN
# (revision included) without the container definitions. That satisfies
# "what is actually deployed" and loses the env var keys.
#
# Deliberate, and recorded as D-017. The alternative — granting the call and
# describing it as keys-only — would put secret values in front of developers
# while the documentation said otherwise, which is worse than a gap somebody
# knows about. B-095 carries the platform-mediated view that would close it.
#
# SSM and Secrets Manager have the same shape and DO separate cleanly:
# DescribeParameters and ListSecrets return names, GetParameter and
# GetSecretValue return values. Those are granted and denied respectively.

Parameters:

  InstanceArn:
    Type: String
    Description: IAM Identity Center instance ARN.

  SsmPrefix:
    Type: String
    Default: /platform
    Description: Where the permission set ARNs are published for other stacks.

Resources:

  # =========================================================================
  # dev — full within guardrails
  # =========================================================================
  # design 11: "Dev is expected to be chaotic. That is acceptable because it is
  # isolated by the account boundary and holds no regulated data."
  #
  # PowerUserAccess rather than a hand-written grant: the guardrails are the
  # SCPs and the permissions boundary, not this policy. Trying to also express
  # them here would be a third copy of the same rules, drifting.

  DeveloperDevPermissionSet:
    Type: AWS::SSO::PermissionSet
    Properties:
      Name: DeveloperDev
      Description: >-
        Full access within the guardrails, for dev accounts only. IAM role
        creation permitted and boundary-enforced by SCP 05.
      InstanceArn: !Ref InstanceArn
      # Four hours, which is the ceiling SSO_PERMISSION_SET_SESSION_DURATION_BOUNDED
      # allows. The first draft said eight and argued that a developer works in
      # this account all day -- true, and the guard's reasoning is better: the
      # session is how long a revoked or compromised federation keeps working.
      # Widening a guardrail to fit a convenience is the wrong direction, so the
      # developer re-authenticates at lunchtime instead.
      SessionDuration: PT4H
      ManagedPolicies:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/PowerUserAccess
      InlinePolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          # PowerUserAccess excludes IAM entirely. design 11 wants role
          # creation in dev -- "which in dev they should be" -- so it is added
          # back, and SCP 05 is what makes it safe by requiring the boundary.
          - Sid: CreateRolesWithinTheBoundary
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - 'iam:CreateRole'
              - 'iam:DeleteRole'
              - 'iam:PutRolePolicy'
              - 'iam:DeleteRolePolicy'
              - 'iam:AttachRolePolicy'
              - 'iam:DetachRolePolicy'
              - 'iam:PassRole'
              - 'iam:TagRole'
              - 'iam:Get*'
              - 'iam:List*'
            Resource: '*'
          # design 11: "Developers can see their Config rules, alarms,
          # findings, flow logs [...] This is a design choice, not an
          # oversight." The prompt says explicitly not to remove it.
          - Sid: SeeTheControlsOperatingOnThem
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - 'config:Describe*'
              - 'config:Get*'
              - 'config:List*'
              - 'config:Select*'
              - 'securityhub:Get*'
              - 'securityhub:List*'
              - 'securityhub:Describe*'
              - 'guardduty:Get*'
              - 'guardduty:List*'
              - 'access-analyzer:Get*'
              - 'access-analyzer:List*'
            Resource: '*'

  # =========================================================================
  # test — read-only plus the operations a pipeline cannot do for you
  # =========================================================================

  DeveloperTestPermissionSet:
    Type: AWS::SSO::PermissionSet
    Properties:
      Name: DeveloperTest
      Description: >-
        Read-only plus limited operations. Changes arrive through AppDeployer,
        not through this. No IAM role creation.
      InstanceArn: !Ref InstanceArn
      SessionDuration: PT4H
      ManagedPolicies:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/ReadOnlyAccess
      InlinePolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          # "Limited ops" from design 11's gradient. Restarting a service and
          # re-running a task are the two things a developer needs during a
          # test cycle that no pipeline does on demand -- and neither changes
          # what is DEPLOYED, only whether it is currently running.
          - Sid: RestartButNotRedeploy
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - 'ecs:UpdateService'
              - 'ecs:StopTask'
              - 'ecs:RunTask'
              - 'lambda:InvokeFunction'
            Resource: '*'
          # ReadOnlyAccess includes s3:GetObject and
          # secretsmanager:GetSecretValue. Test accounts should not hold real
          # data, and "should not" is not a control.
          - Sid: NoDataPlaneEvenInTest
            Effect: Deny
            Action:
              - 's3:GetObject'
              - 's3:GetObjectVersion'
              - 'secretsmanager:GetSecretValue'
              - 'ssm:GetParameter'
              - 'ssm:GetParameters'
              - 'ssm:GetParametersByPath'
              - 'dynamodb:GetItem'
              - 'dynamodb:Query'
              - 'dynamodb:Scan'
              - 'dynamodb:BatchGetItem'
              - 'rds-data:*'
            Resource: '*'

  # =========================================================================
  # prod (and uat) — read and observe
  # =========================================================================
  # Enumerated rather than ReadOnlyAccess-minus-denies. ReadOnlyAccess grows
  # when AWS adds services, so a subtractive prod policy silently widens every
  # time Amazon ships something -- and the first anybody would know is an
  # auditor asking why developers can read a service nobody reviewed.

  DeveloperProdPermissionSet:
    Type: AWS::SSO::PermissionSet
    Properties:
      Name: DeveloperProd
      Description: >-
        Read and observe. Everything about infrastructure state, nothing about
        data. Also used for UAT, which design 11 treats as production because
        it holds real data.
      InstanceArn: !Ref InstanceArn
      # Two hours. Shorter than dev and test: this set sees production, and a
      # forgotten browser tab is the realistic exposure rather than a stolen
      # credential.
      SessionDuration: PT2H
      InlinePolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:

          - Sid: LogsTheirApplication
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - 'logs:Describe*'
              - 'logs:Get*'
              - 'logs:FilterLogEvents'
              - 'logs:StartQuery'
              - 'logs:StopQuery'
              - 'logs:TestMetricFilter'
            Resource: '*'

          # design 11: "all, not a health roll-up. Latency distribution and
          # saturation cannot be reconstructed from logs."
          - Sid: AllMetricsNotARollUp
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - 'cloudwatch:GetMetric*'
              - 'cloudwatch:ListMetrics'
              - 'cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms*'
              - 'cloudwatch:DescribeAnomalyDetectors'
              - 'cloudwatch:GetInsightRuleReport'
            Resource: '*'

          # The failure modes where the application cannot log. Note what is
          # ABSENT: DescribeTaskDefinition. See the header and D-017 -- the
          # deployed revision comes from DescribeServices, which does not
          # carry environment variable values.
          - Sid: WhyItStopped
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - 'ecs:DescribeServices'
              - 'ecs:DescribeTasks'
              - 'ecs:DescribeClusters'
              - 'ecs:DescribeContainerInstances'
              - 'ecs:ListTasks'
              - 'ecs:ListServices'
              - 'ecs:ListTaskDefinitions'
            Resource: '*'

          # Parameter NAMES and secret NAMES, never values. These APIs do
          # separate cleanly, unlike ECS.
          - Sid: NamesNotValues
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - 'ssm:DescribeParameters'
              - 'secretsmanager:ListSecrets'
              - 'secretsmanager:DescribeSecret'
            Resource: '*'

          - Sid: WhatWasDeployedAndWhen
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - 'cloudformation:Describe*'
              - 'cloudformation:List*'
              - 'cloudformation:Get*'
              - 'codedeploy:Get*'
              - 'codedeploy:List*'
              - 'codepipeline:Get*'
              - 'codepipeline:List*'
              # NOT GetFunctionConfiguration: it returns the function's
              # environment variables, the same collision as ECS
              # DescribeTaskDefinition. Versions and aliases answer
              # 'what is deployed' without the configuration. D-017.
              - 'lambda:ListVersionsByFunction'
              - 'lambda:ListAliases'
              - 'lambda:ListFunctions'
            Resource: '*'

          - Sid: Traces
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - 'xray:BatchGet*'
              - 'xray:Get*'
              - 'xray:List*'
              - 'application-signals:Get*'
              - 'application-signals:List*'
              - 'application-signals:BatchGet*'
            Resource: '*'

          # design 11: "They should see what wakes us up on their behalf."
          - Sid: SeeTheControlsOperatingOnThem
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - 'config:Describe*'
              - 'config:Get*'
              - 'config:List*'
              - 'config:Select*'
              - 'securityhub:Get*'
              - 'securityhub:List*'
              - 'securityhub:Describe*'
              - 'guardduty:Get*'
              - 'guardduty:List*'
              - 'ec2:DescribeFlowLogs'
              - 'ec2:DescribeInstances'
              - 'ec2:DescribeSecurityGroups'
              - 'ec2:DescribeNetworkInterfaces'
            Resource: '*'

          # "The restriction on DOING stays absolute. Only the restriction on
          # SEEING relaxes." A deny rather than simply not granting: the set
          # above is enumerated and could acquire a write action through a
          # careless wildcard, and this catches that.
          - Sid: NeverWriteAnything
            Effect: Deny
            NotAction:
              - 'logs:Describe*'
              - 'logs:Get*'
              - 'logs:FilterLogEvents'
              - 'logs:StartQuery'
              - 'logs:StopQuery'
              - 'logs:TestMetricFilter'
              - 'cloudwatch:Get*'
              - 'cloudwatch:List*'
              - 'cloudwatch:Describe*'
              - 'ecs:Describe*'
              - 'ecs:List*'
              - 'ssm:DescribeParameters'
              - 'secretsmanager:ListSecrets'
              - 'secretsmanager:DescribeSecret'
              - 'cloudformation:Describe*'
              - 'cloudformation:List*'
              - 'cloudformation:Get*'
              - 'codedeploy:Get*'
              - 'codedeploy:List*'
              - 'codepipeline:Get*'
              - 'codepipeline:List*'
              - 'lambda:Get*'
              - 'lambda:List*'
              - 'xray:*Get*'
              - 'xray:List*'
              - 'application-signals:*'
              - 'config:*'
              - 'securityhub:Get*'
              - 'securityhub:List*'
              - 'securityhub:Describe*'
              - 'guardduty:Get*'
              - 'guardduty:List*'
              - 'ec2:Describe*'
              - 'sts:GetCallerIdentity'
            Resource: '*'

          # The data plane, denied explicitly as well as not granted. design
          # 11 holds this one firm: "no reading S3 objects, no querying the
          # database, no retrieving Secrets Manager values".
          - Sid: NeverTheDataPlane
            Effect: Deny
            Action:
              - 's3:GetObject'
              - 's3:GetObjectVersion'
              - 'secretsmanager:GetSecretValue'
              - 'ssm:GetParameter'
              - 'ssm:GetParameters'
              - 'ssm:GetParametersByPath'
              - 'dynamodb:GetItem'
              - 'dynamodb:BatchGetItem'
              - 'dynamodb:Query'
              - 'dynamodb:Scan'
              - 'rds-data:*'
              - 'ecs:DescribeTaskDefinition'
              - 'lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration'
            Resource: '*'

  # Published so provisioning (phase 12) can assign these without being told
  # the ARNs. identity/00-commercial-readonly.yaml does the same.
  DevArnParam:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${SsmPrefix}/identity/permission-set/developer-dev'
      Type: String
      Value: !GetAtt DeveloperDevPermissionSet.PermissionSetArn

  TestArnParam:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${SsmPrefix}/identity/permission-set/developer-test'
      Type: String
      Value: !GetAtt DeveloperTestPermissionSet.PermissionSetArn

  ProdArnParam:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${SsmPrefix}/identity/permission-set/developer-prod'
      Type: String
      Value: !GetAtt DeveloperProdPermissionSet.PermissionSetArn

Outputs:

  DeveloperDevArn:
    Description: dev grant. Full within guardrails.
    Value: !GetAtt DeveloperDevPermissionSet.PermissionSetArn

  DeveloperTestArn:
    Description: test grant. Read-only plus restart.
    Value: !GetAtt DeveloperTestPermissionSet.PermissionSetArn

  DeveloperProdArn:
    Description: prod and uat grant. Read and observe.
    Value: !GetAtt DeveloperProdPermissionSet.PermissionSetArn
files.org/00-org-structure.yaml:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  AltDigital Managed Platform — fixed Organizational Unit skeleton.
  Deploys to the Organization management account only. Creates the OUs that
  never change: Security, Infrastructure, Members, Members/direct, Sandbox.
  Partner and client OUs beneath Members are created dynamically by partner
  onboarding and the client provisioning saga — they are NOT in this template.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why OUs and not name prefixes (design doc 15)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# OU placement is what drives everything downstream: SCP and RCP inheritance,
# StackSet targeting, blast radius containment, and — the reason this matters
# for billing — the consolidated billing boundary. Cost Categories derive
# partner, client, application and environment from the account id, so getting
# this tree right is what makes exact per-client and per-partner invoicing fall
# out structurally rather than needing to be assembled from resource tags.
#
# Every OU carries DeletionPolicy and UpdateReplacePolicy Retain. Deleting this
# stack must never attempt to dismantle the Organization. Detaching an OU that
# holds accounts would fail anyway, but a half-succeeded teardown of the top of
# the tree is not a state worth being able to reach.

Parameters:

  RootId:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Organization root id (r-xxxx). Discovered by
      scripts/bootstrap-management-account.sh and published to
      /platform/org/root-id; deploy-org-structure.sh reads it from there.
    AllowedPattern: '^r-[0-9a-z]{4,32}$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be an Organization root id, e.g. r-ab12.

  SsmPrefix:
    Type: String
    Default: /platform
    Description: >-
      SSM Parameter Store namespace for published OU ids. Templates and
      pipelines read OU ids from here so nothing hardcodes an id.
    AllowedPattern: '^/[a-zA-Z0-9._/-]+$'

Resources:

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Security — immutable log destination, aggregation, forensics
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Holds accounts, not sub-OUs: Log Archive, Audit, Forensics.
  # Forensics is isolated by design and receives preserved evidence during a
  # security incident; containment automation writes into it from outside the
  # affected member account (design doc 07).
  SecurityOu:
    Type: AWS::Organizations::OrganizationalUnit
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: Security
      ParentId: !Ref RootId
      Tags:
        - { Key: platform-managed, Value: 'true' }
        - { Key: Purpose,          Value: security-and-evidence }
        - { Key: BillingRollup,    Value: platform-shared }

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Infrastructure — the platform's own machinery
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Platform Tooling (CloudFormation pipeline, StackSet admin), Shared Services
  # (platform automation, Truveon ingestion), Backup (Vault Lock), and Network
  # (reserved — centralised egress is deferred, item D3).
  InfrastructureOu:
    Type: AWS::Organizations::OrganizationalUnit
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: Infrastructure
      ParentId: !Ref RootId
      Tags:
        - { Key: platform-managed, Value: 'true' }
        - { Key: Purpose,          Value: platform-operations }
        - { Key: BillingRollup,    Value: platform-shared }

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Members — every tenant account, nested partner then client
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Members
  #   <partner>/            created by partner onboarding  (org/10-partner-ou.yaml)
  #     <client>/           created by the provisioning saga (org/20-client-ou.yaml)
  #       ad-<partner>-<client>-<env>
  MembersOu:
    Type: AWS::Organizations::OrganizationalUnit
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: Members
      ParentId: !Ref RootId
      Tags:
        - { Key: platform-managed, Value: 'true' }
        - { Key: Purpose,          Value: tenant-workloads }
        - { Key: BillingRollup,    Value: tenant }

  # AltDigital's own clients, with no partner in the chain. Reserved from the
  # outset: without it the first direct client gets bolted on awkwardly, and
  # the billing roll-up would need a special case for "no partner".
  # Accounts here are named ad-direct-<client>-<env>, so 'direct' occupies the
  # partner slot and the naming rule stays uniform.
  MembersDirectOu:
    Type: AWS::Organizations::OrganizationalUnit
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: direct
      ParentId: !Ref MembersOu
      Tags:
        - { Key: platform-managed, Value: 'true' }
        - { Key: Purpose,          Value: altdigital-direct-clients }
        - { Key: PartnerSlug,      Value: direct }
        - { Key: BillingRollup,    Value: tenant }

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Sandbox — the baseline canary
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # First wave of every baseline rollout, and the target for the guardrail test
  # harness. A member account with full local administrator attempting denied
  # actions has to happen somewhere real; this is that somewhere.
  SandboxOu:
    Type: AWS::Organizations::OrganizationalUnit
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: Sandbox
      ParentId: !Ref RootId
      Tags:
        - { Key: platform-managed, Value: 'true' }
        - { Key: Purpose,          Value: baseline-canary-and-guardrail-tests }
        - { Key: BillingRollup,    Value: platform-shared }

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Published OU ids
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # No CloudFormation Exports: cross-stack exports create an update lock, and
  # later consumers live in other accounts and regions where exports cannot
  # reach. SSM is the published contract.
  SecurityOuParam:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${SsmPrefix}/org/ou/security'
      Type: String
      Value: !Ref SecurityOu
      Description: Security OU id
      Tags: { platform-managed: 'true' }

  InfrastructureOuParam:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${SsmPrefix}/org/ou/infrastructure'
      Type: String
      Value: !Ref InfrastructureOu
      Description: Infrastructure OU id
      Tags: { platform-managed: 'true' }

  MembersOuParam:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${SsmPrefix}/org/ou/members'
      Type: String
      Value: !Ref MembersOu
      Description: Members OU id — parent of every partner OU
      Tags: { platform-managed: 'true' }

  MembersDirectOuParam:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${SsmPrefix}/org/ou/members/direct'
      Type: String
      Value: !Ref MembersDirectOu
      Description: Members/direct OU id — AltDigital's own clients, no partner
      Tags: { platform-managed: 'true' }

  SandboxOuParam:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${SsmPrefix}/org/ou/sandbox'
      Type: String
      Value: !Ref SandboxOu
      Description: Sandbox OU id — baseline canary account
      Tags: { platform-managed: 'true' }

Outputs:

  SecurityOuId:
    Description: Security OU id
    Value: !Ref SecurityOu

  InfrastructureOuId:
    Description: Infrastructure OU id
    Value: !Ref InfrastructureOu

  MembersOuId:
    Description: Members OU id
    Value: !Ref MembersOu

  MembersDirectOuId:
    Description: Members/direct OU id
    Value: !Ref MembersDirectOu

  SandboxOuId:
    Description: Sandbox OU id
    Value: !Ref SandboxOu
files.org/10-partner-ou.yaml:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  AltDigital Managed Platform — one partner OU beneath Members.
  Deployed once per partner by partner onboarding (design doc 15). Creates the
  OU and publishes its id; it does not create accounts, SCPs or the partner's
  Truveon tenant.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# One stack per partner, deliberately
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Partner onboarding is a separate, one-time process and a partner must exist
# before any client can be onboarded beneath it. Keeping one stack per partner
# means a partner can be added, amended or (in principle) removed without a
# change that touches every other partner's OU — the same blast-radius argument
# that makes partner an OU rather than a name prefix.
#
# Stack name convention: platform-partner-<slug>
#
# Billing: this OU is the consolidated billing boundary AltDigital invoices
# against. The Cost Category 'Partner' dimension is derived from account id, but
# the OU is what makes the roll-up verifiable — an account in the wrong OU is a
# billing error, and that is detectable here rather than in a spreadsheet.

Parameters:

  PartnerSlug:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Machine-safe partner identifier, used verbatim as the OU name and as the
      <partner> segment of every account alias beneath it. Lowercase
      alphanumeric and hyphens only — account aliases permit nothing else.
      Strip dots: oeight.io becomes oeight.
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,16}[a-z0-9])?$'
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 18
    ConstraintDescription: >-
      1-18 chars, lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens, must start and end
      alphanumeric. The cap is a fixed budget against TWO limits, of which the
      email is the tighter: the 63-char account alias
      (7 + 18 + 1 + 18 + 1 + 10 + 1 + 4 = 60) and the 64-octet RFC 5321 email
      local part (4 + 1 + 18 + 1 + 18 + 1 + 10 + 1 + 1 = 55, using the short
      'mspr' base and a one-character tier). Do not raise it in isolation.

  PartnerLegalName:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Partner legal or trading entity name, for display and for the audit trail.
      The slug is the machine identifier; this is the human one. Kept distinct
      on purpose, the same way an account alias is distinct from an account name.
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 128

  PartnerDomain:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      Partner's primary domain, e.g. oeight.io. Display attribute only —
      recorded here because the slug discards the dot.
    MaxLength: 253

  MembersOuId:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Members OU id. Read from /platform/org/ou/members; not hardcoded.
    AllowedPattern: '^ou-[0-9a-z]{4,32}-[0-9a-z]{8,32}$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be an Organizational Unit id, e.g. ou-ab12-cdef3456.

  SsmPrefix:
    Type: String
    Default: /platform
    AllowedPattern: '^/[a-zA-Z0-9._/-]+$'

Resources:

  PartnerOu:
    Type: AWS::Organizations::OrganizationalUnit
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: !Ref PartnerSlug
      ParentId: !Ref MembersOuId
      Tags:
        - { Key: platform-managed,  Value: 'true' }
        - { Key: PartnerSlug,       Value: !Ref PartnerSlug }
        - { Key: PartnerLegalName,  Value: !Ref PartnerLegalName }
        - { Key: PartnerDomain,     Value: !Ref PartnerDomain }
        - { Key: BillingRollup,     Value: partner }

  # Published so the client OU stack and the provisioning saga can resolve the
  # parent without a list-organizational-units call and without hardcoding.
  PartnerOuParam:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${SsmPrefix}/org/ou/members/${PartnerSlug}'
      Type: String
      Value: !Ref PartnerOu
      Description: !Sub 'Partner OU id for ${PartnerLegalName}'
      Tags:
        platform-managed: 'true'
        PartnerSlug: !Ref PartnerSlug

Outputs:

  PartnerOuId:
    # Outputs' Description must be a literal String — CloudFormation rejects
    # intrinsic functions here, unlike a resource property. The parameterised
    # detail belongs in Value, not in the label.
    Description: OU id for this partner
    Value: !Ref PartnerOu

  PartnerSlugOut:
    Description: Partner slug, echoed for pipeline consumption
    Value: !Ref PartnerSlug
files.org/20-client-ou.yaml:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  AltDigital Managed Platform — one client OU beneath a partner OU.
  Deployed by the client provisioning saga (design doc 13) after the partner
  precondition passes. Creates the OU and publishes its id. Accounts are vested
  into it separately.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Position in the saga
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# This stack is part of step 5 (AWS accounts + baseline), not step 1. The
# registry entry comes first and is the spine; this template consumes the
# partner and client slugs from it and writes the resulting OU id back.
#
# It must not be deployed before the step 0 partner precondition passes —
# partner exists, is active, notification window non-null. An OU created
# beneath an incomplete partner relationship is exactly the half-provisioned
# state the saga is built to avoid, because it looks supported.
#
# Stack name convention: platform-client-<partner>-<client>
#
# Billing: the client OU is the boundary the partner invoices their own client
# against. Two roll-ups, one tree — by client for the partner, by partner for
# AltDigital. Both derive from account id via Cost Categories; this OU is what
# makes the derivation checkable.

Parameters:

  PartnerSlug:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Partner slug this client sits beneath. Must match the parent OU's name.
      Use 'direct' for AltDigital's own clients with no partner in the chain.
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,16}[a-z0-9])?$'
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 18

  ClientSlug:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Machine-safe client identifier, used verbatim as the OU name and as the
      <client> segment of every account alias beneath it.
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,16}[a-z0-9])?$'
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 18
    ConstraintDescription: >-
      1-18 chars, lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens, must start and end
      alphanumeric. Capped by the root-email local-part budget, not just the
      account alias — see scripts/lib/common.sh.

  ClientLegalName:
    Type: String
    Description: Client legal or trading entity name, for display and audit trail.
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 128

  # Ownership and authorship are recorded separately because they vary
  # independently, and the design package models only the case where they move
  # together.
  #
  # Doc 15 treats "is the partner also the application owner?" as a single
  # question (questionnaire 1.0b). OEight's two clients show why that is not
  # enough:
  #
  #   Arc8      OEight owns the IP   and   OEight builds it
  #   Avergent  Avergent owns the IP and   OEight builds it as a service
  #
  # Collapsing these loses precisely the distinction doc 15 warns about — that
  # an auditor must be able to separate what the partner does as a service
  # provider from what it does as an application owner. They also drive
  # different things: ownership drives the IP and exit clauses, authorship
  # drives who is accountable for application-layer patching, change records
  # and remediation on the responsibility matrix.

  ApplicationOwner:
    Type: String
    Default: client
    AllowedValues: [client, partner]
    Description: >-
      Who owns the application intellectual property. Drives the IP boundary
      and the exit clause. Where this is 'partner', design doc 10's position
      that "the customer owns their application and their data" does not hold
      for this client and the contract must say what they leave with.

  ApplicationBuilder:
    Type: String
    Default: client
    AllowedValues: [client, partner, third-party]
    Description: >-
      Who actually writes and maintains the application. Drives the
      responsibility matrix rows for application patching, dependency
      remediation, change records and Tier 2 application response. Independent
      of ownership: a partner can build under contract while the client retains
      the IP.

  PartnerOuId:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Parent partner OU id. Read from /platform/org/ou/members/<partner>.
    AllowedPattern: '^ou-[0-9a-z]{4,32}-[0-9a-z]{8,32}$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be an Organizational Unit id, e.g. ou-ab12-cdef3456.

  SsmPrefix:
    Type: String
    Default: /platform
    AllowedPattern: '^/[a-zA-Z0-9._/-]+$'

Resources:

  ClientOu:
    Type: AWS::Organizations::OrganizationalUnit
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: !Ref ClientSlug
      ParentId: !Ref PartnerOuId
      Tags:
        - { Key: platform-managed,            Value: 'true' }
        - { Key: PartnerSlug,                 Value: !Ref PartnerSlug }
        - { Key: ClientSlug,                  Value: !Ref ClientSlug }
        - { Key: ClientLegalName,             Value: !Ref ClientLegalName }
        - { Key: ApplicationOwner,            Value: !Ref ApplicationOwner }
        - { Key: ApplicationBuilder,          Value: !Ref ApplicationBuilder }
        - { Key: BillingRollup,               Value: client }

  ClientOuParam:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${SsmPrefix}/org/ou/members/${PartnerSlug}/${ClientSlug}'
      Type: String
      Value: !Ref ClientOu
      Description: !Sub 'Client OU id for ${ClientLegalName} under partner ${PartnerSlug}'
      Tags:
        platform-managed: 'true'
        PartnerSlug: !Ref PartnerSlug
        ClientSlug: !Ref ClientSlug

Outputs:

  ClientOuId:
    # Outputs' Description must be a literal String — CloudFormation rejects
    # intrinsic functions here, unlike a resource property.
    Description: OU id for this client, beneath its partner OU
    Value: !Ref ClientOu

  AccountAliasPrefix:
    Description: >-
      Alias stem for every account vested into this OU. The vesting pipeline
      appends -<env>, or -<app>-<env> where the client has more than one
      application.
    Value: !Sub 'altdig-${PartnerSlug}-${ClientSlug}'
files.org/30-organization-trail.yaml:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  AltDigital Managed Platform — organization-wide CloudTrail. One trail in the
  management account capturing every API call in every account, delivered to
  the immutable log archive. Deploys to the management account only.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# One organization trail, not one trail per account
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# An organization trail is created once in the management account and applies
# to every member account automatically — including accounts vested after it
# was created. A member account cannot disable, reconfigure or delete it: the
# trail is not their resource. That property is doing real work here, because
# it is the one detective control that does not depend on the member-account
# baseline having been applied correctly.
#
# The SCPs deny cloudtrail:StopLogging and DeleteTrail as defence in depth, but
# the organization trail would survive even without them.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What this deliberately does not do
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# No CloudWatch Logs delivery. Design doc 07 expects an incident readout to
# answer "what did this principal do in the preceding 24 hours", which against
# S3 means Athena rather than a log-group query — slower, but an organization
# trail across every account is a large ingest volume and CloudWatch Logs is
# charged per GB. Recorded as B-005 in docs/build-backlog.md and revisited when
# Phase 7 can weigh query latency during a live incident against the cost.
#
# No data events. S3 object-level and Lambda invocation logging multiply volume
# by orders of magnitude and belong to a per-tenant decision driven by the
# questionnaire's data classification, not to the platform baseline.

Parameters:

  LogArchiveBucketName:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Bucket in the Log Archive account. Read from
      /platform/org/account/altdig-security-logarchive by the deploy script;
      not hardcoded.
    MinLength: 3

  LogArchiveKeyArn:
    Type: String
    Description: KMS key ARN in the Log Archive account used to encrypt trail objects.
    AllowedPattern: '^arn:aws:kms:[a-z0-9-]+:[0-9]{12}:key/.+$'

  TrailName:
    Type: String
    Default: platform-organization-trail
    Description: Trail name. Appears in every member account's CloudTrail console.

Resources:

  OrganizationTrail:
    Type: AWS::CloudTrail::Trail
    # Retain rather than delete on stack removal. Deleting the trail would stop
    # capture across every account in the Organization at once, which is both
    # an availability event for the evidence pipeline and precisely the action
    # the SCPs exist to prevent a human performing by hand.
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      TrailName: !Ref TrailName
      IsOrganizationTrail: true
      IsLogging: true

      # Multi-region regardless of the platform's region allow-list. A trail
      # limited to permitted regions would not record activity in a region the
      # allow-list is supposed to prevent — and activity in an unexpected
      # region is exactly what you want captured, not skipped. This is the
      # blind spot prompt 10.2 describes, and the trail must not share it.
      IsMultiRegionTrail: true

      # Global service events (IAM, STS, CloudFront, Route 53) are emitted in
      # us-east-1 regardless of where anything is deployed. Without this, every
      # IAM action in the Organization goes unrecorded.
      IncludeGlobalServiceEvents: true

      # Produces a signed digest chain, so tampering with delivered objects is
      # detectable independently of S3 Object Lock. Two mechanisms, different
      # failure modes: Object Lock prevents alteration, validation proves none
      # occurred.
      EnableLogFileValidation: true

      S3BucketName: !Ref LogArchiveBucketName
      KMSKeyId: !Ref LogArchiveKeyArn

      Tags:
        - { Key: platform-managed, Value: 'true' }
        - { Key: Purpose,          Value: organization-audit-trail }

Outputs:

  TrailArn:
    Description: Organization trail ARN
    Value: !GetAtt OrganizationTrail.Arn

  TrailNameOut:
    Description: Organization trail name
    Value: !Ref TrailName

  # Echoed so the deploy script can report the destination without a second
  # lookup, and so the stack records what it was pointed at.
  Destination:
    Description: Log archive bucket receiving this trail
    Value: !Ref LogArchiveBucketName
files.org/30-verification-org-reader.yaml:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  AltDigital Managed Platform — a read-only role in the MANAGEMENT account
  letting the verification sweep ask Organizations where an account actually
  sits and what is actually attached to it. B-112.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why the sweep needs to read Organizations at all
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# design 13's check 6 asks that "the guardrail test harness passes against
# these specific accounts". Decided with Jamie on 2026-09-22 that this is the
# wrong per-account check, and this role serves what replaced it.
#
# The reasoning, in short: SCPs attach to OUs, not to accounts. Running
# `scripts/test-guardrails.sh` for forty accounts in one OU tests the same
# policy forty times. It also cannot run from a read-only role — it proves SCPs
# work by ATTEMPTING DENIED ACTIONS with an administrator, creating IAM roles,
# KMS keys, backup vaults and EBS volumes inside the account it is testing.
#
# What is genuinely true per account, and genuinely a read, is INHERITANCE:
#
#   is this account under the OU we believe it is, and are the policies we
#   believe are attached actually attached to that OU?
#
# The harness stays the per-OU exercise it already is. This answers the
# per-account question without holding admin anywhere.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why the comparison is not vacuous
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The expected OU comes from SSM under /platform/org/ou/members/<partner>/
# <client>, published when the OU was created. The ACTUAL parent comes from
# Organizations. Two different sources, which is the whole point — reading both
# from the registry would confirm the registry agrees with itself.
#
# This is the same construction `scripts/lib/cost_categories.py` uses: the
# registry says what should exist and Organizations says what does, and the gap
# between them is the finding.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why it is in the management account, and why that is not a workload
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The Organizations API answers only in the management account or a delegated
# administrator, and the OU parameters live there too. CLAUDE.md keeps the
# management account holding "the Organization and nothing else" — a read-only
# role over the Organization's own structure is not a workload, it is a view of
# the one thing this account is for. Same argument that puts Cost Categories
# here.

Parameters:

  ToolingAccountId:
    Type: String
    AllowedPattern: '^[0-9]{12}$'
    Description: >-
      The Platform Tooling account, where the verification sweep runs. No empty
      default: unlike the member-side reader this template is deployed
      deliberately to one account, so an operator who does not know the tooling
      account id should stop rather than create a role that trusts nobody.

Resources:

  VerificationOrgReaderRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: PlatformVerificationOrgReader
      Description: >-
        Read-only over Organization structure and the published OU parameters.
        Assumed by the provisioning verification sweep. B-112.
      MaxSessionDuration: 3600
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${ToolingAccountId}:root'
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              # Naming the account alone would let every principal in tooling
              # read the Organization's structure. The sweep is the only
              # legitimate caller.
              #
              # A pattern rather than an exact ARN because the verification
              # function is not deployed (B-110). Still narrow: SCP 03 governs
              # who may create a Platform* role. Replace with the function's
              # role ARN once the provisioning stack exists.
              ArnLike:
                'aws:PrincipalArn': !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${ToolingAccountId}:role/PlatformVerification*'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ReadOrganizationStructure
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:

              - Sid: ReadPlacementAndAttachedPolicies
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  # Where the account actually is.
                  - organizations:ListParents
                  - organizations:DescribeOrganizationalUnit
                  # What is actually attached there. ListPoliciesForTarget
                  # returns attachment, not content — the sweep is asking
                  # whether the guardrails apply to this account, not what they
                  # say. DescribePolicy is deliberately NOT granted: policy
                  # bodies are in the repository and reading them from the API
                  # would answer a question nobody asked.
                  - organizations:ListPoliciesForTarget
                Resource: '*'
                # Organizations list operations admit no resource ARN. The
                # actions are enumerated, none of them mutates, and none can
                # read account contents — only structure.

              - Sid: ReadPublishedOuParameters
                Effect: Allow
                Action: ssm:GetParameter
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:*:${AWS::AccountId}:parameter/platform/org/ou/*'
                # Scoped to the OU tree only. The rest of /platform/ in this
                # account includes identity and config values the sweep has no
                # business reading.

      Tags:
        # CLAUDE.md hard rule, Jamie 2026-09-22.
        - Key: platform-layer
          Value: infrastructure
        - Key: platform-managed
          Value: 'true'

Outputs:

  VerificationOrgReaderRoleArn:
    Description: >-
      Set as ORG_READER_ROLE_ARN on the verification function. Absent, the
      inheritance check reports undeterminable and says why rather than
      passing.
    Value: !GetAtt VerificationOrgReaderRole.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-VerificationOrgReaderRoleArn'
files.quorum/00-executor-role.yaml:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  AltDigital Managed Platform — the role the quorum pipeline assumes to perform
  a two-party-approved action (prompt 8.3). The only permitted path to the
  actions design 03 denies everywhere else.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# This role is the exception to the rule, and that is the point
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLAUDE.md: "Never write code that terminates, deletes, deregisters, rolls back
# or purges a resource as part of automated remediation. Security automation
# isolates and preserves."
#
# containment/00-responder-role.yaml honours that by holding NO destructive
# permission at all. This role is its opposite: it exists precisely to delete a
# KMS key, delete a backup vault, remove an account from the Organization, or
# stop a trail.
#
# The rule is not being bent. It says "as part of automated remediation" —
# automation deciding, on its own, to destroy something. Nothing here decides.
# A person requests the action, two DIFFERENT people approve it, and the
# pipeline carries out the specific thing they approved. design 03:
#
#     These are denied outright in the relevant resource policies and SCPs. The
#     only execution path is a platform pipeline that verifies two recorded
#     approvals before assuming a permitted role.
#
# The alternative — a human holding standing permission to delete keys — is
# strictly worse: no verification, no evidence, and a credential that can do it
# at any time for any reason.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why the permission list is NOT the control here, and what is
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# For the containment role, the absence of destructive permission is the whole
# control. That argument is unavailable to this role. Three things replace it:
#
# 1. WHO CAN ASSUME IT. Exactly one principal: the quorum state machine's
#    execution role, named in full. Not an account, not a wildcard, not a path.
#
# 2. A SESSION POLICY, PER CALL. The pipeline assumes this role passing an
#    inline session policy scoped to the ONE resource ARN that was approved.
#    Effective permission is the intersection, so the credentials handed to
#    execute.py cannot express a request against any other resource. A bug that
#    passed the wrong key ARN gets AccessDenied rather than deleting it. This
#    is the containment role's argument reconstructed at session scope: make
#    the wrong action inexpressible rather than merely un-attempted.
#
# 3. THE SESSION NAME CARRIES THE JIRA KEY. CloudTrail records the assumed-role
#    session name on every call, so every action taken through this role is
#    tied in CloudTrail to the change record that authorised it, without
#    trusting anything the pipeline says about itself. That is what makes the
#    reverse reconciliation in quorum/src/reverse.py cheap: a ScheduleKeyDeletion
#    whose session name does not name an approved change is, on its face, a
#    deletion that did not come through here.
#
# The name is load-bearing for the same reason the containment role's is:
# `DenyPlatformRoleModification` in policies/scp/03-protect-platform-identity.json
# protects `arn:aws:iam::*:role/Platform*`. Rename this outside that prefix and
# a member account can delete the role that governs its own key deletions.

Parameters:

  QuorumPipelineRoleArn:
    Type: String
    AllowedPattern: '^arn:aws:iam::\d{12}:role/.+$'
    Description: >-
      The Audit-account role permitted to assume this one — the quorum state
      machine's execution role. Exactly one principal, named in full. An
      account-root principal here would let anything in Audit assume it.

  QuorumReverseRoleArn:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      The Audit-account role that runs the reverse reconciliation sweep. Given
      a read-only role here so it can call cloudtrail:LookupEvents.

      It cannot use OrganizationAccountAccessRole: that role trusts the
      MANAGEMENT account only, so a sweep running from Audit gets AccessDenied
      against every account in the estate. Empty disables the reader entirely,
      which leaves the sweep reporting that account as unreadable -- visibly,
      rather than as a clean result.

  Scope:
    Type: String
    Default: member
    AllowedValues: [member, management]
    Description: >-
      Which set of quorum actions this instance grants.

      design 03 lists four, and they do not all live in the same account.
      KMS keys, backup vaults, CloudTrail and Config are member-account
      resources. Removing an account from the Organization is an action ONLY
      the management account can perform, against the Organization rather than
      against anything inside the member.

      One template with a scope parameter rather than two near-identical files,
      so the trust policy, naming and boundary cannot drift apart between them.

Conditions:

  IsMember: !Equals [!Ref Scope, member]
  IsManagement: !Equals [!Ref Scope, management]
  HasReverseRole: !Not [!Equals [!Ref QuorumReverseRoleArn, '']]

Resources:

  QuorumExecutorRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: PlatformQuorumExecutor
      Description: >-
        Performs a two-party-approved quorum action. Assumable only by the
        quorum pipeline, and only ever with a session policy narrowing it to
        the single approved resource.
      MaxSessionDuration: 3600
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: OnlyTheQuorumPipeline
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Ref QuorumPipelineRoleArn
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              # The session name must name a Jira issue. Two reasons, and the
              # second is the important one:
              #
              #   it forces the caller to declare which change record it is
              #   acting under, at the moment of assuming the role
              #
              #   CloudTrail then carries that declaration on every subsequent
