"""The monthly tenant cost report. Prompt 9.2, design 10 "Support pricing".

    Flat fee per account per month + a percentage of AWS spend.
    [...] Monthly tenant service report includes raw AWS cost alongside the
    uplift.

Three numbers, shown separately, never one number
--------------------------------------------------
Prompt 9.2 asks for raw AWS cost, flat fee and percentage uplift "shown
separately", and design 10 says why:

    Showing the raw AWS cost alongside the uplift is good practice -- it makes
    the margin transparent and gives the customer a reason to care about
    right-sizing, which benefits both parties.

A single total would hide which of the three moved. A customer whose bill rose
because they left a test cluster running and one whose bill rose because
AltDigital changed its percentage have very different conversations, and only
the separated form tells them apart.

The rates here are INDICATIVE and are not a price list
-------------------------------------------------------
design 10 gives ~$1,000/account/month and 15-20%, and then says:

    Model A is materially less work than Model B. The flat fee and percentage
    should differ accordingly. Worth pricing before the first contract rather
    than after.

So the numbers are a starting point somebody still has to decide. They live in
configuration, every output says which rate it used, and a report generated
before the rates are set says so rather than presenting a plausible invoice.
An indicative figure that reaches a customer becomes the price.

The percentage basis is LIST price, and that will drift
--------------------------------------------------------
design 10 is explicit that the uplift applies to list-price AWS spend, not net
of Savings Plans or Reserved Instance discounts, because AltDigital carries the
commitment risk and retains the arbitrage.

    Interim position: no negotiated discounts exist yet, so list price is the
    actual price.

Today those are the same number, so unblended cost is a correct basis. The
moment a commitment is bought they diverge, and a report still using unblended
cost would quietly bill the uplift on the DISCOUNTED figure -- handing the
customer the arbitrage design 10 says AltDigital keeps, with nothing anywhere
saying it happened.

So the report compares unblended against net-unblended every run and reports
the basis it used. When they differ it says so loudly instead of continuing to
produce believable-looking numbers.
"""
import datetime
import json
import os

import boto3

ce = boto3.client("ce")
ssm = boto3.client("ssm")

RATES_PARAM = os.environ.get("COST_RATES_PARAM", "/platform/cost/rates")

# The Cost Categories sync creates these. Named here because the report is
# useless without them, and a missing category should say which one rather
# than returning an empty grouping.
TENANT_CATEGORY = os.environ.get("COST_TENANT_CATEGORY", "Tenant")
KIND_CATEGORY = os.environ.get("COST_KIND_CATEGORY", "AccountKind")


class RatesNotSet(Exception):
    """Nobody has decided the pricing yet.

    Distinct and fatal. design 10's figures are indicative, and a report that
    quietly used them would put a number in front of a customer that no human
    chose. The failure mode of guessing here is a contract.
    """


class RatesUnreadable(Exception):
    """The rates could not be READ. Not the same as not being set.

    Both stop the report, so the safe outcome is identical -- which is exactly
    why this was wrong for an hour without anyone noticing. The DIFFERENCE is
    where it sends whoever reads it:

        not set      somebody has to decide the pricing
        unreadable   somebody has to fix a credential or a permission

    The first version caught every exception and reported all of them as "run
    scripts/set-cost-rates.sh". An expired SSO token therefore produced
    confident, specific, wrong advice -- the same shape as B-086, B-089, B-091
    and B-092, committed in the same session that documented them.
    """


def _now():
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)


def _month_bounds(month):
    """(start, end) for a YYYY-MM, as Cost Explorer wants them.

    End is EXCLUSIVE and is the first of the next month. Cost Explorer treats
    it that way, and an inclusive reading here would silently drop the last day
    of every month -- roughly 3% of every invoice, consistently, in AltDigital's
    favour. The kind of error that is embarrassing rather than expensive.
    """
    year, mon = (int(p) for p in month.split("-"))
    start = datetime.date(year, mon, 1)
    end = datetime.date(year + (mon == 12), (mon % 12) + 1, 1)
    return start.isoformat(), end.isoformat()


def rates():
    """Flat fee and percentage, per service model. From SSM, never defaults."""
    try:
        raw = ssm.get_parameter(Name=RATES_PARAM)["Parameter"]["Value"]
    except Exception as exc:                       # noqa: BLE001
        code = getattr(exc, "response", {}).get("Error", {}).get("Code", "")
        if code == "ParameterNotFound":
            raise RatesNotSet(
                f"{RATES_PARAM} does not exist. design 10's $1,000 and 15-20% "
                "are INDICATIVE and were never a price list -- no report is "
                "produced until somebody sets the real numbers. Run "
                "scripts/set-cost-rates.sh.") from exc
        raise RatesUnreadable(
            f"could not read {RATES_PARAM}: {code or type(exc).__name__}. "
            "This is NOT 'the rates are unset' -- the parameter may be "
            "perfectly fine and unreachable. Check credentials and the "
            "ssm:GetParameter permission before touching the pricing.") from exc
    try:
        data = json.loads(raw)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise RatesUnreadable(
            f"{RATES_PARAM} is not valid JSON. It was written by something "
            "other than scripts/set-cost-rates.sh.") from exc
    models = data.get("service_models") or {}
    if not models:
        raise RatesNotSet(f"{RATES_PARAM} defines no service models.")
    return models, bool(data.get("rates_are_contractual"))


def _ce_month(start, end, group_by, metrics):
    return ce.get_cost_and_usage(
        TimePeriod={"Start": start, "End": end},
        Granularity="MONTHLY",
        Metrics=metrics,
        GroupBy=group_by,
    )


def _amount(group, metric):
    return float(group["Metrics"][metric]["Amount"])


def _period_total(start, end):
    """Ungrouped spend for the period, to tell 'nothing' from 'not grouped'."""
    try:
        result = ce.get_cost_and_usage(
            TimePeriod={"Start": start, "End": end},
            Granularity="MONTHLY", Metrics=["UnblendedCost"])
        return sum(float(r["Total"]["UnblendedCost"]["Amount"])
                   for r in result.get("ResultsByTime", []))
    except Exception:                              # noqa: BLE001
        # Unknown, and must not be reported as zero -- zero is one of the two
        # answers this call exists to distinguish.
        return None


def report(event=None, context=None):
    """One month, one line per tenant, three numbers each."""
    month = (event or {}).get("month")
    if not month:
        # Last complete month. The current one is always wrong and always
        # looks low, which is the worst shape for a billing artefact.
        today = _now().date()
        first = today.replace(day=1)
        last_month = first - datetime.timedelta(days=1)
        month = f"{last_month.year:04d}-{last_month.month:02d}"
    start, end = _month_bounds(month)

    try:
        models, contractual = rates()
    except (RatesNotSet, RatesUnreadable) as exc:
        out = {"record_type": "tenant-cost-report", "month": month,
               "produced": False,
               # WHICH of the two, not just that it failed. They send whoever
               # reads this to different people.
               "blocked_by": type(exc).__name__,
               "reason": str(exc)}
        print(json.dumps(out, default=str))
        return out

    # Both metrics, every run. See the module docstring: the day these diverge
    # is the day the uplift starts being billed on the wrong basis, and nothing
    # else in the platform would notice.
    grouped = _ce_month(

    accounts = _ce_month(
        start, end,
        [{"Type": "DIMENSION", "Key": "LINKED_ACCOUNT"},
         {"Type": "COST_CATEGORY", "Key": TENANT_CATEGORY}],
        ["UnblendedCost"])

        for group in result.get("Groups", []):
            account_id, tenant = (group["Keys"] + ["", ""])[:2]

        #

        # managed rate, or the reverse, and produce an invoice that looks
        # entirely correct. design 10: "Model A is materially less work than
        # Model B. The flat fee and percentage should differ accordingly."

        model = (event or {}).get("service_model") or "default"

            # report is a tenant nobody invoices.

        pct = float(rate["uplift_percent"])

        flat = round(flat_rate * account_count, 2)
        uplift = round(raw * pct / 100.0, 2)

            "tenant": tenant,
            "billable": True,
            "accounts": account_count,
            # THE THREE, separately. Never summed into one field here: a
            # consumer that wants a total can add them, and one that prints
            # whatever it is given cannot accidentally hide the split.
            "raw_aws_cost": raw,
            "flat_fee": flat,
            "flat_fee_basis": f"{account_count} account(s) x {flat_rate}",
            "uplift": uplift,

        "produced": True,
        "month": month,
        "period": {"start": start, "end_exclusive": end},
        "tenants": lines,
        # design 10 absorbs this rather than allocating it. Shown because the
        # position "the uplift covers it" is otherwise uncheckable. B-090.
        "shared_platform_cost": round(shared_total, 2),
        "rates_are_contractual": contractual,
        # See above. Zero groups means the categorisation is not answering,
        # not that the estate is empty.
        "cost_groups_seen": groups_seen,
    }

        # THREE causes, not two, and only one is a problem. Separated by asking
        # what the period cost WITHOUT any grouping -- which the first version
        # did not do, and so reported "the categories have not backfilled"
        # about a month in which nothing had been spent because the estate did
        # not yet exist.
        #
        #   ungrouped total is zero     nothing was spent. Not a problem.
        #   total > 0, no groups        categorisation is not answering. It is
        #                               either backfilling or misconfigured,
        #                               and both need somebody to look.
        total = _period_total(start, end)
        if total is None:
            out["coverage_warning"] = (
                "Cost Explorer returned no grouped results, and the ungrouped "
                "total could not be read either — so it is not known whether "
                "this period had no spend or whether the categorisation "
                "failed. No conclusion should be drawn from an empty report.")
        elif total == 0.0:
            out["coverage_note"] = (
                "No spend at all in this period, grouped or ungrouped. The "
                "report is empty because nothing was spent, not because the "
                "categorisation failed.")
        else:
            out["coverage_warning"] = (
                f"This period cost {total:.2f} ungrouped, and Cost Explorer "
                "returned NO grouped results. Spend exists and the Cost "
                "Categories are not accounting for it. Most likely they were "
                "created within the last 24 hours and are still backfilling; "
                "if not, check scripts/sync-cost-categories.sh has run. Do "
                "not read this report as an empty estate.")
    elif not lines:

        # answer, and a different one.
        out["coverage_note"] = (
            f"{groups_seen} cost group(s) found, none billable — every "
            "account in this period is kind=shared, which is AltDigital's own "
            "estate. Correct until a tenant account is vested.")

        out["warning"] = (
            "The rates used are NOT marked contractual. design 10's figures "
            "are indicative and it says the flat fee and percentage should "
            "differ by service model, priced before the first contract. This "
            "output is an estimate and must not be sent to a customer.")

        # applies to LIST price, and these have now diverged -- so the basis is
        # understated by exactly this amount and somebody has to decide.
        out["basis_warning"] = (
            f"Unblended and net-unblended cost differ by {discount_delta:.2f} "
            "this month, so negotiated discounts now exist. design 10 applies "
            "the uplift to LIST price because AltDigital carries the "
            "commitment risk and retains the arbitrage. This report used "
            "unblended cost, which no longer equals list price -- the uplift "
            "above is understated. See design 10, 'Percentage basis: gross'.")

    print(json.dumps(out, default=str))
    return out

def handler(event, context):
    return report(event, context)

module does not produce evidence; it recognises it, numbers it, records that it
is owed to Truveon, and hands it to a queue.

The ledger row is written BEFORE the queue send
------------------------------------------------
Same ordering, and the same reason, as execute.py writing its attempt before
performing a quorum action.

If the queue send came first, a crash between the two would leave a record in
flight that the ledger has no row for. It would be delivered, or not, and
either way nothing would ever notice its absence -- the gap detector can only
see holes in a sequence it knows was allocated.

Writing the ledger first means a crash leaves a `pending` row with no message.
That is visible: the row ages past the in-flight grace and is reported as a
gap. A false gap costs somebody ten minutes; a silent loss costs an audit.

------------------------------------------------------------------

against a tenant, and design 15's carve-out means it cannot be filed against a
partner either. The tempting behaviour is to drop it and move on, which would
mean a newly vested account producing evidence that silently goes nowhere --

kept and the attribution gap is visible.

import json
import os

import boto3

import record

ssm = boto3.client("ssm")

UNATTRIBUTED_TENANT = os.environ.get("EVIDENCE_UNATTRIBUTED_TENANT",

#

    # reasonable naming scheme would suggest. The first version of this table

    ("Config Rules Compliance Change", "aws.config",
     "config-compliance", "config-continuous-evaluation"),
    ("Security Hub Findings", "aws.securityhub",
     "security-finding", "security-finding-triage"),
    ("GuardDuty Finding", "aws.guardduty",
     "security-finding", "threat-detection"),
    ("change-reconciliation", "platform.change",
     "change-event", "change-management-reconciliation"),
    ("quorum-reverse", "platform.quorum",
     "change-event", "quorum-two-party-control"),
    ("Platform Incident Dossier", "platform.response",
     "operational", "security-incident-response"),
    ("Platform Incident Dossier", "platform.security",
     "operational", "security-incident-response"),
    ("", "platform.recovery",

def tenant_map():

    detail_type = event.get("detail-type") or ""
    source = event.get("source") or ""
    detail = event.get("detail") or {}

    # specific than the detail-type they share.
    record_type = detail.get("record_type") or ""
    for needle, src, category, control_ref in RECOGNISERS:

        "Source": "platform.evidence",

            "current_state": "ALARM",
            "routing": routing,

            "assessment": {"probable_cause": cause},
            "evidence_collection": detail,

               "reason": "not an evidence category",
               "detail_type": event.get("detail-type"),
               "source": event.get("source")}

        return out

        attribution = tenant_map().get(account_id)

        # and that is said out loud rather than each record being dropped.

              (f"The tenant map at {TENANT_MAP_PARAM} could not be read "
               f"({type(exc).__name__}). Evidence is still being collected and "
               "numbered, filed under the unattributed tenant, but it cannot "
               "be routed to a Truveon tenant until this is fixed."),
              {"account_id": account_id})

    if attribution is None:
        _emit("platform-evidence-unattributed-account",
              (f"Evidence arrived from account {account_id or 'unknown'}, "
               f"which is not in the tenant map. It has been numbered and "
               f"buffered under '{UNATTRIBUTED_TENANT}' so it is not lost, but "
               "it cannot reach a tenant's Truveon until the account is "
               "mapped. A newly vested account will look like this."),
              {"account_id": account_id, "category": category})

        tenant=attribution["tenant"],
        partner=attribution.get("partner"),
        category=category,
        source=event.get("source"),
        payload=event.get("detail") or {},
        control_ref=control_ref,
        occurred_at=event.get("time"),
        account_id=account_id or None,

    dynamodb.put_item(
        TableName=LEDGER_TABLE,
        Item={
            "PK": {"S": item["stream_id"]},
            "SK": {"S": f"{item['sequence']:012d}"},
            "sequence": {"N": str(item["sequence"])},
            "tenant": {"S": item["tenant"]},
            "partner": {"S": str(item.get("partner") or "")},
            "category": {"S": item["category"]},
            "emitted_at": {"S": item["emitted_at"]},
            "status": {"S": "pending"},
            "content_hash": {"S": item["content_hash"]},

        # collectors somehow got the same number -- a bug worth hearing about

        ConditionExpression="attribute_not_exists(PK)")

           "stream_id": item["stream_id"], "sequence": item["sequence"],
           "category": category, "tenant": item["tenant"]}
    print(json.dumps(out, default=str))
    return out

    return collect(event, context)

"""Proving nothing was silently dropped. Prompt 9.1's actual subject.

    Because we push, we must prove nothing was silently dropped.

    - Sequence numbering per tenant stream; gaps are detectable
    - Heartbeat per tenant -- absence of data is itself an event,
      distinguishable from a quiet month
    - Buffering -- ingestion queues so a Truveon outage delays delivery rather
      than losing it
    - Reconciliation -- periodic count comparison between source and Truveon

    A silently failed pipeline that looks like a clean month is the failure
    mode that destroys an audit. This is the control that prevents it.

The pipeline is not built to never drop a record
-------------------------------------------------
That is not achievable against an external endpoint nobody here controls. It is
built so that anything dropped is KNOWN, BOUNDED and EXPLAINABLE BY PERIOD.

    "We lost four hours on the 3rd, here is the range and here is why"
        -- an audit answer

    "Our counts do not match and we are not sure when"
        -- not one

Why these results are WRITTEN and not merely alerted
-----------------------------------------------------
design 15 puts the evidence pipeline inside AltDigital's own SOC 2 scope, which
design 04 does not mention. So the pipeline is not only the thing that carries
evidence for other controls -- it is itself a control in the report partners
rely on through the carve-out.

A SOC 2 Type II auditor asks whether a control operated THROUGHOUT the period.
A heartbeat that fired eight months ago and was acknowledged in a chat channel
proves nothing about the eleven months around it. So every heartbeat, every
detected gap and every count comparison is written as an evidence record in its
own right, in the `pipeline-completeness` category, and pushed like any other.

import datetime
import json
import os

import boto3

import record

dynamodb = boto3.client("dynamodb")
events_client = boto3.client("events")
ssm = boto3.client("ssm")

LEDGER_TABLE = os.environ.get("EVIDENCE_LEDGER_TABLE", "")
SEQUENCE_TABLE = os.environ.get("EVIDENCE_SEQUENCE_TABLE", "")
ALERT_BUS_NAME = os.environ.get("ALERT_BUS_NAME", "platform-alerts")
TENANT_MAP_PARAM = os.environ.get("EVIDENCE_TENANT_MAP_PARAM",
                                  "/platform/evidence/tenants")

# How long a record may sit undelivered before its absence counts as a gap.
#
# Not zero, and the reason is B-043 and B-081. A record allocated a moment ago
# is in flight: queued, retrying, or waiting on a Truveon that is briefly slow.
# Reporting those would raise a finding on every healthy run, and a finding
# that is always true is one that gets muted -- taking the real gaps with it.
#

# reported; a control nobody trusts is not.
INFLIGHT_GRACE_MINUTES = int(

#

def _iso(dt):

def _parse(value):

            str(value).replace("Z", "+00:00"))

    from an estate in perfect health -- and this is the control whose entire
    job is to notice absence.

    See the module docstring: the pipeline is in SOC 2 scope and must evidence

           "tenants": len(registry), "written": len(written),
           "failed": len(failed)}
    print(json.dumps(out, default=str))
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Gap detection
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def detect_gaps(event=None, context=None):
    """Sequence numbers allocated but never delivered, past the grace period.

    A gap is a hole in the ledger: number 41 and number 43 delivered, 42 not,
    and 42 allocated long enough ago that it is not merely in flight.

    Reported with its RANGE and its TIME, because that is what makes it an
    audit answer rather than an admission. "Records 42 to 61 in tenant X,
    between 09:14 and 13:02 on the 3rd" is bounded and explainable. "Counts do
    not match" is not.
    """
    try:
        registry = tenants()
    except TenantsUnknown as exc:
        out = {"record_type": "evidence-gap-scan", "scanned": False,
               "reason": str(exc)}
        print(json.dumps(out, default=str))
        return out

    cutoff = _now() - datetime.timedelta(minutes=INFLIGHT_GRACE_MINUTES)
    findings = []
    scanned = 0

    for tenant, facts in sorted(registry.items()):
        partner = (facts or {}).get("partner")
        for category in sorted(record.CATEGORIES):
            stream = record.stream_id(tenant, category)
            rows = _ledger_rows(stream)
            if rows is None:
                continue
            scanned += 1
            missing = _missing_sequences(rows, cutoff)
            if not missing:
                continue
            finding = {
                "stream_id": stream,
                "tenant": tenant,
                "partner": partner,
                "category": category,
                "missing_count": len(missing),
                # The RANGE, not the list. A four-hour outage can be thousands
                # of numbers, and a finding carrying all of them is one nobody
                # reads.
                "first_missing": missing[0],
                "last_missing": missing[-1],
                "window_start": rows.get("_window_start"),
                "window_end": rows.get("_window_end"),
            }
            findings.append(finding)
            # Persisted as evidence, not only alerted. A gap that was found and
            # explained is a passable audit answer; it has to be findable in
            # eight months to be one. D-016.
            _persist(tenant=tenant, partner=partner, kind="gap-detected",
                     control_ref="evidence-pipeline-completeness",
                     payload=finding)
            _emit({
                "record_type": "evidence-completeness-finding",
                "recorded_at": _iso(_now()),
                "current_state": "ALARM",
                "routing": "digest_and_jira",
                "alarm": {"name": "platform-evidence-sequence-gap",
                          "resource_id": stream},
                "assessment": {"probable_cause": (
                    f"{len(missing)} evidence record(s) in {stream} were "
                    f"allocated a sequence number and never delivered "
                    f"(numbers {missing[0]} to {missing[-1]}). They are past "
                    f"the {INFLIGHT_GRACE_MINUTES}-minute in-flight grace, so "
                    "this is loss rather than delay.")},
                "evidence_completeness": finding,
            })

    out = {"record_type": "evidence-gap-scan", "scanned": True,
           "streams": scanned, "gaps": len(findings),
           "grace_minutes": INFLIGHT_GRACE_MINUTES}
    print(json.dumps(out, default=str))
    return out


def _ledger_rows(stream_id):
    """Every ledger row for a stream, or None if the ledger is unreadable."""
    if not LEDGER_TABLE:
        return None
    rows = {}
    first, last = None, None
    try:
        paginator = dynamodb.get_paginator("query")
        for page in paginator.paginate(
                TableName=LEDGER_TABLE,
                KeyConditionExpression="PK = :p",
                ExpressionAttributeValues={":p": {"S": stream_id}}):
            for item in page.get("Items") or []:
                seq = int(item["sequence"]["N"])
                emitted = item.get("emitted_at", {}).get("S")
                rows[seq] = {
                    "status": item.get("status", {}).get("S"),
                    "emitted_at": emitted,
                }
                if emitted and (first is None or emitted < first):
                    first = emitted
                if emitted and (last is None or emitted > last):
                    last = emitted
    except Exception:                              # noqa: BLE001
        return None
    rows["_window_start"] = first
    rows["_window_end"] = last
    return rows


def _missing_sequences(rows, cutoff):
    """Allocated-but-undelivered numbers older than the grace period."""
    missing = []
    for seq, row in rows.items():
        if not isinstance(seq, int):
            continue
        if row.get("status") == "delivered":
            continue
        emitted = _parse(row.get("emitted_at"))
        if emitted is None or emitted > cutoff:
            # Still in flight. Not a gap yet, and calling it one is how this
            # control gets muted.
            continue
        missing.append(seq)
    return sorted(missing)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Count reconciliation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def reconcile_counts(event=None, context=None):
    """design 04's fourth control: periodic count comparison with Truveon.

    Asks both sides how many records exist for a stream over a window and
    compares. The window is by `emitted_at` -- the platform's clock -- because
    `occurred_at` is the source's, and a Config evaluation arriving late would
    otherwise make a healthy period look short on one side only.

    Counts alone prove less than they look like they do. Equal totals can hide
    one record lost and one duplicated, so the sequence RANGE is compared too:
    a window holding `count` records between `min_sequence` and `max_sequence`
    should satisfy `max - min + 1 == count`, and a stream that does not is
    reporting a total that does not describe its own contents.

    With no endpoint configured this does NOT report a match. It reports that
    no comparison was possible. B-088, and the same rule as everywhere in this
    module: an unanswerable question is not a negative answer.
    """
    endpoint = os.environ.get("TRUVEON_ENDPOINT", "").rstrip("/")
    window_hours = int(os.environ.get("EVIDENCE_RECONCILE_HOURS", "26"))
    until = _now()
    since = until - datetime.timedelta(hours=window_hours)

    if not endpoint:
        out = {"record_type": "evidence-count-reconciliation",
               "compared": False,
               "reason": ("TRUVEON_ENDPOINT is not configured, so the far side "
                          "of the comparison does not exist yet (B-088). No "
                          "conclusion is drawn about whether counts agree.")}
        _emit({
            "record_type": "evidence-completeness-finding",
            "recorded_at": _iso(_now()),
            "current_state": "ALARM",
            "routing": "digest",
            "alarm": {"name": "platform-evidence-reconciliation-impossible",
                      "resource_id": "truveon"},
            "assessment": {"probable_cause": out["reason"]},
        })
        print(json.dumps(out, default=str))
        return out

    try:
        registry = tenants()
    except TenantsUnknown as exc:
        out = {"record_type": "evidence-count-reconciliation",
               "compared": False, "reason": str(exc)}
        print(json.dumps(out, default=str))
        return out

    compared, mismatches = 0, []
    for tenant, facts in sorted(registry.items()):
        partner = (facts or {}).get("partner")
        for category in sorted(record.CATEGORIES):
            stream = record.stream_id(tenant, category)
            ours = _count_ours(stream, since, until)
            if ours is None:
                continue
            theirs = _count_theirs(endpoint, stream, since, until)
            compared += 1
            result = {
                "stream_id": stream, "tenant": tenant, "partner": partner,
                "window_start": _iso(since), "window_end": _iso(until),
                "source_count": ours["count"],
                "truveon_count": (theirs or {}).get("count"),
                "source_range": [ours["min"], ours["max"]],
                "truveon_range": [(theirs or {}).get("min_sequence"),
                                  (theirs or {}).get("max_sequence")],
                "unreadable": theirs is None,
            }
            agrees = (theirs is not None
                      and theirs.get("count") == ours["count"])
            result["agrees"] = agrees
            # Persisted whether or not it agrees. A comparison that matched is
            # evidence the control operated; only keeping the failures would
            # leave an auditor unable to tell "checked and fine" from "never
            # checked". D-016.
            _persist(tenant=tenant, partner=partner, kind="count-reconciled",
                     control_ref="evidence-pipeline-completeness",
                     payload=result)
            if not agrees:
                mismatches.append(result)
                _emit({
                    "record_type": "evidence-completeness-finding",
                    "recorded_at": _iso(_now()),
                    "current_state": "ALARM",
                    "routing": "digest_and_jira",
                    "alarm": {"name": "platform-evidence-count-mismatch",
                              "resource_id": stream},
                    "assessment": {"probable_cause": (
                        f"{stream}: the platform holds {ours['count']} record(s) "
                        f"for this window, Truveon reports "
                        f"{result['truveon_count']}. "
                        + ("Truveon could not be read, so this is not yet a "
                           "disagreement -- it is an unanswered question."
                           if theirs is None else
                           "The two stores disagree about a period that is "
                           "closed, so one of them is missing records."))},
                    "evidence_completeness": result,
                })

    out = {"record_type": "evidence-count-reconciliation", "compared": True,
           "streams": compared, "mismatches": len(mismatches),
           "window_hours": window_hours}
    print(json.dumps(out, default=str))
    return out


def _count_ours(stream_id, since, until):
    """How many records the platform allocated in this window."""
    rows = _ledger_rows(stream_id)
    if rows is None:
        return None
    seqs = []
    for seq, row in rows.items():
        if not isinstance(seq, int):
            continue
        emitted = _parse(row.get("emitted_at"))
        if emitted and since <= emitted <= until:
            seqs.append(seq)
    if not seqs:
        return None
    return {"count": len(seqs), "min": min(seqs), "max": max(seqs)}


def _count_theirs(endpoint, stream_id, since, until):
    """Truveon's count for the same window, or None if it cannot be asked.

    None is distinct from zero throughout. A Truveon that cannot be reached has
    not told us it holds nothing.
    """
    import urllib.error
    import urllib.parse
    import urllib.request
    try:
        import sender
        token = sender._token()
    except Exception:                              # noqa: BLE001
        return None
    query = urllib.parse.urlencode({
        "stream_id": stream_id, "from": _iso(since), "to": _iso(until)})
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        f"{endpoint}/v1/evidence/count?{query}",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
                 "Accept": "application/json"})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=20) as resp:
            return json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
    except Exception:                              # noqa: BLE001
        return None


HANDLERS = {"heartbeat": heartbeat, "detect_gaps": detect_gaps,
            "reconcile_counts": reconcile_counts}


def handler(event, context):
    action = (event or {}).get("action") or "heartbeat"
    fn = HANDLERS.get(action)
    if fn is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"unknown action '{action}'. Known: {', '.join(sorted(HANDLERS))}")
    return fn(event, context)

"""The evidence record, and the sequence number that makes gaps detectable.

Prompt 9.1, design/04-security-controls-and-evidence.md "Evidence pipeline to
Truveon".

    Because we push, we must prove nothing was silently dropped.
    [...] A silently failed pipeline that looks like a clean month is the
    failure mode that destroys an audit.

Sequence numbers are allocated ON INGEST, not on send
------------------------------------------------------
This is the decision the whole completeness argument rests on, and it is easy
to get backwards.

If a number were allocated when a record is successfully SENT, the sequence
would be contiguous by construction. It could never show a gap, because a
record that failed to send would simply never receive a number. The stream
would look perfect precisely when it was lossy -- "a clean month" in design
04's words.

Allocating on ingest means the number is minted the moment the platform becomes
aware of a piece of evidence, before anything can go wrong with delivery. A
record that is then lost leaves a hole at a known position, in a known tenant,
at a known time. The gap is the evidence that something went missing, and its
absence is the evidence that nothing did.

The cost is that a gap can also mean "sent but not yet acknowledged", which is
why the gap detector treats recent numbers as in-flight rather than missing.
A control that cried wolf on every in-flight record would be muted within a
week -- B-043, and B-081 after it.

Attribution travels with the record
-----------------------------------
design 15 makes AltDigital's SOC 2 the reference report that partners rely on
through a carve-out, and the chain is three deep: AWS is a subservice
organisation to AltDigital, AltDigital to the partner, the partner to the
client. A partner's auditor reading a record needs to know which entity's
control produced it.

So tenant and partner are ON the record rather than derivable from the account
id at query time. An account can be re-parented; evidence about what was true
in March must not change because an OU moved in September. D-016.

What is NOT on the record
-------------------------
A Trust Services Criteria reference. Framework mapping lives in Truveon, which
is the GRC tool, not here: a CC6.1 tag in the transport goes stale silently and
has to be maintained again for HIPAA, PCI and whatever the next tenant brings.
Records carry AltDigital's own control reference and Truveon maps it. D-016.
"""
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import os

import boto3

dynamodb = boto3.client("dynamodb")

SEQUENCE_TABLE = os.environ.get("EVIDENCE_SEQUENCE_TABLE", "")

# design 04's "What flows". Anything outside this set is a bug in the collector
# rather than a new category to be invented at runtime.
CATEGORIES = {
    "config-compliance",      # continuous control evidence
    "security-finding",       # Security Hub, normalised and severity-scored
    "change-event",           # CloudTrail-derived, reconciled against the register
    "operational",            # restore tests, instrumentation, remediation,
                              # JIT elevation, notification timestamps
    # The pipeline's own operation. design 04 does not list this, and design 15
    # puts the evidence pipeline inside AltDigital's own SOC 2 scope -- so
    # evidence that the pipeline worked is itself required evidence. D-016.
    "pipeline-completeness",
}


class SequenceUnavailable(Exception):
    """A sequence number could not be allocated.

    Distinct, and the caller must not proceed without one. A record sent
    without a sequence number is a record whose loss would be undetectable,
    which is worse than a record that was never sent -- the second leaves a
    gap and the first does not.
    """


def _now():
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)


def stream_id(tenant, category):
    """One sequence per tenant per category.

    Per CATEGORY as well as per tenant, deliberately. A single stream per
    tenant would interleave four sources with very different volumes and
    cadences, so a gap in the rare one -- restore test results, a handful a
    month -- would be invisible next to the chatty one. Separate streams mean a
    missing quarterly control is as detectable as a missing hourly finding.
    """
    return f"{tenant}#{category}"


def allocate(tenant, category):
    """The next sequence number for this stream. Atomic, monotonic, gapless.

    DynamoDB's ADD on a number is atomic, so two concurrent collectors cannot
    receive the same value and cannot skip one between them. That property is
    the reason this is a counter in a table rather than a timestamp or a uuid:
    both of those are unique and neither can prove that nothing is missing
    BETWEEN two records.

    Numbers are consumed even when the record is later dropped. That is the
    intent -- see the module docstring.
    """
    if category not in CATEGORIES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"'{category}' is not an evidence category. design 04 names: "
            f"{', '.join(sorted(CATEGORIES))}")
    if not SEQUENCE_TABLE:
        raise SequenceUnavailable(
            "EVIDENCE_SEQUENCE_TABLE is unset. No sequence number can be "
            "allocated, so nothing may be sent: an unnumbered record is one "
            "whose loss would be undetectable.")
    try:
        result = dynamodb.update_item(
            TableName=SEQUENCE_TABLE,
            Key={"stream_id": {"S": stream_id(tenant, category)}},
            UpdateExpression="ADD seq :one SET updated_at = :now",
            ExpressionAttributeValues={
                ":one": {"N": "1"},
                ":now": {"S": _now().isoformat()},
            },
            ReturnValues="UPDATED_NEW",
        )
    except Exception as exc:                       # noqa: BLE001
        raise SequenceUnavailable(
            f"could not allocate a sequence number for "
            f"{stream_id(tenant, category)}: {type(exc).__name__}. "
            "Nothing may be sent without one: an unnumbered record is one "
            "whose loss would be undetectable, which is worse than a record "
            "that was never sent. The second leaves a gap; the first does "
            "not.") from exc
    return int(result["Attributes"]["seq"]["N"])


def build(tenant, partner, category, source, payload,
          control_ref=None, occurred_at=None, account_id=None):
    """An evidence record, numbered and ready to buffer.

    `occurred_at` is when the EVENT happened; `emitted_at` is when the platform
    saw it. Both, because they differ -- a Config evaluation can arrive minutes
    late and an auditor asking "did this control operate on the 3rd" means the
    first, while anyone debugging the pipeline means the second.
    """
    sequence = allocate(tenant, category)
    emitted = _now()
    body = {
        "record_type": "evidence",
        "tenant": tenant,
        # Carried, not derived. See the module docstring: an account can be
        # re-parented and evidence about March must not change in September.
        "partner": partner,
        "account_id": account_id,
        "category": category,
        "stream_id": stream_id(tenant, category),
        "sequence": sequence,
        "source": source,
        "control_ref": control_ref,
        "occurred_at": occurred_at or emitted.isoformat(),
        "emitted_at": emitted.isoformat(),
        "payload": payload,
    }
    # Content hash over everything except the hash itself.
    #
    # Not a security control -- anything that can write the record can
    # recompute the hash. It is a TRANSPORT integrity check: it tells the
    # difference between "Truveon holds a different version of record 41" and
    # "Truveon holds record 41 unchanged", which is the question a count
    # comparison cannot answer.
    body["content_hash"] = hashlib.sha256(
        json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True, default=str).encode()).hexdigest()
    return body

"""Delivers evidence to Truveon, and refuses to lie about having done so.

Prompt 9.1. The contract is docs/truveon-ingestion-contract.md, written from
this side because AltDigital builds both ends -- so the API is set by what
design 04's completeness controls require rather than discovered from whatever
the endpoint happens to do. B-088.

The one thing this module must never do
---------------------------------------
Mark a record delivered when it is not.

A ledger row marked `delivered` is excluded from gap detection permanently.
That is the whole point of the ledger: it is how the platform stops looking.
So a premature acknowledgement does not merely lose a record -- it loses it
AND removes the mechanism that would have noticed. The stream reads clean, the
count reconciliation reads clean, and the evidence is gone.

Which is why, with no endpoint configured, this does NOT quietly succeed. It
leaves records pending and says the pipeline is not delivering. A stub that
acknowledged locally would reproduce design 04's "clean month" inside the
component built to prevent it:

    A silently failed pipeline that looks like a clean month is the failure
    mode that destroys an audit.

Retry is safe because ingest is idempotent
-------------------------------------------
The contract requires `POST /v1/evidence` to be idempotent on
`(stream_id, sequence)`: re-posting a sequence Truveon already holds is a
success. Without that, every retry -- after a timeout, a 5xx, or a crash
between sending and recording the send -- would create a duplicate, and the
count reconciliation would report a mismatch on an intact stream.

A 409 is different and is NOT retried. It means Truveon holds that sequence
with a different content hash, so one of the two stores is wrong and neither
side should guess which. That is a finding for a human.
"""
import datetime
import json
import os
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

import boto3

dynamodb = boto3.client("dynamodb")
events_client = boto3.client("events")
secrets = boto3.client("secretsmanager")
sqs = boto3.client("sqs")

LEDGER_TABLE = os.environ.get("EVIDENCE_LEDGER_TABLE", "")
ALERT_BUS_NAME = os.environ.get("ALERT_BUS_NAME", "platform-alerts")
TRUVEON_ENDPOINT = os.environ.get("TRUVEON_ENDPOINT", "").rstrip("/")
TRUVEON_SECRET = os.environ.get("TRUVEON_SECRET_NAME",
                                "platform/truveon/ingest")
TIMEOUT = int(os.environ.get("TRUVEON_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", "20"))
QUEUE_URL = os.environ.get("EVIDENCE_QUEUE_URL", "")
# Matches the gap detector's grace. The two must agree: a record replayed
# before it is considered a gap is wasted work, and one considered a gap before
# it is replayed is a finding raised against something already being fixed.
GRACE_MINUTES = int(os.environ.get("EVIDENCE_INFLIGHT_GRACE_MINUTES", "60"))

_AUTH = {}


class NotDelivered(Exception):
    """The record was not persisted by Truveon. Retryable."""


class ContentConflict(Exception):
    """Truveon holds this sequence with different content. NOT retryable."""


def _now():
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)


def _iso(dt):
    return dt.astimezone(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()


def _token():
    """Bearer token, cached for the execution environment.

    One credential for all tenants, not one per tenant. The `tenant` field
    carries the isolation and Truveon enforces it server-side.

    Per-tenant credentials sound stronger and are worse here: the platform
    would hold and rotate N secrets, and the failure mode is that one expires
    quietly and that tenant's evidence stops while every other tenant looks
    fine. One credential fails loudly for everybody, which is the direction
    this codebase keeps choosing.
    """
    if "token" not in _AUTH:
        raw = secrets.get_secret_value(SecretId=TRUVEON_SECRET)["SecretString"]
        try:
            _AUTH["token"] = json.loads(raw)["token"]
        except (ValueError, KeyError):
            # Tolerated: a bare token string rather than JSON. The secret is
            # set by hand and this is the likely shape of a mistake.
            _AUTH["token"] = raw.strip()
    return _AUTH["token"]


def _post(body):
    """One ingest call. Returns on persistence, raises otherwise."""
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        f"{TRUVEON_ENDPOINT}/v1/evidence",
        data=json.dumps(body, default=str).encode("utf-8"),
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {_token()}",
                 "Content-Type": "application/json",
                 "Accept": "application/json"},
        method="POST")
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=TIMEOUT) as resp:
            payload = resp.read().decode("utf-8")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        detail = ""
        try:
            detail = exc.read().decode("utf-8")[:400]
        except Exception:                          # noqa: BLE001
            pass
        if exc.code == 409:
            raise ContentConflict(
                f"Truveon holds {body['stream_id']} sequence "
                f"{body['sequence']} with different content: {detail}. "
                "One of the two stores is wrong and the platform will not "
                "guess which.") from exc
        raise NotDelivered(
            f"Truveon returned HTTP {exc.code}: {detail}") from exc
    except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, OSError) as exc:
        raise NotDelivered(f"could not reach Truveon: {exc}") from exc

    # The contract says 200 means persisted. Verify it SAYS so rather than
    # inferring persistence from the status code alone -- a proxy, a gateway or
    # a misconfigured stub can return 200 for something that never reached a
    # datastore, and this acknowledgement is what stops the platform looking.
    try:
        answer = json.loads(payload) if payload else {}
    except ValueError:
        raise NotDelivered(
            f"Truveon returned 200 with a body that is not JSON: "
            f"{payload[:200]}")
    if answer.get("stored") is not True:
        raise NotDelivered(
            "Truveon returned 200 but did not confirm storage "
            f"(stored={answer.get('stored')!r}). Treated as undelivered: an "
            "acknowledgement that does not mean persisted is one that would "
            "stop the platform looking for a record Truveon may still drop.")
    return answer


def _mark_delivered(stream_id, sequence):
    dynamodb.update_item(
        TableName=LEDGER_TABLE,
        Key={"PK": {"S": stream_id}, "SK": {"S": f"{sequence:012d}"}},
        UpdateExpression="SET #s = :d, delivered_at = :t",
        ExpressionAttributeNames={"#s": "status"},
        ExpressionAttributeValues={":d": {"S": "delivered"},
                                   ":t": {"S": _iso(_now())}},
        # Only a row that EXISTS may be marked delivered. Creating one here
        # would invent a delivery for a record the ledger never knew about,
        # which is a gap being papered over rather than closed.
        ConditionExpression="attribute_exists(PK)")


def _emit(name, cause, detail, routing="review_queue"):
    events_client.put_events(Entries=[{
        "EventBusName": ALERT_BUS_NAME,
        "Source": "platform.evidence",
        "DetailType": "evidence-completeness",
        "Detail": json.dumps({
            "record_type": "evidence-delivery-finding",
            "recorded_at": _iso(_now()),
            "current_state": "ALARM",
            "routing": routing,
            "alarm": {"name": name,
                      "resource_id": detail.get("stream_id", "evidence")},
            "assessment": {"probable_cause": cause},
            "evidence_delivery": detail,
        }, default=str),
    }])


def send(event, context=None):
    """Deliver one batch. Invoked by SQS, or directly with {"records": [...]}.

    Returns the SQS partial-batch shape so that a failure in one record redrives
    only that record. Failing the whole batch would re-deliver records already
    persisted -- harmless, because ingest is idempotent, but it would also
    delay every healthy record behind one poisoned one.
    """
    records = event.get("records")
    if records is None:
        records = [json.loads(r["body"]) for r in (event.get("Records") or [])]

    if not TRUVEON_ENDPOINT:
        # Deliberately not a silent success. See the module docstring: records
        # stay pending, the gap detector will see them age past the grace
        # period, and the pipeline reports that it is not delivering.
        _emit("platform-evidence-no-endpoint",
              (f"{len(records)} evidence record(s) could not be delivered: "
               "TRUVEON_ENDPOINT is not configured, so Truveon does not exist "
               "for this deployment yet (B-088). The records remain buffered "
               "and pending -- they are NOT lost, and they are not marked "
               "delivered. Set the endpoint and the backlog drains."),
              {"pending": len(records)})
        out = {"record_type": "evidence-delivery", "delivering": False,
               "pending": len(records), "reason": "no endpoint configured"}
        print(json.dumps(out, default=str))
        # Raising would redrive the batch forever and eventually DLQ it. The
        # records are already durable in the ledger; the queue has done its
        # job by handing them over, and the LEDGER is what remembers they are
        # undelivered.
        return out

    delivered, conflicts, failures = 0, [], []
    for body in records:
        stream_id = body.get("stream_id")
        sequence = body.get("sequence")
        try:
            _post(body)
            _mark_delivered(stream_id, sequence)
            delivered += 1
        except ContentConflict as exc:
            # Not retried. Retrying cannot resolve a disagreement about
            # content, and burning the redrive budget on it would hide it.
            conflicts.append({"stream_id": stream_id, "sequence": sequence,
                              "error": str(exc)})
            _emit("platform-evidence-content-conflict", str(exc),
                  {"stream_id": stream_id, "sequence": sequence},
                  routing="digest_and_jira")
        except NotDelivered as exc:
            failures.append({"stream_id": stream_id, "sequence": sequence,
                             "error": str(exc)})
        except Exception as exc:                   # noqa: BLE001
            failures.append({"stream_id": stream_id, "sequence": sequence,
                             "error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"})

    out = {"record_type": "evidence-delivery", "delivering": True,
           "delivered": delivered, "conflicts": len(conflicts),
           "failed": len(failures)}
    print(json.dumps(out, default=str))

    # Partial batch failure, so only the undelivered records redrive. A
    # conflict is NOT returned here: it will not succeed on retry and belongs
    # in front of a person instead.
    if failures and event.get("Records"):
        by_seq = {}
        for r in event["Records"]:
            b = json.loads(r["body"])
            by_seq[(b.get("stream_id"), b.get("sequence"))] = r["messageId"]
        out["batchItemFailures"] = [
            {"itemIdentifier": by_seq[(f["stream_id"], f["sequence"])]}
            for f in failures
            if (f["stream_id"], f["sequence"]) in by_seq]
    return out


def replay_pending(event=None, context=None):
    """Re-queue ledger rows that are still pending past the grace period.

    This is what closes the loop, and the pipeline is incomplete without it.

    The queue is a transport, not the record. Once `send` has taken a message
    it is gone from SQS whether or not delivery succeeded -- including the case
    where no endpoint is configured at all and nothing was even attempted. The
    LEDGER is what remembers a record is owed, so something has to read the
    ledger and put it back on the queue.

    Without this, the gap detector would find a hole, report it correctly, and
    nobody would have any way to fill it: the finding would be permanent and
    the evidence permanently missing. A detection with no remedy is only half a
    control.

    Safe to run repeatedly because ingest is idempotent on
    (stream_id, sequence) -- a record replayed after it was in fact delivered
    is accepted and changes nothing. That is the contract requirement in
    docs/truveon-ingestion-contract.md earning its place: without it, replay
    would manufacture duplicates and the count reconciliation would then report
    a mismatch on a stream this function had just repaired.
    """
    if not LEDGER_TABLE or not QUEUE_URL:
        out = {"record_type": "evidence-replay", "ran": False,
               "reason": "ledger table or queue not configured"}
        print(json.dumps(out, default=str))
        return out

    cutoff = _now() - datetime.timedelta(minutes=GRACE_MINUTES)
    requeued, scanned = 0, 0
    paginator = dynamodb.get_paginator("scan")
    for page in paginator.paginate(
            TableName=LEDGER_TABLE,
            FilterExpression="#s = :p",
            ExpressionAttributeNames={"#s": "status"},
            ExpressionAttributeValues={":p": {"S": "pending"}}):
        for item in page.get("Items") or []:
            scanned += 1
            emitted = item.get("emitted_at", {}).get("S")
            if emitted and emitted > _iso(cutoff):
                # Still in flight. Re-queueing now would duplicate work for
                # every healthy record on every run.
                continue
            body = item.get("body", {}).get("S")
            if not body:
                continue
            sqs.send_message(QueueUrl=QUEUE_URL, MessageBody=body)
            requeued += 1

    out = {"record_type": "evidence-replay", "ran": True,
           "pending_scanned": scanned, "requeued": requeued}
    if requeued:
        # Not a finding in itself -- replay working is the system healing. It
        # is reported so that a replay running every cycle, which means
        # delivery is failing persistently rather than transiently, is visible
        # rather than looking like quiet success.
        _emit("platform-evidence-replayed",
              (f"{requeued} evidence record(s) were re-queued for delivery "
               "after sitting undelivered past the grace period. One cycle of "
               "this is recovery; every cycle means delivery is failing and "
               "the replay is masking it."),
              {"requeued": requeued}, routing="digest")
    print(json.dumps(out, default=str))
    return out


HANDLERS = {"send": send, "replay_pending": replay_pending}


def handler(event, context):
    # SQS batches arrive with Records and no action; schedules name one.
    action = (event or {}).get("action")
    if action and action in HANDLERS:
        return HANDLERS[action](event, context)
    return send(event, context)
