#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Package change reconciliation and publish it to the artifact bucket.
#
#   scripts/publish-change.sh [--dry-run]
#
# One package: reconcile.py captures and compares, jira.py is the read-only
# client both it and the quorum pipeline (8.3) use.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) printf 'Usage: %s [--dry-run]\n' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

PY="$(command -v python || command -v python3)" || die "python not found."
TOOLING="$(get_param /org/account/altdig-infra-tooling)"
[[ -n "${TOOLING}" && "${TOOLING}" != "None" ]] \
  || die "Platform Tooling account not registered."

BUCKET="altdig-platform-artifacts-${TOOLING}"
BUILD="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "${BUILD}"' EXIT
> "${BUILD}/.sources"
for MODULE in reconcile jira filer; do
  cp "${REPO_ROOT}/change/src/${MODULE}.py" "${BUILD}/${MODULE}.py"
  printf '%s\n' "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/change/src/${MODULE}.py")" \
    >> "${BUILD}/.sources"
done

# Derived from the templates, not maintained by hand -- B-060, where a
# hand-written module list left two handlers out of the archive while the stack
# was already deployed with Lambdas pointing at them.
info "Checking every handler the templates reference is packaged"
for HANDLER in $(grep -hoE '^      Handler: [a-z]+\.handler' \
                   "${REPO_ROOT}"/change/*.yaml \
                 | awk '{print $2}' | cut -d. -f1 | sort -u); do
  [[ -f "${BUILD}/${HANDLER}.py" ]] \
    || die "the templates declare handler ${HANDLER}.handler but
      ${HANDLER}.py is not in the package. Add it to the MODULE list above."
  printf '  %s.py\n' "${HANDLER}"
done
ok "every referenced handler is present"

info "Checking they compile"
xargs "${PY}" -m py_compile < "${BUILD}/.sources" \
  || die "change sources do not compile. Nothing packaged."
rm -f "${BUILD}/.sources"
ok "compiles"

# The Jira client's whole safety argument is that it cannot write. A write
# method added later would be invisible in review of a large diff and would
# make the quorum control circular -- a credential able to edit issues can
# manufacture the approval it then verifies.
info "Checking the Jira client is still read-only"
"${PY}" - "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/change/src/jira.py")" <<'READONLYEOF'
import re
import sys

source = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8").read()

# Definitions matched at the START OF A LINE, not as substrings.
#
# The substring form false-positived on the docstring that EXPLAINS this
# guard: prose containing "def create_" tripped a check meant to find a
# function named create_something. A guard that fires on a comment about
# itself is one somebody works around rather than fixes, which is worse than
# not having it. Same lesson as the containment role check -- strip the prose,
# test the code.
definitions = re.findall(r"^def\s+(\w+)", source, re.M)
write_shaped = [d for d in definitions
                if d.startswith(("create_", "update_", "delete_", "transition",
                                 "add_comment", "post_", "put_"))]

# HTTP methods stay a substring test: urllib takes the method as a string
# argument, so there is no line-anchored form to match.
body = "\n".join(l for l in source.split("\n")
                 if not l.strip().startswith("#"))
methods = [m for m in ('method="POST"', "method='POST'", 'method="PUT"',
                       'method="DELETE"', 'method="PATCH"')
           if m in body]

hits = write_shaped + methods
if hits:
    sys.exit("jira.py now contains write-shaped code: " + ", ".join(hits)
             + "\n      A credential that can edit issues can manufacture the"
               "\n      approval the quorum pipeline then verifies.")
print(f"  {len(definitions)} function(s), none write-shaped")
READONLYEOF
[[ $? -eq 0 ]] || die "jira.py is not safe to publish."
ok "jira client is read-only"

# filer.py is ALLOWED to write -- that is its job. The line it may not cross is
# approving: filing a change and approving one are different acts, and if the
# platform could do both, the record it files would prove nothing.
info "Checking the filer cannot approve anything"
"${PY}" - "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/change/src/filer.py")" <<'NOAPPROVEEOF'
import re
import sys

# API PATHS, not English.
#
# The first version searched for the word "approve" anywhere in the file and
# matched the docstring explaining why approving is forbidden. That is the
# third time in this session a guard has fired on prose describing itself --
# jira.py's read-only check twice, and now this. The rule that finally
# generalises: a guard must match the CONSTRUCT it forbids, never a word that
# describes it.
#
# What the filer must never do is issue a request against an approval or
# transition endpoint, so the thing to examine is the set of API paths it
# names. Every one goes to _post or _get as a literal beginning "/rest/".
nl = chr(10)
source = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8").read()
paths = re.findall(r'["\'](/rest/[^"\']*)["\']', source)
#
# The first version also banned the whole servicedeskapi NAMESPACE, which
# was the same over-matching in a new costume: creating a JSM request and
# approving one both live under servicedeskapi, and banning the namespace
# banned the filer's actual job. A change record created through the plain
# issue API is not a JSM request at all -- no Request Type, so every
# servicedeskapi endpoint including approvals returns 404 for it -- which
# made the records unverifiable. That is the opposite of what this guard
# is for.
#
# Match the ACT, not the address space. Approving and transitioning are the
# forbidden acts. Creating is not.
bad = [p for p in paths
       if "approval" in p or "/transitions" in p
       or p.rstrip("/").endswith(("/approve", "/decline"))]
if bad:
    sys.exit("filer.py calls an approval or transition endpoint: "
             + ", ".join(bad) + nl
             + "      The platform may FILE a change and may not APPROVE one."
             + nl
             + "      A component that can do both proves nothing by doing"
             + nl + "      either.")
print(f"  {len(paths)} API path(s), none approval or transition")
NOAPPROVEEOF
[[ $? -eq 0 ]] || die "filer.py is not safe to publish."
ok "filer cannot approve"

info "Packaging"
zip_deterministic "${BUILD}"
HASH="$(package_hash "${BUILD}/package.zip")"
KEY="change/change-${HASH}.zip"

hr
log "Change package"
log "  account : altdig-infra-tooling (${TOOLING})"
log "  key     : ${KEY}"
log "  size    : $(wc -c < "${BUILD}/package.zip" | tr -d ' ') bytes"
hr

if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
  printf '%s DRY%s  would upload s3://%s/%s\n' "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}" "${BUCKET}" "${KEY}"
  exit 0
fi

CREDS="$(aws sts assume-role \
  --role-arn "arn:aws:iam::${TOOLING}:role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole" \
  --role-session-name publish-change \
  --query 'Credentials.[AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey,SessionToken]' \
  --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || true
[[ -n "${CREDS}" ]] || die "Could not assume into ${TOOLING}."
read -r AK SK ST <<<"${CREDS}"
unset AWS_PROFILE
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="${AK}" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="${SK}" AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="${ST}"

if MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws s3api head-object --bucket "${BUCKET}" --key "${KEY}" \
     >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  skip "identical package already published"
else
  MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws s3api put-object --bucket "${BUCKET}" --key "${KEY}" \
    --body "$(win_path "${BUILD}/package.zip")" >/dev/null
  ok "uploaded s3://${BUCKET}/${KEY}"
fi

hr
info "Deploy reconciliation into the Audit account:"
log "  scripts/deploy-to-account.sh --account altdig-security-audit \\"
log "    --template change/10-reconciliation.yaml --stack platform-change \\"
log "    ArtifactBucket=${BUCKET} ArtifactKey=${KEY} \\"
log "    JiraSite=\${PLATFORM_JIRA_SITE} \\"
log "    JiraDefaultChangeProject=\${PLATFORM_JIRA_DEFAULT_CHANGE_PROJECT} \\"
log "    LogsKeyArn=<alerts key> AlertTopicArn=<audit topic>"
log ""
info "Then publish the tenant facts the engine reads:"
log "  scripts/sync-tenant-facts.sh"
hr

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Package the commercial pipeline and publish it to the artifact bucket.
#
#   scripts/publish-commercial.sh [--dry-run]
#
# route.py is the whole module: design 12's fourth destination, and the
# structural separation between being informed and being the notifier.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) printf 'Usage: %s [--dry-run]\n' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

PY="$(command -v python || command -v python3)" || die "python not found."
TOOLING="$(get_param /org/account/altdig-infra-tooling)"
[[ -n "${TOOLING}" && "${TOOLING}" != "None" ]] \
  || die "Platform Tooling account not registered."

BUCKET="altdig-platform-artifacts-${TOOLING}"
BUILD="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "${BUILD}"' EXIT
> "${BUILD}/.sources"
for MODULE in route notify; do
  cp "${REPO_ROOT}/commercial/src/${MODULE}.py" "${BUILD}/${MODULE}.py"
  printf '%s\n' "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/commercial/src/${MODULE}.py")" \
    >> "${BUILD}/.sources"
done
# B-060: a hand-written module list left two handlers out of the archive while
# the stack was already deployed with Lambdas pointing at them.
info "Checking every handler the templates reference is packaged"
for HANDLER in $(grep -hoE '^      Handler: [a-z]+\.handler' \
                   "${REPO_ROOT}"/commercial/*.yaml \
                 | awk '{print $2}' | cut -d. -f1 | sort -u); do
  [[ -f "${BUILD}/${HANDLER}.py" ]] \
    || die "the templates declare handler ${HANDLER}.handler but
      ${HANDLER}.py is not in the package. Add it to the MODULE list above."
  printf '  %s.py\n' "${HANDLER}"
done
ok "every referenced handler is present"

info "Checking they compile"
xargs "${PY}" -m py_compile < "${BUILD}/.sources" \
  || die "commercial sources do not compile. Nothing packaged."
rm -f "${BUILD}/.sources"
ok "compiles"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The guard
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# design 12 asks that informed and notifier stay separate "or the distinction
# erodes the first time someone is being helpful under pressure". A convention
# erodes; this checks the structure that replaces it.

info "Checking informed is still structurally separate from notifier"
"${PY}" - "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/commercial/src/route.py")" <<'SEPEOF'
import re
import sys

nl = chr(10)
source = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8").read()

problems = []

# The awareness filter must be an ALLOW-list. A deny-list lets a field added
# upstream later flow straight through to the commercial channel -- and the
# fields added later are exactly the ones an incident turned out to need.
m = re.search(r"AWARENESS_FIELDS = \((.*?)\)", source, re.S)
if not m:
    problems.append(
        "AWARENESS_FIELDS has gone. Without an allow-list, a security incident "
        "reaches the commercial channel whole and somebody can notify from it.")
else:
    allowed = m.group(1)
    for leaky in ("affected", "individuals", "classification", "blast",
                  "principal", "finding", "objects"):
        if leaky in allowed:
            problems.append(
                f"'{leaky}' appears in AWARENESS_FIELDS. That is notifiable "
                "detail and must not reach the commercial channel.")

# to_awareness must build from the allow-list, not copy and delete.
if "to_awareness" not in source:
    problems.append("to_awareness has gone; nothing strips the incident.")
elif re.search(r"def to_awareness.*? del ", source, re.S):
    problems.append(
        "to_awareness deletes fields rather than selecting them. Deleting is a "
        "deny-list wearing different clothes: a new field survives it.")

# Refusing to emit without a notifier is the other half of the structure.
if "NotifierUnknown" not in source:
    problems.append(
        "the router no longer refuses to emit when the notifier is unknown. An "
        "awareness event naming nobody leaves the reader as the only candidate.")

if problems:
    sys.exit("route.py has lost the separation:" + nl
             + nl.join("      - " + p for p in problems))
print("  allow-list intact; refuses to emit without a named notifier")
SEPEOF
[[ $? -eq 0 ]] || die "route.py is not safe to publish."
ok "informed is not notifier"

info "Packaging"
zip_deterministic "${BUILD}"
HASH="$(package_hash "${BUILD}/package.zip")"
KEY="commercial/commercial-${HASH}.zip"

hr
log "Commercial package"
log "  account : altdig-infra-tooling (${TOOLING})"
log "  key     : ${KEY}"
log "  size    : $(wc -c < "${BUILD}/package.zip" | tr -d ' ') bytes"
hr

if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
  printf '%s DRY%s  would upload s3://%s/%s\n' "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}" "${BUCKET}" "${KEY}"
  exit 0
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Package declaration and containment, and publish to the artifact bucket.
#
#   scripts/publish-containment.sh [--dry-run]
#
# One package, five handlers: declare.py creates the incident, contain.py runs
# the sequence, readout.py assembles the dossier, clock.py counts the
# notification deadlines, and exercise.py drills the whole thing monthly. All
# five read or write the same append-only incident record, so they are
# deployed together and cannot drift apart.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) printf 'Usage: %s [--dry-run]\n' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

PY="$(command -v python || command -v python3)" || die "python not found."
TOOLING="$(get_param /org/account/altdig-infra-tooling)"
[[ -n "${TOOLING}" && "${TOOLING}" != "None" ]] \
  || die "Platform Tooling account not registered."

BUCKET="altdig-platform-artifacts-${TOOLING}"
BUILD="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "${BUILD}"' EXIT
> "${BUILD}/.sources"
for MODULE in contain declare readout clock exercise; do
  cp "${REPO_ROOT}/containment/src/${MODULE}.py" "${BUILD}/${MODULE}.py"
  printf '%s\n' "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/containment/src/${MODULE}.py")" \
    >> "${BUILD}/.sources"
done

# Every handler the template names, checked against what is actually in the
# package. This list was previously written out by hand and a silent edit
# failure left readout.py and clock.py out of the archive while the stack had
# already been deployed with Lambdas pointing at them -- functions that would
# have failed at invocation with "Unable to import module", during an incident.
# EVERY containment template, not one of them. Reading 10-containment.yaml
# alone reproduced the same shape of gap as the hand-maintained module list it
# replaced: exercise.handler is declared in 40-exercise.yaml and went unchecked.
info "Checking every handler the templates reference is packaged"
for HANDLER in $(grep -hoE '^      Handler: [a-z]+\.handler' \
                   "${REPO_ROOT}"/containment/*.yaml \
                 | awk '{print $2}' | cut -d. -f1 | sort -u); do
  [[ -f "${BUILD}/${HANDLER}.py" ]] \
    || die "the template declares handler ${HANDLER}.handler but
      ${HANDLER}.py is not in the package. Add it to the MODULE list above."
  printf '  %s.py\n' "${HANDLER}"
done
ok "every referenced handler is present"

info "Checking they all compile"
xargs "${PY}" -m py_compile < "${BUILD}/.sources" \
  || die "containment sources do not compile. Nothing packaged."
rm -f "${BUILD}/.sources"
ok "compiles"

# The state machine names six stages. One it does not implement fails at RUN
# time -- during an incident -- with "unknown step". Checked here instead.
info "Checking the state machine's stages exist in contain.py"
"${PY}" - "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/containment/10-containment.yaml")" \
          "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/containment/src/contain.py")" <<'CHECKEOF'
import re
import sys

asl = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8").read()
src = open(sys.argv[2], encoding="utf-8").read()

wanted = set(re.findall(r'"step":\s*"([a-z_]+)"', asl))
block = re.search(r"STEPS = \{(.*?)\}", src, re.S)
if block is None:
    sys.exit("could not find STEPS in contain.py")
have = set(re.findall(r'"([a-z_]+)":', block.group(1)))

missing = wanted - have
if missing:
    sys.exit("state machine calls stages contain.py does not implement: "
             + ", ".join(sorted(missing)))
print(f"  {len(wanted)} stage(s) matched: {', '.join(sorted(wanted))}")
unused = have - wanted
if unused:
    print(f"  note: unused stage(s): {', '.join(sorted(unused))}")
CHECKEOF
[[ $? -eq 0 ]] || die "state machine and contain.py have diverged."
ok "state machine and contain.py agree"

# The whole security argument of the responder role is that it cannot destroy
# evidence. That is a property of a list, and a list is easy to extend without
# noticing. Checked on every publish rather than trusted to review.
info "Checking the responder role grants nothing destructive"
"${PY}" - "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/containment/00-responder-role.yaml")" <<'DENYEOF'
import sys

forbidden = (
    "TerminateInstances", "DeleteSnapshot", "DeleteVolume", "StopInstances",
    "DeleteRole", "DeleteUser", "DeleteRolePolicy", "DeleteUserPolicy",
    "DeleteDBInstance", "DeleteObject", "DeleteBucket", "DeleteLogGroup",
    "DeleteTrail", "StopLogging", "ScheduleKeyDeletion", "DeleteBackupVault",
    "DeleteRecoveryPoint", "DeregisterImage",
)
# Comments out: the header promises these are absent, in prose, using the very
# words being searched for.
body = "\n".join(l for l in open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n")
                 if not l.strip().startswith("#"))
hits = [f for f in forbidden if f in body]
if hits:
    sys.exit("responder role grants destructive action(s): " + ", ".join(hits)
             + "\n      design 07: automation may never terminate, delete, "
               "deregister, roll back or purge.")
print(f"  none of {len(forbidden)} destructive actions present")
DENYEOF
[[ $? -eq 0 ]] || die "responder role is not safe to publish."
ok "responder role holds nothing destructive"

info "Packaging"
zip_deterministic "${BUILD}"
HASH="$(package_hash "${BUILD}/package.zip")"
KEY="containment/containment-${HASH}.zip"

hr
log "Containment package"
log "  account : altdig-infra-tooling (${TOOLING})"
log "  key     : ${KEY}"
log "  size    : $(wc -c < "${BUILD}/package.zip" | tr -d ' ') bytes"
hr

if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
  printf '%s DRY%s  would upload s3://%s/%s\n' "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}" "${BUCKET}" "${KEY}"
  exit 0
fi

CREDS="$(aws sts assume-role \
  --role-arn "arn:aws:iam::${TOOLING}:role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole" \
  --role-session-name publish-containment \
  --query 'Credentials.[AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey,SessionToken]' \
  --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || true
[[ -n "${CREDS}" ]] || die "Could not assume into ${TOOLING}."
read -r AK SK ST <<<"${CREDS}"
unset AWS_PROFILE
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="${AK}" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="${SK}" AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="${ST}"

if MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws s3api head-object --bucket "${BUCKET}" --key "${KEY}" \
     >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  skip "identical package already published"
else
  MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws s3api put-object --bucket "${BUCKET}" --key "${KEY}" \
    --body "$(win_path "${BUILD}/package.zip")" >/dev/null
  ok "uploaded s3://${BUCKET}/${KEY}"
fi

hr
info "1. Deploy containment into the Audit account:"
log "  scripts/deploy-to-account.sh --account altdig-security-audit \\"
log "    --template containment/10-containment.yaml --stack platform-containment \\"
log "    ArtifactBucket=${BUCKET} ArtifactKey=${KEY} \\"
log "    AlertTopicArn=<audit alerts topic>"
log ""
info "2. Then the member-side responder role, which trusts the role that"
log "   stack just created:"
log "  scripts/deploy-stackset.sh --name platform-security-responder \\"
log "    --template containment/00-responder-role.yaml --ou sandbox \\"
log "    ContainmentRoleArn=<ContainmentRoleArn output from step 1> \\"
log "    ForensicsAccountId=<forensics account>"
hr
log "Order matters: the responder role names the containment role in its trust"
log "policy, and IAM rejects a trust policy naming a principal that does not"
log "exist yet."
hr

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Package the evidence pipeline and publish it to the artifact bucket.
#
#   scripts/publish-evidence.sh [--dry-run]
#
# collect.py numbers, sender.py delivers, completeness.py proves nothing was
# dropped, record.py is the shape they share.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) printf 'Usage: %s [--dry-run]\n' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

PY="$(command -v python || command -v python3)" || die "python not found."
TOOLING="$(get_param /org/account/altdig-infra-tooling)"
[[ -n "${TOOLING}" && "${TOOLING}" != "None" ]] \
  || die "Platform Tooling account not registered."

BUCKET="altdig-platform-artifacts-${TOOLING}"
BUILD="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "${BUILD}"' EXIT
> "${BUILD}/.sources"
for MODULE in record collect sender completeness; do
  cp "${REPO_ROOT}/evidence/src/${MODULE}.py" "${BUILD}/${MODULE}.py"
  printf '%s\n' "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/evidence/src/${MODULE}.py")" \
    >> "${BUILD}/.sources"
done

# B-060: a hand-written module list left two handlers out of the archive while
# the stack was already deployed with Lambdas pointing at them.
info "Checking every handler the templates reference is packaged"
for HANDLER in $(grep -hoE '^      Handler: [a-z]+\.handler' \
                   "${REPO_ROOT}"/evidence/*.yaml \
                 | awk '{print $2}' | cut -d. -f1 | sort -u); do
  [[ -f "${BUILD}/${HANDLER}.py" ]] \
    || die "the templates declare handler ${HANDLER}.handler but
      ${HANDLER}.py is not in the package."
  printf '  %s.py\n' "${HANDLER}"
done
ok "every referenced handler is present"

info "Checking they compile"
xargs "${PY}" -m py_compile < "${BUILD}/.sources" \
  || die "evidence sources do not compile. Nothing packaged."
rm -f "${BUILD}/.sources"
ok "compiles"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The guards
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Each protects a property whose loss would leave a pipeline that looks
# healthier than it is -- which is the exact failure design 04 names. None of
# them would fail a test or an alarm if removed.
#
# Each matches the CONSTRUCT, never a word describing it. Six guards in this
# codebase have now fired on something that resembles the offence rather than
# committing it -- prose describing the rule, an ARN that was infrastructure
# rather than a target, and below, a function DEFINITION mistaken for a call.

info "Checking the sequence is still allocated on ingest"
"${PY}" - "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/evidence/src/record.py")" <<'SEQEOF'
import re
import sys

nl = chr(10)
source = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8").read()

# `build` must allocate. If a future edit moved allocation to delivery, the
# sequence would become contiguous by construction and a gap would be
# impossible to observe -- every stream perfect, especially the lossy ones.
#
# Matched inside the function body rather than anywhere in the file, because
# the docstring discusses allocation at length.
match = re.search(r"^def build\(.*?(?=^def |\Z)", source, re.M | re.S)
if not match:
    sys.exit("record.build has gone. Nothing else numbers evidence.")
body = nl.join(l for l in match.group(0).split(nl)
               if not l.strip().startswith("#"))
if "allocate(" not in body:
    sys.exit("record.build no longer allocates a sequence number." + nl
             + "      Allocating anywhere later makes the sequence contiguous"
             + nl + "      by construction, and a dropped record leaves no"
             + nl + "      gap. The stream reads clean when it is lossy.")
print("  build() allocates")
SEQEOF
[[ $? -eq 0 ]] || die "record.py is not safe to publish."
ok "sequence allocated on ingest"

info "Checking the ledger is written before the queue"
"${PY}" - "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/evidence/src/collect.py")" <<'ORDEREOF'
import sys

nl = chr(10)
source = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8").read()
body = nl.join(l for l in source.split(nl) if not l.strip().startswith("#"))

put = body.find("put_item(")
send = body.find("send_message(")
if put < 0:
    sys.exit("collect.py no longer writes a ledger row. A record with no row"
             + nl + "      cannot be missed, because nothing knows it exists.")
if send >= 0 and send < put:
    sys.exit("collect.py queues before writing the ledger." + nl
             + "      A crash between the two would leave a record in flight"
             + nl + "      with no row behind it: delivered or not, nothing"
             + nl + "      would ever notice its absence.")
print("  ledger write precedes the queue send")
ORDEREOF
[[ $? -eq 0 ]] || die "collect.py is not safe to publish."
ok "ledger precedes queue"

info "Checking the sender will not claim a delivery it did not make"
"${PY}" - "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/evidence/src/sender.py")" <<'SENDEOF'
import re
import sys

nl = chr(10)
source = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8").read()
body = nl.join(l for l in source.split(nl) if not l.strip().startswith("#"))

problems = []

# A 200 is not enough. The contract says the response must say `stored: true`,
# because a proxy or a misconfigured stub returns 200 for things that never
# reached a datastore -- and this acknowledgement is what stops the gap
# detector looking at that record forever.
if '"stored"' not in body and "'stored'" not in body:
    problems.append(
        "the sender no longer checks that Truveon confirmed STORAGE. A bare "
        "200 would mark records delivered, and a delivered row is excluded "
        "from gap detection permanently.")

# With no endpoint, nothing may be marked delivered: the
# `not TRUVEON_ENDPOINT` branch has to return before any _mark_delivered CALL.
#
# Checked inside send() only. The first version searched the whole file and
# matched the DEFINITION of _mark_delivered, which sits above send() as any
# helper would -- so it reported a control lost on correct code. Sixth guard in
# this codebase to match a shape instead of a construct; the definition and the
# call look identical to a substring search and mean opposite things.
send_body = re.search(r"^def send\(.*?(?=^def |\Z)", body, re.M | re.S)
send_body = send_body.group(0) if send_body else ""
no_endpoint = send_body.find("if not TRUVEON_ENDPOINT")
first_mark = send_body.find("_mark_delivered(")
if not send_body:
    problems.append("send() has gone from sender.py.")
elif no_endpoint < 0:
    problems.append(
        "the sender no longer has a no-endpoint branch. With TRUVEON_ENDPOINT "
        "unset it would attempt delivery against an empty URL and the failure "
        "path would decide what happens -- rather than the pipeline stating "
        "plainly that it is not delivering. B-088.")
elif first_mark >= 0 and first_mark < no_endpoint:
    problems.append(
        "a record can be marked delivered before the no-endpoint check.")

if problems:
    sys.exit("sender.py has lost a control:" + nl
             + nl.join("      - " + p for p in problems))
print("  storage confirmed before delivery is recorded")
SENDEOF
[[ $? -eq 0 ]] || die "sender.py is not safe to publish."
ok "delivery is only claimed when confirmed"

info "Checking an unanswerable question is not reported as a clean result"
"${PY}" - "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/evidence/src/completeness.py")" <<'HONESTEOF'
import sys

nl = chr(10)
source = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8").read()

# B-042, B-054, B-080, B-086. Four times in this codebase an unreadable source
# has been reported as a negative result. The tenant list is this module's
# version of that trap: zero tenants checked must not read as zero problems.
if "TenantsUnknown" not in source:
    sys.exit("completeness.py no longer distinguishes an unknown tenant list"
             + nl + "      from a healthy one. A run over zero tenants writes"
             + nl + "      zero heartbeats and reports success, which is"
             + nl + "      indistinguishable from a perfect estate.")
if '"compared": False' not in source and "'compared': False" not in source:
    sys.exit("the count reconciliation no longer reports when it could NOT"
             + nl + "      compare. Silence from Truveon is not agreement.")
print("  unknown tenants and unreachable Truveon both report as unanswered")
HONESTEOF
[[ $? -eq 0 ]] || die "completeness.py is not safe to publish."
ok "unanswerable is not reported as clean"

info "Packaging"
zip_deterministic "${BUILD}"
HASH="$(package_hash "${BUILD}/package.zip")"
KEY="evidence/evidence-${HASH}.zip"

hr
log "Evidence package"
log "  account : altdig-infra-tooling (${TOOLING})"
log "  key     : ${KEY}"
log "  size    : $(wc -c < "${BUILD}/package.zip" | tr -d ' ') bytes"
hr

if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
  printf '%s DRY%s  would upload s3://%s/%s\n' "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}" "${BUCKET}" "${KEY}"
  exit 0
fi

CREDS="$(aws sts assume-role \
  --role-arn "arn:aws:iam::${TOOLING}:role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole" \
  --role-session-name publish-evidence \
  --query 'Credentials.[AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey,SessionToken]' \
  --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || true
[[ -n "${CREDS}" ]] || die "Could not assume into ${TOOLING}."
read -r AK SK ST <<<"${CREDS}"
unset AWS_PROFILE
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="${AK}" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="${SK}" AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="${ST}"

if MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws s3api head-object --bucket "${BUCKET}" --key "${KEY}" \
     >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  skip "identical package already published"
else
  MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws s3api put-object --bucket "${BUCKET}" --key "${KEY}" \
    --body "$(win_path "${BUILD}/package.zip")" >/dev/null
  ok "uploaded s3://${BUCKET}/${KEY}"
fi

hr
info "Deploy into the Audit account:"
log "  scripts/deploy-to-account.sh --account altdig-security-audit \\"
log "    --template evidence/10-evidence.yaml --stack platform-evidence \\"
log "    ArtifactBucket=${BUCKET} ArtifactKey=${KEY} \\"
log "    LogsKeyArn=<alerts key>"
log ""
info "TruveonEndpoint is deliberately left empty until the endpoint exists."
log "  Evidence is collected, numbered and buffered meanwhile; it is NOT"
log "  marked delivered, and the backlog drains when the endpoint is set."
log "  B-088, docs/truveon-ingestion-contract.md"

log "  scripts/sync-evidence-tenants.sh"
hr

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Package the instrumentation Lambda and publish it to the artifact bucket.
#
#   scripts/publish-instrumentation.sh [--dry-run]
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What this does that a plain zip does not
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Ships design/06a-alarm-specification.yaml as the configuration, converted
#    to JSON.
#
#    06a is AUTHORITATIVE and is consumed directly. There is deliberately no
#    copy under instrumentation/ — an earlier version kept its own
#    alarm-sets.yaml, written before 06a existed, and two copies of an
#    authoritative document disagree silently while the wrong one is always the
#    one somebody edits.
#
#    JSON because the Lambda runtime ships boto3 but not PyYAML, and vendoring
#    PyYAML for one safe_load would add a dependency to audit inside a function
#    that creates alarms in every member account. Authoring stays YAML so 06a's
#    comments survive; only the data ships.
#
# 2. VALIDATES the specification first. A malformed 06a would otherwise surface
#    as every invocation erroring at cold start, in every member account, with
#    a stack trace instead of a reason.
#
#    One package, two handlers. drift.py imports handler.py to reuse
#    plan_alarms — they must never disagree about what an alarm should be, and
#    shipping them separately would make that possible.
#
# 3. Publishes under a CONTENT-ADDRESSED key. CloudFormation decides whether to
#    update a Lambda by comparing S3Key — publish new code to the same key and
#    every member account keeps running the old one while the stack reports
#    itself current.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) printf 'Usage: %s [--dry-run]\n' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Package the quorum pipeline and publish it to the artifact bucket.
#
#   scripts/publish-quorum.sh [--dry-run]
#
# verify.py decides, execute.py acts, reverse.py proves the negative. jira.py
# is the same read-only client reconciliation uses, copied in rather than
# duplicated -- one client, one place where a Jira quirk gets fixed.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) printf 'Usage: %s [--dry-run]\n' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

PY="$(command -v python || command -v python3)" || die "python not found."
TOOLING="$(get_param /org/account/altdig-infra-tooling)"
[[ -n "${TOOLING}" && "${TOOLING}" != "None" ]] \
  || die "Platform Tooling account not registered."

BUCKET="altdig-platform-artifacts-${TOOLING}"
BUILD="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "${BUILD}"' EXIT
> "${BUILD}/.sources"
for MODULE in verify execute reverse; do
  cp "${REPO_ROOT}/quorum/src/${MODULE}.py" "${BUILD}/${MODULE}.py"
  printf '%s\n' "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/quorum/src/${MODULE}.py")" \
    >> "${BUILD}/.sources"
done
# Shared with 8.2. Copied at package time rather than vendored, so a fix to the
# Jira client reaches both pipelines.
cp "${REPO_ROOT}/change/src/jira.py" "${BUILD}/jira.py"
printf '%s\n' "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/change/src/jira.py")" \
  >> "${BUILD}/.sources"

# B-060: a hand-written module list left two handlers out of the archive while
# the stack was already deployed with Lambdas pointing at them.
info "Checking every handler the templates reference is packaged"
for HANDLER in $(grep -hoE '^      Handler: [a-z]+\.handler' \
                   "${REPO_ROOT}"/quorum/*.yaml \
                 | awk '{print $2}' | cut -d. -f1 | sort -u); do
  [[ -f "${BUILD}/${HANDLER}.py" ]] \
    || die "the templates declare handler ${HANDLER}.handler but
      ${HANDLER}.py is not in the package. Add it to the MODULE list above."
  printf '  %s.py\n' "${HANDLER}"
done
ok "every referenced handler is present"

info "Checking they compile"
xargs "${PY}" -m py_compile < "${BUILD}/.sources" \
  || die "quorum sources do not compile. Nothing packaged."
rm -f "${BUILD}/.sources"
ok "compiles"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The guards
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Each one protects a control that would disappear SILENTLY. That is the test
# for whether a guard earns its place here: not "could this be wrong" but
# "if this were wrong, would anything fail visibly?" Nothing below would.
#
# And each matches the CONSTRUCT it forbids, never a word that describes it.
# Four guards in this codebase have fired on their own explanatory prose.

info "Checking the verifier cannot act"
"${PY}" - "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/quorum/src/verify.py")" <<'VERIFYEOF'
import re
import sys

nl = chr(10)
source = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8").read()

# verify.py decides whether an action is permitted. If it could also perform
# one, or write to the evidence table, it could manufacture the record of its
# own decision -- the same circularity that keeps jira.py read-only.
#
# boto3 client METHOD CALLS, not words. `.put_item(` is a construct; "put" in
# a sentence is not.
forbidden = [
    "assume_role(", "put_item(", "update_item(", "delete_item(",
    "schedule_key_deletion(", "delete_backup_vault(", "stop_logging(",
    "delete_trail(", "remove_account_from_organization(",
    "stop_configuration_recorder(", "put_events(",
]
body = nl.join(l for l in source.split(nl) if not l.strip().startswith("#"))
hits = [f for f in forbidden if f in body]
if hits:
    sys.exit("verify.py can act, not just judge: " + ", ".join(hits) + nl
             + "      A component that decides whether an action is permitted"
             + nl + "      must not be able to perform it or to record its own"
             + nl + "      decision.")
print(f"  no acting calls; {len(source.splitlines())} lines checked")
VERIFYEOF
[[ $? -eq 0 ]] || die "verify.py is not safe to publish."
ok "the verifier only judges"

info "Checking the executor still narrows its credentials"
"${PY}" - "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/quorum/src/execute.py")" <<'EXECEOF'
import re
import sys

nl = chr(10)
source = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8").read()

problems = []

# THE control. execute.py assumes the executor role with a session policy
# scoped to the single approved resource, so its credentials cannot express a
# request against anything else.
#
# Delete the `Policy=` argument and everything still works -- every test
# passes, the approved action succeeds, and the only difference is that a bug
# passing the wrong ARN would now delete the wrong thing instead of getting
# AccessDenied. Nothing fails visibly. That is exactly what a guard is for.
if not re.search(r"assume_role\([^)]*Policy\s*=", source, re.S):
    problems.append(
        "assume_role is called without a session Policy. The credentials "
        "would carry the executor role's FULL permissions instead of being "
        "narrowed to the approved resource.")

# The session name is what ties every CloudTrail entry to the change record
# that authorised it, and the executor role's trust policy requires the shape.
if not re.search(r"RoleSessionName\s*=", source):
    problems.append(
        "assume_role is called without a RoleSessionName. CloudTrail would "
        "carry no link to the authorising change record, and reverse.py "
        "would report every action as having come from outside the pipeline.")
if 'f"quorum-{' not in source and "'quorum-'" not in source:
    problems.append(
        "the session name no longer embeds the issue key. The trust policy "
        "requires quorum-*, so this would fail closed -- but reverse.py's "
        "whole method depends on the key being IN the name.")

# It must re-verify before acting. The verification that gated the state
# machine can be minutes old.
if "verify.verify(" not in source:
    problems.append(
        "execute.py no longer re-verifies before acting. Time-of-check to "
        "time-of-use: the record could be edited between the gate and the "
        "action.")

# It must never carry a TARGET of its own. Every resource comes from the
# approved record; a literal target ARN here would be something nobody
# approved.
#
# IAM role ARNs are exempt, and the exemption is the point rather than a
# loophole. The one ARN this module legitimately builds is the executor
# role it assumes -- that is infrastructure, not a target. A target is a
# KMS key, a vault, a trail or an account, and none of those is a role.
#
# The first version flagged every arn: literal and tripped on the
# assume_role line, which is the FIFTH guard in this codebase to fire on
# something that describes the offence rather than commits it. The rule
# that keeps being relearned: match the construct, never the shape.
ARN_LITERAL = r"""["'](arn:aws:[^"']*)["']"""

literals = [a for a in re.findall(ARN_LITERAL, source)
            if not a.startswith("arn:aws:iam:")]
if literals:
    problems.append(
        "execute.py names resource ARNs literally: " + ", ".join(literals)
        + ". Targets come from the approved change record, never from code.")

if problems:
    sys.exit("execute.py has lost a control:" + nl
             + nl.join("      - " + p for p in problems))
print("  session policy, session name, re-verification, no literal targets")
EXECEOF
[[ $? -eq 0 ]] || die "execute.py is not safe to publish."
ok "the executor narrows its own credentials"

info "Checking the reverse sweep stays read-only"
"${PY}" - "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/quorum/src/reverse.py")" <<'REVEOF'
import sys

nl = chr(10)
source = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8").read()
body = nl.join(l for l in source.split(nl) if not l.strip().startswith("#"))

# reverse.py reads CloudTrail and reports. It must not be able to "fix"
# anything it finds: an unapproved key deletion is a finding for a human, and
# a sweep that could act on its own findings would be automated remediation
# against the CLAUDE.md rule -- and would be doing so on the strength of a
# CloudTrail parse.
forbidden = ["schedule_key_deletion(", "delete_backup_vault(", "stop_logging(",
             "delete_trail(", "remove_account_from_organization(",
             "stop_configuration_recorder(", "put_item(", "delete_item(",
             "attach_role_policy(", "put_role_policy("]
hits = [f for f in forbidden if f in body]
if hits:
    sys.exit("reverse.py can act on what it finds: " + ", ".join(hits) + nl
             + "      The reverse sweep reports. A finding is for a human.")
print(f"  reports only; {len(body.splitlines())} lines checked")
REVEOF
[[ $? -eq 0 ]] || die "reverse.py is not safe to publish."
ok "the reverse sweep reports and does not act"

info "Packaging"
zip_deterministic "${BUILD}"
HASH="$(package_hash "${BUILD}/package.zip")"
KEY="quorum/quorum-${HASH}.zip"

hr
log "Quorum package"
log "  account : altdig-infra-tooling (${TOOLING})"
log "  key     : ${KEY}"
log "  size    : $(wc -c < "${BUILD}/package.zip" | tr -d ' ') bytes"
hr

if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
  printf '%s DRY%s  would upload s3://%s/%s\n' "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}" "${BUCKET}" "${KEY}"
  exit 0
fi

CREDS="$(aws sts assume-role \
  --role-arn "arn:aws:iam::${TOOLING}:role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole" \
  --role-session-name publish-quorum \
  --query 'Credentials.[AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey,SessionToken]' \
  --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || true
[[ -n "${CREDS}" ]] || die "Could not assume into ${TOOLING}."
read -r AK SK ST <<<"${CREDS}"
unset AWS_PROFILE
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="${AK}" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="${SK}" AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="${ST}"

if MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws s3api head-object --bucket "${BUCKET}" --key "${KEY}" \
     >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  skip "identical package already published"
else
  MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws s3api put-object --bucket "${BUCKET}" --key "${KEY}" \
    --body "$(win_path "${BUILD}/package.zip")" >/dev/null
  ok "uploaded s3://${BUCKET}/${KEY}"
fi

hr
info "Deploy the pipeline into the Audit account:"
log "  scripts/deploy-to-account.sh --account altdig-security-audit \\"
log "    --template quorum/10-quorum.yaml --stack platform-quorum \\"
log "    ArtifactBucket=${BUCKET} ArtifactKey=${KEY} \\"
log "    JiraSite=\${PLATFORM_JIRA_SITE} LogsKeyArn=<alerts key>"
log ""
info "Then the executor role into each target account, passing the"
info "ExecuteRoleArn the stack above outputs:"
log "  scripts/deploy-to-account.sh --account <target> \\"
log "    --template quorum/00-executor-role.yaml --stack platform-quorum-executor \\"
log "    QuorumPipelineRoleArn=<ExecuteRoleArn> Scope=member"
log ""
info "And publish the approver list, which is NOT in the repository:"
log "  scripts/sync-quorum-approvers.sh"
hr

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Package the restore workflow and publish it to the artifact bucket.
#
#   scripts/publish-recovery.sh [--dry-run]
#
# One package, two functions. worker.py and teardown.py share an archive and
# are separated by handler and by ROLE, not by artifact — see
# recovery/10-restore-workflow.yaml on why the function that can delete has a
# role of its own. Shipping them separately would mean two content hashes that
# can drift, and a teardown built against a worker it has never seen.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) printf 'Usage: %s [--dry-run]\n' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

PY="$(command -v python || command -v python3)" || die "python not found."
TOOLING="$(get_param /org/account/altdig-infra-tooling)"
[[ -n "${TOOLING}" && "${TOOLING}" != "None" ]] \
  || die "Platform Tooling account not registered."

BUCKET="altdig-platform-artifacts-${TOOLING}"
BUILD="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "${BUILD}"' EXIT
cp "${REPO_ROOT}/recovery/src/worker.py" "${BUILD}/worker.py"
cp "${REPO_ROOT}/recovery/src/teardown.py" "${BUILD}/teardown.py"

info "Checking both handlers compile"
"${PY}" -m py_compile \
  "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/recovery/src/worker.py")" \
  "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/recovery/src/teardown.py")" \
  || die "recovery sources do not compile. Nothing packaged."
ok "compiles"

# The state machine names five worker steps and invokes teardown separately. A
# state machine that references a step the worker does not implement fails at
# RUN time, in the middle of a restore, with "unknown step" — and in recovery
# mode that is during an outage. Checked here instead, where it costs nothing.
info "Checking the state machine's steps exist in the worker"
"${PY}" - "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/recovery/10-restore-workflow.yaml")" \
          "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/recovery/src/worker.py")" <<'CHECKEOF'
import re
import sys

asl = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8").read()
src = open(sys.argv[2], encoding="utf-8").read()

wanted = set(re.findall(r'"step":\s*"([a-z]+)"', asl))
block = re.search(r"STEPS = \{(.*?)\}", src, re.S)
if block is None:
    sys.exit("could not find STEPS in worker.py")
have = set(re.findall(r'"([a-z]+)":', block.group(1)))

missing = wanted - have
unused = have - wanted
if missing:
    sys.exit(f"state machine calls steps the worker does not implement: "
             f"{', '.join(sorted(missing))}")
print(f"  {len(wanted)} step(s) matched: {', '.join(sorted(wanted))}")
if unused:
    # Not fatal. A worker step no state calls is dead code, not a broken
    # workflow, and saying so is more useful than refusing to publish.
    print(f"  note: worker implements unused step(s): {', '.join(sorted(unused))}")
CHECKEOF
[[ $? -eq 0 ]] || die "state machine and worker have diverged. Nothing packaged."
ok "state machine and worker agree"

info "Packaging"
zip_deterministic "${BUILD}"
HASH="$(package_hash "${BUILD}/package.zip")"
KEY="recovery/recovery-${HASH}.zip"

hr
log "Recovery package"
log "  account : altdig-infra-tooling (${TOOLING})"
log "  key     : ${KEY}"
log "  size    : $(wc -c < "${BUILD}/package.zip" | tr -d ' ') bytes"
hr

if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
  printf '%s DRY%s  would upload s3://%s/%s\n' "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}" "${BUCKET}" "${KEY}"
  exit 0
fi

CREDS="$(aws sts assume-role \
  --role-arn "arn:aws:iam::${TOOLING}:role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole" \
  --role-session-name publish-recovery \
  --query 'Credentials.[AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey,SessionToken]' \
  --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || true
[[ -n "${CREDS}" ]] || die "Could not assume into ${TOOLING}."
read -r AK SK ST <<<"${CREDS}"
unset AWS_PROFILE
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="${AK}" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="${SK}" AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="${ST}"

if MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws s3api head-object --bucket "${BUCKET}" --key "${KEY}" \
     >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  skip "identical package already published"
else
  MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws s3api put-object --bucket "${BUCKET}" --key "${KEY}" \
    --body "$(win_path "${BUILD}/package.zip")" >/dev/null
  ok "uploaded s3://${BUCKET}/${KEY}"
fi

hr
info "1. The sandbox test fixture (sandbox only — it is scaffolding, not a"
log "   backup policy; see the header of recovery/00-restore-fixture.yaml):"
log "  scripts/deploy-to-account.sh --account altdig-sandbox-canary \\"
log "    --template recovery/00-restore-fixture.yaml \\"
log "    --stack platform-restore-fixture"
log ""

log ""
info "3. The workflow:"
log "  scripts/deploy-to-account.sh --account altdig-sandbox-canary \\"
log "    --template recovery/10-restore-workflow.yaml \\"
log "    --stack platform-restore \\"
log "    ArtifactBucket=${BUCKET} ArtifactKey=${KEY} \\"

log ""
info "4. The schedule (uat and prod only — design/14 line 85):"
log "  scripts/deploy-to-account.sh --account altdig-sandbox-canary \\"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Package the response engine and publish it to the artifact bucket.
#
#   scripts/publish-response.sh [--dry-run]
#
# Converts runbooks/catalog.yaml to JSON the same way the instrumentation
# package converts 06a: the Lambda runtime ships boto3 but not PyYAML, and
# vendoring PyYAML to call safe_load once would add a third-party dependency to
# audit inside a function that can stop a container.
#
# The catalog is VALIDATED against actions.py before packaging. A catalog
# naming an unimplemented action would otherwise raise mid-incident, having
# already decided to act; an implementation of a refused action would restore a
# capability somebody decided against, with nothing about the deployment
# looking unusual.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) printf 'Usage: %s [--dry-run]\n' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

PY="$(command -v python || command -v python3)" || die "python not found."
TOOLING="$(get_param /org/account/altdig-infra-tooling)"
[[ -n "${TOOLING}" && "${TOOLING}" != "None" ]] \
  || die "Platform Tooling account not registered."

BUCKET="altdig-platform-artifacts-${TOOLING}"
SRC="${REPO_ROOT}/runbooks/src"
BUILD="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "${BUILD}"' EXIT

for f in engine.py rails.py actions.py; do
  cp "${SRC}/${f}" "${BUILD}/${f}"
done

info "Validating the runbook catalog"
"${PY}" "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/scripts/lib/validate_catalog.py")" \
  "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/runbooks/catalog.yaml")" \
  "$(win_path "${SRC}/actions.py")" \
  "$(win_path "${BUILD}/catalog.json")" \
  "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/design/06a-alarm-specification.yaml")" \
  || die "runbooks/catalog.yaml is invalid. Nothing packaged."

# Regenerate the human-readable runbooks from the same catalog that is about
# to ship. Generated rather than maintained: a hand-written copy would be wrong
# within two edits, and wrong in the worst direction — a document describing a
# remediation the platform no longer performs is worse than no document,
# because it is believed.
#
# Done at PACKAGING so the document and the deployed behaviour cannot diverge.
info "Rendering docs/runbooks.md"
"${PY}" "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/scripts/lib/render_runbooks.py")"   "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/runbooks/catalog.yaml")"   "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/docs/runbooks.md")"   || die "Could not render docs/runbooks.md"

info "Packaging"
zip_deterministic "${BUILD}"
HASH="$(package_hash "${BUILD}/package.zip")"
KEY="response/engine-${HASH}.zip"

hr
log "Response package"
log "  account : altdig-infra-tooling (${TOOLING})"
log "  key     : ${KEY}"
log "  size    : $(wc -c < "${BUILD}/package.zip" | tr -d ' ') bytes"
hr

if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
  printf '%s DRY%s  would upload s3://%s/%s\n' "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}" "${BUCKET}" "${KEY}"
  exit 0
fi

CREDS="$(aws sts assume-role \
  --role-arn "arn:aws:iam::${TOOLING}:role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole" \
  --role-session-name publish-response \
  --query 'Credentials.[AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey,SessionToken]' \
  --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || true
[[ -n "${CREDS}" ]] || die "Could not assume into ${TOOLING}."
read -r AK SK ST <<<"${CREDS}"
unset AWS_PROFILE
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="${AK}" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="${SK}" AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="${ST}"

if MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws s3api head-object --bucket "${BUCKET}" --key "${KEY}" \
     >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  skip "identical package already published"
else

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Package and upload the HOOP scheduler and its cycle verification.
#
#   scripts/publish-scheduling.sh [--dry-run]
#
# Two handlers in one archive: hoop.handler schedules, cycle.handler verifies.
# They share the manifest and the refusals, so shipping them apart would allow
# a verification running against a scheduler it does not match — and the
# mismatch would surface as a turnup reported incomplete for resources the
# running scheduler never touched.
#
# Written rather than copied from publish-commercial.sh. B-104: a publish
# script copied and renamed only in its head uploaded one component's package
# under another's name, and nothing noticed because both archives existed.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) printf 'Usage: %s [--dry-run]\n' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

PY="$(command -v python || command -v python3)" || die "python not found."
TOOLING="$(get_param /org/account/altdig-infra-tooling)"
[[ -n "${TOOLING}" && "${TOOLING}" != "None" ]] \
  || die "Platform Tooling account not registered."

BUCKET="altdig-platform-artifacts-${TOOLING}"
BUILD="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "${BUILD}"' EXIT

for MODULE in hoop cycle state interactions; do
  cp "${REPO_ROOT}/scheduling/src/${MODULE}.py" "${BUILD}/${MODULE}.py"
done

# B-060: the templates are the authority on which handlers must be present.
info "Checking every handler the templates reference is packaged"
for HANDLER in $(grep -hoE '^      Handler: [a-z_]+\.handler' \
                   "${REPO_ROOT}"/scheduling/*.yaml \
                 | awk '{print $2}' | cut -d. -f1 | sort -u); do
  [[ -f "${BUILD}/${HANDLER}.py" ]] \
    || die "the templates declare handler ${HANDLER}.handler but
      ${HANDLER}.py is not in the package. Add it to the MODULE list above."
  printf '  %s.py\n' "${HANDLER}"
done
ok "every referenced handler is present"

info "Checking they compile"
"${PY}" -m py_compile \
  "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/scheduling/src/hoop.py")" \
  "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/scheduling/src/cycle.py")" \
  || die "scheduling sources do not compile. Nothing packaged."
ok "compiles"

# --- the structural check --------------------------------------------------
#
# CLAUDE.md forbids automation that terminates or purges. The scheduler is
# allowed to stop things precisely because stopping is reversible, and that
# distinction lives one word away from its opposite: stop_instances and
# terminate_instances differ by a verb.
#
# The IAM role already withholds the destructive actions, so a call would fail
# at runtime. This refuses to PACKAGE one, because a failing destructive call
# in a scheduler is still a scheduler somebody wrote a destructive call into.
info "Checking nothing destructive was packaged"
"${PY}" - "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/scheduling/src")" <<'SEPEOF'
import pathlib
import re
import sys

FORBIDDEN = (
    "terminate_instances",
    "delete_db_instance",
    "delete_db_cluster",
    "delete_auto_scaling_group",
    "delete_service",
    "delete_volume",
    "deregister_",
)

problems = []
for path in pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).glob("*.py"):
    source = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    # Strip comments and docstrings so the words may be DISCUSSED. Several of
    # these appear in prose explaining why they are absent, and a guard that
    # fired on its own rationale would be removed within the week -- that
    # lesson cost six false positives elsewhere in this repository.
    code = re.sub(r"#.*", "", source)
    code = re.sub(r'"""(?:.|\n)*?"""', "", code)
    for name in FORBIDDEN:
        if re.search(r"\.\s*" + re.escape(name) + r"\s*\(", code):
            problems.append(f"{path.name} calls {name}()")

if problems:
    print("  " + "\n  ".join(problems))
    print("")
    print("  A HOOP stops compute; it never destroys it. CLAUDE.md: security")
    print("  automation isolates and preserves, operational automation is")
    print("  additive or reversible. Storage, load balancers and NAT gateways")
    print("  persist through a turndown by design.")
    sys.exit(1)
SEPEOF
[[ $? -eq 0 ]] || die "a destructive call is present in scheduling/src. Nothing packaged."
ok "stop and start only; nothing destructive"

info "Packaging"
zip_deterministic "${BUILD}"
HASH="$(package_hash "${BUILD}/package.zip")"
KEY="scheduling/scheduling-${HASH}.zip"

hr
log "Scheduling package"
log "  account : altdig-infra-tooling (${TOOLING})"
log "  key     : ${KEY}"
log "  size    : $(wc -c < "${BUILD}/package.zip" | tr -d ' ') bytes"
hr

if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
  printf '%s DRY%s  would upload to s3://%s/%s\n' \
    "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}" "${BUCKET}" "${KEY}"
  exit 0
fi

CREDS="$(aws sts assume-role \
  --role-arn "arn:aws:iam::${TOOLING}:role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole" \
  --role-session-name publish-scheduling \
  --query 'Credentials.[AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey,SessionToken]' \
  --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || true
[[ -n "${CREDS}" ]] || die "Could not assume into ${TOOLING}."
read -r AK SK ST <<<"${CREDS}"
(
  unset AWS_PROFILE
  export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="${AK}" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="${SK}" \
         AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="${ST}"
  # win_path on the body. A bare MSYS path reaches aws.exe as something it
  # cannot open, and the error -- "Blob values must be a path to a file" --
  # describes a file that exists and is perfectly readable.
  MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws s3api put-object \
    --bucket "${BUCKET}" --key "${KEY}" \
    --body "$(win_path "${BUILD}/package.zip")" \
    --query ETag --output text >/dev/null
)
ok "uploaded s3://${BUCKET}/${KEY}"

hr
info "Next: deploy into the account being scheduled"
log "  scripts/deploy-to-account.sh --account <alias> \\"
log "    --template scheduling/10-hoop.yaml --stack platform-hoop \\"
log "    ArtifactBucket=${BUCKET} ArtifactKey=${KEY} \\"
log "    AccountId=<id> AccountTier=<dev|test|uat> AccountKind=<tenant|shared> \\"
log "    AlertBusArn=<arn> HoopConfig='{\"timezone\":\"America/Chicago\",...}'"
log ""
log "  AccountTier does not accept prod. That refusal is CloudFormation's,"
log "  before any code runs."
hr

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Package the telemetry pipeline and publish it to the artifact bucket.
#
#   scripts/publish-telemetry.sh [--dry-run]
#
# gap.py is the whole module: it gathers five signals per instance and
# matches them against design 11's discriminator table.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) printf 'Usage: %s [--dry-run]\n' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

PY="$(command -v python || command -v python3)" || die "python not found."
TOOLING="$(get_param /org/account/altdig-infra-tooling)"
[[ -n "${TOOLING}" && "${TOOLING}" != "None" ]] \
  || die "Platform Tooling account not registered."

BUCKET="altdig-platform-artifacts-${TOOLING}"
BUILD="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "${BUILD}"' EXIT
> "${BUILD}/.sources"
for MODULE in gap; do
  cp "${REPO_ROOT}/telemetry/src/${MODULE}.py" "${BUILD}/${MODULE}.py"
  printf '%s\n' "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/telemetry/src/${MODULE}.py")" \
    >> "${BUILD}/.sources"
done
# B-060: a hand-written module list left two handlers out of the archive while
# the stack was already deployed with Lambdas pointing at them.
info "Checking every handler the templates reference is packaged"
for HANDLER in $(grep -hoE '^      Handler: [a-z]+\.handler' \
                   "${REPO_ROOT}"/telemetry/*.yaml \
                 | awk '{print $2}' | cut -d. -f1 | sort -u); do
  [[ -f "${BUILD}/${HANDLER}.py" ]] \
    || die "the templates declare handler ${HANDLER}.handler but
      ${HANDLER}.py is not in the package. Add it to the MODULE list above."
  printf '  %s.py\n' "${HANDLER}"
done
ok "every referenced handler is present"

info "Checking they compile"
xargs "${PY}" -m py_compile < "${BUILD}/.sources" \
  || die "telemetry sources do not compile. Nothing packaged."
rm -f "${BUILD}/.sources"
ok "compiles"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The guard
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# One, and it protects the property that would fail most quietly.

info "Checking an unreadable signal is still not a false one"
"${PY}" - "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/telemetry/src/gap.py")" <<'HONESTEOF'
import sys

nl = chr(10)
source = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8").read()

problems = []

# A signal that could not be read must never be recorded as False.
#
# Assuming False for an unreadable telemetry check manufactures the exact
# signature this module hunts: the platform reporting an agent killed because
# it could not see the metric. It would fire on a permissions lapse, name a
# developer, and be entirely wrong.
if "unreadable" not in source:
    problems.append(
        "gap.py no longer tracks unreadable signals. An unreadable check "
        "recorded as False manufactures the agent-kill signature.")

if "if signals.unreadable" not in source:
    problems.append(
        "classify() no longer refuses to judge when a signal was unreadable. "
        "Every row of the table is a positive claim about four signals, and "
        "an unknown is not a value any of them take.")

# Exactly two rows of design 11's table alarm. A third would mean somebody
# widened it; zero would mean the detector is inert.
alarms = source.count('"alarm": True')
if alarms != 2:
    problems.append(
        f"{alarms} scenario(s) alarm; design 11's table has exactly two. "
        "Check SCENARIOS against the table before changing this.")

if problems:
    sys.exit("gap.py has lost a control:" + nl
             + nl.join("      - " + p for p in problems))
print("  unreadable stays unreadable; two rows alarm")
HONESTEOF
[[ $? -eq 0 ]] || die "gap.py is not safe to publish."
ok "unreadable is not false"

info "Packaging"
zip_deterministic "${BUILD}"
HASH="$(package_hash "${BUILD}/package.zip")"
KEY="telemetry/telemetry-${HASH}.zip"

hr
log "Telemetry package"
log "  account : altdig-infra-tooling (${TOOLING})"
log "  key     : ${KEY}"
log "  size    : $(wc -c < "${BUILD}/package.zip" | tr -d ' ') bytes"
hr

if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
  printf '%s DRY%s  would upload s3://%s/%s\n' "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}" "${BUCKET}" "${KEY}"
  exit 0
fi

CREDS="$(aws sts assume-role \
  --role-arn "arn:aws:iam::${TOOLING}:role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole" \
  --role-session-name publish-telemetry \
  --query 'Credentials.[AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey,SessionToken]' \
  --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || true
[[ -n "${CREDS}" ]] || die "Could not assume into ${TOOLING}."
read -r AK SK ST <<<"${CREDS}"
unset AWS_PROFILE
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="${AK}" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="${SK}" AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="${ST}"

if MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws s3api head-object --bucket "${BUCKET}" --key "${KEY}" \
     >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  skip "identical package already published"
else
  MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws s3api put-object --bucket "${BUCKET}" --key "${KEY}" \
    --body "$(win_path "${BUILD}/package.zip")" >/dev/null
  ok "uploaded s3://${BUCKET}/${KEY}"
fi

hr

log "  scripts/deploy-to-account.sh --account altdig-security-audit \\"
log "    --template telemetry/10-telemetry.yaml --stack platform-telemetry \\"

files.scripts/register-delegated-admins.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Delegate administration of the security services to the Audit account.
#
#   scripts/register-delegated-admins.sh --dry-run
#   scripts/register-delegated-admins.sh
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why delegate at all
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Design doc 02: "The Organization management account holds nothing but the
# Organization itself. No workloads, no pipelines, minimal access. Delegated
# administration is used for Config, Security Hub, GuardDuty, Backup, IAM
# Identity Center and CloudFormation StackSets."
#
# Without delegation, every day-to-day security operation — triaging a
# GuardDuty finding, tuning a Security Hub control — requires access to the
# management account, which is the one account no SCP can constrain. Delegation
# moves that work into Audit, where it can be governed like anything else.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Two registration mechanisms, and the regional trap
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ORGANIZATION-LEVEL services register once, globally, through the
# Organizations API.
#
# REGIONAL services (GuardDuty, Security Hub, Macie, Inspector) each have their
# own API and must be registered SEPARATELY IN EVERY REGION. Registering only
# in the home region leaves the others silently unmonitored — and a member
# account is permitted to operate in any of PLATFORM_ALLOWED_REGIONS, so that
# is a real detection gap, not a theoretical one.
#
# This is the same class of problem as the region-restriction SCP in phase 10.2,
# which the prompts document calls out as "entirely innocent in intent" and
# productive of "a total visibility blind spot". Here the blind spot arrives by
# omission rather than by a developer's choice.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) log "Usage: register-delegated-admins.sh [--dry-run]"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

AUDIT_ACCOUNT="$(get_param /org/account/altdig-security-audit)"
[[ -n "${AUDIT_ACCOUNT}" && "${AUDIT_ACCOUNT}" != "None" ]] \
  || die "Audit account not found in SSM. Run:
      scripts/create-platform-account.sh --ou security --role audit"

IFS=',' read -ra REGIONS <<<"${PLATFORM_ALLOWED_REGIONS}"

hr
log "Delegated administration"
log "  delegate to : ${AUDIT_ACCOUNT} (Audit)"
log "  regions     : ${PLATFORM_ALLOWED_REGIONS}"
hr

# --- organization-level ----------------------------------------------------
# Registered once. Region-agnostic.

ORG_SERVICES=(
  access-analyzer.amazonaws.com             # org-wide external access findings
  config.amazonaws.com                      # Config as an organization
  config-multiaccountsetup.amazonaws.com    # Config aggregator in Audit
  backup.amazonaws.com                      # org backup policies and reporting
  reporting.trustedadvisor.amazonaws.com    # org-wide Trusted Advisor
)

info "Organization-level delegation"
CURRENT="$(aws organizations list-delegated-services-for-account \
  --account-id "${AUDIT_ACCOUNT}" --query 'DelegatedServices[].ServicePrincipal' \
  --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr | tr '\t\n' '  ' || true)"

for sp in "${ORG_SERVICES[@]}"; do
  if [[ " ${CURRENT} " == *" ${sp} "* ]]; then
    skip "${sp}"
  else
    run "delegate ${sp}" \
      aws organizations register-delegated-administrator \
        --account-id "${AUDIT_ACCOUNT}" --service-principal "${sp}"
  fi
done
hr

# --- regional --------------------------------------------------------------
# Each of these has its own admin-registration API, and each is per-region.
#
# All four are idempotent-ish but return errors rather than success when the
# account is already the administrator, so failures are inspected rather than
# trusted: "already" in the message is a skip, anything else is real.

delegate_regional() {
  local label="$1" region="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
    printf '%s DRY%s  %-12s %s\n' "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}" "${label}" "${region}"
    return 0
  fi
  out="$("$@" 2>&1)" && rc=0 || rc=$?
  if [[ ${rc} -eq 0 ]]; then
    printf '%s  ok%s  %-12s %s\n' "${C_GREEN}" "${C_RESET}" "${label}" "${region}"
  elif printf '%s' "${out}" | grep -qiE 'already|ConflictException|exists'; then
    printf '%sskip%s  %-12s %s (already delegated)\n' "${C_DIM}" "${C_RESET}" "${label}" "${region}"
  else
    printf '%swarn%s  %-12s %s — %s\n' "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}" "${label}" "${region}" \
      "$(printf '%s' "${out}" | tr -d '\n' | grep -o 'An error occurred.*' | cut -c1-110)"
    REGIONAL_FAILED=1
  fi
}

REGIONAL_FAILED=0
for region in "${REGIONS[@]}"; do
  info "Regional delegation in ${region}"

  delegate_regional "guardduty" "${region}" \
    aws guardduty enable-organization-admin-account \
      --admin-account-id "${AUDIT_ACCOUNT}" --region "${region}"

  delegate_regional "securityhub" "${region}" \
    aws securityhub enable-organization-admin-account \
      --admin-account-id "${AUDIT_ACCOUNT}" --region "${region}"

  delegate_regional "macie" "${region}" \
    aws macie2 enable-organization-admin-account \
      --admin-account-id "${AUDIT_ACCOUNT}" --region "${region}"

  delegate_regional "inspector" "${region}" \
    aws inspector2 enable-delegated-admin-account \
      --delegated-admin-account-id "${AUDIT_ACCOUNT}" --region "${region}"
done
hr

if [[ ${REGIONAL_FAILED} -eq 1 ]]; then
  warn "One or more regional delegations did not succeed."
  warn "Security Hub and GuardDuty must be enabled in a region before an"
  warn "administrator can be delegated there. Re-run after enabling them."
fi

# --- CloudFormation StackSets -> Platform Tooling --------------------------
#
# Deliberately NOT delegated to Audit. Audit's job is to observe the platform;
# the StackSet administrator deploys it. Putting the deployment pipeline inside
# the account that audits the deployment removes the separation that makes the
# audit worth anything.
#
# This needs TWO calls, and the second is easy to miss:
#
#   register-delegated-administrator  names the account
#   activate-organizations-access     lets it actually target OUs
#
# Without the second, the delegated account can create a service-managed
# StackSet and every OU target fails. The error does not mention organizations
# access.
TOOLING_ACCOUNT="$(get_param /org/account/altdig-infra-tooling)"

if [[ -z "${TOOLING_ACCOUNT}" || "${TOOLING_ACCOUNT}" == "None" ]]; then
  warn "Platform Tooling account not found — StackSets delegation skipped."
  warn "  scripts/create-platform-account.sh --ou infra --role tooling"
else
  info "CloudFormation StackSets delegation"
  SS_SP="member.org.stacksets.cloudformation.amazonaws.com"
  SS_CURRENT="$(aws organizations list-delegated-services-for-account     --account-id "${TOOLING_ACCOUNT}" --query 'DelegatedServices[].ServicePrincipal'     --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr | tr '	
' '  ' || true)"

  if [[ " ${SS_CURRENT} " == *" ${SS_SP} "* ]]; then
    skip "${SS_SP}"
  else
    run "delegate ${SS_SP} to ${TOOLING_ACCOUNT}"       aws organizations register-delegated-administrator         --account-id "${TOOLING_ACCOUNT}" --service-principal "${SS_SP}"
  fi

  # Idempotent and safe to repeat; it is an organization-wide switch rather
  # than a per-account grant.
  run "activate organizations access for StackSets"     aws cloudformation activate-organizations-access
  hr
fi

ok "Delegation pass complete."
log ""
log "StackSets delegation does NOT move the four StackSets that already exist"
log "in the management account. A StackSet is owned by the account that created"
log "it and cannot be transferred — moving one means deleting it, which deletes"
log "its stack instances and removes the baseline from every account it covers."
log "Several baseline resources are DeletionPolicy: Retain, so a delete-and-"
log "recreate would orphan KMS keys and aliases that then collide on the way"
log "back in. See D-012."
log ""
log "NOT delegated here, deliberately:"
log "  * IAM Identity Center       -> stays in the management account; moving"
log "    it is disruptive and buys little while the directory holds one user."
