#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Record AltDigital's own accounts in the platform registry.
#
#   scripts/register-platform-accounts.sh [--dry-run]
#
# The registry is the spine — design 13's phrase — and it had no ACCOUNT
# records at all. The six platform accounts were created before the vesting
# flow existed and live only in SSM under /platform/org/account/, so anything
# deriving from the registry (Cost Categories, prompt 9.2) saw an empty estate.
#
# These are `kind: shared`, not tenant. design 10:
#
#     Log Archive, Audit, Forensics, Platform Tooling and Shared Services
#     accounts generate real cost that nobody pays a flat fee for.
#     [...] Position: absorbed into the percentage uplift.
#
# Absorbed is a billing decision, not a reason to leave them out of the
# registry. Left out, they would be invisible to every control that iterates
# accounts — which is B-064 exactly, where a hand-maintained list missed
# Forensics and nothing said so.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) printf 'Usage: %s [--dry-run]\n' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*'
ACCOUNTS="$(aws ssm get-parameters-by-path --path /platform/org/account/ \
  --query 'Parameters[].[Name,Value]' --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)"
[[ -n "${ACCOUNTS}" ]] || die "No accounts under /platform/org/account/."

# The management account, which is NOT in that path and never will be.
#
# CLAUDE.md keeps it holding "the Organization and nothing else", so it is not
# a provisioned member and has no /platform/org/account/ entry. It still costs
# money — Organizations, CloudTrail, the consolidated bill — and the Cost
# Category sync correctly reported it as `unregistered` on its first run.
#
# `unregistered` is the right thing for that check to SAY and the wrong place
# for the spend to live. Appended explicitly, so its absence from the registry
# path reads as the reason rather than as an oversight.
ACCOUNTS="${ACCOUNTS}
/platform/org/account/altdig-management	${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

# Environment per account, from the tier map the alerting layer already
# maintains in Audit. Derived rather than restated here: two lists of which
# account is production is one list too many, and the one nobody updates is
# always the one being read.
AUDIT="$(get_param /org/account/altdig-security-audit)"
CREDS="$(aws sts assume-role \
  --role-arn "arn:aws:iam::${AUDIT}:role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole" \
  --role-session-name read-tiers \
  --query 'Credentials.[AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey,SessionToken]' \
  --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || true
[[ -n "${CREDS}" ]] || die "Could not assume into Audit to read the tier map."
read -r AK SK ST <<<"${CREDS}"
TIERS="$(
  unset AWS_PROFILE
  export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="${AK}" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="${SK}" \
         AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="${ST}"
  MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws ssm get-parameter \
    --name /platform/routing/account-tiers \
    --query Parameter.Value --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr
)"
[[ -n "${TIERS}" ]] || die "Could not read /platform/routing/account-tiers."

PY="$(command -v python || command -v python3)" || die "python not found."

COUNT=0
while read -r NAME ACCOUNT_ID; do
  [[ "${ACCOUNT_ID}" =~ ^[0-9]{12}$ ]] || continue
  ALIAS="${NAME##*/}"
  TIER="$("${PY}" -c "
import json,sys
print((json.loads(sys.argv[1]) or {}).get(sys.argv[2], 'prod'))
" "${TIERS}" "${ACCOUNT_ID}")"

  # The registry's environment vocabulary, from the tier.
  case "${TIER}" in
    dev)  ENV_VALUE="dev" ;;
    test) ENV_VALUE="test" ;;
    uat)  ENV_VALUE="uat" ;;
    *)    ENV_VALUE="prod" ;;
  esac

  # Every platform account is managed by AltDigital and in scope for its own
  # SOC 2 — design 15 puts infrastructure operations, platform controls, the
  # evidence pipeline, incident response and change management in the
  # reference report. That is not a per-account judgement to make here.
  if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
    printf '%s DRY%s  %-32s %s  kind=shared env=%s\n' \
      "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}" "${ALIAS}" "${ACCOUNT_ID}" "${ENV_VALUE}"
  else
    "${REPO_ROOT}/scripts/registry.sh" put-account \
      --account-id "${ACCOUNT_ID}" \
      --kind shared \
      --partner altdigital \
      --slug platform \
      --app "${ALIAS#altdig-}" \
      --env "${ENV_VALUE}" \
      --service-model managed \
      --compliance soc2 \
      --state active >/dev/null \
      || die "Could not record ${ALIAS} (${ACCOUNT_ID})."
    ok "${ALIAS} (${ACCOUNT_ID}) recorded: shared / ${ENV_VALUE}"
  fi
  COUNT=$((COUNT + 1))
done <<<"${ACCOUNTS}"

hr
log "Platform accounts recorded: ${COUNT}"
log "  kind          : shared — cost absorbed into the uplift, not allocated"
log "  service model : managed"
log "  compliance    : soc2 (AltDigital's own reference report, design 15)"
hr
info "Re-run after creating a platform account. A tenant account is recorded"
log "  by the vesting flow, not by this."
hr
files.scripts/registry.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Platform registry CLI — the authoritative record of partners, clients and
# member accounts, and the parameters each was provisioned with.
#
#   scripts/registry.sh <command> [options]
#
# Design doc 13 calls the registry "the spine": every other system is
# provisioned FROM a record here and writes back to it. Prompt 3.2 says keep it
# simple — a DynamoDB table and a query CLI, not a web application. This is the
# CLI.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The two reports this exists for
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Prompt 3.2 names both, as requirements of design principle P9:
#
#   report-baseline    which accounts are behind the current baseline version
#   report-overrides   what declared local overrides exist, why, and who owns
#
# NOTE ON P9: design doc 01 (Design Principles) is NOT present in the design
# package, so P9 is cited in three places and its text exists nowhere readable.
# These two reports are built to the prompt's explicit wording. Whether they
# are the whole of what P9 asks for cannot be confirmed from the package as it
# stands. See docs/build-backlog.md B-004.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Declared vs undeclared difference
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# An account differing from the global baseline is not automatically a problem.
# A difference that someone wrote down, justified and put their name against is
# a local override. The same difference with nobody's name on it is drift.
#
# The registry is the record of the first kind. It is what makes the second
# kind detectable at all — without a statement of what an account was SUPPOSED
# to be, AWS can only tell you what it IS, and everything looks intentional.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

REGISTRY_ACCOUNT_KEY="altdig-infra-tooling"
TABLE="${PLATFORM_REGISTRY_TABLE:-platform-registry}"

usage() {
  cat <<'USAGE'
Usage: registry.sh <command> [options]

Partners
  put-partner    --slug S --state STATE --notify-hours N --altdig-hours N
                 [--downstream-sla PCT] [--altdig-sla PCT]
                 [--owner NAME] [--baa STATE]
  get-partner    --slug S
  list-partners
  check-partner  --slug S        Gate used by create-client-ou.sh. Exit 0 only
                                 if the partner may have clients created.

Clients
  put-client     --partner S --slug S [--state STATE] [--ip-owner WHO]
                 [--tech-contact EMAIL] [--dev-manager EMAIL]
  list-clients   [--partner S]

Accounts
  put-account    --account-id ID --partner S --client S --env ENV
                 [--app S] [--baseline-version N]
  get-account    --account-id ID
  list-accounts

Overrides
  put-override   --account-id ID --name NAME --reason TEXT --owner NAME
                 [--review-by YYYY-MM-DD]
  drop-override  --account-id ID --name NAME

Baseline
  set-baseline   --version N     Record the current global baseline version.
  get-baseline

Reports
  report-baseline    Accounts behind the current global baseline version.
  report-overrides   Every declared override, with reason, owner and review date.

STATE is one of: provisioning | active | suspended | devested
USAGE
}

[[ $# -gt 0 ]] || { usage; exit 1; }
CMD="$1"; shift

SLUG=""; PARTNER=""; STATE=""; NOTIFY_HOURS=""; ALTDIG_HOURS=""; OWNER=""
BAA=""; IP_OWNER=""; ACCOUNT_ID=""; ENVIRONMENT=""; APP=""; VERSION=""
NAME=""; REASON=""; REVIEW_BY=""; TECH_CONTACT=""; DEV_MANAGER=""

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --slug)             SLUG="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --partner)          PARTNER="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --state)            STATE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --notify-hours)     NOTIFY_HOURS="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --altdig-hours)     ALTDIG_HOURS="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --downstream-sla)   DOWNSTREAM_SLA="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --altdig-sla)       ALTDIG_SLA="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --owner)            OWNER="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --baa)              BAA="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ip-owner)         IP_OWNER="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --tech-contact)     TECH_CONTACT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dev-manager)      DEV_MANAGER="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --account-id)       ACCOUNT_ID="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --env)              ENVIRONMENT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --app)              APP="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --service-model)    SERVICE_MODEL="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --compliance)       COMPLIANCE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --kind)             KIND="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --baseline-version) VERSION="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --version)          VERSION="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --name)             NAME="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --reason)           REASON="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --review-by)        REVIEW_BY="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dry-run)          DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help)          usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Version padding
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# baseline_version is the GSI sort key, and DynamoDB sorts string sort keys
# lexicographically. Unpadded, "10" sorts before "9" and report-baseline starts
# quietly lying at version 10 — reporting accounts as up to date when they are
# eight versions behind. Padded to six digits here, in the one place that
# writes it.
pad_version() {
  local v="$1"
  [[ "${v}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || die "Baseline version must be a non-negative integer, got '${v}'."
  printf '%06d' "${v}"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Credentials
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ddb_init() {
  export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
  require_cli
  require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

  REGISTRY_ACCOUNT="$(get_param "/org/account/${REGISTRY_ACCOUNT_KEY}")"
  [[ -n "${REGISTRY_ACCOUNT}" && "${REGISTRY_ACCOUNT}" != "None" ]] \
    || die "No account registered at ${PLATFORM_SSM_PREFIX}/org/account/${REGISTRY_ACCOUNT_KEY}.
      The registry lives in the Platform Tooling account. Create it with:
        scripts/create-platform-account.sh --ou infra --role tooling"

  local creds
  creds="$(aws sts assume-role \
    --role-arn "arn:aws:iam::${REGISTRY_ACCOUNT}:role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole" \
    --role-session-name platform-registry \
    --query 'Credentials.[AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey,SessionToken]' \
    --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || true
  [[ -n "${creds}" ]] || die "Could not assume into ${REGISTRY_ACCOUNT}."
  local a s t; read -r a s t <<<"${creds}"
  unset AWS_PROFILE
  export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="${a}" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="${s}" AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="${t}"
}

ddb() { MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws dynamodb "$@"; }

# ddb_str <value> -> a complete DynamoDB attribute value: {"S": "escaped"}
#
# The type wrapper is part of this, not the caller's job. The first version
# returned just the escaped string and every free-text field failed with
# "Invalid type for parameter Item.owner ... valid types: <class 'dict'>",
# which names the symptom and not the missing two characters.
#
# Escaping matters because reasons and owner names are free text and will
# eventually contain a quote, a backslash or a newline. Hand-rolled quoting
# would produce malformed JSON at exactly the moment someone writes a properly
# detailed override reason.
ddb_str() {
  printf '%s' "$1" | python -c 'import json,sys; print(json.dumps({"S": sys.stdin.read()}))'
}

now_iso() { date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ; }

VALID_STATES="provisioning active suspended devested"
check_state() {
  case " ${VALID_STATES} " in
    *" $1 "*) ;;
    *) die "Invalid state '$1'. Expected one of: ${VALID_STATES}" ;;
  esac
}

put_item() {
  local item="$1"
  if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
    printf '%s DRY%s  put-item %s\n' "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}" "${item}"
    return 0
  fi
  ddb put-item --table-name "${TABLE}" --item "${item}" >/dev/null
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Commands
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

cmd_put_partner() {
  [[ -n "${SLUG}" ]]         || die "--slug is required."
  [[ -n "${STATE}" ]]        || die "--state is required."
  [[ -n "${NOTIFY_HOURS}" ]] || die "--notify-hours is required (partner's incident notification window)."
  [[ -n "${ALTDIG_HOURS}" ]] || die "--altdig-hours is required (AltDigital's window to the partner)."
  check_state "${STATE}"
  validate_slug "partner" "${SLUG}"

  [[ "${NOTIFY_HOURS}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || die "--notify-hours must be an integer."
  [[ "${ALTDIG_HOURS}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || die "--altdig-hours must be an integer."

  # AltDigital's window must be TIGHTER than the partner's, not merely present.
  #
  # The partner has promised their client notification within N hours. If
  # AltDigital tells the partner at N, the partner is already late — they have
  # zero time to act. The whole chain only holds if each link is shorter than
  # the one above it, and equal windows fail in exactly the same way as a
  # longer one while looking reasonable in a table.
  if [[ ${ALTDIG_HOURS} -ge ${NOTIFY_HOURS} ]]; then
    die "AltDigital's notification window (${ALTDIG_HOURS}h) must be STRICTLY
      TIGHTER than the partner's (${NOTIFY_HOURS}h).

      The partner owes their client notification within ${NOTIFY_HOURS}h. If we
      tell the partner at ${ALTDIG_HOURS}h they have no time left to act, so the
      chain cannot be met. Equal windows fail identically to longer ones."
  fi

  ddb_init
  put_item "$(cat <<JSON
{
  "PK":               {"S": "PARTNER#${SLUG}"},
  "SK":               {"S": "META"},
  "record_type":      {"S": "PARTNER"},
  "baseline_version": {"S": "000000"},
  "slug":             {"S": "${SLUG}"},
  "state":            {"S": "${STATE}"},
  "notify_hours":     {"N": "${NOTIFY_HOURS}"},
  "altdig_hours":     {"N": "${ALTDIG_HOURS}"},
  "baa_state":        {"S": "${BAA:-unknown}"},
  # design 15's back-to-back pair. Captured at partner onboarding precisely so
  # AltDigital's number can be compared with the partner's BEFORE signing --
  # partners/src/backtoback.py does the comparison. Absent is a finding, not a
  # default: an unrecorded downstream commitment cannot be checked against.
  "downstream_sla_pct": $(ddb_str "${DOWNSTREAM_SLA:-}"),
  "altdig_sla_pct":     $(ddb_str "${ALTDIG_SLA:-}"),
  "owner":            $(ddb_str "${OWNER:-unassigned}"),
  "updated_at":       {"S": "$(now_iso)"}
}
JSON
)"
  ok "partner ${SLUG} recorded: state=${STATE} notify=${NOTIFY_HOURS}h altdig=${ALTDIG_HOURS}h baa=${BAA:-unknown}"
}

cmd_get_partner() {
  [[ -n "${SLUG}" ]] || die "--slug is required."
  ddb_init
  ddb get-item --table-name "${TABLE}" \
    --key "{\"PK\":{\"S\":\"PARTNER#${SLUG}\"},\"SK\":{\"S\":\"META\"}}" \
    --query 'Item' --output json
}

cmd_list_partners() {
  ddb_init
  ddb query --table-name "${TABLE}" --index-name by-type \
    --key-condition-expression 'record_type = :t' \
    --expression-attribute-values '{":t":{"S":"PARTNER"}}' \
    --query 'Items[].[slug.S,state.S,notify_hours.N,altdig_hours.N,baa_state.S,owner.S]' \
    --output text | no_cr | sed 's/^/  /'
}

# The D-004 gate. Exits non-zero, with a specific reason, if a partner is not
# in a state where clients may be created beneath it.
cmd_check_partner() {
  [[ -n "${SLUG}" ]] || die "--slug is required."
  ddb_init
  local item
  item="$(ddb get-item --table-name "${TABLE}" \
    --key "{\"PK\":{\"S\":\"PARTNER#${SLUG}\"},\"SK\":{\"S\":\"META\"}}" \
    --query 'Item' --output json 2>/dev/null)" || true

  if [[ -z "${item}" || "${item}" == "null" ]]; then
    die "Partner '${SLUG}' has no registry record.

      Design doc 13 requires the partner to exist, be active, and carry a
      non-null notification window before any client is created beneath it.
      Record it first:

        scripts/registry.sh put-partner --slug ${SLUG} --state active \\
          --notify-hours 48 --altdig-hours 24 --owner '<name>'"
  fi

  local st nh ah
  st="$(printf '%s' "${item}" | python -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["state"]["S"])')"
  nh="$(printf '%s' "${item}" | python -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["notify_hours"]["N"])')"
  ah="$(printf '%s' "${item}" | python -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["altdig_hours"]["N"])')"

  [[ "${st}" == "active" ]] \
    || die "Partner '${SLUG}' is '${st}', not 'active'. No clients may be created beneath it."
  [[ "${nh}" -gt 0 ]] \
    || die "Partner '${SLUG}' has no notification window recorded."
  [[ "${ah}" -gt 0 && "${ah}" -lt "${nh}" ]] \
    || die "Partner '${SLUG}': AltDigital's window (${ah}h) is not tighter than the partner's (${nh}h)."

  ok "partner ${SLUG}: active, notify=${nh}h, altdigital=${ah}h (tighter) — clients may be created"
}

cmd_put_client() {
  [[ -n "${PARTNER}" ]] || die "--partner is required."
  [[ -n "${SLUG}" ]]    || die "--slug is required."
  validate_slug "partner" "${PARTNER}"
  validate_slug "client" "${SLUG}"
  check_state "${STATE:=provisioning}"
  ddb_init
  put_item "$(cat <<JSON
{
  "PK":               {"S": "PARTNER#${PARTNER}"},
  "SK":               {"S": "CLIENT#${SLUG}"},
  "record_type":      {"S": "CLIENT"},
  "baseline_version": {"S": "000000"},
  "partner":          {"S": "${PARTNER}"},
  "slug":             {"S": "${SLUG}"},
  "state":            {"S": "${STATE}"},
  "ip_owner":         $(ddb_str "${IP_OWNER:-unrecorded}"),
  "tech_contact":     $(ddb_str "${TECH_CONTACT}"),
  "dev_manager":      $(ddb_str "${DEV_MANAGER}"),
  "updated_at":       {"S": "$(now_iso)"}
}
JSON
)"
  ok "client ${PARTNER}/${SLUG} recorded: state=${STATE} ip-owner=${IP_OWNER:-unrecorded}"
  # Questionnaire 1.5 and 5.8. These are the ONLY personal data in the
  # registry, and they are here because the instrumentation digest has nowhere
  # else to find a recipient — design doc 06 makes that digest the documented
  # evidence that monitoring requirements were communicated, so a digest with
  # no addressee is a compliance gap rather than a missing nicety.
  #
  # DynamoDB, not the repository. Same rule as config/contacts.env: personal
  # data lives in a system with access control and an audit trail, never in
  # git.
  if [[ -z "${TECH_CONTACT}" ]]; then
    warn "No --tech-contact. The instrumentation digest for this client has no
      recipient and will be skipped, which loses the evidence that monitoring
      requirements were communicated. Questionnaire field 1.5."
  fi
}

cmd_list_clients() {
  ddb_init
  if [[ -n "${PARTNER}" ]]; then
    ddb query --table-name "${TABLE}" \
      --key-condition-expression 'PK = :p AND begins_with(SK, :c)' \
      --expression-attribute-values "{\":p\":{\"S\":\"PARTNER#${PARTNER}\"},\":c\":{\"S\":\"CLIENT#\"}}" \
      --query 'Items[].[partner.S,slug.S,state.S,ip_owner.S]' --output text | no_cr | sed 's/^/  /'
  else
    ddb query --table-name "${TABLE}" --index-name by-type \
      --key-condition-expression 'record_type = :t' \
      --expression-attribute-values '{":t":{"S":"CLIENT"}}' \
      --query 'Items[].[partner.S,slug.S,state.S,ip_owner.S]' --output text | no_cr | sed 's/^/  /'
  fi
}

# Two facts design 10 needs and this record did not carry, plus the one that
# tells them apart.
#
# service_model and compliance_scope drive Cost Categories (prompt 9.2) and
# were simply absent: the record had partner, client, app and environment.
#
# `kind` matters more than it looks. design 10:
#
#     Log Archive, Audit, Forensics, Platform Tooling and Shared Services
#     accounts generate real cost that nobody pays a flat fee for.
#
# Those accounts have no tenant and never will. Without a way to say so they
# would either be left out of the registry -- which is how B-064 lost an
# account and B-086 swept an empty estate -- or filed against a fictional
# tenant, which would put AltDigital's own overhead on somebody's invoice.
#
#   tenant   a client workload account. Billable.
#   shared   AltDigital's own. Cost is absorbed into the uplift, not allocated,
#            and B-090 is the report that checks the uplift covers it.
check_kind() {
  case "${1}" in
    tenant|shared) ;;
    *) die "--kind must be tenant or shared, got '${1}'." ;;
  esac
}

# design 10's service models. Unset is allowed and is visible as 'unset' rather
# than blank, so an account nobody classified is findable instead of looking
# like a deliberate choice.
check_service_model() {
  case "${1}" in
    unset|managed|co-managed|advisory) ;;
    *) die "--service-model must be managed, co-managed or advisory." ;;
  esac
}

cmd_put_account() {
  [[ -n "${ACCOUNT_ID}" ]]  || die "--account-id is required."
  check_kind "${KIND:=tenant}"
  check_service_model "${SERVICE_MODEL:=unset}"
  if [[ "${KIND}" == "shared" ]]; then
    # AltDigital's own accounts have no partner and no client. Requiring them
    # would mean inventing values, and an invented partner is one that shows
    # up in a billing roll-up.
    PARTNER="${PARTNER:-altdigital}"
    SLUG="${SLUG:-platform}"
  else
    [[ -n "${PARTNER}" ]]   || die "--partner is required."
    [[ -n "${SLUG}" ]]      || die "--client is required (pass with --slug)."
  fi
  [[ -n "${ENVIRONMENT}" ]] || die "--env is required."
  [[ "${ACCOUNT_ID}" =~ ^[0-9]{12}$ ]] || die "--account-id must be 12 digits."
  check_state "${STATE:=provisioning}"
  local padded; padded="$(pad_version "${VERSION:-0}")"
  ddb_init
  put_item "$(cat <<JSON
{
  "PK":               {"S": "ACCOUNT#${ACCOUNT_ID}"},
  "SK":               {"S": "META"},
  "record_type":      {"S": "ACCOUNT"},
  "baseline_version": {"S": "${padded}"},
  "account_id":       {"S": "${ACCOUNT_ID}"},
  "partner":          {"S": "${PARTNER}"},
  "client":           {"S": "${SLUG}"},
  "app":              {"S": "${APP:-}"},
  "environment":      {"S": "${ENVIRONMENT}"},
  "state":            {"S": "${STATE}"},
  "service_model":    {"S": "${SERVICE_MODEL:-unset}"},
  "compliance_scope": {"S": "${COMPLIANCE:-none}"},
  "kind":             {"S": "${KIND:-tenant}"},
  "updated_at":       {"S": "$(now_iso)"}
}
JSON
)"
  ok "account ${ACCOUNT_ID} recorded: ${PARTNER}/${SLUG}${APP:+/${APP}} ${ENVIRONMENT} baseline=${padded}"
}

cmd_get_account() {
  [[ -n "${ACCOUNT_ID}" ]] || die "--account-id is required."
  ddb_init
  ddb query --table-name "${TABLE}" \
    --key-condition-expression 'PK = :a' \
    --expression-attribute-values "{\":a\":{\"S\":\"ACCOUNT#${ACCOUNT_ID}\"}}" \
    --query 'Items' --output json
}

cmd_list_accounts() {
  ddb_init
  ddb query --table-name "${TABLE}" --index-name by-type \
    --key-condition-expression 'record_type = :t' \
    --expression-attribute-values '{":t":{"S":"ACCOUNT"}}' \
    --query 'Items[].[account_id.S,partner.S,client.S,environment.S,state.S,baseline_version.S]' \
    --output text | no_cr | sed 's/^/  /'
}

cmd_put_override() {
  [[ -n "${ACCOUNT_ID}" ]] || die "--account-id is required."
  [[ -n "${NAME}" ]]       || die "--name is required."
  [[ -n "${REASON}" ]]     || die "--reason is required. An override without a reason is drift with paperwork."
  [[ -n "${OWNER}" ]]      || die "--owner is required. Someone must be accountable for every difference."
  ddb_init
  put_item "$(cat <<JSON
{
  "PK":          {"S": "ACCOUNT#${ACCOUNT_ID}"},
  "SK":          {"S": "OVERRIDE#${NAME}"},
  "record_type": {"S": "OVERRIDE"},
  "baseline_version": {"S": "000000"},
  "account_id":  {"S": "${ACCOUNT_ID}"},
  "name":        {"S": "${NAME}"},
  "reason":      $(ddb_str "${REASON}"),
  "owner":       $(ddb_str "${OWNER}"),
  "review_by":   {"S": "${REVIEW_BY:-unset}"},
  "updated_at":  {"S": "$(now_iso)"}
}
JSON
)"
  ok "override ${NAME} on ${ACCOUNT_ID} declared, owned by ${OWNER}"
  [[ -n "${REVIEW_BY}" ]] || warn "No --review-by date. An override with no review date is permanent by default."
}

cmd_drop_override() {
  [[ -n "${ACCOUNT_ID}" ]] || die "--account-id is required."
  [[ -n "${NAME}" ]]       || die "--name is required."
  ddb_init
  ddb delete-item --table-name "${TABLE}" \
    --key "{\"PK\":{\"S\":\"ACCOUNT#${ACCOUNT_ID}\"},\"SK\":{\"S\":\"OVERRIDE#${NAME}\"}}"
  ok "override ${NAME} on ${ACCOUNT_ID} withdrawn"
  warn "The account's actual configuration has NOT changed. Withdrawing the
      declaration turns a declared override into undeclared difference, which
      is drift. Reconcile the account, or this will surface as a finding."
}

cmd_set_baseline() {
  [[ -n "${VERSION}" ]] || die "--version is required."
  local padded; padded="$(pad_version "${VERSION}")"
  ddb_init
  put_item "$(cat <<JSON
{
  "PK":               {"S": "CONFIG"},
  "SK":               {"S": "BASELINE"},
  "record_type":      {"S": "CONFIG"},
  "baseline_version": {"S": "${padded}"},
  "updated_at":       {"S": "$(now_iso)"}
}
JSON
)"
  ok "current global baseline version = ${padded}"
}

current_baseline() {
  ddb get-item --table-name "${TABLE}" \
    --key '{"PK":{"S":"CONFIG"},"SK":{"S":"BASELINE"}}' \
    --query 'Item.baseline_version.S' --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr
}

cmd_get_baseline() {
  ddb_init
  local v; v="$(current_baseline)"
  [[ -n "${v}" && "${v}" != "None" ]] \
    || die "No baseline version recorded. Set one: scripts/registry.sh set-baseline --version 1"
  log "${v}"
}

# Report 1 — accounts behind the current global baseline version.
cmd_report_baseline() {
  ddb_init
  local cur; cur="$(current_baseline)"
  [[ -n "${cur}" && "${cur}" != "None" ]] \
    || die "No baseline version recorded. Set one: scripts/registry.sh set-baseline --version 1"

  hr
  log "Accounts behind the current baseline"
  log "  current version : ${cur}"
  hr

  # Range query on the GSI sort key. This is the reason baseline_version is
  # zero-padded: an unpadded "9" would sort ABOVE "10" and be reported as up to
  # date.
  local out
  out="$(ddb query --table-name "${TABLE}" --index-name by-type \
    --key-condition-expression 'record_type = :t AND baseline_version < :v' \
    --expression-attribute-values "{\":t\":{\"S\":\"ACCOUNT\"},\":v\":{\"S\":\"${cur}\"}}" \
    --query 'Items[].[account_id.S,partner.S,client.S,environment.S,baseline_version.S]' \
    --output text | no_cr)"

  if [[ -z "${out}" ]]; then
    ok "every account is at ${cur}"
  else
    printf '%s\n' "${out}" | sed 's/^/  /'
    printf '\n'
    warn "$(printf '%s\n' "${out}" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') account(s) behind ${cur}"
  fi
  hr
}

# Report 2 — declared local overrides: what, why, who owns each.
cmd_report_overrides() {
  ddb_init
  hr
  log "Declared local overrides"
  hr
  local out
  out="$(ddb query --table-name "${TABLE}" --index-name by-type \
    --key-condition-expression 'record_type = :t' \
    --expression-attribute-values '{":t":{"S":"OVERRIDE"}}' \
    --query 'Items[].[account_id.S,name.S,owner.S,review_by.S,reason.S]' \
    --output text | no_cr)"

  if [[ -z "${out}" ]]; then
    ok "no declared overrides"
    log ""
    log "  Note that this is NOT the same as 'no differences'. It means nobody"
    log "  has declared one. An undeclared difference is drift, and this report"
    log "  cannot see it — comparing recorded parameters against actual AWS"
    log "  configuration is a separate job. See B-022."
  else
    printf '%s\n' "${out}" | sed 's/^/  /'
    printf '\n'
    local stale
    stale="$(printf '%s\n' "${out}" | awk -F'\t' -v today="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)" \
      '$4 != "unset" && $4 < today {print}' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
    [[ "${stale}" == "0" ]] || warn "${stale} override(s) past their review date"
    local unset_count
    unset_count="$(printf '%s\n' "${out}" | awk -F'\t' '$4 == "unset" {print}' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
    [[ "${unset_count}" == "0" ]] || warn "${unset_count} override(s) have no review date and are permanent by default"
  fi
  hr
}

case "${CMD}" in
  put-partner)      cmd_put_partner ;;
  get-partner)      cmd_get_partner ;;
  list-partners)    cmd_list_partners ;;
  check-partner)    cmd_check_partner ;;
  put-client)       cmd_put_client ;;
  list-clients)     cmd_list_clients ;;
  put-account)      cmd_put_account ;;
  get-account)      cmd_get_account ;;
  list-accounts)    cmd_list_accounts ;;
  put-override)     cmd_put_override ;;
  drop-override)    cmd_drop_override ;;
  set-baseline)     cmd_set_baseline ;;
  get-baseline)     cmd_get_baseline ;;
  report-baseline)  cmd_report_baseline ;;
  report-overrides) cmd_report_overrides ;;
  -h|--help|help)   usage ;;
  *) usage; die "Unknown command: ${CMD}" ;;
esac
files.scripts/render-pagerduty-tenants.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Render pagerduty/tenants.json from the registry.
#
#   scripts/render-pagerduty-tenants.sh [--dry-run]
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why this renders DATA and not Terraform
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generated .tf is reviewable only by someone who reads Terraform, diffs
# noisily whenever the generator's formatting changes, and lets a generator bug
# create a resource nobody intended. Generated data can only populate shapes
# `pagerduty/tenants.tf` already declares, so a generator bug produces a wrong
# VALUE rather than a wrong RESOURCE.
#
# The practical consequence is that adding a client is a one-line diff in a
# JSON map, which Art or Wayne can review in a pull request without knowing
# Terraform.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why it is a script and not part of the saga Lambda
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# design 13 says to treat PagerDuty "exactly like the AWS baseline: versioned,
# staged, drift-detected". The AWS baseline is applied by scripts a person
# runs, and so is this. A Lambda cannot write a file into the repository, and
# a Lambda calling the PagerDuty API directly would make every tenant service
# drift relative to Terraform state -- which would make the drift detector
# design 13 asks for fire on the platform's own work.
#
# So provisioning step 3 BLOCKS and tells the operator to run this, apply, and
# sync. That is the same shape as step 9's go-live gate: a human step inside
# the workflow rather than beside it.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What is included, and what absence means
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#   clients    every TENANT record not in a terminal or dormant state. Dormant
#              tenants have had their paging removed on purpose (design 14 and
#              the deprovisioning UNDO table), so re-rendering them would
#              recreate what a teardown deliberately took away.
#   tiers      ACCOUNT records with kind=tenant, grouped by client and then by
#              environment. EVERY tier, not production only -- see D-018. A dev
#              environment is the developer's own production and needs somewhere
#              for its alerts to go; the separation from production is urgency
#              and escalation policy, not absence.
#   objects    the `app` field on each account, which is the finest granularity
#              the registry currently carries. The empty string is a real value
#              meaning the account's single unnamed application.
#
# A client with no accounts renders an EMPTY tiers map. That is correct -- it
# gets the client-conversation business service and nothing else -- and it is
# not the same as the client being absent. The summary prints both counts so
# the difference is visible rather than inferred.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

OUT="${REPO_ROOT}/pagerduty/tenants.json"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    --out)     OUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -h|--help)
      printf 'Usage: %s [--dry-run] [--out <path>]\n' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

TOOLING="$(get_param /org/account/altdig-infra-tooling)"
[[ -n "${TOOLING}" && "${TOOLING}" != "None" ]] \
  || die "Platform Tooling is not registered in SSM; the registry cannot be read."

info "reading platform-registry from tooling (${TOOLING})"

ITEMS="$(in_account "${TOOLING}" aws dynamodb scan \
  --table-name platform-registry --output json 2>/dev/null)" \
  || die "Could not scan platform-registry in ${TOOLING}."

[[ -n "${ITEMS}" ]] || die "The registry scan returned nothing at all, which is not the same as an empty registry. Refusing to render."

RENDERED="$(ITEMS="${ITEMS}" python - <<'PYEOF'
import json, os, sys

items = json.loads(os.environ["ITEMS"]).get("Items") or []


def s(item, key):
    return (item.get(key) or {}).get("S") or ""


# Dormant is excluded deliberately: a dormant tenant's paging was removed by a
# teardown, and re-rendering it here would quietly put back what that teardown
# took away. Exited tenants are excluded for the same reason, more finally.
LIVE_STATES = {"provisioning", "provisioned", "verifying", "live"}

clients, apps, skipped, unplaced = {}, {}, [], []

for item in items:
    kind = s(item, "record_type")

    if kind == "TENANT" or (not kind and s(item, "tenant_id")):
        tid = s(item, "tenant_id")
        state = s(item, "state")
        if not tid:
            continue
        if state not in LIVE_STATES:
            skipped.append({"client": tid, "state": state})
            continue
        clients[tid] = s(item, "partner")

    elif kind == "ACCOUNT":
        # Tenant accounts in every tier. A PLATFORM account is AltDigital's own
        # and is covered by the platform service, not by a tenant one -- that
        # is the only exclusion here.
        if (s(item, "kind") or "tenant") != "tenant":
            continue
        env = s(item, "environment")
        if not env:
            # An account with no environment cannot be placed in a tier, and
            # guessing one would put a production workload behind dev-tier
            # urgency. Reported rather than assigned.
            unplaced.append({"account_id": s(item, "account_id"),
                             "client": s(item, "client")})
            continue
        apps.setdefault(s(item, "client"), {}).setdefault(env, set()).add(
            s(item, "app"))

tenants = {}
for tid, partner in sorted(clients.items()):
    tiers = {}
    for env, objects in sorted((apps.get(tid) or {}).items()):
        tiers[env] = {"objects": sorted(objects)}
    tenants[tid] = {"partner": partner, "tiers": tiers}

# Accounts whose client has no TENANT record. Reported rather than dropped:
# a production account with no registry tenant is a real inconsistency, and
# silently omitting it would mean an account whose alarms page nowhere.
orphans = sorted(set(apps) - set(clients))

print(json.dumps({
    "tenants": tenants,
    "_summary": {
        "records_scanned": len(items),
        "clients_included": len(tenants),
        "clients_skipped": skipped,
        "clients_with_accounts": sum(
            1 for t in tenants.values() if t["tiers"]),
        "tiers_total": sum(len(t["tiers"]) for t in tenants.values()),
        "objects_total": sum(
            len(c["objects"]) for t in tenants.values()
            for c in t["tiers"].values()),
        "orphan_accounts": orphans,
        "unplaced_accounts": unplaced,
    },
}, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
PYEOF
)" || die "Rendering failed."

SUMMARY="$(printf '%s' "${RENDERED}" | python -c 'import json,sys; print(json.dumps(json.load(sys.stdin)["_summary"]))')"
PAYLOAD="$(printf '%s' "${RENDERED}" | python -c '
import json, sys
d = json.load(sys.stdin)
d.pop("_summary", None)
print(json.dumps(d, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
')"

SCANNED="$(printf '%s' "${SUMMARY}" | python -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["records_scanned"])')"
INCLUDED="$(printf '%s' "${SUMMARY}" | python -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["clients_included"])')"
WITHPROD="$(printf '%s' "${SUMMARY}" | python -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["clients_with_accounts"])')"
TIERS="$(printf '%s' "${SUMMARY}" | python -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["tiers_total"])')"
OBJECTS="$(printf '%s' "${SUMMARY}" | python -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["objects_total"])')"
UNPLACED="$(printf '%s' "${SUMMARY}" | python -c 'import json,sys; print(len(json.load(sys.stdin)["unplaced_accounts"]))')"
ORPHANS="$(printf '%s' "${SUMMARY}" | python -c 'import json,sys; print(" ".join(json.load(sys.stdin)["orphan_accounts"]) or "none")')"
SKIPPED="$(printf '%s' "${SUMMARY}" | python -c '
import json, sys
rows = json.load(sys.stdin)["clients_skipped"]
print(", ".join(r["client"] + "(" + r["state"] + ")" for r in rows) or "none")')"

hr
log "PagerDuty tenant map"
# What was EXAMINED, not only what was found. A render that emitted an empty
# map because the scan returned nothing would otherwise look identical to a
# render of an estate with no tenants in it.
log "  registry records scanned : ${SCANNED}"
log "  clients included         : ${INCLUDED}"
log "  of which with accounts   : ${WITHPROD}"
log "  tiers                    : ${TIERS}"
log "  objects                  : ${OBJECTS}"
log "  accounts with no tier    : ${UNPLACED}"
log "  clients skipped          : ${SKIPPED}"
log "  orphan accounts          : ${ORPHANS}"
hr

if [[ "${ORPHANS}" != "none" ]]; then
  # Not fatal, and not silent. A production account whose client has no tenant
  # record gets no paging service, which means its alarms page nobody.
  warn "Account(s) for client(s) with no TENANT record: ${ORPHANS}"
  warn "These get no service, so their alarms would reach nobody."
fi

if [[ "${UNPLACED}" != "0" ]]; then
  # An account with no environment cannot be placed in a tier. Guessing would
  # put a production workload behind dev-tier urgency, which is the wrong
  # direction to be wrong in.
  warn "${UNPLACED} account(s) carry no environment and were not placed in any tier."
  warn "Their alarms have no service to reach. Fix the registry record."
fi

if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
  printf '%s DRY%s  would write %s\n' "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}" "${OUT}"
  printf '%s\n' "${PAYLOAD}"
  exit 0
fi

printf '%s\n' "${PAYLOAD}" > "${OUT}"
ok "wrote ${OUT}"

hr
info "Next:"
log "  scripts/pagerduty-apply.sh            # plan, and read it"
log "  scripts/pagerduty-apply.sh --apply"
log "  scripts/sync-pagerduty-tenants.sh     # routing keys -> Secrets Manager,"
log "                                        # service ids -> registry"
hr
files.scripts/seed-restore-fixture.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Take the first recovery point of the sandbox restore-test fixture, so the
# restore workflow has something real to restore.
#
#   scripts/seed-restore-fixture.sh [--account <alias>] [--dry-run]
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why this is a script and not a backup plan
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A backup PLAN would be policy: a schedule, a retention rule, a lifecycle, a
# selection. None of those values exist anywhere in the design package —
# design/05-resilience.md is absent — and inventing them is what CLAUDE.md
# forbids. See the header of recovery/00-restore-fixture.yaml and B-043.
#
# What the restore workflow needs to be PROVEN is not a policy. It is one
# recovery point. So this takes one, on demand, by hand, in the sandbox, and
# does not pretend to be anything else.
#
# Re-run it whenever the sandbox needs a fresher recovery point. It is
# idempotent in the sense that matters: a second run makes a second recovery
# point, the workflow picks the most recent COMPLETED one, and nothing is
# overwritten or deleted.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

ACCOUNT_KEY="altdig-sandbox-canary"
VAULT="platform-restore-fixture"
STACK="platform-restore-fixture"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --account) ACCOUNT_KEY="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --vault)   VAULT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --stack)   STACK="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) printf 'Usage: %s [--account <alias>] [--dry-run]\n' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

TARGET="$(get_param "/org/account/${ACCOUNT_KEY}")"
[[ -n "${TARGET}" && "${TARGET}" != "None" ]] \
  || die "Account ${ACCOUNT_KEY} is not registered in SSM."

info "Assuming into ${ACCOUNT_KEY} (${TARGET})"
CREDS="$(aws sts assume-role \
  --role-arn "arn:aws:iam::${TARGET}:role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole" \
  --role-session-name seed-restore-fixture \
  --query 'Credentials.[AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey,SessionToken]' \
  --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || true
[[ -n "${CREDS}" ]] || die "Could not assume into ${TARGET}."
read -r AK SK ST <<<"${CREDS}"
unset AWS_PROFILE
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="${AK}" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="${SK}" AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="${ST}"

# The volume ARN comes from the fixture stack's output rather than being
# constructed here. Two places building the same ARN is two places to get the
# partition or the region wrong.
VOLUME_ARN="$(aws cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name "${STACK}" \
  --query "Stacks[0].Outputs[?OutputKey=='VolumeArn'].OutputValue | [0]" \
  --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)"
[[ -n "${VOLUME_ARN}" && "${VOLUME_ARN}" != "None" ]] \
  || die "Stack ${STACK} has no VolumeArn output. Deploy
      recovery/00-restore-fixture.yaml first."

# AWS Backup needs a role to assume to take the backup, just as it does to
# restore. The restore role from recovery/10-restore-workflow.yaml cannot be
# reused: its managed policy grants RESTORE permissions, and a backup job needs
# CreateSnapshot on the source. AWS's own backup service role is used instead,
# created on demand here because it belongs to this scaffolding and not to the
# platform.
ROLE_NAME="PlatformRestoreFixtureBackup"
ROLE_ARN="arn:aws:iam::${TARGET}:role/${ROLE_NAME}"

if ! aws iam get-role --role-name "${ROLE_NAME}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  info "Creating ${ROLE_NAME}"
  if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" != "1" ]]; then
    MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws iam create-role --role-name "${ROLE_NAME}" \
      --description "Scaffolding for the sandbox restore-test fixture. Not part of the platform baseline." \
      --assume-role-policy-document '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"Service":"backup.amazonaws.com"},"Action":"sts:AssumeRole"}]}' \
      >/dev/null
    MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name "${ROLE_NAME}" \
      --policy-arn 'arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSBackupServiceRolePolicyForBackup'
    ok "${ROLE_NAME} created"
    # IAM is eventually consistent and StartBackupJob validates the role at
    # submission. Without this the first run after creating the role fails with
    # "Role cannot be assumed", which reads as a policy error and is not one.
    info "Waiting for IAM to settle"
    sleep 12
  fi
else
  skip "${ROLE_NAME} already exists"
fi

if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
  printf '%s DRY%s  would start a backup job for %s into %s\n' \
    "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}" "${VOLUME_ARN}" "${VAULT}"
  exit 0
fi

info "Starting the backup job"
JOB="$(MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws backup start-backup-job \
  --backup-vault-name "${VAULT}" \
  --resource-arn "${VOLUME_ARN}" \
  --iam-role-arn "${ROLE_ARN}" \
  --query BackupJobId --output text | no_cr)"
ok "backup job ${JOB}"

# Waited on rather than fired and forgotten. The point of this script is that a
# recovery point EXISTS afterwards; returning before it does would leave the
# next step to fail with "no recovery point", which is the very message the
# workflow uses for the real gap this is working around.
info "Waiting for it to complete"
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  STATUS="$(aws backup describe-backup-job --backup-job-id "${JOB}" \
    --query State --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)"
  case "${STATUS}" in
    COMPLETED)
      RP="$(aws backup describe-backup-job --backup-job-id "${JOB}" \
        --query RecoveryPointArn --output text | no_cr)"
      hr
      ok "recovery point ready"
      log "  ${RP}"
      hr
      log "Now deploy recovery/10-restore-workflow.yaml with:"
      log "  BackupVaultName=${VAULT}"
      log "  SourceResourceArn=${VOLUME_ARN}"
      exit 0 ;;
    FAILED|ABORTED|EXPIRED)
      REASON="$(aws backup describe-backup-job --backup-job-id "${JOB}" \
        --query StatusMessage --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)"
      die "Backup job ${STATUS}: ${REASON}" ;;
    *)
      printf '  %s ...\n' "${STATUS}"
      sleep 15 ;;
  esac
done

die "Backup job ${JOB} did not complete within 15 minutes. It is still running;
      check with: aws backup describe-backup-job --backup-job-id ${JOB}"
files.scripts/set-cost-rates.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Publish the support pricing rates to SSM.
#
#   scripts/set-cost-rates.sh [--dry-run]
#
# Reads config/rates.env, which is gitignored. Rates are commercial terms: they
# do not belong in the repository, they are not printed by this script, and the
# monthly report reads them from Parameter Store rather than carrying them.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why this refuses to default to design 10's numbers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# design/10-commercial-model.md gives ~$1,000/account/month and 15-20%, and
# immediately says:
#
#     Model A is materially less work than Model B. The flat fee and percentage
#     should differ accordingly. Worth pricing before the first contract rather
#     than after.
#
# They are a starting point for a conversation, not a price list. A report that
# quietly used them would put a number in front of a customer that no human
# chose, and an indicative figure that reaches a customer becomes the price.
#
# So cost/src/report.py refuses to produce anything until this has run, and
# marks every output as an estimate until RATES_ARE_CONTRACTUAL is set.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) printf 'Usage: %s [--dry-run]\n' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

RATES_FILE="${REPO_ROOT}/config/rates.env"
[[ -f "${RATES_FILE}" ]] || die "config/rates.env not found.
      Copy config/rates.env.example and fill in the agreed figures.
      That file is gitignored: pricing is a commercial term, not source."

# `set -a` so the rates are EXPORTED, not merely set.
#
# The helper below reads them from os.environ, and a plain `source` creates
# shell variables that a child process cannot see -- so it found nothing and
# reported "config/rates.env defines no RATE_<MODEL>_FLAT / _PERCENT pairs"
# about a file full of them.
#
# Turned off immediately after: leaving allexport on would export every
# variable this script later assigns, including the assembled payload, into
# anything it runs.
set -a
# shellcheck disable=SC1090
source "${RATES_FILE}"
set +a

PY="$(command -v python || command -v python3)" || die "python not found."

PAYLOAD="$("${PY}" - "$@" <<'PYEOF'
import json
import os
import sys

models = {}
for key, value in os.environ.items():
    # RATE_<MODEL>_FLAT and RATE_<MODEL>_PERCENT
    if not key.startswith("RATE_"):
        continue
    parts = key.split("_")
    if len(parts) < 3:
        continue
    model = "_".join(parts[1:-1]).lower()
    field = parts[-1].lower()
    entry = models.setdefault(model, {})
    try:
        entry[field] = float(value)
    except ValueError:
        sys.exit(f"{key} is not a number.")

out = {}
for model, entry in models.items():
    if "flat" not in entry or "percent" not in entry:
        sys.exit(
            f"service model '{model}' needs both RATE_{model.upper()}_FLAT and "
            f"RATE_{model.upper()}_PERCENT. A model with only one of them "
            "would bill a flat fee with no uplift, or the reverse, and the "
            "report would look correct.")
    out[model] = {
        "flat_fee_per_account_month": entry["flat"],
        "uplift_percent": entry["percent"],
    }

if not out:
    sys.exit("config/rates.env defines no RATE_<MODEL>_FLAT / _PERCENT pairs.")

print(json.dumps(
    {"service_models": out,
     "rates_are_contractual":
         os.environ.get("RATES_ARE_CONTRACTUAL", "").lower() == "true"},
    separators=(",", ":")))
PYEOF
)" || die "Could not build the rates document."

MODELS="$("${PY}" -c "
import json,sys
print(' '.join(sorted(json.loads(sys.argv[1])['service_models'])))
" "${PAYLOAD}")"
CONTRACTUAL="$("${PY}" -c "
import json,sys
print(json.loads(sys.argv[1])['rates_are_contractual'])
" "${PAYLOAD}")"

hr
log "Support pricing rates"
log "  account      : management (${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID})"
log "  service models: ${MODELS}"
log "  contractual  : ${CONTRACTUAL}"
log "  parameter    : /platform/cost/rates"
hr
# The figures themselves are NOT printed. This output lands in terminals, CI
# logs and screenshares, and a rate is a commercial term.

if [[ "${CONTRACTUAL}" != "True" ]]; then
  warn "Rates are not marked contractual. Every report will carry a warning"
  warn "that it is an estimate and must not be sent to a customer. Set"
  warn "RATES_ARE_CONTRACTUAL=true once the figures are agreed."
fi

if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
  printf '%s DRY%s  would write /platform/cost/rates\n' "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}"
  exit 0
fi

export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*'
aws ssm put-parameter \
  --name /platform/cost/rates \
  --value "${PAYLOAD}" \
  --type String \
  --description "Support pricing per service model. design 10. Set by scripts/set-cost-rates.sh from gitignored config/rates.env." \
  --overwrite --output text --query Version >/dev/null \
  || die "Could not write /platform/cost/rates."
ok "published /platform/cost/rates"

hr
info "The monthly report reads this. It refuses to run without it, rather"
log "  than falling back to design 10's indicative figures — those are a"
log "  starting point for pricing, not a price list."
hr

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Store the Jira Cloud service account credential in Secrets Manager, in every
# account that reads it, in one run.
#
#   scripts/set-jira-token.sh                  # prompts, input hidden
#   ... | scripts/set-jira-token.sh --stdin    # token on stdin
#   scripts/set-jira-token.sh --propagate      # fan an existing value out
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why the email lives in the secret and not in config/platform.env
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Jira Cloud's REST API authenticates with HTTP Basic using
# `<account-email>:<api-token>`. Both halves are required, and they rotate
# together — a token reissued for a different service account is useless
# against the old email.
#
# Keeping them in one secret has a second benefit: the email is a direct
# address for a person or a platform identity, and CLAUDE.md keeps those out of
# the repository. Secrets Manager is where it belongs anyway.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What this credential can do, which is a lot
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# This credential both reads and WRITES, and the write half is not optional.
#
#   reconciliation (8.2)   reads issues
#   quorum (8.3)           reads issues, changelogs and approvals
#   the filer (8.2)        raises change requests and edits them
#   provisioning (12.3)    creates onboarding issues, obligations and the
#                          per-tenant JSM organization
#
# An earlier version of this header said to scope the account read-only. That
# was true when only reconciliation used it and is now wrong: the filer raises
# a JSM request and then edits it, because Labels and Approver groups are not
# on the request type's form and both are load-bearing. In JSM terms that means
# AGENT access to the change project, not customer access - a customer can
# raise a request and cannot edit one.
#
# So the circularity the old text worried about cannot be handled by scoping.
# It is handled in code and in Jira instead:
#
#   code   jira.py has no write method and publish-change.sh refuses to
#          package it if one appears. filer.py may write but may not call an
#          approval or transition endpoint. jira_tenant.py checks every write
#          path against an allow-list of issue and organization endpoints.
#   Jira   this account MUST NOT be a member of any approver group. A
#          credential that can edit issues and also approve them can
#          manufacture the approval the quorum pipeline then verifies, and the
#          control is circular however the code is arranged.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Every consuming account, in one run — B-110
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A secret is only useful in the account that reads it, and there are now two
# such accounts:
#
#   audit     reconciliation (8.2) and quorum (8.3), alongside the router and
#             containment, because that is where deployment events land and
#             where Security Hub is aggregated.
#   tooling   provisioning (12.3), because that is where `platform-registry`
#             lives and the saga reads the registry on every step.
#
# The obvious alternative — one copy in audit, read cross-account from tooling —
# is NOT available. The secret is encrypted under the AWS-managed
# `aws/secretsmanager` key, and AWS-managed keys cannot be shared across
# accounts. It would have to be re-created under a customer-managed key first.
#
# So there are two copies, and two copies of a credential is a rotation
# hazard: update one, miss the other, and the missed account keeps working on
# the old value until the old value is revoked — at which point it fails in a
# way that looks like an outage rather than like a half-finished rotation.
#
# This script removes that hazard by construction. One invocation writes ALL
# consuming accounts, then reads each one back and compares fingerprints. There
# is no supported way to rotate one and not the other, and if a write fails
# part way the script says exactly which accounts hold which value rather than
# reporting a generic failure.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Never on a command line
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# No --token flag, deliberately. An argument is visible in the process list to
# every user on the machine and lands in shell history. Input comes from a
# hidden prompt or from stdin.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

FROM_STDIN=0
PROPAGATE=0
SECRET_NAME="platform/jira/service-account"
EMAIL=""

# The consuming accounts, by SSM alias. Order matters only for --propagate,
# which sources the existing value from the first one that has it.
CONSUMER_KEYS="altdig-security-audit altdig-infra-tooling"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --stdin)     FROM_STDIN=1; shift ;;
    --propagate) PROPAGATE=1; shift ;;
    --email)     EMAIL="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --secret)    SECRET_NAME="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    # Overrides the whole list, not one entry. Comma or space separated.
    # Narrowing this is how a half-rotation gets done deliberately, so it is
    # deliberately awkward to do by accident.
    --account)   CONSUMER_KEYS="${2//,/ }"; shift 2 ;;
    -h|--help)
      printf 'Usage: %s [--email <addr>] [--stdin] [--propagate] [--secret <name>] [--account <alias>[,<alias>]]\n' "$0"
      exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

# --- resolve the consuming accounts ----------------------------------------

mapfile -t ACCOUNTS < <(resolve_accounts ${CONSUMER_KEYS})
info "consuming accounts: ${ACCOUNTS[*]}"

# --- obtain the payload -----------------------------------------------------

if [[ "${PROPAGATE}" == "1" ]]; then
  # Repair, not rotation. The credential already exists somewhere and one or
  # more accounts are missing it or hold an older value. Nothing is prompted,
  # because re-typing a token to fan it out is how a typo becomes a rotation
  # nobody meant to do.
  PAYLOAD=""
  for entry in "${ACCOUNTS[@]}"; do
    candidate="$(read_secret "${entry##*:}" "${SECRET_NAME}")"
    if [[ -n "${candidate}" && "${candidate}" != "None" ]]; then
      PAYLOAD="${candidate}"
      ok "propagating the value already held by ${entry%%:*}"
      break
    fi
  done
  [[ -n "${PAYLOAD}" ]] \
    || die "--propagate found no existing credential in any consuming account. There is nothing to fan out; run without --propagate to store one."
else
  if [[ -z "${EMAIL}" ]]; then
    # The email is not secret in the way the token is, so it is prompted
    # normally. It is still not accepted as a positional argument, because a
    # mistyped positional would be stored silently.
    printf 'Jira service account email: '
    read -r EMAIL
  fi
  [[ -n "${EMAIL}" ]] || die "No email supplied."
  [[ "${EMAIL}" == *"@"* ]] || die "That does not look like an email address."

  if [[ "${FROM_STDIN}" == "1" ]]; then
    read -r TOKEN
  else
    printf 'Jira API token (input hidden): '
    # -s so it is never echoed to the terminal or captured by a screen recorder.
    read -rs TOKEN
    printf '\n'
  fi
  [[ -n "${TOKEN}" ]] || die "No token supplied."

  # Length check only. The value is never printed, never logged, and never
  # interpolated into a message — an error that quotes a credential back is how
  # credentials end up in terminal scrollback and support tickets.
  if [[ ${#TOKEN} -lt 20 ]]; then
    warn "That token is shorter than any Jira Cloud API token observed so far."
    warn "Storing it anyway; verify with scripts/jira-check.sh."
  fi

  PAYLOAD="$(EMAIL="${EMAIL}" TOKEN="${TOKEN}" python -c '
import json, os
print(json.dumps({"email": os.environ["EMAIL"],
                  "api_token": os.environ["TOKEN"]}))
')"
  unset TOKEN
fi

store_secret_everywhere   "${SECRET_NAME}"   "Jira Cloud service account for change reconciliation (8.2), quorum verification (8.3) and tenant provisioning (12.3). Written by scripts/set-jira-token.sh."   "${PAYLOAD}"   "${ACCOUNTS[@]}"
unset PAYLOAD
