#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Store the PagerDuty REST API token in Secrets Manager, in every account that
# reads it, in one run.
#
#   scripts/set-pagerduty-token.sh              # prompts, input hidden
#   ... | scripts/set-pagerduty-token.sh --stdin
#   scripts/set-pagerduty-token.sh --propagate  # fan an existing value out
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# An ACCOUNT key, not a personal one
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# prompt 12.2: "Authenticate as a platform service account with tokens in
# Secrets Manager, rotated. Not a personal account."
#
# PagerDuty has no separate service-account object in the classic model. The
# equivalent is a **General Access REST API Key**, created under
# Integrations -> API Access Keys, which belongs to the account rather than to
# a person. That distinction is the whole requirement:
#
#   a user token     dies when the person leaves, consumes a seat, and
#                    attributes every platform action to a human who did not
#                    take it
#   an account key   survives staff changes and is revocable without
#                    disturbing anyone's login
#
# It must NOT be read-only. This creates services, escalation policies and
# business services.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What reads it
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#   tooling   provisioning renders a tenant's PagerDuty configuration from the
#             registry (saga step 3) and reads back what exists to confirm it
#   audit     the drift detector, alongside the rest of the detection estate
#
# And Terraform, run from a workstation by a person. `pagerduty-apply.sh`
# reads the token from Secrets Manager rather than requiring PAGERDUTY_TOKEN
# to be exported by hand — an exported credential outlives the shell it was
# meant for and ends up in a scrollback.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Never on a command line
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# No --token flag, deliberately. An argument is visible in the process list to
# every user on the machine and lands in shell history. Input comes from a
# hidden prompt or from stdin.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

FROM_STDIN=0
PROPAGATE=0
SECRET_NAME="platform/pagerduty/api-token"

# Overriding this narrows the fan-out, which is how a half-rotation gets done
# on purpose. Comma or space separated.
CONSUMER_KEYS="altdig-security-audit altdig-infra-tooling"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --stdin)     FROM_STDIN=1; shift ;;
    --propagate) PROPAGATE=1; shift ;;
    --secret)    SECRET_NAME="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --account)   CONSUMER_KEYS="${2//,/ }"; shift 2 ;;
    -h|--help)
      printf 'Usage: %s [--stdin] [--propagate] [--secret <name>] [--account <alias>[,<alias>]]\n' "$0"
      exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

mapfile -t ACCOUNTS < <(resolve_accounts ${CONSUMER_KEYS})
info "consuming accounts: ${ACCOUNTS[*]}"

if [[ "${PROPAGATE}" == "1" ]]; then
  PAYLOAD=""
  for entry in "${ACCOUNTS[@]}"; do
    candidate="$(read_secret "${entry##*:}" "${SECRET_NAME}")"
    if [[ -n "${candidate}" && "${candidate}" != "None" ]]; then
      PAYLOAD="${candidate}"
      ok "propagating the value already held by ${entry%%:*}"
      break
    fi
  done
  [[ -n "${PAYLOAD}" ]] \
    || die "--propagate found no existing token in any consuming account. Run without --propagate to store one."
else
  if [[ "${FROM_STDIN}" == "1" ]]; then
    read -r TOKEN
  else
    printf 'PagerDuty REST API key (input hidden): '
    # -s so it is never echoed to the terminal or captured by a screen recorder.
    read -rs TOKEN
    printf '\n'
  fi
  [[ -n "${TOKEN}" ]] || die "No token supplied."

  # Shape check only, and it is a warning rather than a refusal. PagerDuty's
  # general access keys have been 20 and 32 characters at different times, and
  # a length rule that hard-failed would reject a valid key the first time
  # they changed the format again. The value is never printed.
  if [[ ${#TOKEN} -lt 20 ]]; then
    warn "That key is shorter than any PagerDuty API key observed so far."
    warn "Storing it anyway; verify with scripts/pagerduty-check.sh."
  fi
  if [[ "${TOKEN}" == R0* ]]; then
    # PagerDuty prefixes read-only keys. Catching it here saves discovering it
    # as a 403 from a Terraform apply half way through creating a tenant.
    die "That looks like a READ-ONLY key (they begin R0). This must create services, escalation policies and business services, so it needs a full-access key."
  fi

  PAYLOAD="$(TOKEN="${TOKEN}" python -c '
import json, os
print(json.dumps({"api_token": os.environ["TOKEN"]}))
')"
  unset TOKEN
fi

store_secret_everywhere \
  "${SECRET_NAME}" \
  "PagerDuty REST API key for tenant provisioning (12.2) and drift detection. Account-level key, not a personal token. Written by scripts/set-pagerduty-token.sh." \
  "${PAYLOAD}" \
  "${ACCOUNTS[@]}"
unset PAYLOAD

printf '\n'
info "Next: scripts/pagerduty-check.sh confirms the key authenticates and is not read-only."
files.scripts/setup-tooling.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Install the local validation toolchain.
#
# Run once per workstation. Nothing here touches AWS.
#
#   cfn-lint    — pip, cross-platform
#   cfn-guard   — Rust binary, downloaded from the GitHub release page
#   terraform   — PagerDuty only (design doc 13); winget on Windows
#   pyyaml      — questionnaire parsing for the vesting pipeline
#   jsonschema  — questionnaire validation for the vesting pipeline
#
# This script PRINTS what it would install and asks for confirmation. It does
# not silently pull binaries onto the machine.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

hr
log "Local toolchain check"
hr

# find_tool, not `command -v`.
#
# find_tool is what the pre-commit hook and every other script use: it looks on
# PATH first, then in the places pip --user and winget actually install to on
# Windows, which are frequently not on PATH.
#
# This script used `command -v` and therefore disagreed with the rest of the
# repository — reporting cfn-lint and cfn-guard as "not installed" and printing
# install instructions for tools that were present and working, on the same
# machine, in the same session. A setup checker that is wrong about the setup is
# worse than none, because the natural response is to install a second copy.
need_cfn_lint=0
if LINT_PATH="$(find_tool cfn-lint)"; then
  ok "cfn-lint  $("${LINT_PATH}" --version 2>&1)"
else
  warn "cfn-lint  not installed"
  need_cfn_lint=1
fi

need_cfn_guard=0
if GUARD_PATH="$(find_tool cfn-guard)"; then
  ok "cfn-guard $("${GUARD_PATH}" --version 2>&1)"
else
  warn "cfn-guard not installed"
  need_cfn_guard=1
fi

need_terraform=0
if TF_PATH="$(find_tool terraform)"; then
  ok "terraform $("${TF_PATH}" version 2>&1 | head -1)"
else
  warn "terraform not installed"
  need_terraform=1
fi

# The vesting pipeline validates a completed questionnaire before it creates
# three AWS accounts. Both libraries are pure Python and tiny; the reason they
# are checked here rather than left to fail at run time is that the failure
# would land midway through an onboarding.
need_py=0
for mod in yaml jsonschema; do
  if python -c "import ${mod}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ok "python ${mod}"
  else
    warn "python ${mod} not installed"
    need_py=1
  fi
done

if [[ ${need_cfn_lint} -eq 0 && ${need_cfn_guard} -eq 0       && ${need_terraform} -eq 0 && ${need_py} -eq 0 ]]; then
  hr; ok "Toolchain complete."; exit 0
fi

hr
log "To install:"
[[ ${need_cfn_lint} -eq 1 ]] && log "  pip install --user cfn-lint"
if [[ ${need_cfn_guard} -eq 1 ]]; then
  log ""
  log "  cfn-guard — download the Windows build from:"
  log "    https://github.com/aws-cloudformation/cloudformation-guard/releases/latest"
  log "    file: cfn-guard-v3-x86_64-windows-latest.tar.gz"
  log "    extract cfn-guard.exe somewhere on PATH"
  log ""
  log "  or, if Rust is available:  cargo install cfn-guard"
fi
if [[ ${need_terraform} -eq 1 ]]; then
  log ""
  log "  terraform — used ONLY for PagerDuty, per design doc 13."
  log "    winget install --id Hashicorp.Terraform -e"
  log "    (find_tool knows the winget install path; a new shell is not needed)"
fi
if [[ ${need_py} -eq 1 ]]; then
  log ""
  log "  python -m pip install --user pyyaml jsonschema"
fi
hr
warn "Not installing automatically. Run the commands above, then re-run this script."
files.scripts/sync-account-tiers.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Publish the account -> environment tier map the routing layer reads.
#
#   scripts/sync-account-tiers.sh [--dry-run]
#
# Why the router needs this
# -------------------------
# A Security Hub or GuardDuty finding carries no environment tier, and neither
# does a raw CloudTrail event forwarded by one of 06a's event rules. The router
# has to decide whether a CRITICAL finding pages, and that answer is different
# in a sandbox and in production.
#
# Without the map it assumed "prod" for everything. Findings from the canary
# account were recorded with environment_tier null and routed as production;
# only their MEDIUM severity stopped them paging. A CRITICAL finding in a
# sandbox would have woken somebody at 3am for a dev box.
#
# Where the tier comes from
# -------------------------
# The DEPLOYED stack sets, not the account name.
#
# Account names end in a tier character by convention (-d, -t, -u, -p), and
# reading that would have been simpler and wrong in both directions: the
# platform's own accounts have no tier suffix at all, and the canary account is
# named altdig-infra-canary while its baseline is deployed with
# EnvironmentTier=dev. The name says what an account is called; the stack set
# parameter says how it is actually being monitored, which is the question the
# router is asking.
#
# Reading it from the stack sets also means the map cannot claim a tier for an
# account the platform has not actually instrumented.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) printf 'Usage: %s [--dry-run]\n' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

PY="$(command -v python || command -v python3)" || die "python not found."
AUDIT="$(get_param /org/account/altdig-security-audit)"
[[ -n "${AUDIT}" && "${AUDIT}" != "None" ]] || die "Audit account not registered."

PARAM_NAME="/platform/routing/account-tiers"

# Every stack set that carries an EnvironmentTier. Each one's instances are the
# accounts at that tier. Listed explicitly rather than discovered, because a
# stack set that happens to have an EnvironmentTier parameter is not necessarily
# authoritative about monitoring.
STACKSETS=(platform-instrumentation platform-response)

info "Reading tiers from the deployed stack sets"
MAP="{}"
for ss in "${STACKSETS[@]}"; do
  TIER="$(aws cloudformation describe-stack-set --stack-set-name "${ss}" \
    --call-as SELF \
    --query "StackSet.Parameters[?ParameterKey=='EnvironmentTier'].ParameterValue | [0]" \
    --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || true
  [[ -n "${TIER}" && "${TIER}" != "None" ]] || { skip "${ss}: no EnvironmentTier"; continue; }

  ACCOUNTS="$(aws cloudformation list-stack-instances --stack-set-name "${ss}" \
    --call-as SELF --query 'Summaries[].Account' --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || true
  [[ -n "${ACCOUNTS}" ]] || { skip "${ss}: no instances"; continue; }

  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  MAP="$("${PY}" -c "
import json,sys
m = json.loads(sys.argv[1])
for a in sys.argv[3].split():
    m[a] = sys.argv[2]
print(json.dumps(m, sort_keys=True))
" "${MAP}" "${TIER}" "${ACCOUNTS}")"
  ok "${ss}: tier ${TIER} over $(printf '%s\n' ${ACCOUNTS} | wc -l | tr -d ' ') account(s)"
done

# The platform's own accounts. They run production infrastructure regardless of
# what tier the tenants they serve are at, so a finding in one of them pages.
#
# DISCOVERED from SSM, not listed here.
#
# This was a hand-written list of three names, and creating the Forensics
# account proved the shape wrong: a new platform account simply was not in the
# map, and the router treated it as prod — which pages. The right answer by
# luck, from an omission, and the luck runs out the first time a new account is
# meant to be anything else.
#
# Every platform account is registered under /platform/org/account/<alias> by
# scripts/create-platform-account.sh, so that prefix IS the list. Accounts that
# already picked up a tier from a deployed stack set above are skipped, which
# is what keeps the sandbox and exercise accounts at dev rather than being
# overwritten to prod here.
#
# Same lesson as B-060: derive the list from the thing that creates the
# entries, rather than maintaining a second copy of it by hand.
PLATFORM_IDS="$(aws ssm get-parameters-by-path \
  --path "${PLATFORM_SSM_PREFIX}/org/account" \
  --query 'Parameters[].Value' --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr | tr '\t' '\n')"

for ID in ${PLATFORM_IDS}; do
  if [[ -z "${ID}" || "${ID}" == "None" ]]; then
    continue
  fi
  # Already tiered by a deployed stack set — that answer is better than this
  # one, because it reflects how the account is actually instrumented.
  if printf '%s' "${MAP}" | grep -q "\"${ID}\""; then
    continue
  fi
  MAP="$("${PY}" -c "
import json,sys
m = json.loads(sys.argv[1]); m[sys.argv[2]] = 'prod'
print(json.dumps(m, sort_keys=True))
" "${MAP}" "${ID}")"
done

hr
log "Account tier map"
"${PY}" -c "
import json,sys
m = json.loads(sys.argv[1])
for a, t in sorted(m.items(), key=lambda kv: (kv[1], kv[0])):
    print(f'  {a}  {t}')
print(f'  {len(m)} account(s)')
" "${MAP}"
hr

if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
  printf '%s DRY%s  would write %s in %s\n' \
    "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}" "${PARAM_NAME}" "${AUDIT}"
  exit 0
fi

CREDS="$(aws sts assume-role \
  --role-arn "arn:aws:iam::${AUDIT}:role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole" \
  --role-session-name sync-account-tiers \
  --query 'Credentials.[AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey,SessionToken]' \
  --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || true
[[ -n "${CREDS}" ]] || die "Could not assume into the Audit account (${AUDIT})."
read -r AK SK ST <<<"${CREDS}"
unset AWS_PROFILE
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="${AK}" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="${SK}" AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="${ST}"

MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws ssm put-parameter \
  --name "${PARAM_NAME}" \
  --type String \
  --overwrite \
  --value "${MAP}" \
  --description "Account to environment tier, for the routing layer. Derived from deployed stack set parameters by scripts/sync-account-tiers.sh. An account absent from this map is treated as prod, which pages." \
  --query 'Version' --output text >/dev/null
ok "wrote ${PARAM_NAME} in ${AUDIT}"

hr
info "The router caches this for the life of its execution environment, so a"
log "change takes effect within a few minutes rather than instantly. Re-run"
log "this whenever an account is vested or a tier changes."
hr
files.scripts/sync-cost-categories.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Generate Cost Categories from the platform registry and apply them.
#
#   scripts/sync-cost-categories.sh [--dry-run]
#
# design/10-commercial-model.md, "Cost visibility and allocation":
#
#     Cost Categories map account IDs to tenant, application, environment,
#     service model and compliance scope -- without requiring a single resource
#     tag.
#
# Cost Categories are a BILLING construct and live in the management account,
# which is the payer. That is the one thing in this platform that legitimately
# has to be there: CLAUDE.md keeps the management account nearly empty, and
# this is not a workload, it is a view over the consolidated bill.
#
# Run after vesting an account. Until this runs, a new account's spend appears
# as `unregistered` rather than under its tenant -- visible, and wrong in the
# direction that gets noticed.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) printf 'Usage: %s [--dry-run]\n' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

PY="$(command -v python || command -v python3)" || die "python not found."
export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*'

TOOLING="$(get_param /org/account/altdig-infra-tooling)"
[[ -n "${TOOLING}" && "${TOOLING}" != "None" ]] \
  || die "Platform Tooling account not registered."

WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "${WORK}"' EXIT

# --- the registry, from Tooling ------------------------------------------
CREDS="$(aws sts assume-role \
  --role-arn "arn:aws:iam::${TOOLING}:role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole" \
  --role-session-name sync-cost-categories \
  --query 'Credentials.[AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey,SessionToken]' \
  --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || true
[[ -n "${CREDS}" ]] || die "Could not assume into Platform Tooling."
read -r AK SK ST <<<"${CREDS}"
(
  unset AWS_PROFILE
  export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="${AK}" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="${SK}" \
         AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="${ST}"
  MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws dynamodb scan --table-name platform-registry \
    --query 'Items' --output json
) > "${WORK}/registry.json" 2>/dev/null \
  || die "Could not read the platform registry."

# --- every account the Organization actually contains ---------------------
#
# From Organizations, not from the registry. That is the whole point of the
# comparison: the registry says what SHOULD exist and Organizations says what
# does, and the gap between them is the finding. Reading both from the same
# place would make the check vacuous.
aws organizations list-accounts \
  --query 'Accounts[?Status==`ACTIVE`].Id' --output json \
  > "${WORK}/org.json" 2>/dev/null \
  || die "Could not list Organization accounts."

"${PY}" -c "
import json, sys
reg = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8'))
org = json.load(open(sys.argv[2], encoding='utf-8'))
json.dump({'registry': reg, 'org_accounts': org}, open(sys.argv[3], 'w', encoding='utf-8'))
" "$(win_path "${WORK}/registry.json")" "$(win_path "${WORK}/org.json")" \
  "$(win_path "${WORK}/input.json")"

"${PY}" "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/scripts/lib/cost_categories.py")" \
  < "${WORK}/input.json" > "${WORK}/out.json" \
  || die "Could not generate the Cost Category definitions."

UNREGISTERED="$("${PY}" -c "
import json,sys
d=json.load(open(sys.argv[1],encoding='utf-8'))
print(' '.join(d['unregistered']))
" "$(win_path "${WORK}/out.json")")"

NAMES="$("${PY}" -c "
import json,sys
d=json.load(open(sys.argv[1],encoding='utf-8'))
print(' '.join(c['Name'] for c in d['definitions']))
" "$(win_path "${WORK}/out.json")")"

hr
log "Cost Categories"
log "  account    : management (${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID})"
log "  categories : ${NAMES}"
hr

# --- the two-level roll-up ------------------------------------------------
#
# design 15: the bill rolls up twice, by client for the partner's invoicing and
# by partner for AltDigital's. An account carrying one and not the other is
# allocated on both categories and wrong on one invoice, which no other check
# here would report.
#
# The POPULATION is printed alongside the verdict deliberately. Until the first
# tenant account is vested this reports zero gaps over zero tenant accounts,
# and a reader needs to see the second number to know what the first one is
# worth.
"${PY}" -c "
import json,sys
r=json.load(open(sys.argv[1],encoding='utf-8'))['rollup']
print('%d|%d|%d|%d' % (len(r['gaps']), r['tenant_accounts'],
                       r['shared_accounts'], r['accounts_examined']))
for g in r['gaps']:
    print('GAP %s has %s, missing %s' % (g['account_id'], g['has'], g['missing']))
" "$(win_path "${WORK}/out.json")" > "${WORK}/rollup.txt"

ROLLUP_HEAD="$(head -n 1 "${WORK}/rollup.txt" | no_cr)"
IFS='|' read -r R_GAPS R_TENANT R_SHARED R_TOTAL <<<"${ROLLUP_HEAD}"

log "  roll-up    : ${R_GAPS} gap(s) across ${R_TENANT} tenant and ${R_SHARED} shared account(s)"
if [[ "${R_GAPS}" != "0" ]]; then
  warn "Accounts that roll up on one invoice and not the other:"
  grep '^GAP ' "${WORK}/rollup.txt" | no_cr | while read -r _ ACC _ HAS _ MISSING; do
    warn "    ${ACC}  has ${HAS}, missing ${MISSING}"
  done
  warn "Their spend reaches one of the two invoices and lands in"
  warn "'unregistered' on the other. Fix with scripts/registry.sh put-account."
  hr
elif [[ "${R_TENANT}" == "0" ]]; then
  # Not a warning. A statement of what the zero above is worth.
  info "No tenant accounts exist yet, so the roll-up check passed over"
  log "  AltDigital's own ${R_SHARED} shared account(s) and nothing else."
fi

if [[ -n "${UNREGISTERED}" ]]; then
  # Loud, and not fatal. An unregistered account is a real finding -- newly
  # vested and not yet recorded, or something nobody meant to create -- but
  # refusing to sync would leave EVERY category stale because of one account,
  # which trades a visible problem for an invisible one.
  warn "Accounts in the Organization with no registry record:"
  for A in ${UNREGISTERED}; do warn "    ${A}"; done
  warn "Their spend will appear under 'unregistered' rather than under a"
  warn "tenant. Record them with scripts/registry.sh put-account, or"
  warn "scripts/register-platform-accounts.sh for AltDigital's own."
  hr
fi

if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
  "${PY}" -c "
import json,sys
d=json.load(open(sys.argv[1],encoding='utf-8'))
for c in d['definitions']:
    print('  %-18s %d rule(s): %s' % (
        c['Name'], len(c['Rules']),
        ', '.join(r['Value'] for r in c['Rules'])))
" "$(win_path "${WORK}/out.json")"
  printf '%s DRY%s  would create or update %s definition(s)\n' \
    "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}" "$(echo "${NAMES}" | wc -w | tr -d ' ')"
  exit 0
fi

EXISTING="$(aws ce list-cost-category-definitions \
  --query 'CostCategoryReferences[].[Name,CostCategoryArn]' \
  --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)"

for NAME in ${NAMES}; do
  "${PY}" -c "
import json,sys
d=json.load(open(sys.argv[1],encoding='utf-8'))
c=[x for x in d['definitions'] if x['Name']==sys.argv[2]][0]
json.dump(c['Rules'], open(sys.argv[3],'w',encoding='utf-8'))
" "$(win_path "${WORK}/out.json")" "${NAME}" "$(win_path "${WORK}/rules.json")"

  ARN="$(printf '%s\n' "${EXISTING}" | awk -v n="${NAME}" '$1==n {print $2}')"
  if [[ -n "${ARN}" ]]; then
    # UPDATE, never delete-and-recreate.
    #
    # A Cost Category's history is attached to its ARN. Recreating it starts a
    # new one from today and orphans every closed month, so a report run over
    # last quarter would return nothing and look like a quarter with no spend.
    aws ce update-cost-category-definition \
      --cost-category-arn "${ARN}" \
      --rule-version CostCategoryExpression.v1 \
      --rules "file://$(win_path "${WORK}/rules.json")" >/dev/null \
      || die "Could not update Cost Category ${NAME}."
    ok "updated ${NAME}"
  else
    aws ce create-cost-category-definition \
      --name "${NAME}" \
      --rule-version CostCategoryExpression.v1 \
      --rules "file://$(win_path "${WORK}/rules.json")" >/dev/null \
      || die "Could not create Cost Category ${NAME}."
    ok "created ${NAME}"
  fi
done

hr
info "Cost Explorer takes up to 24 hours to backfill a new category."
log "  Until then a grouped report shows the dimension with no values, which"
log "  is AWS populating it rather than the platform having failed."
hr

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Publish the evidence tenant map into the Audit account.
#
#   scripts/sync-evidence-tenants.sh [--dry-run]
#
# The evidence pipeline files every record against a tenant and a partner, and
# both travel ON the record rather than being derived at query time -- an
# account can be re-parented, and evidence about March must not change because
# an OU moved in September. D-016.
#
# Derived from the account registry, never hand-written here. B-064: a
# hand-maintained account list was missing Forensics, an entire account went
# unchecked, and nothing said so.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) printf 'Usage: %s [--dry-run]\n' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

PY="$(command -v python || command -v python3)" || die "python not found."

AUDIT="$(get_param /org/account/altdig-security-audit)"
[[ -n "${AUDIT}" && "${AUDIT}" != "None" ]] \
  || die "Audit account not registered in SSM."

# Every registered account, from the registry in the management account.
export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*'
ACCOUNTS="$(aws ssm get-parameters-by-path --path /platform/org/account/ \
  --query 'Parameters[].[Name,Value]' --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)"
[[ -n "${ACCOUNTS}" ]] || die "No accounts found under /platform/org/account/."

# The account list goes in a FILE, not on stdin.
#
# `python -` reads its program from stdin, so a here-string carrying the data
# has nowhere to go -- the script ran with empty input and produced a valid,
# empty tenant map. Every evidence record would then have filed as
# unattributed, which the pipeline reports but which is not what anyone
# intended. Silent, syntactically fine, and wrong.
ACCOUNTS_FILE="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "${ACCOUNTS_FILE}"' EXIT
printf "%s\n" "${ACCOUNTS}" > "${ACCOUNTS_FILE}"

# win_path on both. MSYS_NO_PATHCONV is exported above, so REPO_ROOT stays a
# POSIX path that python.exe cannot open -- it reads /c/AltDigital/... as a
# relative path and looks for C:\c\AltDigital.
PAYLOAD="$("${PY}" \
  "$(win_path "${REPO_ROOT}/scripts/lib/evidence_tenants.py")" \
  "$(win_path "${ACCOUNTS_FILE}")")"

COUNT="$("${PY}" -c "
import json,sys
d=json.loads(sys.argv[1])
print(sum(len(v['accounts']) for v in d['tenants'].values()))
" "${PAYLOAD}")"

hr
log "Evidence tenant map"
log "  account  : altdig-security-audit (${AUDIT})"
log "  tenants  : 1 (altdigital-platform — no client tenants vested yet)"
log "  accounts : ${COUNT}"
log "  parameter: /platform/evidence/tenants"
hr

if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
  printf '%s DRY%s  would write /platform/evidence/tenants into %s\n' \
    "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}" "${AUDIT}"
  exit 0
fi

CREDS="$(aws sts assume-role \
  --role-arn "arn:aws:iam::${AUDIT}:role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole" \
  --role-session-name sync-evidence-tenants \
  --query 'Credentials.[AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey,SessionToken]' \
  --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || true
[[ -n "${CREDS}" ]] || die "Could not assume into ${AUDIT}."
read -r AK SK ST <<<"${CREDS}"
(
  unset AWS_PROFILE
  export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="${AK}" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="${SK}" \
         AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="${ST}"
  MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws ssm put-parameter \
    --name /platform/evidence/tenants \
    --value "${PAYLOAD}" \
    --type String \
    --description "Tenants, partners and their accounts for the evidence pipeline. Derived from the account registry; see scripts/sync-evidence-tenants.sh." \
    --overwrite --output text --query Version >/dev/null || exit 1
)
[[ $? -eq 0 ]] || die "Could not write the parameter into ${AUDIT}."
ok "published /platform/evidence/tenants"

hr
info "Re-run this after vesting an account, or evidence from it files under"
log "  the unattributed tenant and raises a finding until it is mapped."
hr

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Publish the account -> notification window map the incident clock reads.
#
#   scripts/sync-notification-windows.sh [--dry-run]
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why the clock needs this, and why it is a published map
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# design 07's notification chain runs from discovery_time against two windows:
#
#   AltDigital -> Partner   (PARTNER.altdig_hours)
#   Partner    -> Client    (PARTNER.notify_hours)
#
# Both live in the registry, which is a DynamoDB table in another account. The
# clock runs in Audit, during an incident, and making it read across an account
# boundary to find out what its own deadline is would put a second account's
# availability on the path of a legally significant clock.
#
# So the map is published INTO Audit as a single SSM parameter, exactly as
# scripts/sync-account-tiers.sh publishes the tier map for the router. Same
# reasoning, same shape, same failure mode if it is not re-run: a newly vested
# account has no entry, and the clock reports that its obligations are unknown
# rather than assuming a default. Re-run this after vesting a client or
# changing a partner's windows.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What is NOT here
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# design 07 says notification windows are fields "at TWO levels — per partner
# and per client". The registry carries them at the PARTNER level only;
# scripts/registry.sh writes no window onto a CLIENT record, and the vesting
# questionnaire's own baa_window_partner_to_client_hours (field 2.6) is
# validated by derive-vesting.py and then not stored anywhere the clock can
# read.
#
# So a client-specific window that differs from its partner's default cannot
# currently be honoured. The partner default is used for every client under it.
# B-059.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) printf 'Usage: %s [--dry-run]\n' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

PY="$(command -v python || command -v python3)" || die "python not found."
TABLE="${PLATFORM_REGISTRY_TABLE:-platform-registry}"
PARAM_NAME="/platform/incident/notification-windows"

AUDIT="$(get_param /org/account/altdig-security-audit)"
[[ -n "${AUDIT}" && "${AUDIT}" != "None" ]] || die "Audit account not registered."

REGISTRY_ACCOUNT="$(get_param "/org/account/altdig-infra-tooling")"
[[ -n "${REGISTRY_ACCOUNT}" && "${REGISTRY_ACCOUNT}" != "None" ]] \
  || die "Registry account not registered."

info "Reading the registry in ${REGISTRY_ACCOUNT}"
CREDS="$(aws sts assume-role \
  --role-arn "arn:aws:iam::${REGISTRY_ACCOUNT}:role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole" \
  --role-session-name sync-windows-read \
  --query 'Credentials.[AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey,SessionToken]' \
  --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || true
[[ -n "${CREDS}" ]] || die "Could not assume into the registry account."
read -r AK SK ST <<<"${CREDS}"

# A SUBSHELL with `unset AWS_PROFILE`, not an inline `AWS_PROFILE=` prefix.
#
# An inline assignment sets the variable to the EMPTY STRING, and the AWS CLI
# then looks for a profile literally named "" and fails with
# "The config profile () could not be found" -- which reads like a broken
# ~/.aws/config rather than like the credentials being overridden correctly.
# There is no way to unset a variable for the duration of one command, so the
# subshell is the mechanism.
#
# stderr is captured rather than discarded for the same reason: the previous
# version sent it to /dev/null and reported "could not read the registry",
# which points at the table and at permissions, and the cause was neither.
SCAN_ERR="$(mktemp)"
SCAN="$( unset AWS_PROFILE
         export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="${AK}" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="${SK}"
         export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="${ST}" MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1
         aws dynamodb scan --table-name "${TABLE}" --output json \
           2>"${SCAN_ERR}" )" || true
if [[ -z "${SCAN}" ]]; then
  die "Could not read the registry table ${TABLE} in ${REGISTRY_ACCOUNT}:
      $(cat "${SCAN_ERR}")"
fi
rm -f "${SCAN_ERR}"

MAP="$(SCAN_JSON="${SCAN}" "${PY}" - <<'MAPEOF'
import json, os, sys

scan = json.loads(os.environ["SCAN_JSON"])
items = scan.get("Items", [])


def val(item, key):
    cell = item.get(key)
    if not cell:
        return None
    return next(iter(cell.values()))


def _int(v):
    try:
        return int(v)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


partners, accounts = {}, []
for item in items:
    kind = val(item, "record_type")
    if kind == "PARTNER":
        partners[val(item, "slug")] = {
            "altdig_to_partner_hours": _int(val(item, "altdig_hours")),
            "partner_to_client_hours": _int(val(item, "notify_hours")),
        }
    elif kind == "ACCOUNT":
        accounts.append(item)

out = {}
for item in accounts:
    account_id = val(item, "account_id")
    partner = val(item, "partner")
    if not account_id:
        continue
    w = partners.get(partner) or {}
    out[account_id] = {
        "partner": partner,
        "client": val(item, "client"),
        # Both may be null. The clock reports an unset window as a finding
        # rather than skipping the incident -- an unknown deadline is worse
        # than a tight one.
        "altdig_to_partner_hours": w.get("altdig_to_partner_hours"),
        "partner_to_client_hours": w.get("partner_to_client_hours"),
    }

print(json.dumps(out, sort_keys=True))
MAPEOF
)" || die "Could not build the window map."

COUNT="$(printf '%s' "${MAP}" | "${PY}" -c 'import json,sys; print(len(json.load(sys.stdin)))')"

hr
log "Notification window map"
log "  accounts : ${COUNT}"
log "  parameter: ${PARAM_NAME}"
log "  target   : altdig-security-audit (${AUDIT})"
hr
printf '%s\n' "${MAP}" | "${PY}" -m json.tool

if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
  printf '%s DRY%s  would write %s in %s\n' \
    "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}" "${PARAM_NAME}" "${AUDIT}"
  exit 0
fi

CREDS="$(aws sts assume-role \
  --role-arn "arn:aws:iam::${AUDIT}:role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole" \
  --role-session-name sync-windows-write \
  --query 'Credentials.[AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey,SessionToken]' \
  --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || true
[[ -n "${CREDS}" ]] || die "Could not assume into the Audit account (${AUDIT})."
read -r AK SK ST <<<"${CREDS}"
unset AWS_PROFILE
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="${AK}" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="${SK}" AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="${ST}"

MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws ssm put-parameter \
  --name "${PARAM_NAME}" \
  --value "${MAP}" \
  --type String \
  --description "Account -> notification windows. Written by scripts/sync-notification-windows.sh from the registry PARTNER records. Read by the incident clock." \
  --overwrite \
  --output text --query Version >/dev/null

ok "wrote ${PARAM_NAME} in ${AUDIT}"
hr
log "The clock re-reads this on a cold start. Re-run after vesting a client or"
log "changing a partner's notification windows, or new accounts will report"
log "their notification obligations as unknown."
hr
files.scripts/sync-pagerduty-secrets.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Copy the PagerDuty routing key from Terraform state into AWS Secrets Manager.
#
#   scripts/sync-pagerduty-secrets.sh [--account <canonical-alias>] [--dry-run]
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why the key moves at all
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CloudFormation resolves {{resolve:secretsmanager:...}} at deploy time, in the
# account and region it is deploying to. Terraform holds the key and
# CloudFormation needs it; Secrets Manager is the handoff.
#
# The alternative — a NoEcho stack parameter — puts the key in the changeset,
# where anyone who can describe the stack can read it. NoEcho hides a value
# from `describe-stacks`; it does not hide it from the changeset, and that gap
# is not widely known.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ONE account holds this, deliberately
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The obvious design puts an alerting topic in every account, which copies this
# credential into every account in the Organization — including member
# accounts, which are the ones a tenant's application can compromise. Instead
# there is one topic in the Audit account and alarms publish to it
# cross-account, so the key exists once and rotates in one place.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The key is never printed
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Not to stdout, not into a temp file read by another process, not into an
# argument. `terraform output -raw` writes it to a variable and the AWS CLI
# reads it from a here-doc on stdin via file://-style indirection. Anything
# that puts it on a command line makes it visible in the process list.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

ACCOUNT_KEY="altdig-security-audit"
SECRET_NAME="platform/pagerduty/routing-key"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --account) ACCOUNT_KEY="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --secret)  SECRET_NAME="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help)
      printf 'Usage: %s [--account <alias>] [--secret <name>] [--dry-run]\n' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

TF="$(find_tool terraform)" || die "terraform not found. Run scripts/setup-tooling.sh."
TFDIR="${REPO_ROOT}/pagerduty"

[[ -f "${TFDIR}/terraform.tfstate" ]] || die "No Terraform state in pagerduty/.
      Run scripts/pagerduty-apply.sh --apply first."

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

TARGET="$(get_param "/org/account/${ACCOUNT_KEY}")"
[[ -n "${TARGET}" && "${TARGET}" != "None" ]] || die "Unknown account: ${ACCOUNT_KEY}"

KEY="$(cd "${TFDIR}" && "${TF}" output -raw cloudwatch_integration_key 2>/dev/null)" || true
[[ -n "${KEY}" ]] || die "Could not read cloudwatch_integration_key from Terraform output."

# The low-urgency key is optional: the low-urgency service may not have been
# applied, and on a plan tier without Event Orchestration its priority half
# fails while the service itself still exists. Absent means the dev/test path
# is simply not wired, which is a supported state.
LOW_KEY="$(cd "${TFDIR}" && "${TF}" output -raw cloudwatch_low_integration_key 2>/dev/null)" || true

# Events API v2 routing keys, added alongside the CloudWatch ones rather than
# replacing them. Two integrations on the same service:
#
#   cloudwatch    the SNS subscription. Parses an SNS-wrapped CloudWatch alarm
#                 and nothing else. Kept as the fallback that still works when
#                 the router is broken.
#   events_v2     the router. Takes arbitrary JSON in custom_details, which is
#                 how the page carries the full dossier, and a dedup_key, which
#                 is how the raw alarm and the dossier that follows become one
#                 incident instead of two.
#
# Empty is tolerated: a tenant that has not applied the Terraform change yet has
# no v2 integration, and the router refuses to page rather than pretending it
# did. Failing here instead would break the CloudWatch key sync as well.
V2_KEY="$(cd "${TFDIR}" && "${TF}" output -raw events_v2_routing_key 2>/dev/null)" || true
V2_KEY_LOW="$(cd "${TFDIR}" && "${TF}" output -raw events_v2_routing_key_low 2>/dev/null)" || true

# Length check only. The value is never echoed, and a routing key is a 32
# character hex-ish token — a wildly different length means the wrong output
# was read, which is worth catching before it becomes a subscription that
# silently discards every page.
[[ ${#KEY} -ge 20 ]] || die "Routing key looks wrong (${#KEY} characters). Refusing to write it."

hr
log "PagerDuty routing key -> Secrets Manager"
log "  account : ${ACCOUNT_KEY} (${TARGET})"
log "  secret  : ${SECRET_NAME}"
log "  keys    : cloudwatch $([[ -n "${KEY}" ]] && echo present || echo MISSING), events_v2 $([[ -n "${V2_KEY}" ]] && echo present || echo 'MISSING — run terraform apply; the router cannot page without it')"
log "  region  : ${AWS_DEFAULT_REGION}"
log "  key     : ${#KEY} characters (not printed)"
hr

if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
  printf '%s DRY%s  would write %s into %s\n' "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}" "${SECRET_NAME}" "${TARGET}"
  exit 0
fi

CREDS="$(aws sts assume-role \
  --role-arn "arn:aws:iam::${TARGET}:role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole" \
  --role-session-name platform-pd-sync \
  --query 'Credentials.[AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey,SessionToken]' \
  --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || true
[[ -n "${CREDS}" ]] || die "Could not assume into ${TARGET}."
read -r AK SK ST <<<"${CREDS}"
unset AWS_PROFILE
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="${AK}" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="${SK}" AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="${ST}"

PAYLOAD="$(printf '{"integration_key":"%s","events_v2_routing_key":"%s"}'   "${KEY}" "${V2_KEY}")"

if MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws secretsmanager describe-secret \
     --secret-id "${SECRET_NAME}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  info "secret exists — updating"
  MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws secretsmanager put-secret-value \
    --secret-id "${SECRET_NAME}" \
    --secret-string "${PAYLOAD}" \
    --query 'VersionId' --output text >/dev/null
  ok "rotated ${SECRET_NAME}"
  warn "Rotation is only half done. CloudFormation resolved the OLD key into
      the SNS subscription endpoint at deploy time, and it does not re-resolve
      on its own. Redeploy alerting/10-alert-topic.yaml, then confirm the
      subscription is Confirmed rather than PendingConfirmation."
else
  info "creating secret"
  MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws secretsmanager create-secret \
    --name "${SECRET_NAME}" \
    --description "PagerDuty CloudWatch routing key for the platform alerting topic" \
    --secret-string "${PAYLOAD}" \
    --tags Key=platform-managed,Value=true \
    --query 'ARN' --output text >/dev/null
  ok "created ${SECRET_NAME}"
fi

# --- low-urgency key ------------------------------------------------------
if [[ -n "${LOW_KEY}" ]]; then
  [[ ${#LOW_KEY} -ge 20 ]] || die "Low-urgency routing key looks wrong (${#LOW_KEY} characters)."
  LOW_SECRET="${SECRET_NAME}-low"
  LOW_PAYLOAD="$(printf '{"integration_key":"%s","events_v2_routing_key":"%s"}'     "${LOW_KEY}" "${V2_KEY_LOW}")"
  if MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws secretsmanager describe-secret        --secret-id "${LOW_SECRET}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws secretsmanager put-secret-value       --secret-id "${LOW_SECRET}" --secret-string "${LOW_PAYLOAD}"       --query 'VersionId' --output text >/dev/null
    ok "rotated ${LOW_SECRET} (${#LOW_KEY} characters, not printed)"
  else
    MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws secretsmanager create-secret       --name "${LOW_SECRET}"       --description "PagerDuty routing key for the LOW-URGENCY platform service (dev and test)"       --secret-string "${LOW_PAYLOAD}"       --tags Key=platform-managed,Value=true       --query 'ARN' --output text >/dev/null
    ok "created ${LOW_SECRET} (${#LOW_KEY} characters, not printed)"
  fi
else
  warn "No low-urgency integration key in the Terraform output. Dev and test
      alarms will be created with no actions. Apply the low-urgency service
      first if that is not intended."
fi

# --- commercial routing key -----------------------------------------------
#
# design 12's client-conversation class. A DIFFERENT service from the platform
# one and a different urgency: these notify, they do not page.
#
# Kept separate from the platform secret rather than added as another field in
# it, because the two have different blast radii. Anything holding the platform
# key can page the on-call rotation; anything holding this one can raise a
# low-urgency notification. A consumer that only needs the second should not be
# given the first as a side effect of them sharing a secret.
COMM_KEY="$(cd "${TFDIR}" && "${TF}" output -raw commercial_routing_key 2>/dev/null)" || true
if [[ -n "${COMM_KEY}" ]]; then
  [[ ${#COMM_KEY} -ge 20 ]] || die "Commercial routing key looks wrong (${#COMM_KEY} characters)."
  COMM_SECRET="platform/pagerduty/commercial-routing-key"
  COMM_PAYLOAD="$(printf '{"events_v2_routing_key":"%s"}' "${COMM_KEY}")"
  if MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws secretsmanager describe-secret        --secret-id "${COMM_SECRET}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws secretsmanager put-secret-value       --secret-id "${COMM_SECRET}" --secret-string "${COMM_PAYLOAD}"       --query 'VersionId' --output text >/dev/null
    ok "rotated ${COMM_SECRET} (${#COMM_KEY} characters, not printed)"
  else
    MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws secretsmanager create-secret       --name "${COMM_SECRET}"       --description "PagerDuty Events API v2 routing key for the client-conversation service (design 12). Notifies; does not page."       --secret-string "${COMM_PAYLOAD}"       --tags Key=platform-managed,Value=true       --query 'ARN' --output text >/dev/null
    ok "created ${COMM_SECRET} (${#COMM_KEY} characters, not printed)"
  fi
else
  # Not fatal, and not silent. B-115: the commercial service was committed as
  # deployed and had never been applied, so an absent key here is exactly the
  # symptom that went unnoticed.
  warn "No commercial_routing_key in the Terraform output. design 12's
      client-conversation events have a router and no destination. Apply the
      PagerDuty configuration first if that is not intended."
fi

hr
info "Next: redeploy the alerting stack so it creates the subscription"
log "  scripts/deploy-to-account.sh --account ${ACCOUNT_KEY} \\"
log "    --template alerting/10-alert-topic.yaml --stack platform-alerting \\"
log "    OrganizationId=<o-...> PagerDutySecretName=${SECRET_NAME} \\"
log "    LowUrgencySecretName=${SECRET_NAME}-low"
hr
files.scripts/sync-pagerduty-tenants.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# After a PagerDuty apply: routing keys into Secrets Manager, service ids back
# into the registry.
#
#   scripts/sync-pagerduty-tenants.sh [--dry-run]
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why this is a separate step and not part of the apply
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A routing key does not exist until the integration exists. It cannot be known
# in advance, cannot be written by hand, and cannot be resolved by
# CloudFormation at deploy time. So the order is fixed:
#
#   render-pagerduty-tenants.sh   registry  -> pagerduty/tenants.json
#   pagerduty-apply.sh --apply    tenants.json -> PagerDuty
#   sync-pagerduty-tenants.sh     PagerDuty -> Secrets Manager + registry
#
# The last step is what makes the saga resumable. Provisioning step 3 does not
# call PagerDuty and does not parse Terraform output; it asks the registry
# whether this tenant has a PagerDuty footprint, and the answer got there from
# here. A saga resumed next week on a different machine reaches the same
# conclusion, because the state was never in anybody's shell.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Where the keys go, and where they eventually need to go
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Written into AUDIT today, alongside the platform's own routing keys.
#
# That is NOT where they finally belong. A tenant's alarms fire in the tenant's
# own account, and the SNS subscription that carries them to PagerDuty is
# created by the baseline in that account -- so the key has to be readable
# there. Distributing it is part of provisioning step 6 (instrumentation),
# which is not built.
#
# Audit is the right interim home rather than a wrong one: it is where the
# alerting layer lives, the keys are inert until something subscribes using
# them, and leaving them unwritten would mean the apply's only durable output
# existed solely in local Terraform state. B-119 records the distribution.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

ACCOUNT_KEY="altdig-security-audit"
PREFIX="platform/pagerduty/tenant"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    --account) ACCOUNT_KEY="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --prefix)  PREFIX="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -h|--help)
      printf 'Usage: %s [--dry-run] [--account <alias>] [--prefix <path>]\n' "$0"
      exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

TF="$(find_tool terraform)" || die "terraform not found. Run scripts/setup-tooling.sh."
TFDIR="${REPO_ROOT}/pagerduty"

TARGET="$(get_param "/org/account/${ACCOUNT_KEY}")"
[[ -n "${TARGET}" && "${TARGET}" != "None" ]] || die "Unknown account: ${ACCOUNT_KEY}"

TOOLING="$(get_param /org/account/altdig-infra-tooling)"
[[ -n "${TOOLING}" && "${TOOLING}" != "None" ]] \
  || die "Platform Tooling is not registered in SSM; the registry cannot be written."

# `terraform output -json`, not `-raw`. The tenants output is a nested map and
# is marked sensitive, so -raw cannot render it and the redaction that applies
# to console output does not apply to -json.
TENANTS="$(cd "${TFDIR}" && "${TF}" output -json tenants 2>/dev/null)" || true
[[ -n "${TENANTS}" && "${TENANTS}" != "null" ]] \
  || die "No 'tenants' output from Terraform. Run scripts/pagerduty-apply.sh --apply first."

COUNT="$(cd "${TFDIR}" && "${TF}" output -raw tenant_count 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || COUNT=0

hr
log "PagerDuty tenant sync"
log "  clients in terraform state : ${COUNT:-0}"
log "  secrets into              : ${ACCOUNT_KEY} (${TARGET})"
log "  registry in               : altdig-infra-tooling (${TOOLING})"
hr

if [[ "${COUNT:-0}" == "0" ]]; then
  # Zero clients is a legitimate state and NOT a failure. Saying so explicitly,
  # because "wrote 0 secrets" and "could not read the output" look identical in
  # a log and mean opposite things.
  ok "no tenants under management; nothing to sync."
  exit 0
fi

# The plan is computed in python and executed in bash, so that what gets
# written is inspectable before anything is written. Routing keys are never
# printed -- only their lengths and the secret names.
PLAN="$(TENANTS="${TENANTS}" PREFIX="${PREFIX}" python - <<'PYEOF'
import json, os

tenants = json.loads(os.environ["TENANTS"])
prefix = os.environ["PREFIX"]

secrets, registry, problems = [], [], []

for client, data in sorted(tenants.items()):
    objects = data.get("objects") or {}
    counts = data.get("counts") or {}

    # Declared-versus-found, per client. counts comes from Terraform and says
    # how many services the module BUILT; objects is what came back with a
    # routing key. A mismatch means an apply half-succeeded, and reporting the
    # keys we happen to have would hide it.
    if len(objects) != counts.get("objects", len(objects)):
        problems.append({
            "client": client,
            "problem": "the module reports {0} object services and {1} came "
                       "back with routing keys".format(
                           counts.get("objects"), len(objects))})

    for key, svc in sorted(objects.items()):
        tier, obj = key.split("/", 1)
        name = "{0}/{1}/{2}/{3}".format(prefix, client, tier, obj or "app")
        routing = svc.get("routing_key")
        if not routing:
            problems.append({
                "client": client, "object": key,
                "problem": "service exists with no routing key; the "
                           "integration was not created"})
            continue
        secrets.append({"name": name, "key": routing,
                        "client": client, "tier": tier,
                        "object": obj or "app",
                        "service_id": svc.get("service_id")})

    registry.append({
        "client": client,
        "business_service_id": data.get("conversations_business_service_id"),
        "tier_services": json.dumps(data.get("tiers") or {}, sort_keys=True),
        "object_services": json.dumps(
            {k: v.get("service_id") for k, v in sorted(objects.items())},
            sort_keys=True),
    })

print(json.dumps({"secrets": secrets, "registry": registry,
                  "problems": problems}))
PYEOF
)" || die "Could not build the sync plan."

PROBLEMS="$(printf '%s' "${PLAN}" | python -c 'import json,sys; print(len(json.load(sys.stdin)["problems"]))')"
if [[ "${PROBLEMS}" != "0" ]]; then
  printf '%s' "${PLAN}" | python -c '
import json, sys
for p in json.load(sys.stdin)["problems"]:
    print("  " + json.dumps(p))
'
  die "${PROBLEMS} inconsistency(ies) between what the module built and what came back. Re-run the apply; do not sync a partial result."
fi

NSECRETS="$(printf '%s' "${PLAN}" | python -c 'import json,sys; print(len(json.load(sys.stdin)["secrets"]))')"
info "${NSECRETS} routing key(s) to write"

if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
  printf '%s' "${PLAN}" | python -c '
import json, sys
d = json.load(sys.stdin)
for s in d["secrets"]:
    print("  DRY  would write {0} ({1} characters, not printed)".format(
        s["name"], len(s["key"])))
for r in d["registry"]:
    print("  DRY  would stamp TENANT#{0} with business_service_id={1}".format(
        r["client"], r["business_service_id"]))
'
  exit 0
fi

# --- routing keys ----------------------------------------------------------

while IFS=$'\t' read -r NAME KEYVAL; do
  [[ -n "${NAME}" ]] || continue
  PAYLOAD="$(printf '{"events_v2_routing_key":"%s"}' "${KEYVAL}")"
  if in_account "${TARGET}" aws secretsmanager describe-secret \
       --secret-id "${NAME}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    in_account "${TARGET}" aws secretsmanager put-secret-value \
      --secret-id "${NAME}" --secret-string "${PAYLOAD}" \
      --query VersionId --output text >/dev/null \
      && ok "rotated ${NAME} (${#KEYVAL} characters, not printed)"
  else
    in_account "${TARGET}" aws secretsmanager create-secret \
      --name "${NAME}" --secret-string "${PAYLOAD}" \
      --description "PagerDuty routing key for a tenant service. Written by scripts/sync-pagerduty-tenants.sh." \
      --tags Key=platform-managed,Value=true \
      --query ARN --output text >/dev/null \
      && ok "created ${NAME} (${#KEYVAL} characters, not printed)"
  fi
done < <(printf '%s' "${PLAN}" | python -c '
import json, sys
for s in json.load(sys.stdin)["secrets"]:
    print(s["name"] + "\t" + s["key"])
')
unset PAYLOAD

# --- registry write-back ---------------------------------------------------
#
# The saga reads THIS, not Terraform state. Stamped last, so a failure above
# leaves the registry saying the tenant has no PagerDuty footprint -- which is
# recoverable by re-running -- rather than saying it has one that is not fully
# wired.

while IFS=$'\t' read -r CLIENT BSID TIERS OBJECTS; do
  [[ -n "${CLIENT}" ]] || continue
  in_account "${TOOLING}" aws dynamodb update-item \
    --table-name platform-registry \
    --key "{\"PK\":{\"S\":\"TENANT#${CLIENT}\"},\"SK\":{\"S\":\"META\"}}" \
    --update-expression "SET pagerduty_business_service_id = :b, pagerduty_tier_services = :t, pagerduty_object_services = :o, updated_at = :u" \
    --expression-attribute-values "{\":b\":{\"S\":\"${BSID}\"},\":t\":{\"S\":${TIERS}},\":o\":{\"S\":${OBJECTS}},\":u\":{\"S\":\"$(now_iso)\"}}" \
    --condition-expression "attribute_exists(PK)" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    && ok "stamped TENANT#${CLIENT}" \
    || warn "could not stamp TENANT#${CLIENT} -- the registry record must exist first (saga step 1)."
done < <(printf '%s' "${PLAN}" | python -c '
import json, sys
for r in json.load(sys.stdin)["registry"]:
    print("\t".join([r["client"], r["business_service_id"] or "",
                     json.dumps(r["tier_services"]),
                     json.dumps(r["object_services"])]))
')

hr
info "Next: re-run the provisioning saga. Step 3 reads the registry and will"
log "  now find pagerduty_business_service_id, so it advances rather than"
log "  blocking."
hr
files.scripts/sync-quorum-approvers.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Publish the authorised quorum approvers to SSM in the Audit account.
#
#   scripts/sync-quorum-approvers.sh [--dry-run]
#
# Reads config/quorum.env, which is gitignored. An Atlassian accountId
# identifies an individual, so the list lives in a local file and in Parameter
# Store, never in the repository.
#
# design/03-identity-and-access.md: two approvals from {Jamie, Wayne, Art},
# requester and approvers distinct, for KMS key deletion, backup vault deletion
# or lock modification, account removal from the Organization, and disabling
# CloudTrail or the Config recorder.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) printf 'Usage: %s [--dry-run]\n' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

QUORUM_FILE="${REPO_ROOT}/config/quorum.env"
[[ -f "${QUORUM_FILE}" ]] || die "config/quorum.env not found.
      Copy config/quorum.env.example and fill in the accountIds.
      Find one with scripts/jira-check.sh, or from
      https://<site>.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/myself"

# shellcheck disable=SC1090
source "${QUORUM_FILE}"

APPROVERS=()
for VAR in QUORUM_APPROVER_1 QUORUM_APPROVER_2 QUORUM_APPROVER_3 \
           QUORUM_APPROVER_4 QUORUM_APPROVER_5; do
  VALUE="${!VAR:-}"
  [[ -n "${VALUE}" ]] || continue
  # An Atlassian accountId looks like 712020:uuid or a bare hex id. An email
  # address here is the mistake worth catching by name: the approval records
  # carry accountIds, so an address would match nobody and every approval
  # would read as unauthorised -- a configuration error wearing the costume of
  # a security finding.
  [[ "${VALUE}" != *"@"* ]] \
    || die "${VAR} looks like an email address: ${VALUE}
      Quorum approvers are Atlassian accountIds, not addresses. An address
      matches no approval record, so every approval would be reported as
      coming from an unauthorised person."
  APPROVERS+=("${VALUE}")
done

MINIMUM="${QUORUM_MINIMUM_APPROVALS:-2}"

[[ "${#APPROVERS[@]}" -gt 0 ]] || die "config/quorum.env lists no approvers."

# design 03 says two. Refuse to publish a quorum of one rather than letting it
# be discovered at execution time -- a control that one person can satisfy is
# not two-party control, and the failure is silent unless somebody looks.
[[ "${MINIMUM}" -ge 2 ]] || die "QUORUM_MINIMUM_APPROVALS is ${MINIMUM}.
      design 03 requires two approvals from distinct people. A quorum of one
      is not a quorum, and this script will not publish one."

if [[ "${#APPROVERS[@]}" -lt "${MINIMUM}" ]]; then
  # Not fatal. The list grows as partners are onboarded, and a platform that
  # refuses to hold the parameter until then is harder to bootstrap than one
  # that holds it and refuses to EXECUTE. The verifier enforces the count.
  warn "${#APPROVERS[@]} approver(s) configured but ${MINIMUM} are required."
  warn "Quorum actions will correctly refuse to execute until there are"
  warn "${MINIMUM} distinct people on this list. This is B-079, not a bug."
fi

PAYLOAD="$("$(command -v python || command -v python3)" -c '
import json, sys
print(json.dumps({"approvers": sys.argv[1:-1],
                  "minimum": int(sys.argv[-1])}, separators=(",", ":")))
' "${APPROVERS[@]}" "${MINIMUM}")"

AUDIT="$(get_param /org/account/altdig-security-audit)"
[[ -n "${AUDIT}" && "${AUDIT}" != "None" ]] \
  || die "Audit account not registered in SSM."

hr
log "Quorum approvers"
log "  account  : altdig-security-audit (${AUDIT})"
log "  approvers: ${#APPROVERS[@]}"
log "  minimum  : ${MINIMUM}"
log "  parameter: /platform/quorum/approvers"
hr
# The ids themselves are not printed. They identify people, and this output
# lands in terminals and CI logs.

if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
  printf '%s DRY%s  would write /platform/quorum/approvers into %s\n' \
    "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}" "${AUDIT}"
  exit 0
fi

CREDS="$(aws sts assume-role \
  --role-arn "arn:aws:iam::${AUDIT}:role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole" \
  --role-session-name sync-quorum-approvers \
  --query 'Credentials.[AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey,SessionToken]' \
  --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || true
[[ -n "${CREDS}" ]] || die "Could not assume into ${AUDIT}."
read -r AK SK ST <<<"${CREDS}"
(
  unset AWS_PROFILE
  export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="${AK}" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="${SK}" \
         AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="${ST}"
  # MSYS_NO_PATHCONV: the parameter name starts with a slash and would
  # otherwise arrive as C:/Program Files/Git/platform/quorum/approvers.
  MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws ssm put-parameter \
    --name /platform/quorum/approvers \
    --value "${PAYLOAD}" \
    --type String \
    --description "Atlassian accountIds authorised to approve a quorum-controlled action, and how many are required. design 03." \
    --overwrite --output text --query Version >/dev/null \
    || exit 1
)
[[ $? -eq 0 ]] || die "Could not write the parameter into ${AUDIT}."
ok "published /platform/quorum/approvers"

hr
info "The verifier reads this on every quorum request. To change the list,"
log "  edit config/quorum.env and run this again."
log ""
info "It does NOT change who Jira lets approve. That is the Approver groups"
log "  field and the group membership, and the two lists are independent by"
log "  design: Jira decides who CAN answer, this decides whose answer COUNTS."
hr
files.scripts/sync-tenant-facts.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Publish the account -> tenant facts map the reconciliation engine reads.
#
#   scripts/sync-tenant-facts.sh [--dry-run]
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What is in it and why it is per account
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Two facts, both per tenant, both needed by change reconciliation (8.2):
#
#   jira_change_project   which Jira project holds THIS tenant's change records
#   change_approver       who an unapproved-deployment ticket is routed to
#
# design 08 routes a deployment with no change record to "the tenant's change
# approver", and questionnaire 1.7 collects that per client. Tenants must not
# see each other's change records, so the project is a property of the account
# rather than a platform constant.
#
# Same publishing arrangement as /platform/routing/account-tiers and
# /platform/incident/notification-windows: the registry is the source of truth
# and lives in another account, and the consumer runs in Audit. Reading across
# an account boundary on every reconciliation run would put a second account's
# availability in the path of a compliance control.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Three maps, three scripts, one registry
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# This is the third script that scans the registry and publishes a slice of it
# into Audit. The duplication is real and is deliberate for now: each map has
# one consumer and one meaning, and collapsing them into a single tenant-facts
# document would couple the routing layer, the incident clock and the
# reconciliation engine to one another's release cycles.
#
# Worth revisiting once there is a fourth. B-066.

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/common.sh"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) printf 'Usage: %s [--dry-run]\n' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "Unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="${PLATFORM_HOME_REGION}"
require_cli
require_account "${PLATFORM_MGMT_ACCOUNT_ID}"

PY="$(command -v python || command -v python3)" || die "python not found."
TABLE="${PLATFORM_REGISTRY_TABLE:-platform-registry}"
PARAM_NAME="/platform/change/tenant-facts"

AUDIT="$(get_param /org/account/altdig-security-audit)"
[[ -n "${AUDIT}" && "${AUDIT}" != "None" ]] || die "Audit account not registered."

REGISTRY_ACCOUNT="$(get_param /org/account/altdig-infra-tooling)"
[[ -n "${REGISTRY_ACCOUNT}" && "${REGISTRY_ACCOUNT}" != "None" ]] \
  || die "Registry account not registered."

info "Reading the registry in ${REGISTRY_ACCOUNT}"
CREDS="$(aws sts assume-role \
  --role-arn "arn:aws:iam::${REGISTRY_ACCOUNT}:role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole" \
  --role-session-name sync-facts-read \
  --query 'Credentials.[AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey,SessionToken]' \
  --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || true
[[ -n "${CREDS}" ]] || die "Could not assume into the registry account."
read -r AK SK ST <<<"${CREDS}"

# Subshell with `unset AWS_PROFILE`, not an inline AWS_PROFILE= prefix -- that
# sets an EMPTY profile name and the CLI fails with "The config profile ()
# could not be found", which points at ~/.aws/config. B-061.
SCAN_ERR="$(mktemp)"
SCAN="$( unset AWS_PROFILE
         export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="${AK}" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="${SK}"
         export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="${ST}" MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1
         aws dynamodb scan --table-name "${TABLE}" --output json \
           2>"${SCAN_ERR}" )" || true
if [[ -z "${SCAN}" ]]; then
  die "Could not read the registry table ${TABLE} in ${REGISTRY_ACCOUNT}:
      $(cat "${SCAN_ERR}")"
fi
rm -f "${SCAN_ERR}"

MAP="$(SCAN_JSON="${SCAN}" DEFAULT_PROJECT="${PLATFORM_JIRA_DEFAULT_CHANGE_PROJECT:-}" \
       "${PY}" - <<'MAPEOF'
import json, os

scan = json.loads(os.environ["SCAN_JSON"])
default_project = os.environ.get("DEFAULT_PROJECT") or None


def val(item, key):
    cell = item.get(key)
    if not cell:
        return None
    return next(iter(cell.values()))


clients, accounts = {}, []
for item in scan.get("Items", []):
    kind = val(item, "record_type")
    if kind == "CLIENT":
        clients[(val(item, "partner"), val(item, "slug"))] = item
    elif kind == "ACCOUNT":
        accounts.append(item)

out = {}
for item in accounts:
    account_id = val(item, "account_id")
    if not account_id:
        continue
    client = clients.get((val(item, "partner"), val(item, "client"))) or {}
    out[account_id] = {
        "partner": val(item, "partner"),
        "client": val(item, "client"),
        # Null is meaningful, not missing. design 08 allows a tenant to keep
        # their own pipeline, and some will keep their own Jira -- the engine
        # then reports the change source as UNAVAILABLE rather than reporting
        # every deployment as unapproved.
        "jira_change_project": val(item, "jira_change_project")
                               or val(client, "jira_change_project")
                               or default_project,
        "change_approver": val(client, "change_approver"),
        # B-127. Which PagerDuty service an APPLICATION-layer alarm reaches.
        # The tenant services are keyed (tier, object) and the object is this
        # app, so without it the router cannot name the tenant's own service
        # and falls back to paging AltDigital.
        "app": val(item, "app"),
    }

print(json.dumps(out, sort_keys=True))
MAPEOF
)" || die "Could not build the tenant facts map."

COUNT="$(printf '%s' "${MAP}" | "${PY}" -c 'import json,sys; print(len(json.load(sys.stdin)))')"

hr
log "Tenant facts map"
log "  accounts : ${COUNT}"
log "  parameter: ${PARAM_NAME}"
log "  target   : altdig-security-audit (${AUDIT})"
log "  default  : ${PLATFORM_JIRA_DEFAULT_CHANGE_PROJECT:-<unset>}"
hr
printf '%s\n' "${MAP}" | "${PY}" -m json.tool

if [[ "${COUNT}" == "0" ]]; then
  warn "No member accounts in the registry yet."
  log  "      Reconciliation will have nothing to reconcile, which is correct"
  log  "      before the first tenant is vested -- not a failure."
fi

if [[ "${DRY_RUN}" == "1" ]]; then
  printf '%s DRY%s  would write %s in %s\n' \
    "${C_YELLOW}" "${C_RESET}" "${PARAM_NAME}" "${AUDIT}"
  exit 0
fi

CREDS="$(aws sts assume-role \
  --role-arn "arn:aws:iam::${AUDIT}:role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole" \
  --role-session-name sync-facts-write \
  --query 'Credentials.[AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey,SessionToken]' \
  --output text 2>/dev/null | no_cr)" || true
[[ -n "${CREDS}" ]] || die "Could not assume into the Audit account (${AUDIT})."
read -r AK SK ST <<<"${CREDS}"
unset AWS_PROFILE
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="${AK}" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="${SK}" AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="${ST}"

MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 aws ssm put-parameter \
  --name "${PARAM_NAME}" \
  --value "${MAP}" \
  --type String \
  --description "Account -> tenant facts for change reconciliation. Written by scripts/sync-tenant-facts.sh from the registry." \
  --overwrite \
  --output text --query Version >/dev/null

ok "wrote ${PARAM_NAME} in ${AUDIT}"
hr
log "Re-run after vesting a client or changing a tenant's change project."
log "An account absent from this map has its deployments reconciled against"
log "the platform default, and every finding records that it did so."
hr
